elements.label: text
elements.text: INTRODUCTION

elements.label: text
elements.text: As an important branch of the national economy the textile industry is called on to expand so as to satisfy the needs of the growing personal and industrial use of textiles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: This is possible due to recent advances in the process and engineering developments in all of the fields of production, including

elements.label: text
elements.text: good and reliable maintenance and repair.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Modern machinery is characterized not only by high productivity and efficiency, but also by high complexity. A more economical operation necessitates a good organization of technical maintenance and repairs of the available machines and equipment, and their proper adjustment according to prescribed technological procedures.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Referring particularly to textile machinery, it should be said that it works under extremely difficult conditions, i.e. high speeds (the rotational speed of the shaft at open-end spinning is 60 000 m i n -1 and higher), high dynamic loads (such as obtained in scutchers, cards, drawing frames, and looms), etc. The majority of textile machines operate in a dust-laden atmosphere at high humidity. The working organs of textile machines are in direct contact with the processed raw materials which causes machine wear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The proper lubrication of all rubbing machine parts is always important in order to ensure their faultless running especially under conditions where textile enterprises are working in more than two shifts which results in high loading on the machines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: This causes the accelerated physical wear of working elements, mechanisms and parts of textile machines, and various disarrangements that result in the reduction of labour productivity, machine efficiency, and products quality.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The equipment used at textile enterprises is maintained in good operational condition by adjusters, assistant foremen, repair workers, fitters, oilers, etc. For the same purpose, textile enterprises have various facilities to carry out repair, design and experimental jobs relating to the never-ending search for new methods and more economical operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 8 Introduction

elements.label: text
elements.text: The operation and repair of modern textile machinery involve considerable labour and money inputs. The quality and the costs of machine repairs are greatly dependent on the type of equipment used in repair shops which must be efficient and reduce production costs. However, in order to be more economical, repair and maintenance operationsshould be performed by highly qualified and properly trained personnel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The present manual is designed as a study aid for the training of repair and maintenance personnel.

elements.text: GENERAL NOTES ON DISARRANGEMENTS

elements.label: text
elements.text: IN MACHINES

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Longevity and Reliability of Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: Terms characterizing longevity and reliability Serviceability is the state of a machine in which it will give good service (accomplish predetermined functions) under the normal operating conditions. Any disarrangement in machine serviceability iscalled a failure.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The time (in hours) or the volume of accomplished work (in running metres or other units) is called theoutput. In the course of m a chine operation, a difference ismade between the daily and monthly output to the first failure, the output between failures, and so on.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The capacity of the machine to perform predetermined functions, maintaining performance values within preset limits during the required time or output is called reliability.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Longevity is the capacity of the machine to give good service- (with required breaks envisaged for technical maintenance and repairs) during the time till its ultimate condition specified in the technical documentation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Resource is the output of the machine during the time till its ultimate condition specified in the technical documentations.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Servicelifeis the length of machine operation till its ultimate condition specified in the technical documentation or till the moment when the machine is discarded.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The following classification has been adopted: service life to first overhaul or medium repairs, service life between overhauls, and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Although there is much in common between the machine resourceand its service life as they both are determined by its ultimate state, they differ only in the following: the service life is the calendar time of operation, while machine resource is the output till the time of its ultimate condition. With the same machine resource the service lifem a y be different depending on the intensity of machine operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Machines used in textile enterprises are constructed from different parts and attachments (auxiliary materials). Some parts are replaced by new ones after the first failure. Such parts are called.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 10 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: non-restorable. To such pertain, for instance, different small axles, rollers, certain antifriction bearings, levers, elements of automatic equipment (diodes, triodes, resistances, condensers, etc.), paper tubes,

elements.label: text
elements.text: harnesses, healds, small aprons, nuts, etc. Other partsmay have more than one failure in the course of operation. After every failure they are reconditioned (repaired). Such parts are called repairable. To such pertain most of the machine parts such as shafts, bearings, fluted rollers, spindles, flyers, cams, ratchets, rods and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The capacity of machines to keep serviceability, without forced interruptions, for the time a certain output is produced is called failure-freeperformance. The reliability of repaired machines (parts) ■considerably depends on failure-free performance, and on maintain­

elements.label: text
elements.text: abilitywhich is the state of a machine amenable to failure and disarrangement prevention and elimination. An important indicator of the reliability of the reconditioned jnachine is its availability factor Faand utilization factor Fu.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The availabilityfactor (Fa) characterizes a portion of the machine •operation time from the total time, for the failure-free operation T and restoration process Tr, i.e. for the elimination of consequences of one failure

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fa= T/(T+Tr) The utilizationfactor (Fu) characterizes a portion of the machine failure-free operation time from the total time of failure-free operation, the process of restoration, and preventive maintenance caused by one failure

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fu=T/(T+Tr+ Tp.m .)

elements.label: text
elements.text: The normal operation of the machine is impaired when different

elements.label: text
elements.text: kinds of troubles crop up in its parts, conjugated units, assemblies and mechanisms, i.e. wear of friction surfaces, residual deformations {dents and notches, residual sagging, twisting, etc.), breakages, cracks and corrosion defects.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Determining the technical condition of the equipment in operation. In the course of machine operation, its serviceability decreases. This results in frequent disarrangements of mechanisms, assemblies, ■deterioration of the quality of products, increased rejects, greater consumption of raw materials, lower efficiency, and higher power consumption, noise, knocks, vibrations, etc. When proceeding to

elements.label: text
elements.text: the outward examination of the machine the following points are to be established: the degree of contamination of separate parts and assemblies, the proper position of parts, visible traces of their deteri­

elements.label: text
elements.text: oration, loose fitting, deterioration of protection coatings, improper feed of lubricant, and other possible troubles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Defects of products reveal the kind of disarrangements in assemblies and mechanisms. So, for instance, ifthe yarn produced in a spinning frame is twitty, this means that there are disarrangements in

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 11

elements.label: text
elements.text: the drafting system, such as loose keys in the gears of the drive to the cylinders, broken teeth on the gears of the drive to the drafting system, and the eccentricity of pressure rollers. When in good condition and not subjected to the effect of ambient heat, machine assemblies usually heat up to 40-50°C. Heating-up to higher temperatures occurs due to improper mating of parts, their misalignment, small clearances, high specific loads and poor lubrication.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The general technical condition of the equipment may be assessed indirectly by checking the duration of run-out, or the time of machine self-braking.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The time of run-out or self-braking is t h e t i m e r e q u i r e d for full s t o p page of the machine at idle running after drive disengagement.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The longer is the time of self-braking, the lower are the mechanical losses and consequently the power consumption.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When proceeding to the examination of the machine and of the proper mating of its parts, it is necessary to know the maximum increase of clearances for drawing a conclusion whether this conjugation is capable of working or not.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Wear of Machine Parts and Improvement of Their Resistance

elements.label: text
elements.text: Types of friction. Contacting parts are subjected to wear under the action of frictional forces appearing at the displacement of parts in respect to each other.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the nature of the relative motion performed by the friction surfaces, there are three types of friction: slidingfriction

elements.label: text
elements.text: (e.g. shaft in sliding (plain) bearing), rollingfriction(e.g. against roller cam) and pivoting friction (e.g. spindle heel against footstep).

elements.label: text
elements.text: It frequently occurs that friction of one type is accompanied by friction of another type. So, for instance, in gear drives rolling friction between the teeth is accompanied by sliding friction, i.e. there occurs combined friction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the kind of lubrication used for rubbing surfaces, friction may be classified as follows: pure friction, when there are no traces of foreign substances on the rubbing surfaces (pure friction m a y be only in

elements.label: text
elements.text: vacuum and is not encountered in working mechanisms and machines; dry (static) friction, when the rubbing surfaces are not coated with a layer of lubricant (Fig. la); liquidfriction,

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 1. Kinds of friction

elements.label: text
elements.text: 12 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: when the friction surfaces are completely separated by a thick stable layer of lubricant (Fig. 1b); boundary friction, appearing when on the rubbing surfaces there is a very thin strongly

elements.label: text
elements.text: adherent oil film (of less than 0.1 pm thin) with properties different from the properties of the liquid layer (Fig. lc); and semi-liquid friction, which is a combination of the liquid and boundary frictions (Fig. id).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 2. Diagram of wear

elements.label: text
elements.text: Liquid friction (e.g. between shaft and bearing) ensures a m i n i m u m wear of parts and power consumption. This is achieved by a higher circumferential velocity of the shaft, a better finish and smoothness of the rubbing surfaces, an optimum clearance, the precise fitting of parts, a good stability of the shaft and the bearing, an increased viscosity and purity of lubricant, an inexhaustible lubricant layer,, and an optimum pressure of the shaft on the hearing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Provided the above-mentioned conditions are satisfied, the lubricant is self-sucked into the gap between the rubbing surfaces, thus causing their separation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Moreover, liquid friction may be obtained by employing forced lubrication.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Wear and its varieties. Friction is always accompanied by gradual destruction of the surfaces of mating parts moving one upon the other. This gradual destruction is called wearing. As a consequence of wearing, there is a change in the original size and shape of the rub­

elements.label: text
elements.text: bing parts which is termed wear. The capacity of the material or parts to withstand wearing is wear resistance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The process of part wear in time is irregular (Fig. 2). During the initial period I of machtine operaion, when new parts are run-in, there is a stronger wear; further, comes the period II when the speed of wearing is at its minimum, i.e. when the process stabilizes; and finally follows the period III, when wear is progressively increasing up to an emergency state so that the part may be brought completely out of use.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The period / may be reduced by better finishing of rubbing surfaces, proper assembly of parts, and by using various polishing compositions. The period II is prolonged to the maximum by using wearresisting materials, high quality parts, and accurate assembly, as well as careful maintenance in operation. Owing to regular observation and control over the operation of machines, the friction parts are protected from deteriorating into emergency condition.

elements.label: text
elements.text: There exist the following kinds of wear: mechanical, molecularmechanical, and corrosive-mechanical wear. Mechanical wear is

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 13

elements.label: text
elements.text: produced by abrasive particles that groove and scratch the surfaces, plastic deformation of contacting surfaces, brittle destruction of the surface layer (by work-hardening in rubbing), and repeated deformation causing fatigue deterioration of the surface layers. Molecularmechanical wear is caused by molecular adhesion on separate spots of rubbing surfaces followed by mechanical destruction of formed

elements.label: text
elements.text: bonds and the transfer of particles from one surface to the other. Corrosive-mechanical wear occurs at the formation of products by the chemical interdiffusion of metal with the aggressive agents of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: medium, and their mechanical elimination at rubbing. To the corrosive-mechanical wear relates fretting-corrosion which appears due to the oxydation of metal and its abrasive wear by these oxides at very small relative displacement of the conjugated surfaces (for

elements.label: text
elements.text: instance, in stationary connections). All working parts of textile machines (such as the fillet needles of all kinds, spikes, saw-toothed fillets, pressure rollers of drafting systems in drawing, roving and spinning frames, runners, etc.) come in direct contact with the processed material (fibre, roving, yarn and others). Most parts subject to wearing by a slipping yarn are intended for guiding the yarn in the required direction (yarn guides), or for creating a required yarn tension (tension arrangements). Depending on the purpose for which these parts are intended, they may be made ofmetal, plastics, rubber, metal and mineral ceramics.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Main Factors Influencing the Wear of Machine Parts and Methods of Increasing Their Wear

elements.label: text
elements.text: Resistance

elements.label: text
elements.text: Material of Parts and Quality of Rubbing Surfaces

elements.label: text
elements.text: Material of rubbing parts. Parts are manufactured from different materials, such as cast iron, steel and other antifriction materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cast iron. Gray iron is used in greater amounts than any other construction material for manufacturing the textile machine parts. Cast iron parts come in contact with steel or other cast iron parts and sometimes with parts of nonferrous alloys and nonmetallic materials. They operate under conditions of sliding, pivoting, rolling, or combined friction (for instance, sliding and rolling friction) with or without lubrication, static and dynamic load, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the working conditions, cast iron must satisfy different requirements. Distinction should be made between the wearresistant and antifriction cast iron. The cast iron wear resistance great­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ly depends on its microstructure and particularly its metal base, while the wear resistance of cast iron parts depends on the total amount, shape and nature of graphite segregations (free carbon distribution in the main structure). Graphite plays a double role in the

elements.label: text
elements.text: 14 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: wearffljf cast irqp parts, graphite has the less strong structure it mayrathftrhva«%jrbe pi€ked upjto form a thin film on the rubbing surfaces protecting them against contact of metals. Due to the affinity with graphite, lubricating oil is reliably retained on the cast iron rubbing surface and in the recesses formed on graphite pitting. At the same time as it crosses the cast iron metal base, the graphite reduces its strength so that at higher loads particles of metals are torn off in the rubbing process, especially when thick graphite plates mutually intersect and form closed contours. Usually, it is desirable to obtain cast irons with graphite in the shape of middlesized plates which are separated and regularly distributed in all the metal mass.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cast iron hardness also affects its wear resistance. The wear resistance decreases with an increase in hardness.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cast iron wear resistance may be increased by thermal treatment which reduces the cast iron wear by factor of 5 to 7. In some cases it proves necessary to have only wear-resistant surface layers of cast iron parts, while the structure of the core obtained at casting remains unchanged. For this, the cast iron parts are subjected to case hardening by high-frequency current, nitriding, thermal chromizing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: High-frequency current (induction) hardening reduces for instance the wear of parts from ordinary gray iron by factor of 2 to 7. Nitriding, i.e. saturation of surface with nitrogen, imparts a high hardness to cast iron parts (a Brinell hardness of 700 to 800), a good wear resistance (the wear resistance increases by factor of 2- 2.6) and the resistance to corrosion caused by the moisture of the ambient atmosphere. The thermal chromizing, i.e. the saturation of the part surface with chromium at the account of the diffusion process (similarly to the saturation with carbon or cementation) increases the surface hardness of cast iron parts almost by factor of 14 and their wear resistance by factor of 6 to 8; moreover, the corrosion resistance is markedly improved. However nitriding and thermal chromizing are used more rarely than induction hardening, as they are time-consuming operations requiring the use of special equipment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cast iron parts (such as bosses, rollers, and cams) with chilled surface are sometimes used for textile machinery; in this case the structure contains from 20 to 30 % of cementite with a microhardness up to 1000 Bhn. Many parts are made of malleable iron, the wear resistance of which depends mainly on its metal structure.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Steel. In textile machinery the steel parts operate most frequently in conditions of sliding friction in contact with cast iron or bronze parts and more rarely with steel ones; in conditions of rolling friction they operate more frequently with steel parts. With increased carbon content and at greater hardness of the steel its wear resistance increases. Heat and chemical treatment of steel also considerably

elements.label: text
elements.text: The heat treatment of metals, ferrous and nonferrous and plastic materials is intended to obtain certain desirable conditions and properties, especially in the nature, form, size or distribution of the structural constituents. The main kinds of thermal treatment are annealing, hardening, tempering and so on.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Annealing involves changes in the direction of the restoration of the properties of a cold worked metal obtaining before cold deformation at various annealing temperatures, with time period of annealing being constant or variable. Annealing increases the relative elongation and the impact strength of steel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Hardening implies the heating of steel to a temperature exceeding the critical temperature, keeping it a certain time in these conditions followed by sharp cooling (quenching). Hardening with subsequent tempering is effected to increase the hardness of tool steel, impart

elements.label: text
elements.text: wear resistance, strength, and endurance to structural steel, to increase the corrosion resistance of anticorrosive steel and also as a preliminary operation before chemical and thermal treatment. The quality of hardening depends on the speed and temperature of heating, the time of processing and the cooling speed. When the mass of the part is big and the steel heat conductivity is low the speed of heating is slow. Parts of alloyed steel should be heated slower than those of carbon steel as the heat conductivity of alloyed steel is lower. Parts of large dimensions (with thick walls) should be heated slowly. Heating is carried-out progressively together with furnace heating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In certain cases the parts are preliminarily heated to a temperature slightly lower than hardening temperature in another furnace or close to the door of the furnace used for heating at hardening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Tempering is a heat treatment of steel which follows hardening, carburizing and cyaniding (case hardening), removes stresses, increases ductility and impact resistance, and decreases the tensile and yield strengths of the hardened material. Moreover it is treated by cold.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kinds of chemical and heat treatment of steel and cast iron are carburizing, cyaniding, nitriding, aluminizing and chromizing. The chemical and heat treatment of metals and alloys is effected by their heating and keeping at high temperature in active solid, liquid, and gas mediums. Parts and tools are chemical and heat treated to increase their surface hardness and resistance with the tenacity (ductility) of interior layers preserved unchanged. Some kinds of chemical and heat treatment should be followed by other types of heat treatment (for instance, carburizing is followed by hardening and tempering, etc.). Some kinds of chemical and heat treatment ope-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 16 k Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: rations are designed to increase the corrosion resistance of parts and tools? ‘ Carburizing is a process that introduces carbon into a solid ferrous alloy by heating the metal in contact with a carbonaceous material — solid, liquid, or gas— to a temperature above the transfor­

elements.label: text
elements.text: mation range and holding at that temperature. Carburizing is generally followed by quenching to produce a hardened case at a temperature of 780-800°C with subsequent tempering at 180-260°C. This ensures a high wear resistance of the surface layer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cyaniding is a process of case hardening a ferrous alloy by heating in a molten or solid cyanide thus causing the alloy to absorb nitrogen and carbon simultaneously. Depending on the level of tempera­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ture used, the process falls into high and low temperature cyaniding

elements.label: text
elements.text: (800-860 and 550-660°C, respectively), and depending on the kind of medium— in liquid gas and solid medium cyaniding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Nitriding is a process that saturates alloyed steels and cast iron with nitrogen by heating parts in ammonia atmosphere. Prior to

elements.label: text
elements.text: nitriding, steel is subjected to heat treatment. The aim of nitriding is to increase the hardness, wear resistance and fatigue strength of machine parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Aluminizing is a process of saturating steel and cast iron with aluminium for increasing their resistance to scale formation. Aluminizing is mainly used for low-carbon steel, for gray iron and high-

elements.label: text
elements.text: alloy heat-resistant steel. Aluminizing is used to increase the useful life of parts operating at high temperatures (for instance, pressure casting moulds for non-ferrous alloys, grid bars, steam boiler pipes,

elements.label: text
elements.text: valve heads, etc.). Aluminizing is carried out in hard powder compounds and in a melted aluminium alloy, by metallization of the sur­

elements.label: text
elements.text: face with subsequent diffusion annealing, and by other methods.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Chromizing is a process of surface saturation of steel or cast iron parts with chromium in order to increase their corrosion resistance and surface hardness; so the wear resistance of chromized steel is ten times that of the same hardened steel. Textile machinery parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: are made from carbon, medium- and low-alloy steels (mainly manganese and chromium steel). The wear resistance of steel depends on the methods of its manufacture and hot treatment. Acid and openhearth steels are more wear resistant than basic steels; crucible and electrical steels have a more uniform structure and are more wear resistant than Bessemer and open-hearth steels. At hot treatment by

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressure (forging, stamping, and rolling) owing to the consolidation

elements.label: text
elements.text: and splitting of grains in steel (especially in exterior layers) the wear resistance as compared with cast steel is increased.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Antifriction materials. To such relate: nonferrous antifriction alloys, antifriction carbon-iron alloys (cast iron), cermet (metal ceramic), and nonmetal antifriction materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Antifriction property is the material property which in metal-to-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 17

elements.label: text
elements.text: metal rubbing ensures the smallest friction factor with all other conditions being equal (speed, kind of lubrication and applied load).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The antifriction materials, used for manufacturing bearings, should work well with materials ofother mating parts, should exhibit good wear resistance, high mechanical and technological properties, good thermal conductivity and corrosion resistance; and should be able to absorb the products of wear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Nonferrous antifriction alloys. Most of these alloys have approximately the same structure — a plastic mass with embedded hard particles. During operation the soft mass wears more rapidly than the hard particles and as a result a microrelief is formed with protru­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ding hard particles which carry the mating part, such as shaft in bearing. The oil circulates easier along the formed canals and cools quicker the rubbing surfaces carrying-away with it the products of wear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To nonferrous antifriction alloys relate: babbitts, antifriction bronze, brass, zink and aluminium alloys.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The babbitts are subdivided into the tin-base, lead-base and cadmium-base babbitts. They are used for lining in bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Bronze and brass are copper-base alloys. Bronzes are subdivided into casting and wrought bronzes as well as tin and tinless bronzes. Tin bronze is used for bearings (linings, bushings) operating under loads not over 5-8 MPa, average speeds (up to 3-4 m/s) and normal temperatures. Tin bronze may take impact loads (up to 15-25 MPa) and high speeds (up to 8 m/s). The aluminium-iron bronze is used at high temperatures (up to 200-250°C) and under high loads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Aluminium ferrous-manganese brass and silica-lead brass are used for parts operating under high specific loads (up to 10-30 MPa) and at slow speeds (3-4 m/s). Parts wearing against brass (shaft necks and worms) should have a hardened surface (by nitriding, cementation, and hardening).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Zinc-base alloys have a high linear expansion factor so that the clearance between the bearings made of such alloys and shaft must

elements.label: text
elements.text: be increased. Aluminium-base alloys are used to replace babbitt and tin bronze for linings in cast iron and steel bodies and for casting linings and bushings; however minding the high linear expansion factor of these alloys the clearances must be increased.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Antifriction carbon-iron alloys. Antifriction cast iron presents a high wear resistance, good casting properties but is more difficult to run-in than bronze. Antifriction cast iron is subdivided in gray, high-strength, and malleable grades. All these grades of cast iron are successfully used for manufacturing different kinds of liners, bear­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ings and other sliding bearers operating at steady or alternating loads. In case of impact loads, it is recommended to use malleable antifriction cast iron presenting a high strength (at= 480...550 MPa) and a toughness of 6 = 4...6%.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 18 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: In order to ensure the normal operation of antifriction cast iron parts, the rubbing parts must be of high smoothness and perfect mating, the lubrication must be reliable and the clearances must be 15% greater than those in the bronze bearings. Cermet (metal ceramic) materials. The cermet parts (bushings, linings, etc.) are made by pressing mixtures of metal powders with additives acting as hard lubricants in die casting moulds and cintering in protective or neutral gas medium. Usually iron or bronze powders are used, and more rarely copper, aluminium, or titanium powders. Mainly graphite and more rarely sulphur are used as additives. The parts of metal ceramic materials are distinguished by their porosity and consequently by high antifriction properties and wear resistance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The use of porous bearings in textile machines is highly expedient, considering that they are capable of operating a long time without additional lubrication. Not long ago a new material— a metal-base laminate— has found application; it is obtained by sintering a bronze spherical powder loosely strewn on a steel ribbon with copper plated surface. The life of parts made ofsuch a metal-base laminate by swaging is twice longer than that of parts made of usual metal ceramics. In use such parts do not require any lubrication and are called for this reason dry friction bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Polymer materials. These materials are easily run-in and are endowed with low wear, high damping property, etc. Polyamide materials (capron, cylon, perlon, caprolon, polyamide resins, amide, and nylon 66) are used to manufacture bearingsoperating without exterior lubricant supply at a temperature not in excess of 85°C in dustladen atmosphere and under impact loads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Their main drawbacks are humidity absorption causing a change in part dimensions and low thermal conductivity. The properties of the antifriction polyamide material are considerably improved by the introduction of fillers (graphite, talc, etc.). Capron filled with graphite is with low humidity absorption and ensures a good stability of dimensions being characterized by high strength and hardness. The following polymer materials also find use: polyformaldehyde, acryloplastics, epoxy plastics, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Plastic materials on a wood and cloth base. T o s u c h p e r t a i n l a m i n a ted wood plastics, compressed wood, fabric-based laminate, and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The laminated wood plastics contain a binder— abakelite varnish in which the phenol formaldehyde resin is dissolved in ethyl spirit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Laminated wood plastics are used for manufacturing large-size bushings, lining, gears and other parts which were produced before from nonferrous and ferrous metals, fabric-based laminate, and other materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 19

elements.label: text
elements.text: To improve the antifriction properties of the rubbing surfaces of these parts, 7-10% of graphite are introduced in their surface layers, and to increase the thermal conductivity— a metal powder (bronze, aluminium, copper, and lead).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Plasticized wood is produced by piezothermal processing (by application of pressure with heating), the aim of which is to condense the wood. Hard wood is used to manufacture rubbing parts (birch, asp, alder, beech, maple, and hornbeam).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Compressed wood is capable of absorbing lubrication oil. After impregnation in hot machine oil (at a temperature of 80-100°C) the parts of compressed wood become selflubricating. Parts of compressed wood easily absorb oscillation and are capable to withstand high impact loads. Moreover, the part (shaft) operating in couple with the part made of compressed wood (bearer) wears less than in rubbing against any other material. Parts of compressed wood are easily worked in. Liquid and consistent mineral oils and greases may

elements.label: text
elements.text: be used for their lubrication.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fabric-based laminate is a material obtained on the base of a cloth impregnated with resol resin. As cloth may be used chiffon, plain and grey cloth, duck; linen fabrics and fabrics of synthetic fibres are used more rarely. Its mechanical properties depend on the kind of fabric weave and on the direction of the load in relation to the disposition of layers. Fabric-based laminate is produced in sheets (up> to 8 m m thick) and slabs (thickness more than 8 mm), as well as rods and pipes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: All-use and metallurgical fabric-based laminates are used for manufacturing bushings, bearers, gears and other loaded parts operating in couple with metal parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: There are available also plastic materials on the base of phenolformaldehyde resin with cotton fibre (voloknite), asbestos fibre (asbovoloknite), and glass fibre (glassvoloknite, or glass-fibre-base laminate). The friction factor of these plastics is reduced by introducing in their compositions such fillers as graphite, fluoroplastic and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Quality of nibbing surfaces. Characterized by macro- and microirregularities and waviness.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Microirregularitiesare located inside a square with a side of about one or several millimetres. The microirregularities in the direction of the cutting tool motion are called longitudinal irregularities and those in cross direction (perpendicular to the longitudinal ones)— transverse irregularities.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Macroirregularities are nonrecurring separate deviations of the surface from the nominal shape (conicity, ellipticity, nonflatness,

elements.label: text
elements.text: convexity, concavity, etc.).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Wavinessis a combination of recurring in alternate order peaks and valleys of nearly the same dimensions and forming irregularities 2*

elements.label: text
elements.text: 20 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: spaced at much larger distances than in case of microirregularities. Waviness has the following effect on the wear: with an increse in the wave height the wear increases, but at the same time the scoring resistance of the rubbing surfaces is improved.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The initial condition of the part (surface quality) changes in the course of operation (or wear). During machine parts working-in, the initial surface irregularities formed at machining are completely or partially eliminated, worn out and crushed; new irregularities appear with different shape, dimensions, and direction. If the con­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ditions of wear remain the same after working-in of the part, new irregularities differing from the initial ones appear on its surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Qualify of Machine Assembly, Operating Conditions, Lubrication and Maintenance

elements.label: text
elements.text: Quality of machine assembly. Mistakes made during machine assembly affect the wear resistance of parts. Canting shafts, overtight bearings, misaligned multiple-seated shafts, improperly meshed gears, incorrectly matched cams, poor balancing of rotating

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts may become a cause of the rapid wear of machine parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A canting shaft at the beginning adheres only to the edges of the bearing so that a high specific load created at this point causes an intense heating and wear of parts. It should be taken into account that in case of shaft canting the liquid friction is impossible. If the shaft is of low rigidity, i.e. it m a y be easily bent, it is liable to be canted in the supports during operation even if the assembly has

elements.label: text
elements.text: been done correctly. In this case self-adjustable bearings are used.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Overtight bearings caused by high friction would result in the enhanced scoring of shafts and hard (bronze, or cast iron) linings or in the melting of the babbitt lining, including other troubles. At enterprises where there is a strong dust formation the strong heating of bearings may be the cause of fire especially when oil has a low ignition temperature.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Improper meshing of gears is due to the non-observance of radial and side clearances, the non-parallelism of axles and others. Such mistakes cause the teeth to contact over a small surface, increase their slipping, cause poor rolling and the rapid wear of gears. Skewness in meshing is frequently the main cause of gear teeth chipping out and breakage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Improper balancing of heavy rotating parts (e.g. cylinders of card, drawing, warping, and sizing machines), causes a strong vibration

elements.label: text
elements.text: and rapid and nonuniform (one-side) wear of the shaft and bearings. . Mode of operation. Frequent stoppages of textile machines during

elements.label: text
elements.text: operation (e.g. in case of thread breakages) have a serious influence on the wear resistance of parts: the more often the machines are stopped, the lower is the wear resistance of parts. At each new star-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 21

elements.label: text
elements.text: ting of the machine after stoppage its assembly units have to overcome theinertia of rest and consequently theload on the units increases. On machine stoppage, the displacement speed of rubbing surfaces is sharply reduced causing a lossin the oillubricating capacity. Therefore, a reduction in yarn breakage and in the time needed for breakage elimination not only ensures an improvement in machine efficiency and product quality, but also increases the wear resistance of the equipment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Lubrication of machines and their maintenance. As mentioned above, lubrication is intended for reducing the wear of machine parts. The effect obtained by lubrication in increasing the wear resistance of parts is considerable. For instance, lubrication brings about more than a 5-fold decrease in the wear of cast iron linings which were not worked-in, and of worked-in linings— more than 30 times.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The lubricants are chosen taking into account the speed and design parameters of the parts. Thus, for instance when the choice is made for a couple shaft— hearing,the following factors shall be considered: the load, rotational speed of the shaft, clearance, thickness of lubricant layer, shaft diameter, and ratio of the bearing length and diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The most important properties of lubricating oils is their viscosity. The greater are the load applied on the rubbing couple, the clearance, and the thickness of the lubricating layer, the higher must be the oil viscosity; the greater are the shaft rotational speed and diameter, and the ratio of the hearing length and diameter, the lower should be the oil viscosity. It must be taken into account that viscosity is not a stable characteristic which depends in a large measure on the temperature of the liquid lubricant and on the pressure. With an increase in the temperature, the viscosity is sharply reduced, especially in the temperature range from 0 to 40-60°C. Further, this drop in viscosity slows down, and at the temperatures above 80-100°C viscosity changes but little. With an increase in the pressure, the viscosity of the liquid lubricant increases, this change being essential only at considerable pressures.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Alongside with the proper choice of oil, the wear resistance of rubbing parts depends in a large measure on careful maintenance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The lubrication and cleaning of machines must he carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements. In case of their violation the wear of machine parts and power consumption increase. For example in the case of flax spinning machines this increase is from 1.5 to 4 times, i.e. 20-35% correspondingly. The lubrication chart of a scutcher is given in Table 1.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To increase the wear resistance of parts operating with insufficient lubrication (some units of textile machines are insufficiently lubricated considering the possibility of contaminating the web, roving, yarn and fabric with oil) use is made of special lubricants, in

elements.text: Graphitized oil is an ordinary acid-free mineral oil containing 1-2% of fine ground graphite of lamellar structure and characterized by a high mobility of its layers owing to which it has a low friction factor. The wear of such parts as cast iron bearings and shafts due to the use of this oil is reduced from 3 to 4 times as compared with the wear of the same parts when ordinary mineral oil is used for the purpose. elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4. Break-downs of Machine Parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: The break-downs of machine parts are mainly caused by overloads. They may be due to improper threading and gaiting of looms (when

elements.label: text
elements.text: a light loom is gaited to produce a fabric with a high filling factor), improper balancing of rotating heavy parts (the drum of a section warper), low quality of manufactured and repaired parts and equipment, including poor maintenance of textile machinery.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 23

elements.label: text
elements.text: Variable loads may cause more frequent breakdowns of parts. This phenomenon is called the fatigue deterioration (destruction) of m a terials. Fatigue break-downs occur suddenly without visible manifestations. This may often be the cause of the deterioration of other machine parts and break-downs of different kinds.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The fatigue strength of parts is determined by the character and the intensity of variable load, the shape and dimensions of the part, the character of mating parts and the quality of their surface, the extent of corrosion, and the mechanical properties of the material from which the parts are made, their amenability to notching, and

elements.label: text
elements.text: the technological process of part manufacturing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Character and intensity of variable load. The variable load acting on the part causes alternating stresses. Any single change in the stresses is called a cycle. The time during which the cycle is effected is called a period, and the number of cycles performed per unit of time (e.g., one minute) is called the cycle frequency.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The maximum stress at which the material is not destructed at the unlimited number of cycles is called the endurance limit, or the fatigue limit. At testing, this stress is set to 10-20 min cycles for steel, and 50-100 min cycles for nonferrous metals. If the part withstands the indicated number of cycles without cracking, it means that it is capable of withstanding an infinitely great number of cycles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Overloading of parts affects in different ways the fatigue strength. With light overloads an increase in strength is observed, while with great overloads the strength is reduced. Ifthe stress is close to the endurance limit of parts which are not subjected to a constantly growing variable load, the fatigue resistance may considerably rise. This phenomenon is called the training of material. Consequently, working-in and running-in of assembled machines are necessary not only for working-in the rubbing surfaces of parts, but also for their training under the conditions of variable loads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In case of considerable overloads, i.e. stresses greatly exceeding the fatigue limit, the ability of metal to work without cracking under the action of cyclic loads, that is its endurance, noticeably decreases. To reduce the danger connected with fatigue break-downs of

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts due to overload, it is necessary to carefully balance the rapidly rotating parts, to eliminate out-of-true and misalignment of parts, to adjust the dampers of impact loads, to use vibration dampers, to check the proper mating of parts, to check regularly and to tighten

elements.label: text
elements.text: slack fixtures, to adjust the clearances between rotating parts avoiding operation with big clearances, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shape and dimensions of parts. The fatigue destructions are usually observed at the points where the part sharply changes in shape, as for instance in keyways 4,threads 3,head pieces 2,holes 5 and 6, steep steps 1 (Fig. 3), etc. In such places, stresses are concentrated

elements.label: text
elements.text: 24 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: to become many times greater than the stresses in the smooth section of the part. The presence of concentrated stresses greatly reduces the endurance limit of the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: As is known, the endurance limit of the part decreases with

elements.label: text
elements.text: an increase in its diameter. This relates to various metal properties and the effect of a sharper drop of stresses from the exterior case-hardened and harder layers towards the inner layers which have not been subjected to hardening. For reducing the causes of fatigue and break-down of parts it is necessary to smooth down all the places where the stresses are apt to concentrate; so for instance it is efficacious to round off all the steep steps.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 3. Fatigue destruction of ma­

elements.label: text
elements.text: chine parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: Moreover, these points should be work-hardened to create compressive stresses. Thus, the thread obtained by knurling has a longer life than the thread obtained by cutting.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Conjugation of parts. Close fits affect the fatigue strength more than all other factors: the fatigue strength may be decreased four times and more (the greater the interference, the less is the fatigue strength). At the same time the fatigue strength greatly depends

elements.label: text
elements.text: on the kind of material from which the mating parts are made and on the kind of their conjugation. So for instance, the fatigue strength of the shaft decreases with the increase of the bush hardness; a longer or thinner hub, annular grooves on the butt of a pressed-on part, including the fit of parts on a special shoulder (thickening of the shaft) and the surface knurling of the shaft to fit parts are the factors which cause a decrease in the strength concentration.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Quality of part surface* The higher is the surface finish of the part, i.e. the less is its roughness, the greater is the fatigue resistance of the part. Stresses are concentrated on the rough surface of parts (in the cavity of every notch) which causes a decrease of its fatigue strength. Even inconsiderable scratches on a polished surface may cause a decrease in the endurance limit to 40%. Therefore, in repairs, the parts are subjected to artificial work-hardening owing to which their fatigue strength is increased from 1.5 to 2.5 times.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Corrosion. The surface corrosion of parts causes a considerable decrease in their endurance limit. The destruction of parts by corrosion is called corrosion fatigue. It increases when there is a concentration of stresses and the parts work in a more corroding medium, when the parts work in tension and compression, when the surface is coarse and the number of applied cycles is increased.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The anticorrosive coatings of the parts differently affect the cor-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in Machines 25-

elements.label: text
elements.text: rosion fatigue. The coatings obtained by electrolytic chromium, cop­

elements.label: text
elements.text: per and nickel plating, as well as sulphurizing reduce the corrosion. fatigue, while the coatings obtained by zink plating eliminate the harmful effect of the corroding medium on the fatigue strength. Moreover, anticorrosive (short time) nitriding, spinning with rollers, and blowing with shots are also used to avoid the corrosion of machine parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Mechanical properties of part material and its notch sensitivity. The more homogeneous and pure is the structure of the material used for part manufacturing, the higher is its endurance limit. The notch sensitivity increases with endurance limit. Notches decrease the endurance limit of steel by 35-55% and of cast iron by 5-20%.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The fatigue strength of metals is greatly affected by their capacity of absorbing and damping oscillations appearing during machine operation (cast iron parts are in this case preferable to steel parts).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Technological process of part manufacturing. The fatigue strength of parts depends on many technological factors encountered during manufacturing and repair operations, i.e. the kind of metal cutting, rolling, forging, welding, metal coating, electroplating, heat treat­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ment, or thermal chemical treatment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During the process of cutting not only irregularities are formed on> the surface, but also there occurs work-hardening of surface layers. Rolling effected by means of steel hardened rollers increases the fatigue resistance. The effect of forging on the steel strength depends on the direction of load application: the change in the amount of reduction by forging slightly affects the static strength and the impact strength of steel with the grain, while when the forging reduction ratio increases the impact strength of steel across the grain is considerably reduced. Consequently, the fatigue limit is less across thegrain than with the grain. Concentrated stresses have also a stronger effect on the longitudinal grain than upon the traverse ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Welded and built-up parts present a smaller endurance limit than whole parts made of the same metal. The endurance limit depends; on the method of welding. Electric arc welding ensures a higher endurance limit than gas welding (especially when heavy-coated electrodes are used); automatic welding permits us to obtain jointswith better endurance than manually welded joints; forging, annealing, machining and rolling of built-up metal also increase its endurance limit. The highest endurance limit is obtained at contact, flash welding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sprayed metal coating at conjoint operations with the baseincreases the endurance of the main metal by 15-20%. Electrolytic coating, i.e. chromium, nickel, and copper plating, decreases the endurance limit of parts which is the more reduced, the greater is the coating layer. Heat treatment (hardening) increases the endurancelimit of parts. The fatigue strength of parts is considerably increased.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 26 Chapter One

elements.label: text
elements.text: by heat hardening with high frequency currents and also at thermal and chemical treatment— by carburizing and nitriding. Hardening

elements.label: text
elements.text: with current of high frequency is especially efficacious for parts with cuts, cross holes and provided with close-fit bushings and other points of stress concentration. In these cases the endurance limit of steel parts may be increased 1.8-2.5 times. The endurance limit is

elements.label: text
elements.text: two-fold and more increased by carburizing and nitriding.

elements.text: METHODS OF MACHINE PARTS RESTORATION

elements.label: text
elements.text: AND INCREASING THEIR LONGEVITY

elements.label: text
elements.text: Parts which in course of operation have lost their essential properties (dimensions and shape), with breakages etc., may be used for further operation after repairing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Any parts with different defects and disarrangements may be repaired. However, not all defectuous parts are repaired. The need of

elements.label: text
elements.text: repair and the choice of the methods applied at the repairs are determined by economic considerations which are the cost of repairs and the longevity factor of the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Modern technological processes used to restore parts not only allow the restitution of the parts, but also permit imparting them pro­

elements.label: text
elements.text: perties better than in the original parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The advanced experience shows that the best effect in part restoration is achieved in series production using modern technology. Therefore, the restoration of mass parts (mainly) should be carried out in a special shop servicing one or several enterprises of the same type.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During repairs the initial dimensions and shape of parts are restored (repair of worn-out gear toothing), including fits and tolerances (clearances between shaft and bearing). For this purpose use is made of the following operations: insertion of intermediate bodies, application of pressure, welding of surfaces, metal coating, chemical

elements.label: text
elements.text: and heat treatment, spark machining, glueing, soldering, and others. These processes can be used separately or in combination, as for instance welding with metal coating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Repair offParts by Mechanical Methods and by Plastic Deformation (Pressworking)

elements.label: text
elements.text: Mechanical methods of repair. To the mechanical methods of repairing defective parts pertain: ringing (placing rings), the use of stitches or straps, patches or inserts and repair sizes. The first three

elements.label: text
elements.text: methods ensure the restoration of design sizes of parts, force or shrink fits, while the latter process is employed only to ensure force or shrink fit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 28 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: Ringing is the restoration of parts by placing rings on wornout cylindrical surfaces. Ringing may be exterior (Fig.4a, b) and interior (Fig. 4c, d). Exterior ringing is used to restore shaft journals, and interior ringing— to restore different holes, as for instance in the body, framework, hushing, solid bearings, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: iwM/yjm

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reliable fitting of rings depends on the diameter of mating, the circumference of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: ring, the contact pressure, and the friction factor. Rings may be placed withthe aid of apress machine; by preliminaryheating of a ring (inthe case ofexteriorringing) or heating of the part to be restored (at internal ringing); by preliminary deep cooling of a ring (in the case of interior ringing), or of the part (at exterior ringing).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 4. Ringing of defective parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: Hot ringing ensures a better strength of the joint, as compared with the other methods. Moreover, the strength of joint between the ring and the part is influenced by the surface finish. For increasing the fatigue strength of parts restored by exterior ringing, the surface of the parts on which the ring is to be placed should be work-hardened or subjected to short-time nitriding. In case of excessive stresses, the negative allowance is reduced, the ring is welded around and work-hardened by means of a roller. When restoring the crankshaft rod nuts and split antifriction bearings, half-rings (half-bushings)

elements.label: text
elements.text: are used. They are attached by welding, screws, and by other methods. In the case of exterior ringing, steel and cast-iron rings are employed, while for interior ringing bronze rings find application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Stitchesorstrapsare used to stay the broken part. O n the both sides of the crack T, holes are drilled in which dowels 1(Fig. 5a) of the heated strap 2 (stitches or straps) are introduced; after cooling the strap tightens the crack. The number of straps used depends on the length of the crack. The distance between the holes must be smaller than the distance between the dowels (in a cold state), by the amount of interference fit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The tightening straps may be of different shape: H-shaped (Fig. 5byc), round (Fig. 5d)or oval (Fig. 5e). Insertsorpatchesare used for repairing shafts (journals and necks), gears (toothing), cams (tips) and others. According to this method, a new portion is placed instead of the worn-out or broken portions of the parts. The inserts or patches are attached to the part with the aid of thread, cone, dovetail and others, usually by welding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: a shaft, or for preparing a stock of cheaper replacements as for instance bearings. This would considerably accelerate repair operations.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Plastic deformation (pressworking). This method is used to repair parts of simple shape, as well as parts made of maleable materials (steel, brass and soft bronze). Depending on the direction of the forces acting at pressure and deformation in respect to the centre line

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the part to be restored, the repairs may be classified as follows: heading, flaring, reducing, forcing-in, knurling, rolling and straightening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Heading is used to reduce the interior diameter of a hollow part (or bushing) or to increase the exterior diameter of a whole part (finger or stud). The direction of the deformation bis perpendicular to the direction of the exterior effort T (Fig. 6a).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Flaring is used to increase the exterior diameter of a hollow part by spreading it from inside. The direction of the deformation coincides with the direction of the exterior effort (Fig. 66).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Reducing is employed to reduce the exterior and interior diameter by applying an external effort to the outer cylindrical surface of the hollow part (bushing). In this case, directions of deformation and of the applied efforts coincide (Fig. 6c).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Forcing-in is an operation combining heading and flaring which is used to increase the outside diameter of solid flat parts. Forcing-in

elements.label: text
elements.text: 30 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 6. Diagrams of machine part repairs by plastic deformation

elements.label: text
elements.text: is achieved by the application of concentrated forces (Fig. 6d).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Knurling (Fig. 6e-f)is the process of plastic displacement of metal by pressing a steel roller into the corrugations of the part to be restored. W h e n restoring fluted rollers, a steel roller is forced into cavities between the flutes, and its rolling along the recess of the wornout flute displaces metal from hollows to the crest.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rolling. One or several easily rotating rollers with a smooth surface of hardened steel or hard alloy are pressed to the rotating cylindrical part lubricated with oil. The rollers are imparted not only with a rotational, but also with a translatory motion (along the surface of the part). The metal on the surface of the part is redistributed, and work-hardening of the surface layer takes place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The apertures of the parts to be restored are brought to required dimensions by punching with a mandrel or a ball, and also by expanding with a special tool. Finishing with rollers, calibration, and expansion also use the process of the plastic deformation of the surface metal layers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To ensure the plastic deformation of parts by rolling the portions to be deformed are subjected to electric heating. This method is called electromechanical treatment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 31

elements.label: text
elements.text: Straightenitig (Fig. 6g, h) is the restoration of a part which became bent or twisted in the course of operation. Straightening may be carried-out on cold and hot parts (the latter method is used in case of strong bending of the part). The accuracy of cold straightening is higher. Since the required sizes are not always obtained after cold straightening, it isrecommended to carry out stabilizing, i.e. heating of the parts after straightening to 400-500°C.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Steel parts which are slightly bent are also straightened using surface cold-working. This kind of straightening is used for the repair of

elements.label: text
elements.text: shafts, axles, knives, beams, guides, cylinders, and other parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Stamps or special jigs and fixtures are necessary to carry out heading, flaring, reducing and pressing-in operations performed on press machines. Knurling requires special knurling devices which are mounted on lathes, planing or other special machine tools- Straightening is done on presses or special devices.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Welding and Building-up

elements.label: text
elements.text: There are two kinds of welding: fusion welding and pressure welding (plastic). To fusion welding pertain arc welding and gas welding- Pressure welding may be classified into resistance welding (butt, welding, seam welding and spot welding), gas pressure welding, and forge welding. The electric arc welding and gas welding are used for the repair (joining) of broken and cracked parts of steel, cast iron, bronze and other metals and alloys; the electric butt welding is used for butt joining of broken parts of steel and other plastic materials;: electric spot welding and seam welding are used for overlap joining of sheet materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For welding and building up (surfacing) of parts one mainly employs fusion welding. To prepare parts for welding and surfacing, the joints are imparted the required shape for ensuring a sufficient cohesion between the original metal and the overlay. The method and kind of preparation depend on the character of the wear, the material, shape and size of parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The edges of broken parts should be thoroughly prepared for different types of weld joints. The type of joint depends on the thickness of the part wall. W h e n the wall thickness <pis 1.5 m m or less the edges are not bevelled, when (pis 12 m m or less V joints are used, and when <pis more than 12 m m — double V joints are used. The fracture line is followed if one has to preserve the initial dimensions of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: broken pieces.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When welding thick-walled cast-iron parts, steel pins are screwed into the bevelled faces for increasing the bond between the fused m e tal and the parent metal. The diameter d of the pins depends on the thickness b of the part at the place of fracture: d = (0.3...0.4)b. The length of pin threaded part is h — 1.5 d,and the distance between

elements.label: text
elements.text: 32 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: the pins (spacing) £= (4...6)d. The strength of the joint may be increased by using steel anchors. Drilling, threading of sockets and driving-in of pins should be done without oil, and as tight as the pins will go.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cracks in the part should be prepared for welding, so that the electrical arc or gas flame would come in contact with the intact material. The crack running throughout the whole length of the part must be prepared for single or double V joints and drilled at the end (to avoid the increase vof the crack in length on welding).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Arc welding and building-up are most widely used for restoring the parts of textile machines and equipment. Arc welding employs the heat of an electric arc to bring the metals to a molten state. Arc welding and building-up may be performed manually and automatically.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Hand welding and building-up may be carried-out by different processes: carbon-arc welding (an arc between the electrode and the work); the metal-arc welding (method of N. G. Slavyanov); and carbon-arc welding (with an arc between two electrodes).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The most largely used ismetal-arc welding and building-up elaborated by Slavyanov (Fig. 7). The intense heat of the arc melts both the work 2and the metal electrode 1.The metal electrode is covered with a chemical coating. The burning coating forms a gaseous cloud which surrounds the arc and molten pool shielding molten metal from contamination with oxygen and nitrogen. The coating controls the chemical analysis of the weld by preventing the vapourization of essential elements in the electrode core wire such as manganese and

elements.label: text
elements.text: in some electrodes serves to supply alloying elements that improve the molten weld, arc characteristics, increase welding speed, etc. The quality of weld depends considerably on the arc stability which

elements.label: text
elements.text: in its turn depends on the kind of current used and the length of the arc. The stability of arc is greater at direct current than at alternating current, and for this reason with alternating current, it is necessary to employ heavily coated electrodes, and higher voltages and •current frequencies. Coating of electrodes is necessary for the following reason. If molten metal contains oxides and nitrogen in the form of iron nitrides, the mechanical properties of the metal aresharply impaired, and itbecomes brittle and has low strength. The absorption of oxygen and nitrogen is stronger with the use of bare welding-wire electrodes than with coated ones. The thicker is the electrode coating, the less is the

elements.label: text
elements.text: It should also be taken in account that with welding using direct current and coated electrodes, weld metal is contaminated considerably less with oxides and nitrides than when using alternating current (all other conditions being equal). Welding repair work is usu­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ally done with a.c. welders. The use of heavily coated electrodes permits obtaining a high-quality weld-joint (not inferior to that obtained when welding with direct current). Moreover, the a.c. welding sets are more economical than d.c. welding units, as the employment of direct current necessitates the use of a generator. In this case, the current consumption is 2-3 times lower, the no-load power

elements.label: text
elements.text: is 10 times less, and the cost of the set is 3-5 times lower as compared with that of the generator. The industrial area is three times less.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Automatic metalware welding is used for the repair of comparatively large surfaces and for series restoration of parts. It is based on the principle of using the submerged arc heat under a layer of flux

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 8). An arc is created between the bare welding-wire electrode 1 and the workpiece 4to which electric current is supplied from a welding transformer. The flux 5 is fed from the bin 2.The electrode wire is automatically fed from the spool 7 into the arc zone by means of the welding head 3 or an automatic welding machine. In the course of hard-facing, the welding head (and consequently the arc) is displaced by means of the carriage 6 along the work with a speed equal to that of welding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building-up of a cylindrical or spiral surface is effected on a special unit (Fig. 9). The part 2 is fixed in a versatile milling machine

elements.label: text
elements.text: between the dividing head 4 and the back stock 1.Then, it is imparted a rotational and translational motion. The welding head 3 is firmly fixed on the machine. The automatic surfacing may also be performed on a turning lathe. In this case, the work attached in a

elements.label: text
