elements.label: text
elements.text: chuck is imparted rotation, while the welding head fixed on the carriage performs a longitudinal movement.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The automatic metal-arc welding of worn-out parts under a layer of flux presents the following advantages as compared with manual building-up: higher efficiency, better quality of the overlay, lower current consumption, and better working conditions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gas shielded-metal-arc welding is carried out as follows. Shielding gas (carbon dioxide, argon, hydrogen, and others) is constantly fed into the zone of the electric arc burning between the work and the electrode. The shielding gas displaces the air around the arc to protect molten metal against contamination with oxygen and nitrogen. Argon is used for building-up parts of high-alloy chrome-nickel steels, copper-, aluminium- and titanium-base alloys. The highest stability of the electric arc is obtained in that shielding gas. In carbon dioxide the arc stability is somewhat lower, and in hydrogen,

elements.label: text
elements.text: it is minimum. The choice of the electrode wire depends on the kind of shielding gas.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The gas shielded-metal-arc welder (carbon dioxide) consists of a bulb 1 (Fig. 10), heater 2t drier 3> step-down reducer 4, rotameter-flowmeter 5, and burner 6.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Short-circuited arc building-up is a variety of metal-arc welding and is used to restore worn-out surfaces of cylindrical parts from 8 to 200 m m in diameter. Workpiece 1 (Fig. 11) and the wire electrode 3 are connected in the circuit of power source 5. The Fig. H. Unit for short-circuited arc vibrator 4 imparts longitudinal building-up oscillations to the wire 3, owing

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 35

elements.label: text
elements.text: to which there are periodical short-circuitings (up to 50 per second

elements.label: text
elements.text: and even more) of the arc gap and the positive transfer of electrode drops into the welding bath. The vibration of the wire electrode

elements.label: text
elements.text: (with an amplitude of 0.5-3 mm) ensures the alternation of electric discharges in the form of an arc, short-circuiting, and idle stroke.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The wire is passed across a short-circuited head 2. In the course of surfacing, a cooling liquid with alkaline properties ispassed through the nozzle in the head 2 into the weld zone. The emitted vapours press away the air and protect the molten metal from oxygen and nitrogen owing towhich the sprayed metal acquires high mechanical properties. The workpiece to be restored is fixed in a lathe and

elements.label: text
elements.text: brought in rotation (in the sense of the arrow A), while the short-circuited head is attached on the lathe carriage and imparted a longitudinal motion (along the arrow B).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Short-circuited metal-arc surfacing may be submerged (under a layer of flux or a medium of water vapour) with simultaneous cooling of the work.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gas welding and building-up are used for restoring parts made of thin sheet steel 0.2-5 m m thick, low-melting (non-ferrous) metals and their alloys, of metals requiring gradual heating and slow cooling at welding (tool steels), and also metals requiring preheating before welding (cast iron and some grades of special steels). Moreover, this kind of repairs is used for hard facing with hard alloys and for brazing. A m o n g combustible gases the most frequently used is acetylene which when burning in mixture with oxygen develops a temperature of 3000 to 3200°C.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At gas welding the molten metal absorbs oxygen and nitrogen from air less intensively than at electric arc welding. This is explained by the protective action ofthe flame and fluxes: the flame surrounding the metal melt attracts almost all the atmospheric oxygen necessary for the combustion of carbon and hydrogen.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Acetylene used for welding is obtained in acetylene generators directly at the point ofwelding, or brought in acetylene bottles. Usual­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ly for welding at repairs, a high-pressure portable generator is employed allowing the use of long hoses and welding burners of higher pressure and operation at low temperatures. Generators of all types have a water seal and a chemical cleaner. The water seal protects the generator from explosion because of backflash. The chemical cleaner is intended for purifying acetylene from hydrogen sulphide and hydrogen phosphate which are noxious impurities that would impair welding quality.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Oxygen is supplied to the point of welding in special seamless steel bottles provided with pressure reducers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main types of oxyacetylene torches are in common use today: the medium-pressure type and the low-pressure or injector type.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 36 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: Moreover multi-jet oxyacetylene torches also find application in wel­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Plasma hardfacing iscarried out by means of plasma torches having two arcs burning simultaneously, i.e. the plasma-forming arc and the arc for melting the work metal and the overlay metal. Surfacing is applied on parts made of low-carbon or chrome-nickel steel, aluminium alloy, etc. In electroslag building-up the current from the wire electrode passes to the work metal through the electroconducting liquid slag. The work to be surfaced is disposed vertically in parallel with a copper mould so that the clearance between the work surface and the mould is equal to the thickness of the built-up layer (not less than 10 mm). In this gap, a bath of liquid slag is formed in which heat is emitted. By displacing the mould gradually in vertical direction the entire gap is filled with the metal. This method is used for restoring badly worn out parts of cylindrical, conical and flat shape.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The kind of welding (arc, gas, etc.), the types of weld joints, their shape and dimensions must correspond to the technical requirements and standards. The area where metal is to be cut must be clean of all foreign matter such as moisture, rust, dirt, oil grease, and paint primer. Works made of sheet, bar, and structural rolled shapes must be checked, and ifnecessary straightened. Hot bending of rolled shapes (angles, rods and sheets) must be completed at a temperature not under 800°C. After heating, the work must be slowly and uniformly cooled to avoid hardening, warping, or cracking. Prior to welding, the joint edges must carefully be cleaned from dirt, rust, scale, and oil using steel brushes or other means.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In automatic submerged welding (under a layer of flux), it is necessary to clean with special care the edges to be welded as well as the adjoining metal over a width of 10-15 m m from both sides. After gas cutting, the edges of parts to be welded must be cleaned from bends of metal and adhering slag to the clean metal, and the burrs and irregularities on the joined surfaces must be eliminated. The adherence of parts must be regular over the entire length of the weld. In manual single-side butt-welding the fill on the other side of the weld must have the shape of a uniform roll throughout the whole seam length. In double-side butt welding, after the seam has been obtained, the fill on the other side of the joint must be cut away and cleaned with a steel brush. When welding with a multilayer seam, the surface of each layer must be cleaned from slag before applying the following one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In inspecting welded structures, loaded seams must be examined with a magnifying glass over the whole weld length; and the seams which do not carry loads must be inspected over not less than 1/3 of their length. Simultaneously, the dimensions of the seam and its quality are checked by knocking with a hammer weighing 0.5-0.8 kg

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 37

elements.label: text
elements.text: and with a handle 300 m m long. The sound emitted on knocking the weld metal with a hammer must be the same, as when knocking the intact metal. When defective parts are detected— poor fusion of fill metal, cracks of any shape and delamination, porosity or slag inclusions— they are cut away and welded anew. Portions with strongly irregular seams, faults, waviness and sharply defined boundaries of scales must also be cut out and welded anew.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is allowable to have cuttings in the work metal, which must not be more than 0.5 m m deep for metal thickness of up to 10 mm, and 1 m m deep for metal more than 10 m m thick. In case ofgreater depths, the work portion is cleaned and welded. Opened cavities must also

elements.label: text
elements.text: be welded after preliminary cleaning.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Interior faults (interior cracks, undercuts, porosity, and poor fusion) are checked by knocking and drilling ifno special tools are avail­

elements.label: text
elements.text: able. Drilling of conical recesses by means of drills, ground at an angle of 90°, is effected for opening the whole section of the seam, by cutting away the parent metal 1.5 m m from each side. After testing is completed, the drilled areas are welded.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Welded seams in containers and vessels are tested for tightness with kerosene. For this, the seam is painted from the external side with a chalk solution and after it has dried the seam is richly humi­

elements.label: text
elements.text: dified with kerosene from the inside. In case of a defective seam dark stains appear on the surface painted with chalk. The time during which the seam has been left under the action of kerosene depends on the thickness and disposition of the seam and is about 20-40 min.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The defectuous portions detected on testing are cut out and welded. Welding is preferably carried out in closed premises. When welding in open air it is necessary to provide devices protecting the wel­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ding zone from the direct action of wind, rain and snow.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Soldering and Application of Metal Coatings

elements.label: text
elements.text: Soldering is a method of joining metals in a preheated state by means of nonferrous alloys (solders) whose melting points are low. Unlike in welding, in soldering the parent metal isnot brought into plastic state and is not melted; the melting temperature of the sol­

elements.label: text
elements.text: der is considerably lower than that of the parent metal.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Soldering may be used to join metal parts of different shape and dimensions made of the same and different materials (steel with steel, steel with cast iron, steel with copper, etc.). Soldering is used for the repair of tin drums and cages, flyers, reeds, drums of sizing m a chines, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Soldering may be done with soft solders (with melting temperatures of 480 to 300°C) and with hard solders (melting temperatures 620 to 870°C). Soft soldering is used in cases when soldered joints need not be exceptionally strong; and hard soldering— when solde-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 38 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: red joints must be sufficiently strong and fit for operating at high temperatures.

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: The soldering process consists of the preparation for soldering and of soldering proper. The preparation for soldering consists in grinding, washing, drying, etching, and tinning of metals

elements.label: text
elements.text: vrrrr \^ W\\va

elements.label: text
elements.text: ZZZ2

elements.label: text
elements.text: to be joined. Grinding is performed with a file or scraper, and with subsequent sand papering. The soldered points are degreased by etching; oxide and slags are removed from the molten solder. Rosin and borox fluxes are most commonly used for soft and hard soldering respectively.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 12. Kinds of soldered joints

elements.label: text
elements.text: Soldering is preceded by etching. Alloys of lead and tin are used as soft solders. Soft soldering is carried out as follows. After grinding and etching, the copper soldering iron isheated to a temperature of 300-400°C, its heated tip isrubbed with ammonia spirit and dip­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ped into the solder which melts and as metal drops is transferred onto the soldered work. The molten solder is evenly distributed along the seam by means of the soldering iron; the thinner is the seam, the stronger it is. Types of soldered seams are shown in Fig. 12.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For hard soldering copper-zink alloys are used. After grinding the surface or joints to be soldered, the parts with an applied solder are heated in a hearth to soften the solder. The softened solder is covered with borax without removing the part from the hearth and heating is continued until the solder melts completely. The molten solder is uniformly distributed along the seam with a steel scraper.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Soldering methods (using soft orhard solders), types of seams and their dimensions must be in conformity with the technical requirements and standards. The edges of mating parts must be carefully cleaned from rust, slag, oil, and other contamination. The solder layer must be minimum and uniformly applied on the surface of the part. After soldering the surfaces adjoining the seam are cleaned from solder.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Metal coating. The essence of metal coating is in melting of a metal wire in a special device and spraying it in automized condition under the compressed air pressure (0.5-0.7 MPa) by means of a spray gun with a speed of 140-300 m/s onto the surface to be restored. A s a result, a very hard porous layer is formed on the surface of the work.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Metal coating by spraying is used for restoring the dimensions and geometrical shape of deteriorated parts as well as for obtaining antifriction coatings in bearings, for the elimination of cavities, cracks

elements.label: text
elements.text: and porosity in cast iron and nonferrous castings and for protecting

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 39

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts and different structures from corrosion. Only parts which are not subjected to sharp impact loads may be metal coated (gears cannot be restored by this method). Metal coating cannot be used for building-up small surfaces which are subject to the action of high loads, as for instance shallow grooves, slots, and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The process of metal coating consists of two operations: preparing the surface and spraying it with metal. The preparation of surface is carried out as follows. The part is cleaned from dirt (washed in kerosene or other solvents). Cast iron parts operating with ample lubrication are heated in a hearth or with a gas burner to a temperature of 200 to 250°C for extracting the oil from the pores. W h e n preparing parts which are bodies of revolution the irregularities of the worn-out surface (ovality, conicity, burrs, etc.) are eliminated by cutting on lathe machines. Next the surface is made rough, by cutting on it a “drunken thread”,or annular grooves. Roughing of parts with hard surfaces (hardened or cement-hardened) is achieved by means of the electric sparkor short-circuiting (vibration) methods. Parts of more complicated or flat shape are shot- or sandblasted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The prepared surface is metal coated by spraying, after which the metal layer is machined by turning, grinding, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4. Repair of Parts by Elecfrospark Machining and Electroplating

elements.label: text
elements.text: Electrospark machining. This method is used for restoring wornout surfaces (for instance, spindle bolsters, blades, etc.) by building them up with hard alloys and other material with the aim of strengthening rubbing surfaces; and for the extraction of broken studs, bolts and other parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The essence ofthis method comes to the following. When two metal electrodes connected to different poles of the power source (anode and cathode) are brought together, a high voltage electric field is created causing a strong electric discharge. As a result, the metal in the shape of a liquid drop is ejected from the electrode acting as an anode and is transferred to the electrode acting as a cathode. If the anode (tool) is a rod of hard alloy or of any other current conducting material, its particles which are detached on the formation of the electric spark discharge are brought on the cathode (i.e. the part to be restored) and stay fast on the surface of the work. As a result, a new layer is formed on the surface of the workpiece, the properties of this layer being dependent on the properties of the anode material. If the part to be repaired is an anode and the tool— a cathode, an aperture, a slot, or a cavity is formed in the part under the action of the electric spark discharge. The shape and dimensions ofthe aperture or any other depression depend on the shape and dimensions of the cathode (or the tool).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 40 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 13. Diagram of unit for electro- Fig. 14. Diagram of the unit for elespark building-up and hardening of ctroplating parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: The unit for electric spark building-up and hard facing of parts consists of a d.c. source 1 (Fig. 13), the resistance 2,the fixed capacitor 3 and the vibrator. The metal (plate 8)with which the part 7 is covered, is attached with the screw 6 in the vibrator holder 5. The electromagnet 4 is engaged into the ax. line.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building up is effected as follows. The carefully cleaned part 7 is connected to the negative pole (cathode) after which the plate 8 attached in the vibrator is brought to the part to be restored and this plate is smoothly moved over the surface of the part by means of the vibrator.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building up and hard facing of parts in the shape of shafts may be mechanized by fixing the part in the spindle of a turning lathe and the vibrator in the carriage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The coating applied by the electrospark method has a great number of small pores formed as a result of current discharges. The porosity of the surface improves its wettability, i.e. the surface retains the lubricant more reliably. The applied metal layer is strongly joined with the parent metal of the part. The layer is deposited without special preparation of the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Electroplating. From all the available kinds of electroplating, chromium, copper, steel, or iron plating are the most largely used for the repair of parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The essence of electoplating comes to the following. The part 1 (Fig. 14) is placed as a cathode into the electrolyte 2 containing metal salts used for coating the part. When direct current is passed from the source 3through the anode 4, the metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the surface of the part to be restored.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Chromium plating is used for the restoration of spinning spindles, fluted and pressure rollers, shafts, axles, spindles and other parts with a wear not in excess of 0.1-0.2 m m per side.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The chromium plating process consists of the preparation of the deteriorated part, chromium plating proper and the machining of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 41

elements.label: text
elements.text: the chromium plated surface. The part prepared for chromium plating must satisfy the following requirements: it must have a regular geometric shape and a high finish (8-9 class), it must be free from notches and scores, and be clean. The places on the parts which are not to be chromium plated must be insulated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: An important drawback of a smooth chromium-plated coating is its low wettability with oil. For increasing the wettability porous chromium plating is used which is effected by mechanical, chemical, or electrochemical methods.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Prior to chromium plating by the mechanical method recesses are made on the surface of the part to be restored in the shape of pores or grooves by knurling (on steel parts), or by sandblasting (on cast iron parts). Next, the cavities are coated by chromium plating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The chemical method of chromium plating consists in shorttime etching of the chromium coating in diluted hydrochloric acid

elements.label: text
elements.text: (1:1). In this way, the microcracks in the chromium coating arewidened and deepened.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the electrochemical method, the chromium coating is subjected to anode pickling by reversing the polarity (the chromium plated part becomes an anode). In microcracks the chromium is dissolved, and as a result the cracks become wider and deeper.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Copperplatingis used to hard face the outer surfaces of rings in antifriction bearings, various bearing linings and bushings, as well as other parts with a view to restoring the initial tightness and the worn-out helical surface of the worm gear drive, and thus obtaining smoothness of meshing and also an underlayer for chromium plating. Copper plating is used on steel, cast iron, zinc and other metals. The surface of parts for copper plating is to be prepared in thesame way as for chromium plating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Steel plating (ironplating) is used for building-up w o r m surfaces,, restoring close fits and forming an underlayer for chromium plating. The sequence of operations in steel plating is the same as in chromium plating. After steel plating, the part is heated to a temperature of 300-400°C in order to eliminate the brittleness of the over­

elements.label: text
elements.text: layer. The layer may beeasilymachined, and subjectedtoheattreatment and case hardening without cracking or flaking.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 5. Glueing and Riveting

elements.label: text
elements.text: Glueing. Epoxy adhesives present the following favourable properties: a good adhesion (sticking capacity) to different materials,, low shrinkage at hardening (0.15-0.14%), good hardening at a temperature of 15-100°C without application of pressure, chemical resistance in different media, waterproofness, high physical and mechanical properties in hardened state, etc. The adhesive consists of epoxy resin, a plastifier, and accumulatory and hardening agents.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 42 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair of parts by glueing is simple and reliable. Most various defects of flat parts m a y be eliminated by glueing, i.e. cracks, indentations, cuts, cavities, and pores; it is possible to restore by glue­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing: bushes, rings of antifriction bearings, pins, axles, holes in the

elements.label: text
elements.text: bushings of sliding bearings, shafts, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The surfaces of the parts to be repaired must be adequately prepared: they must be machined on a lathe, cleaned with sand paper, filed, scraped, or cleaned with a metal brush or with a jet of shot

elements.label: text
elements.text: blast. The method of preparation depends on the material of the part to be repaired, its design and sizes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The part after preparation is degreased and a layer of glue is spread over the surfaces, and using a special mandrel or a new part the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 15. Methods of part repairing by glueing

elements.label: text
elements.text: layer is calibrated before its hardening (30 min or 1 hour after its application). After calibration, the part is kept at a temperature of 20°C for 24 hours or at a temperature of 60°G for 4-5 hours until the glue becomes hard, after which the hard layer is subjected to

elements.label: text
elements.text: mechanical working to obtain the required shape and size.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Let us discuss examples of repair by glueing. Conical parts are apt to develop cracks which impair the hermeticity of bodies causing oil leakage or other damages. The cracks are repaired as follows.

elements.label: text
elements.text: First, the crack is worked to a V-shaped joint (angle of opening <60-70°) to a depth of 2-3 mm; the ends of the crack are drilled with

elements.label: text
elements.text: holes 2.5-3.5 m m in diameter. The surface is cleaned from both sides with sand paper or with a brush until a metal shine is obtained.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The crack is prepared as said above with acetone and at the elapse -of ten or fifteen minutes after the evaporation of the solvent, an epo­

elements.label: text
elements.text: xy glue is applied and carefully levelled with a palette knife. The -crack is filled with a rope of glass fibre impregnated with epoxy resin. The rope is placed in the V-shaped joint, pressed with a smooth

elements.label: text
elements.text: metal sheet and kept in this condition for 25-30 hours. After the crack has been stopped up, the glued joint (Fig. 15a) may be machined with any cutting tool (scraper, file, milling cutter, etc.). For planing or milling dents and scores, the defective portion of the work 3 (Fig. 155) is imparted the shape of a groove in which the insert 1

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods of Machine Parts Restoration 43

elements.label: text
elements.text: is attached with the use of glue 2;the insert is made with adequate precision from the same material as the part to be repaired, and it should be 1-2 m m above the groove. The surfaces of the insert and of the part to be repaired are washed with a solvent and coated with

elements.label: text
elements.text: a layer of glue. Next, the insert is tightly fitted to the groove and pressed with a load creating a pressure of 0.8-0.9 MPa. After the glue has hardened, the defectuous point is machined to the preset size.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Scores appearing at the wear of rubbing surfaces in the parts are worked up with epoxy glue and smoothened. The defective portion of the part ismachined with an abrasive wheel or a scraper, and carefully wiped with a solvent. After the solvent has evaporated, the damaged portion is coated with a layer of epoxy glue so that it slight­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ly protrudes above the surface of the part. After the glue has hardened this place is worked with a file, a grinding wheel, or a scraper.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For putting pins in place, the worn-out thread of the hole is cleaned with a wire brush and the pin threaded end with a flat brush, after which they are twice degreased with acetone and kept for 8-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 10 min at normal temperature. Next, a thin layer of epoxy glue is applied onto the thread in the hole and the pin, the pin is screwed-in as far as it will go (Fig. 15c) and the excess of glue which has been pressed out of the hole is eliminated. The glue is left to harden after which the joint is cleaned.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For fixing bearings in machine parts, the cavity 2 (Fig. 15d) of the bobbin and the exterior ring of the bearing 1 are cleaned and degreased. After the evaporation of the solvent, the surfaces of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: ring and the bearing are coated with a thin layer of epoxy resin 3, the bearing isintroduced together with the shaft 4 into the cavity 2 and kept there until the glue becomes hard. Then, the glue downflows are cleaned. The bush 1 is fixed in the recess of the body 2 (Fig. 15c) proceeding in the same manner. To ensure a good coaxiality the two shaft bearings must be installed simultaneously.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The kind of glue and the shape of edges must correspond to the technical requirements and standards. The edges of mating parts must be carefully cleaned from rust, scale, oil, and other contaminations by means of steel brushes or other methods. The thickness of the glue layer, the number of applied layers, and the conditions under which the parts are kept after glueing depend on the type of technological machining and the kind of glue employed. The quality of glue­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing is checked by breaking the glued surfaces. Not less than 5% of glued parts must be subjected to testing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Riveted joints. The holes for rivets must be carefully cleaned from burrs by counterboring and the face edge should not exceed

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1.5-2 mm. Steel rivets with a diameter up to 10 m m may be set in cold condition and rivets of greater diameter only with heating. Joints which must satisfy high requirements in respect to density

elements.label: text
elements.text: and when the thickness of sheets exceeds 4 mm, are to be caulked

elements.label: text
elements.text: 44 Chapter Two

elements.label: text
elements.text: along the joint edge and rivet heads. When the sheet thickness is less than 4 m m a good density of the joint is achieved by placing a packing hand between the riveted sheets (tow or flax impregnated with red lead diluted in natural drying oil or any other composition).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The quality of riveting is determined by exterior examination, knocking and random inspection of the head size using gauges and feelers; moreover the setting of the rivet rod is also checked (filling up of the hole by the rivet body). Knocking of rivet heads with a diameter up to 19 mm is carried out with a hammer weighing 250 g, and of rivets with heads over 19 m m in diameter— with a hammer weighing 400 g. When knocking with a hammer causes the vibration or displacement of the rivet head, the rivet should be sheared and replaced with a new one. When the rivets have cracks in the head, or the head has irregular tolerances of shape, with dimensions exceeding the tolerances established by standards and norms, the rivets must be sheared and replaced with new ones. Notching of the metal by a hobby tool to a depth over 0.5 m m is not allowed. To check the degree of rod setting, it is necessary to take out 0.5% of the total number of rivets, and in case there is an incomplete filling of holes with rivets it is necessary to shear-off all the rivets which seem doubtful on head knocking.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTES ON MACHINE PARTS

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Axles, Shafts and Bearings

elements.label: text
elements.text: Axles and shafts. Intended for supporting rotating parts— pulleys, blocks, gears, sprockets, rollers, etc. Though slightly differing in design, axles and shafts operate in a different manner; axles support rotating parts, and therefore they are subject to the bending load from the mass of these parts and from the loads applied to them, while shafts are members of a mechanism transmitting the torque. Depending on operational conditions, the axles may be stationary or rotating together with the parts fitted on them (car wheels, blocks), while shafts are only rotatable.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Loads taken up by shafts and axles are transmitted to the bodies or frameworks of machines through supports, i.e. bearings. Depending on the kind of friction all the bearings are classified in sliding and rolling friction plain and antifriction bearings. The parts of axles and shafts which arein direct contact with the bearings have a common name— journals (Fig. 16). The journal transmitting to the bearing the radial load and disposed at the end of the shaft is called a pin (7) and that disposed in the middle of the shaft is called the neck (2). That part of the shaft which transmits the axial load to the bearings (5) is called the thrust journal (5) while the sliding bearing taking up this axial load is called the thrust bearing

elements.label: text
elements.text: Axles are always straight while shafts may be straight, cranked, and flexible. Mostly, straight shafts are used. As classified by their design the shafts and axles m a y be smooth, stepped, solid, and hollow. For mounting gears, pulleys, couplings and bearings on the shafts and axles, adequate cylindrical or bevel mountings are provided with certain diameters and lengths. To fix these parts in axial direction the shafts

elements.label: text
elements.text: are equipped with shoulders and

elements.label: text
elements.text: 46 Chapter Three

elements.label: text
elements.text: threading for fixing the parts with a nut, etc. For transmitting the torque to the shafts keyed, splined and pinned joints are used. Mostly solid shafts and axles are used, but in the case when the mass of parts must be reduced or it isnecessary to pass the shaft through another part, as for instance a tie rod, the shafts and axles are made hollow.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Axle and shaft bearings. Bearings may be classified according to the following features. For instance, depending on the kind of friction they may be classified into sliding or plain bearings in which the supporting part of the axle or shaft (journal, pin, neck, heel) slides on the interior surface of the bearing and into rolling or antifriction bearings in which the sliding friction is replaced by the rolling friction (this being achieved by the introduction of rollers or balls

elements.label: text
elements.text: between the journal and the bushing). Depending on the direction of the load applied the bearings are subdivided into radial bearings taking up radial loads, thrust bearings taking up axial loads, and radial thrust bearings taking up radial and axial loads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Sliding orplain bearings. The advantages presented by these bearings are: smaller dimensions as compared with the rolling antifriction bearings; the use of split bearings which may be mounted on the main journal of crankshafts; the operation with shafts rotating at a speed of 10 000 min-1 and higher; possible operation in water and other aggressive mediums under vibration and impact loads; the possibility of using large-size journals.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drawbacks of sliding bearings are the need of constant observation and continuous oiling, the reduced efficiency, the nonuniform wear of bearings and journals, the use of costly nonferrous metals and alloys (bronze, babbitt), and relatively long journals and linings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The friction determines the wear and heating of the bearing and its efficiency. To reduce friction the bearings are lubricated with special lubricants. Depending on the bearing working conditions the friction may be classified into dry, semidry, semifluid, and fluid friction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the absence of lubricant between rubbing surfaces, a dry friction is created. In this case, there is an intensive wear and jamming of rubbing surfaces, the friction coefficient being / = 0.1 ....0.3. In case of semidryfriction the lubricant is supplied irregularly and in an insufficient amount to the rubbing surfaces. When this kind of friction occurs, the surfaces of the pin and bearing come in contact which results in their wear, the friction coefficient being/ = 0.1 . . .

elements.label: text
elements.text: .. .0.25. If the layer of lubricant between the rubbing surfaces is very thin and is easily impaired by the surface roughness a semifluid friction is created. W h e n the oil film is ruptured, the metal rubbing surfaces come directly in contact with each other which causes their wear, and the friction coefficient in this case is / = 0.005 . . .0.1.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Notes on Machine Parte 47

elements.label: text
elements.text: When the oil layer between the rubbing surfaces is sufficient (2- 70 [Am) so that their contact is avoided a fluidfriction is created. One part of the lubricant layer adheres to the pin surface and the other to the bearing surface; with friction occurring between these layers the part wear is almost completely obviated; / = 0.001. ..0.005.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The aim of bearing lubrication is to reduce losses on friction, to reduce or obviate wear, to eliminate heat formed at rubbing, to protect the bearings from corrosion, to lessen noise, and to provide a better sealing by filling the gaps with grease between the rotating and stationary surfaces. All the lubricants are subdivided into liquid

elements.label: text
elements.text: oils, consistent, and solid grease.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Liquid oils are the most largely used lubricants. As a rule, for oiling the machines petroleum oils find application. The most important characteristic of the oils is their viscosity. The viscosity or internal friction is the resistance against the shifting of one lubricant layer relative to the other. Viscosity m a y be dynamic or absolute and kinematic. Dynamic viscosity is determined by the hydrodynamic calculations of a given lubricant. Kinematic viscosity is determined by the time necessary for the flow of a preset amount of oil through a capillary tube under the action of gravity. The unit of kinematic viscosity is stokes (the name of the English scientist Stokes). The list of the main liquid oils used in machine-building is given below:

elements.label: text
elements.text: Liquid oils may be used for high-speed shafts and axles at low and high temperatures; they have a low internal friction, ensure good heat elimination, and ifnecessary can be changed without disassembling the unit. These oils are disadvantageous in that they require frequent replenishing and the use of packings of more intricate shape to prevent the leak.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Greases are obtained by adding thickening agents such as calcium and sodium oils into liquid oil. The most largely used greases on a calcium base are the cup greases and on a sodium base— constalines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Greases are employed with high loads and small rotational speeds of shafts and axles. Greases are entirely leakless (it is enough to use simple packings), completely fill the clearances between the rotating and stationary parts, may operate during a long period of time {ayear and more without change) and reliably protect the parts against corrosion. Greases present the following disadvantages: they are sensitive to changes in temperature, present a high internal friction and are difficult to replace. Usually greases are packed at the assembly of a unit and are periodically replenished by means of special cup oilers or a grease gun through grease cups.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When usual lubricants cannot ensure normal operating conditions for the parts and units, solid lubricants are used. Most largely employed is graphite grease which is a mixture of graphite powder with consistent grease or as a suspension in liquid oil. Such greases are

elements.label: text
elements.text: used in heavily loaded bearings with a low sliding speed and high temperatures. Molybdenum disulphide ameliorates the antifriction properties of the metal. It is applied as a powder or paste on the m e tal surface rubbed in with soft material and polished. The formed film is not ruptured in an aggressive medium, sustains high loads and may operate at temperatures from — 70 to +300°C. Antifriction bearings are largely used in the industry including textile machinery. The main advantages of antifriction bearings in contrast to sliding bearings are the low friction coefficient, a high­

elements.label: text
elements.text: er load carrying capacity with a smaller width of the bearing, a lower consumption of lubricants, the ease of erection, maintenance and servicing, interchangeability, and the possibility of mass production of standard bearings which considerably reduces their cost. The main disadvantages of antifriction bearings are a limited^ ability of taking-up impact loads, different life at equal rotational speed and load, and big exterior diameter of bearings as compared with plain bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Usually the antifriction bearing consists of the balls and rollers, the outer and inner rings and separators. Used sometimes are bearings without outer or inner rings. In this case the functions of the ring are performed by adequate parts of the shaft and body. In some casesuse ismade of bearings having no rings, with balls fixed

elements.label: text
elements.text: Notes on Machine Parts 49

elements.label: text
elements.text: in a retainer. In needle bearings there are no separators and the races are completely filled with

elements.label: text
elements.text: balls or rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Antifriction bearings are classified as follows:

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the shape of rolling solids— balls and rollers. The rollers may be cylindrical Fig. 1L Kinds of(rollers and short, cylindrical and long, helical, needle, barrel-shaped and conical (Fig. 17); according to the direction of the applied load— radial, thrust, and radial thrust bearings. Radial bearings take up the radial load which is perpendicular to the geometrical axis of the shaft (simultaneously they m a y take-up only an inconsiderable axial load); thrust bearings take up the axial load applied along the rotational axis, and radial

elements.label: text
elements.text: and thrust bearings— a combined load, i.e. simultaneously the radial and axial loads;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the number of ball or roller rows— single-row, doublerow and four-row bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the method of shaft misalignment compensation— self-aligning (with a spherical interior surface of outer rings in radial bearings) and non-selfadjusting;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to overall dimensions with the same inner diameter— extra-light and superlight, light, medium and heavy bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the width— narrow, normal, wide, and superwide; according to the precision of execution— standard class, higher class, high class, extra-high class, and super-high class.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The life of antifriction bearings highly depends on their proper mounting and disassembling. The bearing is mounted on the shaft with an interference fit by pressing the inner ring by a hand press

elements.label: text
elements.text: or by heating the bearing in oil at a temperature of 80-100°C. On heating the bearing hole increases and it can be freely fitted on the shaft. For removing the bearing from the shaft or body special remo­

elements.label: text
elements.text: vers or pullers are used. Prior to the erection, all the mounting sets should be carefully cleaned and the bearing washed in gasoline. When mounting or dismounting an antifriction bearing the force should be applied only to the ring which is being or was mounted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is not allowable to apply force through the balls and rollers, as indents will appear on their surfaces or on the races, and the bearing will be ruined.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Clutches, Couplings and Springs

elements.label: text
elements.text: COUPLINGS are used for transmitting rotation from one shaft to another disposed on the same centre line with the first one, for dam-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 50 Chapter Three

elements.label: text
elements.text: ping impact loads, connecting and separating shafts during machine operation and also for transmitting rotation only in one direction or at a preset rotational speed, etc. Couplings may be subdivided into three groups: rigid, flexible, and elastic.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rigidcouplings are used in cases when a built-up shaft must operate as a whole one. Such couplings require a precise coincidence of connected shafts as the non-axiality appearing in the course of operation may cause bending and damaging of bearings. The simplest rigid coupling is a sleeve mounted with an interference fit on the ends of the shafts. The torque is transmitted by means of semi-circular or sunk keys. This kind of coupling is called an end sleeve. Wide application find flange couplings consisting of two flanged halfcouplings keyed on the ends of the shafts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Flexible couplings are used to compensate the misalignment of shafts. To such pertain jaw extension couplings which compensate only the longitudinal displacement ofshafts. The double slider coupling compensates for the radial (within 0.04 shaft diameter) and an inconsiderable angular (not more than 30") displacement of shafts. The couplings are used at low rotation speeds— under 250 min*1 and with small diameters of connected shafts— under 100 mm). A tooth-type coupling compensates different shafts for misalignments (longitudinal, radial— within 1-8 mm, and angular — 1°).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Classification of Clutches and Couplings

elements.label: text
elements.text: Elasticcouplingsnot only compensate for the shaft misalignment, but also ensure dampening of jerks and impacts by the deformation of the elastic elements, -There are couplings with nonmetallic elastic elements (rubber and leather) and metal flexible elements (steel spring). For instance elastic couplings with rubber bushed studs may compensate for a radial misalignment of 6 « 0.3-0.6 mm, an-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Notes on Machine Parts 51

elements.label: text
elements.text: gular misalignment a < 1°, and an inconsiderable axial displacement of shafts. These couplings are used for connecting shafts with

elements.label: text
elements.text: a diameter of 16-150 mm. The deformation of elastic elements dampens jerks and impacts, but the damping capacity of the coupling is inconsiderable.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Clutches ensure the connection and disconnection of two shafts in the course of machine operation without its stoppage and dismantling. There are two kinds of clutches: jaw and friction clutches.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Jaw clutches consist of two half-couplings, the left half-coupling being attached on the shaft by means of a sunk key with an interference fit, while the right-hand one is fitted on the driven shaft by virtue of a sunk key and with a slide fit so that it may be displaced along the shaft axis by a forked shifter. On the faces of both halfcouplings there are provided protrusions (cams) and recesses. The cam profile may be rectangular or trapezoidal (which facilitates coupling engagement and allows the reverse motion without jolts).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The use of jaw clutches is recommended when the shafts to be connected rotate at relatively slow speeds.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Frictionclutchesensure a smooth impactless engagement owing to the slippage of the half-coupling rubbing surfaces. Depending on the shape of their working surfaces, friction clutches may be subdivided into disk clutches (flatsurface), cone clutches (conical surface), shoe, band and other types of clutches (cylindrical surface). Both the friction and jaw clutches are used to prevent shaft misalignment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Special clutches are designed to protect the drive from overloads (breakages) and to transmit the torque only in one direction or at the preset rotational speed. There are different types of special clutches, i.e. safety, centrifugal, and overrunning clutches, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Safety clutcheswith a shearing pin consists of two half-couplings keyed to shafts with interference fit. The torque is transmitted through the pin which is sheared at overloads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Centrifugal clutches automatically connect the shafts only when the preset rotational speed is exceeded. Such clutches are used for the automatic engagement and disengagement of mechanisms at a certain rotational speed of shafts with great mass, and for obtaining

elements.label: text
elements.text: a smoother start.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The overrunning clutch transmits the torque only in one direction and allows free relative rotations in the reverse direction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: SPRINGS. These are elastic elements which are used for tensioning or pressing couplings, brakes, and friction drives, for accumulating energy with its subsequent use (impact mechanisms, dampers and others), for the return of valves and cam mechanisms, and for measuring the efforts in dynamometers, and other instruments.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the load applied, the springs are subdivided into extension, compression, torsion, and bending springs; and accor-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 52 Chapter Three

elements.label: text
elements.text: ding to their design into coil, cylindrical and shaped, disk, sheet, flat, spiral etc. Most largely used in machines are coiled cylindrical extension and compression springs made of round wire.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Transmissions

elements.label: text
elements.text: Devices for transmitting power from the motor to the executive mechanism are called transmissions. Transmissions between the m o tor and executive mechanisms are used to change and adjust the rotational speed, to transform rotational movement into translatory; and to increase the torque, etc. Mechanical, pneumatic and hydraulic transmissions have found wide application in textile machinery building.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kind of transmissions are mechanical drives, that may be classified as follows:

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the principle of operation— friction, belt, toothed, worm, screw, and chain drives;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the kind of rotational feed changing*— step down (reducers) and step-up transmissions (multipliers);

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the mutual disposition in space— those placed between parallel, intersecting and crossing shafts;

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the kind of shaft motion— ordinary (the shafts rotate around their axis) and planetary (the shafts with the parts mounted on them move in space around stationary axles as planets move around the sun);

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the number of separate transmissions taking part simultaneously in a given drive— one and multi-step (two, threeetc. stop);

elements.label: text
elements.text: according to the design— open transmissions, having no cases to cover them; half-closed— mounted in the same way as the open transmissions, but provided with a light protection housing; closed and housed in a common strong and rigid case which also encloses the bearings (closed transmissions are used for heavily loaded highspeed drives).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Friction transmissions are subdivided into two groups; one with a constant and the other with an adjustable gear ratio. The first group of transmissions is employed for mechanisms requiring smooth motion, noiseless operation, impactless engagement in running, etc. The second group of transmissions relates to variable-speed drives ensuring a smooth and stepless change of the gear ratio within certain limits. Friction drives present the following advantages: simplicity of design, absence of impacts, smooth and noiseless ope-

elements.label: text
elements.text: * Depending on the kind of transmission the ratio of the angular speed or the rotational speed of the driving (input) and driven (output) shafts may be constant, or may change within certain limits according to the stepped (gear box) or smooth stepless (variable speed drives) law.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Notes on Machine Parts 53

elements.label: text
elements.text: ration, the most precise gear ratio instant value, the possibility of smooth stepless change of gear ratio and the protection against breakages in case of casual overload due to the slippage of rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drawbacks of friction transmissions are: a limited power transmission (up to 10 kV), a heavy load on the shafts and their bearings due to the compression forces of rollers, the strong wear of rollers being the cause of noises in operation and the comparatively low efficiency (q = 0.7-0.92).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Friction drives cannot ensure a rigid kinematic connection. The friction drive rollers are made of materials capable of ensuring a good surface and wear resistance, and also a greater friction factor. For operating without lubrication use is made of hardened steel rollers. It is observed that in friction transmssiions, there occurs a fatigue flaking of the roller working surfaces (when working with lubrication), wear (when working without lubrication), and scoring of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: surface (when operating at high speeds and loads).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Belt drives are a veriety of friction transmissions by a flexible connection, i.e. belting. Depending on the shape of the belt cross section the drives may be of the flat-belt, V-belt, and round-belt type. The advantages presented by the belt drive are the possibility of power transmission over long distances (up to 15 m and more), smooth and noiseless operation, the absence of sharp deviations in loads owing to flexible stretching of the belt, protection of mechanisms from overloads owing to the possible belt slippage, simplicity of design and the ease of operation, and the possibility of different arrangement of shafts in space. The drawbacks of belt drives are their large sizes, the inconstancy of the gear ratio due to belt slippage, the high load on the shafts and bearings which is necessary to ensure the preliminary tension of the belt and the short life of belts (1000-5000 h).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The belts must have a high traction ability, i.e. high cohesion with the pulley surface without slippage; high resistance, long life and wear resistance, as well as low elasticity at bending; moreover they must have a low cost.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on operation conditions, driving belts may be made of different materials, such as leather, rubberized cotton, and wool. Endless standard belts are used for high-speed drives which considerably enhances the quality of transmission, but their application is limited due to the complexity of their manufacturing. V-belts have a trapezoidal shape in cross section and are made of rubberized textile cord. The belt pulley consists of the rim carrying the belt, the hub keyed on the shaft, and the spokes or the disk connecting the rim with the hub. The shape of the rim working surface is determined by the kind of belt to be used.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the linear feed, the pulleys are made of gray cast iron (at v^ 30 m s-1) of a steel casting (at v= 30-45 m s”1) and of alloyed steel or duralumin (at v> 45 m s-1).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The pulleys used for V-belts operating at a speed of v^ 25 m s-1 are usually made of gray cast iron or aluminium alloys.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gear transmissions. Consist of two meshing gears— a small and a big one. Gearings are classified according to:

elements.label: text
elements.text: the shape of the tooth profile— involute and cycloidal gearing (used in watch mechanisms);

elements.label: text
elements.text: the mutual disposition of the driving and driven shaft axes— with cylindrical gears and shaft axes disposed in parallel (Fig. 18a-d), with conical gears and intersecting shaft axes (Fig. 18c, /), with screw gears and crossing shaft axes (Fig. 18g), with gear and rack for transforming the rotational motion in translation, and vice versa (Fig. 18h);

elements.label: text
elements.text: the relative rotation of gears and teeth disposition— with external gearing (the gears rotate in the opposite directions), and with internal gearing (the gears rotate in the same direction, see Fig. 18d);

elements.label: text
elements.text: the disposition of teeth in relation to the gear generatrix— spur gearing (see Fig. 18a, d, e, h), helical gearing (see Fig. 186), herringbone gearing (Fig. 18c), and curvilinear gearing (Fig. 18/);

elements.label: text
elements.text: the operation conditions and design— open (not enclosed in a housing, working without lubricant or with periodical lubrication and not protected against dust and dirt), closed (enclosed in a special housing protecting them against the penetration of dust and dirt and working with constant ample lubrication), and half-closed (protected against free penetration of dust and dirt by means of a thin protection hood);

elements.label: text
elements.text: Notes on Machine Parts 55

elements.label: text
elements.text: the linear speed— slow speed (v^ 3 m s-1), average speed (v= = 3 ... 15 m s -1) and high-speed (v> 15 m s-1). The advantages of gear transmissions are a constant gear ratio, high efficiency (up to 0.99), rugged design, the ease of service, and an unlimited range of transmitted power (from hundred fractions of a kilowatt to tens of thousands of kW). The drawbacks of gear transmissions are their comparatively complicated manufacture requiring special precise equipment and tools, and noisiness at high speeds.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on their use, the gears are manufactured by different methods. For instance, for low-speed drives gears with cast teeth are employed. The precision of their manufacture is not high, but owing to the hard crust on the tooth surface its wear resistance is high. To improve the precision of gearing, the gears with cast teeth are sometimes subjected to additional mechanical treatment. At present, in mass production hot gear generation is used without further machining.

elements.label: text
elements.text: As a rule the manufacture of gears consists of the following operations: the production of a blank (by casting, forging, or stamping) with further turning on a lathe; gear teeth cutting on milling machines, gear shapers, or other special machine tools; heat treatment (if such is needed); teeth finishing (by grinding, shaving, or lapping) for gears of not under the 7th class of precision.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gear teeth cutting may be carried out by the template or by the generating methods. According to the first method the cavity between the teeth is cut on a milling machine by a special single-angle gear tooth cutter (Fig. 19a) or by a side mill (Fig. 196) after which the blank is turned to one tooth and the operation is repeated. The precision of this method of cutting is not high as the cutter profile m a y

elements.label: text
elements.text: be distorted, the work and tool may be inaccurately mounted, or the divider has not been set precisely. Therefore such gears are used for slow and average speed transmissions. According to the second method of gear cutting or generating the cutting tool, gear shaping cutter (Fig. 19c), the rack-type gear cutter (Fig. 19d), or the gear hob

elements.label: text
elements.text: are generated in the process of gear cutting together with the gear blank as a couple of gears which ensures a higher precision of meshing than the template method. For this reason, the gears are mainly manufactured by the generating method.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The serviceability of the tooth is mainly affected by contact stresses applied for a short moment of contact at a given point and bending stresses acting during the whole time the given tooth is engaged. These variable stresses cause the wear destruction of teeth—

elements.label: text
elements.text: breakage from the bending stresses and surface flaking from the action of contact stresses. Let us discuss the most characteristic

elements.label: text
elements.text: kinds of teeth deterioration.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Teeth breakage may be caused by heavy overloads and fatigue of the metal under the action of variable stresses. Sometimes, tooth

elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: breakage is caused by shaft misalignment and a nonuniform loading in tooth length (Fig. 20a). The measures to avoid teeth breakage are: the increase of the module, a modification of meshing, heat treatment and the reduction of stress concentration.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kind of teeth surface destruction in closed transmissions with proper lubrication is the fatigue flaking or spalling (Fig. 20b). Though there is no metal contact of teeth in such transmissions, but in the course of a lengthy operation there appears fatigue of the surface layer. Big recesses appear on the surface which continue to develop into cavities followed by flaking and deterioration of the oil film which result in an intensive destruction of the tooth surface. When the teeth are not very hard, favourable results may also be

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 20. Kinds of teeth wear

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: obtained,such as better running-in of teeth surfaces and smoothening of cavities. Flaking may be avoided by increasing the tooth surface hardness through the application of heat treatment and obtaining a higher precision of execution, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Abrasive wear (Fig. 20c) is the most largely encountered kind of open gear deterioration because of poor lubrication (dirt and abrasive particles get into the gearing); in this case the surface is worn out, the tooth thickness is reduced, the clearances in the gearing ar& increased, and noisy running develops (knocks). All this can lead to teeth breakage. To avoid wear, it is necessary to increase the hard­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ness, to improve the finish of the teeth surface, and to protect them, from contamination.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Jamming (Fig. 20d)is observed in high-speed and heavily loaded transmissions. At the point of contact under the action of high pressure and temperature, oil is squeezed out and metal particles as if

elements.label: text
elements.text: become welded and torn off from one of the surfaces. The build-up* is formed which scratches the working surfaces. A special oil is used to reduce jamming.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Plastic shearing of the teeth surface layer is characteristic for heavily loaded slow speed transmissions with gearings made of materials of low hardness. To avoid this, it is necessary to increase tho hardness of the teeth material. In such gearings it is observed that the surface layer obtained by nitriding, cyaniding, and cementation,

elements.label: text
elements.text: would peel off as a result of high contact stresses. Peeling is very dangerous as bits of metal getting between the teeth rapidly bring the whole gear transmission out of order.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worm gearings serve for transmitting the motion between two nonparallel but nonintersecting shafts. In that transmission the motion is effected on the principle of a wormgear, with a w o r m having: trapezoidal threading 1 which comes in engagement with a gear having spiral level teeth 2 (Fig. 21).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 38 Chapter Three

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worm gearings are largely used in textile machine building owing to the possibility of obtaining high gear ratio* in one couple (10-80 for power transmissions and up to 500 for dividers), smoothness of meshing and noiseless operation, the possibility of self- Fig. 22. Diagram of chain drive braking, comparatively small overall dimensions and mass. "Worm gearings present disadvantages, such as comparatively low

elements.label: text
elements.text: efficiency, strong heating at lengthy operation, high cost of the material (bronze) used for the worm gear, and the passibility of

elements.label: text
elements.text: transmitting power only up to 60 kW.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Considering the hard working conditions the materials for the -worm gear must have good antifriction properties, high wear resistance and a low jamming ability. In modern transmissions the

elements.label: text
elements.text: worms are made of carbon and alloy steel. In heavily loaded transmissions the worm is subjected to heat treatment (cementation, hardening, etc.) with subsequent grinding or polishing. The worm gears are mainly made of bronze, and for minor slow-speed gearing •cast iron is employed. Tin bronze is considered as the best material for worm gears. They are used for manufacturing heavily loaded gearings operating at high sliding speeds (up to 25 m/s). Tinless bronze is used for gearings operating at sliding speeds up to 10 m/s and cast iron for speeds up to 2 m/s.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Chain drives are largely used in textile machinery mainly as a stepdown transmission. Their main advantages are: the possibility of using smaller overall dimensions than in belt drives at considerable interaxial distances (up to 8 m), constant gear ratio (imas =

elements.label: text
elements.text: = 8), high efficiency (up to 0.98), unlike in belt drives, lower loads on the shafts, and the possibility of imparting rotation to several shafts by one chain. The drawbacks presented by the chain drives

elements.label: text
elements.text: are chain stretching due to wear in articulations, the high cost of the chain, the impossibility of reversing without stopping the machine, loud noise during operation and the necessity of a careful maintenance (adjustment, lubrication, and elimination of misalign­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ment).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The chain drive consists of two sprockets (the smaller driving sprocket and the greater driven sprocket) keyed onto shafts (Fig. 22). The sprockets are connected by an endless chain. In mechanical

elements.label: text
elements.text: Roller chains (Fig. 23a) consist of exterior movable links 1 and interior links 5. The interior links are force fitted on the ends of the bushings 4 and the exterior links— on the shaft 2having its ends riveted over. The bushing 4 and shaft 2 form a hinge. For reducing the wear, rollers 3 are fitted on the bushing. Toothed chains (Fig. 23b) consists of a set of toothed plates and hinges. The working surfaces of the teeth are limited by surfaces at an angle of a = 60°. The material used for the chain parts must be highly wear-resistant and strong. The plates are made of plain and chrome plated steel while the shafts,

elements.text: bushings and rollers— of carburized steels with further hardening. Gear boxes (reducers) are mechanisms composed of toothed or worm gearings enclosed in separate housings and working in an oil

elements.label: text
elements.text: bath. The reducing gear box is intended for decreasing the shaft rotational speed and consequently for increasing the torque. Mechanisms designed for increasing the shaft rotational speed and made as a se­

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reducers are classified according to the following characteristics: by the type of the drive— into toothed, worm, and toothedworm reducers; according to the number of steps— into one-step reducer (when the transmission is effected by one couple of gears), two-, three- and multistep reducers; according to the type of gears— into cylindrical (with straight or skew tooth), conical (with straight or curvilinear tooth), conical-cylindrical and so on; and according to the disposition of the reducer shafts in space the reducers are subdivided into horizontal, vertical and inclined reducers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Acceptance of Machines for Repair and Their Disassembly

elements.label: text
elements.text: Acceptance of machines for repair. All the machines and looms are accepted for the following major overhaul or medium repair in strict conformity with the adopted schedule. If the machine or loom is to be subject to medium repair,the shop foreman makes out a list of defects not later than five days before the repair term. This is done to determine the amount of parts and materials necessary to

elements.label: text
elements.text: have at hand for carrying-out the repair. If the machine or loom has been accepted for major overhaulthe list of defects is written by the personnel of the mechanical repair department during the last medium repair. The list is specified and checked ten days before the beginning of the major overhaul. It should contain: the enumeration of mechanisms and units to be repaired; parts to be replaced or restored; and assessment of operational capability of the machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The machine received for scheduled repairs must contain all the parts and mechanisms, as otherwise the machine is not accepted for repair. The list of defects is specified in the course of repairs. The assistant foreman and the worker attending to the machine take part in compiling the list of defects.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disassembling the machine into units. Disassembling is carried-out in reverse order as compared to the assembly, i.e. parts which are the last ones to be assembled are the first to be removed. Depending on the kind of the repair to be carried out, the disassembly may be complete (major overhaul) or partial (medium repairs). First, the machine is dismantled into assembly units and next the latter are disassembled into parts. Sometimes in addition to units, large assemblies, such as loom dobbies, are removed from the machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of machine repair different kinds of work are carried out: nuts, bolts, pins and screws are screwed-in and out; bushes, bearings and axles are unpressed and pressed again; pulleys, gears and

elements.label: text
elements.text: cams are removed and fitted in place. Different kinds of tools and devices are used for these operations (mallets, hammers, wrenches, drifts, screwdrivers, strippers, presses, etc.).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Hammers and malletsm a y be of different types: ordinary steel mallets and soft mallets made of lead, copper, aluminium alloy, babbit, and wood. In contrast to ordinary mallets, soft mallets cause no deterioration of removed parts, but wear out rapidly. Mallets with detachable impact soft parts mounted in a steel holder prove to be more durable.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Wrenches(Fig. 24a-h)are intended for unscrewing and driving nuts, bolts, pins, and screws. Ordinary wrenches are of the open, box and ratchet type, while the adjustable wrenches are used for driving and unscrewing nuts of hexagonal and square section. Adjustable wrenches may be used with mouths of different dimensions, but they do not ensure good hold of the bolt or nut head. For small-size nuts and bolts located in areas with difficult access— box or hinged wrenches are used. A hinged wrench is a combination of the box wrench with a double hinged head (replaceable or constant) which allows its use even when the wrench rod is strongly inclined.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Special wrenches are used for round nuts and pins. So for instance for unscrewing pins a wrench is used shown in Fig. 24g. The hexagonal nut 2isscrewed on the protruding end of pin 1 and reliably locked by the screw 3, after which, the nut isturned together with the pin in reverse direction using an ordinary wrench.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The machines and looms manufactured by machine building works are supplied with a set of ordinary and special wrenches. For example, the ring spinning frame is provided with aset of 26 wrenches, eleven of which are ordinary ones, six box wrenches, and nine special wrenches.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drifts(Fig. 25a-d) are used for the disassembly of units in which parts are tightly fitting in the hole. Drifts are made as solid onepiece tools of soft steel or with a removable end-piece of copper, brass, lead, aluminium, etc. The shape of the endpiece is determined by the shape of the part to be knocked out. Steel drifts with hardened working surface are used for knocking out cylindrical and bevel pins, as well as sheared cotter pins.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Screwdrivers (Fig. 26a-d) are used for driving in and out wooden screws, as well as screws with heads of different shapes having slotsin diameter. Screwdrivers may be made of wire and have wooden or plastic handles. To facilitate the work screwdrivers of different shapes are available, for instance, brace screwdrivers or screwdrivers with inserted plates.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Strippers and presses are used to disassemble units consisting of parts with interference fit (pulleys, handwheels, gears, bushings, ball and roller bearings, couplings, cams, etc.)

elements.label: text
elements.text: Strippersare subdivided into mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic types. For the repair of machines wide use is made of mechanical strippers, but when a great effort is to be applied hydraulic strippers are more adequate. Pneumatic strippers have a complex design and find rare application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: General-purpose strippers are employed for lifting parts of different shape and sizes (Fig. 27), while special strippers are used for removing parts of the same type and dimensions.

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: If badly rusted parts and units are to be disassembled they are immersed for a 1-2 h into a bath with kerosene, after which they are disassembled using if necessary mallets (hammers) and other tools.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Broken pins may be extracted by different methods. If the point of breakage is not very deep, slot is cut with a groove chisel and the

Sometimes, a hole is drilled in the pin into which a square or toothed hardened steel rod (Fig. 29c) is inserted and to extract the pin. In the given case, use m a y also be made of a steel hardened rod (extractor) with five spiral grooves having an angle of spiral 30° on its conical surface. The extractor which is screwed into the hole drilled in the pin drives it out of the part body (Fig. 29d). If the broken end of the pin protrudes

elements.label: text
elements.text: above the surface of the part, the pin is removed by means of a special eccentric wrench (Fig. 29c).

elements.label: text
elements.text: In some cases when it is impossible to extract the pin from the part, it is drilled out after which the hole is threaded anew; drilling

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Cleaning and Washing of Paris

elements.label: text
elements.text: After they have been disassembled, the parts are cleaned and if required washed. Large-size parts (stands, frameworks) are cleaned

elements.label: text
elements.text: with hand and mechanized brushes or by blowing with compressed

elements.label: text
elements.text: air or by means of an industrial-type vacuum cleaner. The interior thread in these parts is cleaned with a brass wire bent as a loop with loose pointed ends.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cleaning of small parts by scrapers, hooks and rags is inefficient and of low quality. In this case, it is more expedient to use special cleaning devices and brushes with a diameter not over 250-300 m m

elements.label: text
elements.text: and having a pile 50-60 m m long operating at a speed of 35-40 m s-1. Steel and cast iron parts are cleaned by metal brushes of low carbon steel wire, while for brass parts— brushes of brass wire are to be used. Brushes of fibre cord or other synthetic materials are used for cleaning the parts from burrs and small rust as well as for eliminating dirt remained after washing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cleaning efficiency may be two or three times increased by using an electric polishing machine with an induction high-frequency

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: motor which is provided with a metal brush 1 (Fig. 30) instead of an abrasive wheel. This brush is powered from a transformer 4 through a contact ring 2 and copper-graphite brushes. The other pole is connected by the wire 5 from the transformer 4 through a clip to the work 6 to be cleaned. The brush 1 is rotated by the motor 3. The impurities on the surface of the part are destroyed by electric discharges as well as by the mechanical action of the brush which at the same time eliminates them from the surface. Washing and cleaning

First they are washed in kerosene or immersed in a soap solution (25 g of soap per liter of water) and further treated for several hours in a solution containing 45% of kerosene, 35% ofturpentineand 20% of ammonium hydroxide (industrial). Then the parts are washed with clean kerosene and wiped with cotton rags. Washing with hot aqueous solutions of alkalies is more convenient and cheaper.

Washing is carried out in baths of different designs or in conveyertype washing machines with three or four chambers, where the parts are washed in consecutive order with alkaline solutions and water and dried with hot air.
