elements.label: text
elements.text: Washing of small parts in mass production is carried out in tanks and tubs of different design using kerosene or other washing liquids.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 67

elements.label: text
elements.text: Lately ultrasonic cleaning of parts and units has acquired wide application. Its principle is described below. High-frequency oscillations are created in the washing liquid owing to which cavitation bubbles are created which exercise mechanical action on the contaminated surface. The impact waves intensively destroy the layers of lubricant and dirt covering the part surface. Simultaneously the impurities chemically interact with the washing solution which may be an aqueous alkaline solution, solutions of synthetic surface-active substances and organic solvents.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Inspection and Sorting of Parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: After they have been dismantled from themachine, cleaned, washed, degreased and dried, the parts are inspected and sorted. The parts are sorted in three groups: fitfor further use without repair, needing repair, and unserviceable. The first group includes parts which have retained their structural or repair dimensions or when the degree of their wear has not exceeded the allowable limits (there are no cracks and other defects and their outward appearance satisfies the specifications).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The second group is assigned to parts with modified structural or repair dimensions, having cracks and other defects but which may be repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Badly worn, broken, cracked parts which are very difficult to repair and not worth to be restored pertain to the third group.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Sorting of parts makes it possible to specify defects in the list which was established prior to the complete disassembly of the m a chine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The serviceable parts are collected in one place, the parts requiring restoring are sent to the shop and unserviceable parts are scrapped to the scrap yard where they are sorted by materials used for their manufacture. To replace the unserviceable parts, the repair team receives new ones from the store.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When inspecting and sorting parts, the latter are classified into three groups, i.e. movable important parts, stationary important parts and non-important ones. The parts pertaining to the third group are subjected to outward examination, while the parts of the first two groups are inspected for concealed defects, measured and

elements.label: text
elements.text: examined for outward appearance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sorting inspector must be thoroughly acquainted with the design of machines to be repaired, the conditions of their operation and the technological process of the repair to be carried out. Special instructions and albums of drawings are used for technical inspection of parts. Concealed defects (surface and interior cracks) are uncovered by means of magnetic ultrasonic and luminescent flaw detectors.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 68 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: Magnetic flaw detectors are used for the examination of steel and cast-iron parts. The part is sprayed with a finely dispersed metal powder in suspension in kerosene or transformer oil. When the part is magnetized by the flaw detector, the particles of the powder are disposed according to the power lines of the magnetic flow, while in case of a crack they run along it thus marking itsdisposition and shape.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Ultrasonic flaw detectors are based on the capacity of sonic waves with an oscillation frequency of 0.5-10 M H z and higher to propagate in a solid state in the shape of a thin slightly diverging jet. If there is a defect (crack or cavity) in the part it becomes an obstacle for the passage of the ultrasonic wave as the latter is partially reflected and partially dispersed. This testing method allows the detection of defects deeply located in the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Luminescent flaw detectors u s e t h e c a p a c i t y o f f l u o r e s c e n t s u b s t a n c e s to glow on their irradiation by ultraviolet rays. The part is immersed in bath with fluorescent liquid which penetrates in the finest cracks (if such are present). Further, the part surface is dried and sprayed with silica gel powder, and then irradiated in a chamber with ultraviolet rays. The fluorescent layer remaining in the crack starts glowing and marks out the point and shape of the crack.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The exterior concealed cracks may be determined by more simple methods. On washing and drying, the part is immersed for 10-15 min in a bath with clean kerosene, then taken out and wiped, and the point of the supposed crack is coated with chalk. If a crack is there, after a certain time a dark trace would appear on the coating due to the evaporation of kerosene from the crack. According to another method of testing, the cleaned part is subjected to etching by a heated 10-20% solution of sulphuric acid after which the surface of the part is examined with a magnifying glass.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4. Repair of Shafts

elements.label: text
elements.text: The shafts used in textile machines may be straight (the spinning frame main shaft) and shaped shafts (roving frame main shaft, loom crankshaft). The dimensions of the shaft may vary greatly, i.e.

elements.label: text
elements.text: from 20 to 250 m m and more in diameter and from 200 to 8000 m m and more long. The mass of some shafts may reach several tons.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The shafts of textile machines are made of different grades of steel: structural carbon steel of standard quality or high-quality structural carbon steel. The following typical defects may be observed in the course of operation: local and overall deflections, cracks, breakages, wear of running surfaces, crushing of keyways, deformation at places intended for fitting other parts, stretching and stripping of thread, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Bent shafts. Usually bent shafts are straightened in cold condi-

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: Surfaoe hardwork L_L_L_L_L_Ll

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 31. Straightening of bent shafts

elements.label: text
elements.text: tion. The main disadvantage of cold straightening is an unbalanced state of the shaft after straightening. However, cold straightening ensures a higher precision and ismuch easier than hot straightening. Cold straightening is carried out in a press equipped with centres or fulcrums as for instance in a hydraulic press.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If there is no hydraulic press available, straightening may be carried out on an old turning lathe using a screw jack 1 (Fig. 31<z) and hooks 2 or a special clamp (Fig. 316). The accuracy of cold straightening would in this case be 0.05-0.15 m m per running metre of shaft. Shafts which are slightly bent (0.03-0.05% of the shaft length) are dressed by surface cold work using a pneumatic hammer. Figure 31c shows impact load application for obtaining cold work hardening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shafts of greater diameter (over 50 mm) including shafts with a considerable deflection are straightened in hot condition (heated to 750-800°C) by means of a sledge hammer or an ordinary hammer. The accuracy of straightening is 0.5 m m for one running metre of the shaft. The surface of the shaft may be damaged in the course of hot straightening and moreover the cost of repairs in this case exceeds that of cold straightening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cracked and broken shafts. These are restored by welding and by inserting new parts mechanically or in combination with welding. Shafts with very deep cracks are made broken and repaired as broken shafts. The crack must be broken to the full depth so that it could be reached by electric arc, heated to full depth and rapidly welded u p * .

elements.label: text
elements.text: * Cracks are welded up rapidly so as not to make parts brittle.

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 32. Preparing shafts for welding

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 33. Repair of broken shafts by

elements.label: text
elements.text: and jigs for shaft welding

elements.label: text
elements.text: welding

elements.label: text
elements.text: The shaft ends to be butted are prepared for welding as follows (Fig. 32a, b).Prior to welding, marks are made on the shaft at equal distances from the point of breakage which is necessary for checking the shaft length. After cleaning the butts, the parts of the shaft to

elements.label: text
elements.text: be welded are set in place, centered and secured in jigs of adequate design depending on the shape of the shaft. Figure 32c shows the jig for welding straight shafts, while Figure 32d— for welding crankshafts. Figure 33a and bshows how the welding joint is strengthened.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Sometimes new parts (necks, journals, etc.) are welded to the broken shaft. For instance on the loom crankshaft with a crack on its neck, a new neck is welded (Fig. 33c) as welding of the old neck is impractical and reinforced weld seams cannot be applied. In case the crankshaft jaw is broken joining is made by inserting two pins into the butt, a band 2 is placed on the jaw 1 (Fig. 33d) in hot state

elements.label: text
elements.text: and welded. After welding, the shaft is checked for deflection and if necessary straightened. Bulges formed at the point of joining are removed on a lathe and if possible left in place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worn-out shafts. The following parts need repairs due to the wear of shafts: journals, surfaces for mounting pulleys, gears and other parts, keyways, threads, etc. The main kinds of repairs of a worn-out shaft are: building-up (hard facing) of the worn-out surface, metal coating or electroplating, placing a ring on the worn plate, or the use of repair sizes in shafts to be repaired. If the wear and crushing of separate shaft elements are very great, new elements are built-up by welding or by a mechanical process in combination with welding. The kind of repairs is a function of the extent of wear, the

elements.label: text
elements.text: conditions of shaft operation, the availability of repair facilities

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 71

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 34. Restoring broken shafts by

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 35. Repair of worn shafts by

elements.label: text
elements.text: building-up

elements.label: text
elements.text: •metal coating

elements.label: text
elements.text: and of the use of repair dimensions system, as well as economic considerations.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In repairing shafts by building-up their worn-out surfaces (journals and necks) must be prepared so that the metal overlay is of about the same thickness. The welding beads are placed in an increasing order (Fig. 34a)or as a spiral (Fig. 34b). This sequence is necessary to prevent shaft warping in building-up. Breaks in the building-up process

elements.label: text
elements.text: (for turning the part or cleaning the beads) serve to equalize the welding temperature conditions and to partially protect the part from warping.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The crushed or stripped thread is cut off by a cutter and built-up with a big allowance for further machining.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In centralized repairs of shafts, the building-up of worn-out places should be carried out automatically on special machines under a layer of flux (see Chapter 2).

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n the shafts are repaired by metal coating, their surface should be prepared to eliminate the distortions of its geometrical configuration and to increase the surface roughness. O n the surface of the shaft

elements.label: text
elements.text: to be metal-coated a rough thread is cut with a pitch of 0.8-1.2 m m and a depth of 0.5-0.8 m m . Then the surface is cleaned from oil stains and dirt by sand blasting. If the journal end is worn out the surface to be metal-plated must be stepped (Fig. 35a) to avoid the loss in journal strength and to retain the pulverized layer. To prevent the end surface from flaking and to strengthen it, safety beads are made by turning or welding (Fig. 35b, c)or also slots may be cut on the surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In metal coating shafts of intricate shape (crankshafts, shafts with shoulders, flanges, etc.), they are first coated with sprayed metal at places of sharp changes (cranks, ledges, etc.) and then the rest of the surface is sprayed with metal. Metal-coated shafts are machined on lathes as usual.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Chromium plating of shafts is carried out as follows: grinding and buffing of the surfaces to be chromium plated; insulating places which are not to be chromium plated, and screening sharp edges and relief points, sand papering; suspending parts from frames, electrolytic degreasing; washing in hot water; etching and chromium plating; washing in running cold water; neutralizing in an alkaline solution;

elements.label: text
elements.text: 72 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: rinsing in hot water; removing the parts from the frame; washing in hot water on nets; inspection; if necessary machining of the chromium-plated surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When preparing the shafts for ringing, the worn-out journal is turned to obtain a regular shape and the size necessary for appropriate fit. The minimum diameter of the turned place is determined by calculating the strength of the journal. The worn-out journals are fitted with solid rings (couplings) and composite rings are placed on the necks. W h e n necks and journals are passed into the group of parts with repair dimensions they may be restored by turning, or by turning with subsequent grinding, or by grinding only. In case of considerable distortion of the shape, untreated necks and journals are usually turned on a lathe and then ground. When the distortion is inconsiderable, grinding is sufficient. The allowance should be the same as for new shafts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 36. Centre shifters

elements.label: text
elements.text: The aim of machining is to impart the shafts definite shape and dimensions after welding, building-up, metal spraying, chromium plating and also to use the repair dimensions of the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n choosing conditions for the machining of built-up and metalcoated shafts, it should be taken into account that the hardness of layers is usually higher than that of the parent metal, the surface of coating is not smooth, etc. For this reason, it is necessary to use a lower cutting speed, depth, and a smaller feed as compared with those recommended for working the parent metal.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When turning the neck, the crankshafts are fixed in special devices— centre off-setting fixtures. The simplest centre shifter designed for one radius R (Fig. 36a) consists of two chuck plates 3 and 5 and counterweights 8 and 7. The shaft 4 is attached in the central holes, while the shifted holes are used for clamping the chucks in the centres of the headstock 1 and tailstock 6 of the turning lathe. The shaft 4 isrotated by the carrier stud 2at the rotation of the headstock spindle.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The universal centre shifter (Fig. 36b) consists of the chuck plate 1 with guiding plates 2 and movable slides 3. The chuck plate 1 is screwed on the end of the lathe spindle to the slides 3\ the chuck (not shown) fixed with three screws has prismatic jaws in which the shaft end is held. The slides with the chuck are displaced along the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 73

elements.label: text
elements.text: guiding plates 2 by the screw 5. The amount of shifting of the shaft axis is controlled by the vernier rule 4. To avoid strong vibrations impeding machining the crankshaft must be balanced by counterweights.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Straight shafts are ground in circular grinders with special grinding heads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shafts with worn-out necks may also be restored by applying a layer of polyamide polymer. In this case the working surfaces of the sliding friction bearings may be made not only of hard antifriction materials, but also of hardened steel. Such combinations of friction pairs are called opposite in difference from direct pairs when the working surface of the shaft is of steel and that of the bearing of antifriction material. The advantages of opposite pairs are an easier elimination of rubbing heat, smaller wear of rubbing surfaces and a higher strength of the plastic coating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 5. Repair of Bearings

elements.label: text
elements.text: The antifriction and sliding bearings used in textile machines are of most various designs, yet sliding friction bearings only are repaired in textile enterprises. The repair of antifriction bearings is carried out in special bearing repair plants as complicated special equipment is required for this kind of repair.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Sliding bearings m a y be classified into solid bearings (with or without bushes) and split bearings (with or without linings). M a n y machines have open bearings (e.g. for fluted rollers of spinning frames).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bearing shells are mainly made of cast iron, while the bushes and linings are made of antifriction cast iron, bronze, zinc and aluminium alloys, metal ceramics (cermet), hard plastics and laminated wood plastics. Also used are bimetallic linings and bushings; cast iron or steel linings and bushings lined with babbitt, bronze, zinc, aluminium and other antifriction alloys. Some bearings (for instance on the shaft of the drawing frame coiler) are cast as a whole with a bracket.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main drawback of sliding bearings is the wear of rubbing surfaces and sometimes their cracks and breakages. Depending on the type, dimensions, materials and kind of defects the bearings are repaired by different methods: metal coating, building-up, pouring with babbitt and bronze, pressing the repair bushings, replacing the worn part, and plastic compression.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Metal coating may be used for the repair of bearings of different designs with the exception of long bearers with deep holes of small diameter (for instance spindle tubes and bolsters). When preparing the surface of a bearing or bushing for metal coating, i.e. when eliminating their ovality or conicity by boring and cutting a rough thread, care should be taken that the walls of the workpiece are

elements.label: text
elements.text: 74 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: not excessively weakened. If the bearing is strongly worn-out, the rough thread is to be cut without preliminary boring.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Split liningsare prepared for metal coating proceeding as follows. Both halves of a bearing are connected by a clip or soldered together after which they are carefully checked (trued) and secured in a device on the lathe, bored, and rough threaded to a depth of 0.8 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The split bearings without linings are tightened with bolts and clamped in a four-cam chuck or on the carriage of a turning lathe. The non-split bearings are metal-coated in the same manner. Split linings and bearings are sometimes metal coated in disassembled state manually for obtaining a more uniform metal layer through the use of thickness gauges.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Metal-coated bearings are subjected to heat treatment in a reducing m e d i u m at 700-750°C for 2-3 h. This increases the strength of the part and moreover improves the antifriction property and the wearresistance of the part. After metal coating the bearings are bored and reamed and thesplitliningsare complementary scraped. The allow­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ance for machining must be 0.6-0.7 m m at each side.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building-up. If there isno metal coating plant at the enterprise the bearings and linings are repaired by building-up. Building-up ismade with the same materials from which the workpieces have been manufactured. However the antifriction properties of cast-iron linings and

elements.label: text
elements.text: bearings are considerably increased by building-up with bronze. The worn surface is prepared for building-up by boring. After the m e ­

elements.label: text
elements.text: chanical treatment, the layer of built-up metal must not be under 1 mm. It is recommended to make longitudinal grooves in dovetail shape on the bearings so that the built-up metal is more reliably retained on the surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building-up is done by electric arc or gas welding. Preliminarily the parts are slowly heated: cast-iron linings— to a temperature of 500°C, and bronze linings to 400°C. Building-up is carried out according to a thickness gauge which ensures a greater uniformity of the layer. The allowance for machining is 2-3 mm. After building-up the bronze linings are annealed at a temperature of 500-550°C, then cooled in water. The built-up linings are bored, reamed and scraped.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Lining of bearings. Sliding bearings lined with non-ferrous antifriction alloys: babbitt, bronze, zinc and aluminium alloys, polymer materials, etc. find wide application in textile machines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the lining of alloys is worn out itmust be removed, and a new lining made. When lining the bearers with babbitt the following operations are to be made: cleaning, degreasing, eliminating the worn layer of babbitt, tinning of bearings, shaping forms of bearings to pour the linings; melting and lining with babbitt; machi­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ning of bearings lined with babbitt.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn layer of babbitt is removed by heating with a soldering torch, melting-out in special electric furnaces, immersing the bearer

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 75

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 37. Device for babbitting Fig. 38. Machine for centrifugal lining linings of bearings

elements.label: text
elements.text: in a crucible with molten babbitt or knocking it out by means of a chisel. The best method for eliminating the worn-out layer of bab­

elements.label: text
elements.text: bitt is its melting-out in electric furnaces.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In order to obtain a good joint between the babbitt and the lining, the surface of the lining is covered with a thin layer of tin. Tlhis process is called tinning. The layer of solder or tin ensures a ceose joining of the babbitt with the lining owing to the mutual penetration of metal into the other. A mixture of lead, tin and sodium thloride is used as a solder. Sometimes leading is superceded by inning. In this case pure lead is used as a solder. The bearings and linings of gray cast iron are not tinned, but may be copper-plated.i

elements.label: text
elements.text: After tinning, the linings are formed in special devices (Fag. 37). Both halves of the linings 2 are tightened with a screw sheckle 3 and an asbestos or untinned iron gasket is placed between thr faces of the joint, so that it reaches the rod 1 and prevents the solde ing of the two halves together. The form is mounted on the pan 4retaining in place the babbitt at pouring. The rod 1 (or core) made of a pipe, sheet material, or dry tight wood is placed strictly in the centre. The rod should be slightly slanted for better convenience of driving it out. The diameter of the rod is chosen to suit the thickness of the poured layer, the allowance for machining is 1-1.5 m m , and the shrinkage of babbitt 0.7-0.5%.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Prior to babbitting, the device is heated with a soldering lamp to a temperature of 150-200°C and the lining to 250-270°C.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Babbitt is melted in deep cast iron or steel melting pots heated in an electric furnace, by means of a soldering lamp or in a forge. Pouring should be done quickly and without interruptions, otherwise the babbitt may peal off. The poured linings are taken out from the device only when the babbitt gets completely hardened.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Pouring may be also carried out by the centrifugal method using a special device (Fig. 38) which may be manufactured using an old

elements.label: text
elements.text: 76 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: lathe. Tinned, tightened and preliminarily heated linings 3 are fixed

elements.label: text
elements.text: in the clamping device 2 and closed with the housing 1;then the lathe drive is switched on. Pouring is done after the rotational speed has been accelerated to the preset value. The centrifugal method of lining is more efficacious and ensures a better quality of lining. The molten metal introduced into the hollow hot rotating cylinder (lining) is rejected by centrifugal forcesto the cylinder walls to which it adheres fastly. The babbitted linings are bored and scraped atthe assembly.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Both new and repaired bearings are lined with bronze owing to which they are imparted higher strength and wear resistance. For this reason, bronze is used for lining heavily loaded bearings. Lining with bronze may be done both manually and by the centrifugal method. Lining with a zinc alloy is usually made on the untinned surface of bearings, while lining with aluminium alloy may be done only when the layer is mechanically attached to the surface of the lined bearing. For this reason it is necessary to provide circular grooves or to cut a thread on the surface of the bearing. Lining may also be made of polymer materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair by mechanical methods and presswork (plastic deformation). Worn-out bearings, linings and bushings are repaired depending on their design either by mechanical methods (by placing inner rings, inserts, and patches) or by presswork (plastic deformation). Heavily worn-out solid bearings are repaired by pressure, placing repair rings

elements.label: text
elements.text: (bushings) of antifriction material (cast iron, bronze, aluminium and zinc alloys, fabric-base laminates and other plastic materials).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The exterior diameters of the repaired rings depend on the chosen fit and class of accuracy, while the internal diameter ofthe ring (bushing) corresponds to the dimension of the new part or to the next repair dimension. At pressure fitting of rings (bushings) their interior diameter and shape are reduced and for this reason when choosing the interior diameter of the ring it is necessary to take into account the allowance for the final machining in assembly (reaming). Multipillow blocks are subjected to reaming in an assembled and installed state. Sizing may be also done with a ball or punch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Splitted and open bearings without linings are repaired by installing repair semi-rings. In this case the worn-out pillow block is bored and semi-rings or linings of antifriction material are secured on dowels or with glue.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Bearings and bushings of complicated design and cast as a whole with flanges and brackets are also used in different machines (the bushing of the side wall of the card taker-in, the bearing of the roving frame shaft, and others). When repairing such pillow blocks the worn-out part is cut off and a new one is put in its place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing bearings with pressure fitted bronze bushings and split linings use is made of different methods of plastic deformation, i.e. heading, reducing and straightening for reducing the dia-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 77

elements.label: text
elements.text: meter of the interior worn-ont surface of the part.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Heading of worn-out bushings, pressure-fitted in the bearing proceeds from the butt ends around the shaft at a high pressure; as a result, the diameter of the inner surface of the bushing is reduced. If the bushing has an oval hole it is reamed prior to heading. (a) Figure 39a illustrates a device for heading worn-out bushings. It consists of the steel hardened

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 39. Diagrams of devices (a) for heading; (b) for reducing worn bush­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ings die 7, counter-die 5, plunger 4 and support 6. The bushing 2 to be headed and the parts 3 in which this bushing is fitted are attached in the said device. Heading is carried out in a press.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Reducingis used to decrease the worn-out hole in bronze bushings which are not pressure fitted in the bearings. The bushing 1 (Fig. 396) is inserted into a steel hardened die 2 and a punch is run through it in the press. The die 2 has a gradually decreasing hole to obtain a progressive reduction of the bushing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: , If the bushing has ledges (as spindle bushes in linen roving frames) the reduction is carried out by means of rollers. After the reduction, the bushing is reamed. The outside diameter of the bushing after reduction decreases and it must be built-up by metal plating, copper

elements.label: text
elements.text: plating or by any other means after which it is machined in an arbor.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Split bronze linings with walls of inconsiderable thickness and subjected to strong wear are repaired by straightening. Both halves

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the lining tightened with shackles are compressed in a screw press after which the halves are taken apart, the points of butt joints are planed or milled, and chamfered at an angle of 45° for soldering. This done, the halves are again tightened together and the precision of assembly is checked to avoid misalignment after which the linings are soldered along the chamfers. The exterior surfaces of the pillow block fillets (girths) and the inner surfaces of shoulders are metalplated or built-up with brass or bronze, taking into account the allowance for subsequent machining. After coating the shackles are removed and the lining is machined on a lathe. The inner diameter is bored and the outer built-up surface is turned to the required size, while the inner surfaces of the shoulders are cut. All other surfaces

elements.label: text
elements.text: are dressed. Finally, the lining is taken apart (unsoldered), the inner edges are filed and the both halves are scraped on the place of straightening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 78 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing sliding bearings they must be subjected to boring. With this aim, special devices are provided in textile enterprises. Figure 40 illustrates a fixture for boring the bearings of preparation machines and spinning frames in flax mills. The fixture consists of the body 4with two movable jaws 2and 7 arranged in guiding slots with a dovetail shape. These jaws may be brought together or set apart by a screw 3 with a left- and right-hand thread. This fixture is attached on a lathe. A boring bar 1 with the cutter 6 is fixed in the centres of the lathe; and the bearing 5 to be centrally bored is placed between the jaws 2 and 7. The boring bar is imparted rotation and the fixture carrying the bearing is moved in longitudinal direction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 6. Repair of Gears and Pulleys

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gears used in textile machines may be of most different kinds: spur and helical gears, cylindrical, bevel and combined gears, worm gears, and special gears with external and internal toothing; solid and split gears with different angles of meshing (for machines of Soviet and foreign makes); with various modules (from 1 to 15 and higher) and with different number of teeth (from 5 to 250); made separately or as a whole with other parts; manufactured as single gears

elements.label: text
elements.text: or a train of two, three and more spur cylindrical gears.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gears may be of cast iron, steel, bronze, fibre-based laminates, capron, leather, etc. They operate at different speeds (from 0.2 to 30 m/min) and transmit different powers. The accuracy of gear manufacture is from coarsely machined to polished ones. The number of gears and toothed quadrants and racks exceeds 100. In the course of operation different kinds of damages occur: wear and breakage of teeth, cracks in the rims and spokes, crushing of butt faces, hubs, walls of key grooves and holes, deterioration of thread in stopping holes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Faulty gears are replaced in couples by new ones at the repairs. If there are no reserve gears available or in urgent cases, the gears should be repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gears with worn-out and broken teeth are repaired by building-up, fitting of tyres or toothed sections and by using cap-screws; and in some cases the gear is turned to the other side to make use of good teeth.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 79

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 41. Kinds of gear building-up

elements.label: text
elements.text: The toothed surface is repaired by overall circular building-up (Fig. 41a), building-up of separate damaged teeth (Fig. 41&-e), and building-up with the formation of tooth contour (Fig. 41f-h).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Overall circular building-up as well as building-up of separate teeth are used to repair gears having fine pitch, while welding with formation of teeth contour is employed for repairing gears with a big pitch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Building-up ismade by electric arc and gas welding with preheating (hot building-up) or without it (cold building-up). Hot building-up is usually used for the repair of big gears. If the broken or worn-out teeth are disposed in different places of the gear circumference, building-up should be carried out successively in diametrically opposite places to avoid warping and cracking. Cold building up is employed at the repair of cast-iron gears with small pitch and diameter and especially for the repair of toothed quadrants.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n repairing gears with a sufficiently strong rim, several steel pins (cap-screws) with a diameter inferior to the thickness of the tooth are screwed-in in place of the removed tooth.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After building-up, the gears are subjected to mechanical treatment. The gears whose teeth have not been formed in the process of building-up are machined as follows: the butts are cut to suit the width of the gear; they are machined on a lathe to the exterior diameter; the teeth are milled and ground. Gears with teeth formed by building-up are manually worked to the marking out. In this case, it is recommended to grind off the preliminarily built-up metal with a grinding wheel and then to proceed to milling.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For fitting segments of gears and tyres, worn-out or crumbled teeth are removed and replaced by new ones. Segments of gears are used

elements.label: text
elements.text: 80 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 42. Securing segment gears on threads

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 43. Welding-in of segment gear

elements.label: text
elements.text: when there are several (2-4) adjacent damaged teeth; individual teeth are used if there is one or several damaged teeth disposed in different places; toothed tyres are employed in case of wear or breakage of the greatest part of teeth.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worn or broken teeth are removed on a planing or milling machine, after which the place forthe new segment gear or tooth is planed or milled and the segment gear or tooth is secured by screws or welding (Fig. 42a-d).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Welding of segment gears is less labour consuming and ensures better results. The part of the rim with faulty teeth is cut out from the gear to be repaired and in its place a good segment gear (Fig. 43a) is welded-in with the aid of a cast aluminium template (Fig. 436). After welding is completed, using a vernier caliper and an indicator

elements.label: text
elements.text: checking is carried out to verify the pitch between the extreme teeth of the segment gear and the teeth of the gear, the parallelism of the segment teeth and the basic teeth, the outside, base and pitch diameters of the gear. This done, the repaired toothed wheels are run-in

elements.label: text
elements.text: at the place of installation of the segment gear with the master or mating gear which is brought in reverse motion either on a special device or manually. This is done to make the profile of the segment teeth correspond to the profile of the basic teeth of the gear and to avoid gear vibration and non-uniform wear of the mating gear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Tyre fitting is used for the repair of gears made as one whole with other parts (intricate bushings, sleeves, gears, etc.). The tyres may

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 81

elements.label: text
elements.text: be made of steel, bronze, or cast iron. The shape and dimensions of the tyres depend on the design of the gear to be repaired and on the method of its joining with the tyre (by fit, splines, rivets, and bolts).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The tyre may also be filled with molten metal or polyamide. In order to obtain a joint of greater strength between the tyre and the base, an annular groove is made and several holes are drilled along the circumference. After fitting or pouring, the tyre is subjected to finishing and the teeth are cut. W h e n repairing the worn-out gears in flax roving frames, the teeth are cut off and in their place a steel ring or tyre is pressure-fitted by the hot method. Further the tyre is turned and milled. Cast-iron tyres are also pressure-fitted at the repair of roving frame differential gears, drawing frame gears, etc. In duplex tooth gear cast as a whole, the smaller gear wears quicker. At repairs the worn-out gear isremoved by turning and a new one isinstalled in itsplace being secured with a spline or a stock screw. In case of teeth wear on bevel and worm gears (as for example the roving frame bevel gears or the opener worm gear) the teeth are cut-off by turning and in their place a toothed tyre is bolted or riveted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 44. Diagram of device for shaping

elements.label: text
elements.text: inner teeth on horizontal shaper

elements.label: text
elements.text: The teeth of cylindrical gears, when repaired, are usually cut on milling or gear-hobbing machines (if there are no gear shapers and planers available).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The built-up or inserted teeth should be worked so that their pitch, profile and dimensions do not differ from those of undamaged teeth. If this is not the case, the meshing of the repaired gear will be irregular and cause impacts and rapid wear of the mating gear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Bevel gears are cut in special machines, such as gear planers, or all-purpose milling machines (with lower precision).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Many machines use gears with interior toothing (such are the rim of the differential gear in a roving frame, the plate gear of the planetary warp stop-motion of an automatic loom, etc.). For the repair of such gears special gear-shapers or other devices are necessary, e.g.

elements.label: text
elements.text: for cutting the interior teeth of the differential gear rim in a roving frame (Fig. 44). The rigid cast angle 7 with a wide slot in its upper part is attached on the table of a gear shaping machine. The rim 4 to be shaped issecured in the master gear 6by the plate the bolt 5 and the pin 8. The master gear 6rests on the block 9 and is fixed in required position by two locks 2 pressed by the springs 1. The cutter

elements.label: text
elements.text: 82 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: which is shaped to fit the tooth space is secured with its cutting head turned upwards in a special arbor. After one tooth has been shaped, the locks 2 are retreated, the master gear is turned through one tooth and fixed in this position. All the teeth are shaped in the same way.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gears with teeth worn-out from one side may he used without repair. For this, they are turned about 180° and made to operate with the unworn side. Gears which operate’without rotation, i.e. only part of the teeth is subject to wear, may be used for further operation by turning them on the shaft to make use of the good teeth. For instance, the worm gear of the building mechanism in spinning frames operates with only several teeth. When the latter are worn out the gear is turned through a certain angle and a new keyway is cut in the hub. Thus, the useful life of gears is increased several times.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Sometimes if cracked or broken rims of gears, pulleys, and flywheels cannot be replaced by new ones, the worn out parts are repaired by welding the cracks and welding-in the crumbled part of the wheel rim. To eliminate stresses appearing in welding, the part must be slowly cooled. It is also possible to weld cover plates on the inner side of the cracked or broken rim or cover plates and moreover screw couplings may he used for repair (combined method).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The best method for repairing the cracks appearing on one or several spokes is by hot or cold welding. In some emergency cases one or two cracked spokes (disposed at different places) may temporarily be tightened together with a clip. For better reliability the cracked spoke must be welded after which a clip is put on. Crushed keyways are filed up or new keyways are cut at some other place and the crushed ends are built-up or cut.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 7. Assembly of Equipment

elements.label: text
elements.text: The proper operation of equipment depends on its correct assembly. The parts must be received for assembly only after their checking in the technical control department. Prior to the assembly♦ the parts are cleaned from dust and their working surfaces should be in proper condition and without defects (impressions, scratches, indentations, etc.). The assembled equipment as well as its units

elements.label: text
elements.text: and mechanisms should have clean rubbing, contacting and interior surfaces without chips, scale and dirt. After final assembly, no drilling of holes, thread cutting, etc. should be done in the mechanisms to avoid chips getting on the rubbing surfaces. All butt joints of parts (covers, pipe unions, etc.) that are fixed to the body and containers must be tight so as to avoid leakages. Good sealing of the joints should be checked at testing of the assembled machine. No minium or white paint should be used to ensure a good sealing in pipe connections with nipples and other design packings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 83

elements.label: text
elements.text: To avoid residual deformation at the assembly of steel parts no heating above 300°G is allowed for the enveloping part. Heat-treated parts may be heated during assembly at a temperature not exceeding the tempering temperature. Centre punching and knurling with a roller for restoring the part dimensions are not allowed. Filing of cylindrical surfaces for mating is also forbidden. Rapidly rotating parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: should be balanced to avoid causing vibrations. The disbalance should be within permissible tolerances.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Prior to their installation in place, ball and roller bearings must be cleaned from oil and dirt, washed in an anticorrosion solvent and dried. The level of liquid lubricant must be at the axis of balls in their lowest position. The grease should fill not more than two thirds of the free space in the frame cavity at low and medium rotational speed of bearings and not over 1/3-1/2 at high rotational speed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of assembly, use is made of presses and erection tubes to ensure the proper fitting of rings without misalignment and to

elements.label: text
elements.text: avoid scoring of the setting surface. It is forbidden to hit directly the bearing with a hammer. At the time of erection of solid bearings in the frame and on the shaft simultaneously the pressing effort should be applied to the ring with an interference fit. The adjustment of the bearings must exclude the jamming of balls or rollers. Special attention should be paid to the adjustment of radial thrust bearings and horizontal thrust ball bearings where excessively big or small clear­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ances are inadmissible.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Felt packing rings must be impregnated with oil at a temperature of 80-90°C. Labyrinth packings must be filled with grease. In sliding bearings poured with babbitt, bronze, zinc- or aluminium-base alloys, the non-ferrous alloy must be reliably connected with the bearing which is achieved by mechanical fixing or by an adequate preparation of the surface for pouring. The reliable connection at pouring is checked by knocking.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Scraping must ensure an adherence of contact surfaces at which there will be at least five stains per cm2. The cam and toothed couplings must be mounted so as to ensure a full meshing on their engagement. The clearance between the apex of the tooth on one gear

elements.label: text
elements.text: and the tooth space on the other in radial direction should be equal to 0.25 of the pitch in cylindrical gears and to 0.2 pitch in conical gears. The accuracy ofskew gears cuttingmust be additionally checked prior to the assembly. The smaller gear is fitted with a clearance on the shaft and is run around the greater gear. After the smaller gear has made a full revolution around the greater gear its axial position in respect to the greater gear is the same as before. The gears must run smoothly without jamming.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transmission including the reducers must be run idle with oil filling. During running the noise must be regular without attenuation and increase; the packings and butt joints should not allow.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 84 Chapter Four

elements.label: text
elements.text: oil leakage and the temperature of the oil in the frame should not exceed the ambient temperature more than by 40°C, while the temperatute of the frame should not exceed the ambient temperature

elements.label: text
elements.text: by more than 30°C. Oil for running-in must be of the same brand and viscosity as the oil during operation, but with an addition of 5% of sulphofreesol. All the defects detected at running-in should be eliminated.
