elements.label: text
elements.text: CHAPTER 5

elements.label: text
elements.text: REPAIR AND ADJUSTMENT OF THE EQUIPMENT

elements.label: text
elements.text: IN THE SPINNING DEPARTMENT

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Blowing Range

elements.label: text
elements.text: The blowing range consists of several blending feeders, the waste and head feeders, the feeding lattice, the horizontal and vertical openers, the high-speed condenser, the rake distributor and of several single-process scutchers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To prepare the machines of the blowing ranges for repairs they are cleaned from waste and rests of raw materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Blending feeder. At the time of medium repairs the following operations are carried out in the following units:

elements.label: text
elements.text: feeding lattice— checking and replacing faulty balls, rollers, plates and belts;

elements.label: text
elements.text: spiked lattice— checking and replacing faulty bearings and plates, straightening and filing spikes, checking belts and the lattice;

elements.label: text
elements.text: evening lattice— checking and replacing the evening and side rollers, and of the lattice proper;

elements.label: text
elements.text: knock-off roller— checking and replacing faulty bearings, dressing of blades, cleaning of burrs, adjustment or replacement of the leather, checking the grid bars and setting the reach;

elements.label: text
elements.text: transmissions— checking and replacing faulty pulleys, tension pulleys (block wheels), shafts and bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: fan and lattice— checking and oiling the bearing, checking the drive, replacing faulty parts, checking and repairing the delivery lattice;

elements.label: text
elements.text: bracket with block wheels and the shaft of the riser— checking grid bars and grinding burrs, installation of grid bars according to the template, checking, cleaning and greasing of antifriction bearings, checking the lifting mechanism of the vertical shaft and replacing its faulty parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In addition to the aforementioned operations, the following jobs are done in overhaul repairs: checking and replacing faulty bearings of the feeding lattice, and if necessary replacing the lattice proper; checking the cylinders of the feeding mechanism and deburring of cylinders and journals; checking and replacing faulty bearings of the blade cylinder; checking the blades of the cylinder and grinding

elements.label: text
elements.text: 86 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: the burrs, removing grid bars and deburring; checking the doffing knives and deburring, setting the reaches according to a template; dismantling and checking the regulator, cleaning the pedals with graphite, adjusting and checking the bevel drums for easy rotation and checking and replacing faulty bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Single process scutcher. The following work is carried-out in the following units in the course of intermediate repairs:

elements.label: text
elements.text: feedingmechanism— checking and repairing the feeding lattice and the rollers, checking and repairing the feeding and pedal cylinders, deburring;

elements.label: text
elements.text: beater— opening the beater and disassembling the grid bars; elimination of burrs on the beater blades and grid bars; assembling the grid bars and setting the reaches of the beater and grid bars according to the template; repairing the mechanism for automatic locking; checking the beater bearings and replacing the grease.

elements.label: text
elements.text: pedal regulator— dismantling and checking the regulator, cleaning the knife-edge and pedals with graphite, adjustment of the belt shifter, checking for the easy rotation of bevel drums and replacement of

elements.label: text
elements.text: worn-out bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: cagesand gridbars— checking the cages and bearings, checking the fan bearings, the delivery roller and deburring, replacement of wornout leather packings, removal of grid bars from the waste box and

elements.label: text
elements.text: deburring;

elements.label: text
elements.text: front part of the cutter— disassembling and checking the calender rollers, the cut-off mechanism and lap winding mechanism; deburring the shafts and cleaning the bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: drive— checking and repairing of faulty parts in the drive and their replacement with new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At capital repairs in addition to the aforementioned operations the following work is carried-out: removing and checking the bottom cages; replacing collars; disassembling the grid bars in the waste chambers, their straightening and cleaning; replacing and repairing evening and knock-off rollers; checking and repairing the transmissions and levers of treadle regulators; complete disassembly and repair of the knocking-off mechanism and transmission to the pedal cylinder; checking and repairing the bottom main shaft; removing, checkingand balancingtheknock-offroller in the reserve chamber, and checking the frames with a cord and a level.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the disassembly, sorting, and repairs of parts, assembly and adjustment of the blowing range the admissible deviations and wear of working parts established at repairs are to be strictly followed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cage and fan. The main disarrangements in cages are: the opening of the longitudinal joint, the detachment of the cage from the rims, cage breakage in one or several points, the wear of tyres due to rubbing against other machine parts, and cracks in different points of the rims.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 87

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gages with open longitudinal joints are repaired by resoldering or stitching with wire. Lately different kinds of mechanical jointing have been used by means of the net 1

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig.45), the rings 2 and dowels 3,

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 45. Mechanical methods of fastening

elements.label: text
elements.text: net on cage

elements.label: text
elements.text: A completely worn-out net is replaced by a new one: the net is fastened onto the rims by means of clips and soldered or mechanically attached in place. Figure 46 illustrates a machine for mechanical covering the cage with a net. The machine stand 5carries two clamping cylinders 3, the axle 4 with a strap for making clips, a manual gear drive 2 and the pressure carriage 1 displaced

elements.label: text
elements.text: along the stand.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Patches are placed in separate points of the worn-out or broken net which are further interlaced and soldered.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For better convenience in disassembly and removal, the cages have a dismountable shaft. In single-process scutchers TO-18 first the cage bearings are inserted from the interior side of the frame, after which the cage and shaft are mounted onto them. The faulty rims of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 46* Machine for covering cage with net

elements.label: text
elements.text: 88 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 47. Reinforcement of fan blades Fig. 48. Methods of attaching fillet in single-process scutcher on rollers of blowing range

elements.label: text
elements.text: the cage are repaired in the similar way as the belt drive pulleys.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For reducing the contamination of the net with fluff, trash and dust it is coated from inside and outside with spirit varnish so that the cage surface becomes smooth and there is no accumulation of fluff

elements.label: text
elements.text: and dirt. Owing to this, the machine idle time is reduced and the quality of laps is improved.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main disarrangement in the fan is the breakage of blades when they get loose from the shaft. The repair consists in welding the blades. To ensure a stronger fixing of fan blades, holes are drilled at their ends 1 (Fig. 47) after which the blades are tightened together by bolting with steel plates 2 (the mass of the plates must be the same). After the repairs, the fan rotor is balanced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rollers and beaters. In blowing scutchers, blade, doffer, cleaning, evening, and spiked rollers are used as well as blade and needle beaters. They are removed from the scutcher and mounted on it by means of a special crane-truck with a hoisting capacity up to 4 kN.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bladerollergets out of order as a result of the deformation and the detachment of separate blades. At repairs the faulty blades are straightened according to the template and loose blades are riveted. Next, the screw space between the blades is checked and the roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: is balanced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The dofferrollerconsists of a steel shaft on which six steel rimmed sections are mounted. Between the rims leather blades are clamped which are liable to crack in service.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the repair of doffers, the faulty blades are replaced with new ones made of rubberized belting. The leather or rubberized belt 1 (Fig. 48a) used for making blades must easily bend, but at the same time must be very rigid. Excessively soft blades will bend very qui-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 89 *

elements.label: text
elements.text: ckly and will fail to reach the teeth of the spiked lattice, and on the contrary excessively rigid blades will knock against the teeth causing the slackening of the plate on the lattice. In the blade, V-shaped

elements.label: text
elements.text: slots are cut out with a pitch corresponding to the pitch of the teeth

elements.label: text
elements.text: on the spiked lattice or on the opening roller. This is made to ensure a better removal of fibre from the teeth of the spiked lattice.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cleaning rollersare repaired in the same way as doffer rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The evening rolleris made of a steel shaft carrying three disks towhich sixsteel blades with thick riveted-over needles are attached. In the course of the work the needles become loose and bent. At the time of repair, the faulty needles are cut-off and new needles 24 (Fig. 486) are fixed in place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The spiked rolleris m a d e of a steel pipe with flanges. The cylindrical part of the pipe has four rows of beveled spikes (the angle of inclination is 10°). W h e n the spikes are deteriorated they are cut away, the point of cut is dressed and new spikes 3 (Fig. 48c) are arc-welded. The point of welding is filed or sand-papered.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The automatic bale feeder has seven spiked rollers. Each spiked roller has a shaft which carries disks and plates with spikes 4 (Fig. 48d) attached to these disks. Deteriorated spikes are replaced by new

elements.label: text
elements.text: ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing rollers of all kinds care should be taken that all spikes or needles are of the same height and the rollers have the same exterior diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The blade beater is a shaft with cross-pieces carrying steel trapezoidal plates. These plates have a reserve edge so that at blunting (wear) of the working edge the plate may be turned round and the reserve edge is used as a working one. After both edges have been used, the plate is removed and machined on a planer (the angle of edge inclination is 75°). The edge should be well defined but not sharp and its plane must pass through the centre line of the beater shaft.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The restored blade 3 (Fig. 49) is attached on the spider 4 by means of a bevel screw 1 and locked with a dowel 2. The point of fixing to the spokes is carefully finished.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After the repair or replacement of blades, the beater is subjected to balancing. If in this case, the blade must be made heavier, then building-up may be carried-out from the interior side of the blade. The width of the weld must be narrower than that of the blade back plane and must have an oval surface. If at balancing of a three-blade beater it appears that one blade is heavier than the other, it must be planed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Modern scutchers are provided with saw-toothed or needle threeblade beaters, as smooth blade beaters do not ensure efficacious cleaning and separation of staples. The main deteriorations of saw-toothed and needles beaters observed in practice are due to the bending and

elements.label: text
elements.text: *90 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1 To expand

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 149. Method Tof fixing blade Fig. 50. Methods of fixing needles (a) and on^spider of three-blade beater saw-toothed fillet (5) in the beater lags

elements.label: text
elements.text: breakage of teeth or needles. At the repair,the needle or saw-toothed lags are removed from the beater. If the needle or toothed covering is deteriorated by 25-30%, the lags are replaced by new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The methods of fixing the needles and saw-toothed ribbon to the beater lags are shown in Fig. 50. At repairs, care should be taken that the wooden lags to which the needles are attached have no excessively high moisture content, no cracks and other defects. The needles must be set at the same angle and should protrude from the wooden lag at the same height. The points of the needles should be in the .same plane which is eccentrically disposed relative to the center line

elements.label: text
elements.text: •ofthe beater (the front edge should be three or four millimetres closer to the axis than the rear one); the needle surface should be parallel

elements.label: text
elements.text: to the axis of rotation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the replacement, the blades are chosen of suitable mass to avoid •disbalance of the beater. Repaired beaters are balanced together with the attached fillet (a dynamical balancing is necessary).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Grid bars. During the operation of the grid bar (in conjunction with the doffing and blade rollers, and beaters), the grid bars are liable to deformation, their surface becomes clogged with fibre and

elements.label: text
elements.text: burrs appear on it.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the reparation of the machines and prior to their installation, the grid bars are carefully cleaned and bent bars are straightened, indentations and burrs are eliminated and they are polished. Straight-

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing of grid bars in horizontal and vertical directions (along the faces) is made in a screw press. First, the indentations and burrs are eliminated by a rapidly rotating grinding wheel and next polished using

elements.label: text
elements.text: a feltwheel impregnated with polishing paste. The working faces of the grid bars are set parallel to the beater with a deviation not in ♦excess of 0.5 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 91

elements.label: text
elements.text: If pivotable grid bars are used, itisnecessary to check that they should easily and simultaneously turn, the maximum angle being

elements.label: text
elements.text: 30°. For inclined grid bars it is necessary to additionally check the good condition of the bottom cover and its tight fitting.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Pedal evener motion or pedal regulator. It consists of a feeding cylinder, pedals resting on a prism or roller, pedal pendants, links

elements.label: text
elements.text: and cone drums.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During operation the feeding cylinder may be deformed and its journals and bearings may be worn. The feeding cylinder is straightened so that it is strictly rectilinear and has a constant diameter throughout the full length. The journals are restored by chromium

elements.label: text
elements.text: plating or ground for obtaining the repair dimensions. Worn bearings are replaced by new ones. The journals and bearings are adjusted to avoid swinging in radial and axial directions, but so that the feeding cylinder may easily rotate in the bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation, small cracks and pits appear on the pedals and if their number is more than three or their diameter exceeds 3-4 mm, the pedal isreplaced by a new one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Considering that the fibre passes over the surface of the pedals, high requirements are set towards their quality. Small pits are soldered with tin and carefully smoothened. The surface profile of the pedals is worked strictly to the template. Wear of pedals should not exceed 1 mm, otherwise they should be replaced by new ones (the whole set should be replaced at once). The side surfaces of the pedals should have no ledges and cavities are soldered with tin. The total width of pedals should be 2 m m less than the machine width. It is necessary to keep under observation the uniform and tight adherence of the pedals to the cylinders (the clearance should not exceed 0.2- 0.4 mm). The maximum stroke of the pedals (their lowering) in respect to the feeding cylinder should not be under 12 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The pedals rest on a prism which must be strictly rectilinear and should have no surface indentations and other defects. The bent prism is dressed and, if damaged, soldered with tin. Prior to its installation the prism is carefully checked by the template (Fig. 51), cleaned and wiped with graphite. The template consists of a metal plate 2 with a shackle 4 and foot 5. The templates are attached on the feeding cylinders 3 using the plumb bob 1. If the depression on the foot accurately rests on the prism 6it means that the latter is set properly.

elements.label: text
elements.text: All the system of pedal pendants, links and levers is checked for proper mating and mobility of joints. If the joints are worn more than 0.3 mm, the parts should be replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bevel drums shafts m a y be bent in operation. They are straightened on a press machine or by means of a crank. A level is used for the installation of rollers. The drums are balanced so that they can be out of true not more than 0.2 m m .

elements.label: text
elements.text: 92 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly and adjustment of the blowing range. At the assembly of the blending feeders and head feeders, all spiked and transport lattices must be disposed symmetrically relative to the machine centre line and should not catch its side walls. The same concerns the roller, beaters, calender and lapping rollers and cages. Sagging of the lattice and falling-out of the fibre are not allowed. The blades must be reliably fixed to the belts. The evening roller is installed according to a level and the roller teeth must be in the middle of the space between the spikes of the lattice. The leather covering the cleaning and doffing rollers should not catch the lattice spikes. The blade roller must

elements.label: text
elements.text: be set strictly horizontally (according to a level) and must be properly balanced. Deteriorated (bent) grid bars are not to be put in place and only polished grid bars may be installed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 51. Template for installation of pedal prism in single-process scutcher

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly of horizontal (porcupine) and vertical openers using a level, rule and feeler it is necessary to see that the stand is strictly horizontal. The surface of parts coming in contact with the fibremust be carefully cleaned with sandpaper, polished with chalk and wiped with graphite. Special attention should be paid to the checking of reliability of fixtures and to the proper disposition of the working face of blades. The blade roller is set strictly horizontal with a level and balance (the roller must be easily rotated by hand). There must be no airsuction between the wall of the stand and the face of the cage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly of a single-process scutcher using a lever, rule and feeler the stand is checked for horizontality. The blade rollers, heaters, calender and lapping rollers as well as cages are installed symmetrically in respect to the centre line of the scutcher so that they do not catch its side wall. All the surfaces of parts coming in contact with the fibre, are cleaned with an abrasive paper, and wiped with chalk and graphite. At time of adjusting of the blowing range it is necessary to adhere to the allowable deviations or wear of working parts established in the course of repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 93

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Cards

elements.label: text
elements.text: The production of modern cards manufactured in the USSR is 10-40 kg/h. The card consists of the feeding arrangement, the main cylinder and doffer, the flats, the doffing comb, the transmissions and the coiler. Prior to putting the cards in repairs, the wastes are eliminated,

elements.label: text
elements.text: the card is dedusted and cleaned. At the time of intermediate repairs of cards the following work is performed in the following units:

elements.label: text
elements.text: thefeedingarrangements— the back part of the card is disassembled, the taker-in cylinder is removed, the saw-toothed band is repaired and deburred. The taker-in bearings are dismantled and they are checked for good condition. The flanges are deburred and fastenings

elements.label: text
elements.text: are checked, the grid bars are removed and restored, and the burrs on the receiving table are ground. The bearings and journals of the feeding cylinder are checked and deburred, the mote knives are exa­

elements.label: text
elements.text: mined, and it is ascertained that the taker-in and lattices are in proper condition;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the main cylinder and the doffer— the condition of the card fillet (whole-metal saw-toothed fillet or needle fillet) is checked, and if

elements.label: text
elements.text: necessary it is brought in good working condition, the doffer and main cylinder bearings are opened and examined, the grease replaced, the pulleys are examined and repaired as well as the brackets for the grinding roller, the front and back knives and the lattice grid bars;

elements.label: text
elements.text: theflats— the set of flats is disassembled, the flats are replaced, and if necessary the flats cleaning comb and shaft are repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: thedoffingcomb mechanism— the comb box, the shaft journal and the doffing comb bearings are examined, the comb teeth are dressed and cleaned, the box is washed and filled with oil;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the transmission— the entire system of transmission is checked and repaired with replacement of worn-out gears and spindles;

elements.label: text
elements.text: thecoiler— the wheel gear is removed after which the transmission is disassembled, checked and repaired as well as the calender rollers, can rotating tables and covers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the time of intermediate repairs, if necessary, the maintenance personnel shall check and repair the following units: the braking arrangement for the automatic interlocking of the main cylinder front cover, the mechanical or electrical stop of the card, and of the lubrication system, and the anti-friction bearings are cleaned. Then general lubrication, adjustment and running-in of the card are carried out.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At capital repairs in addition to the aforementioned operations much complementary work is done, i.e. the comb box and coiler are disassembled and completely repaired; the elastic bows and set bolts are removed, checked and put in place; the main cylinder and doffer are raised and the shells of their bearings are disassembled,

elements.label: text
elements.text: 94 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: washed, and put in place; the machine stand and coiler are checked with a level, cords and rules; the fillet on the cylinders and flats are replaced according to schedule.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The licker-in, main cylinder and doffer. Cards have a licker-in, a main cylinder and a doffer — all of big dimensions and mass. Each of them is made of a hollow cast-iron or steel cylinder (shell), crosspieces and a shaft attached in them. The main cylinder and doffer are covered with a fillet and with their shaft journals rest in antifriction bearings (in old cards in sliding bearings).

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation various disarrangements occur such as notches on the journals, slackening of the shaft attachment in the crosspieces, running out of true, deterioration of the taker-in side plates, pulleys, couplings and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Lifting, removal and transport of the licker-in, main cylinder and doffer for

elements.label: text
elements.text: repairing in the shop as well as their transport and installation after repair are rather complicated and heavy, and require special jigs and fixtures. For this reason, it is more convenient to carry out these repairs directly on the card using for this aim the jacks illustrated in Figure 52. The jack has a stand 5 welded of angles. Welded to the stand is the nut 3 in which the power transmission screw 4 with a trapezoidal thread is accommodated. The screw has a shackle 1 freely arranged on its end and on which the shaft end is bearing. The screw 4 has a hexahedron 2 for raising and lowering the screw with the aid of a wrench. The licker-in or any other cylinder israised by uniformly screwing-in the power transmissionscrew (theflexiblebows ofthecard need not be set apart). Different operations (dimension control, building-up, fixing of repair bushings, replacement and repairs of bearings and others) may be carried out on the cylinder after raising it by means of jack.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the antifriction bearing is out of order the shaft of the taker-in, main cylinder or doffer comes also out of order. In this case, the bearing is replaced by a new one for which the shaft is turned, a split bearing is fitted on the shaft and over it an antifriction bearing preliminarily heated to a temperature of 70-90°C (in mineral oil).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The device for turning the said shaft on the card (Fig. 53a) has a base 1 which is fixed instead of the removed bearing shell. The shait rests on a temporary split bearing 2 mounted on the base shelf. The

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and. Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 95 >

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 53. Device for turning main cylinder (a) and doffer (6) on card

elements.label: text
elements.text: device has a slide rest with top carriage 6 and bottom carriage 8 each of which has its own screws 5 and 9. The top carriage ensures the cross motion; and the bottom carriage — the longitudinal move­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ment of the cutter 7 (relative to the shaft to be ground). The cutter 7 of bent shape is attached according to the shaft centre by the plate 3 with the bolt 4.The device is mounted using the template and taking

elements.label: text
elements.text: care that the axis of bottom carriage movement isparallelto the axis of the shaft to be turned. On shaft turning, the adequate cylinder is brought in rotation by a driving belt running on the pulley at the opposite end of the shaft.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When turning the shaft of the doffer a special device is used (Fig.53b). Attached on the plate 6 is the slide 4 travelling on which is the holder 2 with the cutter 3. Using the screw 1 the cutter is brought to the rotating shaft 5 while the screw 7serves for the longitudinal feed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation, the holes of the main cylinder may get worn-out at the place of the keyed joint of the shaft with crosspieces due to which the reach between the main cylinder and the cleaners is impaired, and the run-out of the main drum and its disbalance are increased.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The holes are restored by means of a boring bar (Fig. 54) ensuring their coaxiality. The supports and guides of the boring bar 2 are made as bronze bushings 7, pressure fitted in two crossheads 8 which are mounted over the exterior diameter of the main cylinder 9with close fit; the crossheads are attached on the main cylinder by means of ties. The boring tools are put in the through sockets of the boring

elements.label: text
elements.text: bar, which carries also reamers 3 for hole finishing. One end of the boring bar isconnected (by thread) with the nut of the clip 1 attached tothe crosshead. Using the crank 6, the main cylinder isdispla-

elements.label: text
elements.text: *96 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 54. Boring bar for cylinder boring

elements.label: text
elements.text: ced in axial direction. The radial effort at boring is taken-up by the crosshead bearings while the axial effort— by the thrust ring 5 connected with the crosshead by three springs 4.After boring is finished, a new shaft is inserted into the main cylinder and fixed in place. The assembled cylinder is subjected first to static and then to dynamic balancing. The cause of the short service lifeof sliding bearings (bushings) is unreliable lubrication. In order to ensure a reliable feed of lubricant into the bushing from the inside and all over the length,

elements.label: text
elements.text: a helical groove is provided and at the end, at the lubrication hole, a deep recess is made through which the oil can freely enter and may

elements.label: text
elements.text: be properly distributed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During card repair, the sliding bearings are frequently replaced by antifriction bearings. For this, the bearing shell is extended and a cover is made which is attached with several screws.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation the bushings of the licker-in side plates are gradually worn-out due to which the reaches between the taker-in and feeding table, the main cylinder grid bars and knives are impaired. At the time of repair, the side plate with a worn-out bushing is replaced by a new or restored one. The worn-out bush is cut off and in the side plate a recess is bored into which a new bushing is pressure-fitted and tightened with four dowels.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Covering with card fillet. In cards the main cylinders and doffers are covered with a whole-metal saw-toothed or needle fillet, while the licker-ins are covered with a saw-toothed fillet. The cleaners and workers are also covered with a whole-metal fillet.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After the elimination of the old fillet, the licker-in, main cylinder and doffer are ground on movable grinders and then covered with a new fillet. Grinding is done to impart the cylinder surface a regular cylindrical shape. The speed of the grinding wheel is 10 m s~l. After grinding the cylinders are checked for run-out at the ends and

elements.label: text
elements.text: Hepair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 97

elements.label: text
elements.text: in the middle by means of

elements.label: text
elements.text: a watch-type indicator; the run-out should not exceed 0.05 mm. After this, the cylindricity is checked. For this, the circumferential length from each side face of the cylin­

elements.label: text
elements.text: der is divided into the same number of lengths and the marked-out points are con­

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 55. Diagram of device with variable induction pick-up for determining dynamic parameters of card cylinders operation

elements.label: text
elements.text: nected along the generatrices. A metal rule is placed with its edge on these lines and the clearance between it and the cylinder is measured by a feeler (the clearance should not exceed 0.04 mm).

elements.label: text
elements.text: I— pickup; 2— oscillograph; 3— guide; 4— slider

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cylinders are covered with a whole-metal saw-toothed fillet by means of special units (for instance the fillet covering unit IIO-l).

elements.label: text
elements.text: One of the main causes of reach violation, resulting in the deterioration of the fillet, is the irregular deformation of the cylinders. A

elements.label: text
elements.text: strong cylinder deformation may be due to the heating of the saw­

elements.label: text
elements.text: toothed fillet at covering and further at its cooling on the cylinder shell. The proper position of the saw-toothed fillet on the cylinder depends on the tension applied in covering.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The process of card cylinder covering with whole metal saw-toothed fillet has been considerably improved and stabilized by the modernization of the fillet covering unit IIO-l and the incorporation of a shoe-brake at the fillet holder, the elimination of front pressure rollers and the incorporation of rollers effecting the preliminary bending of the fillet, the use of a compressing blade in the shape of a moving roller and the use of a stationary drive.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The doffers are also covered with a whole-metal saw-toothed fillet at a variable tension of the fillet in the unit IIO-l.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To determine the dynamic parameters of the card cylinders in practice, instruments are used with an electromagnetic parametrical system in which the cylinder acts as a core (Fig. 55). With a change in the air gap 6 between the core and the bobbin (i.e. with some impairment in the surface of the cylinder covered with a whole-metal sawtoothed fillet) the inductivity of the bobbin is modified which is immediately recorded by an oscillograph. In this way, it is possible

elements.label: text
elements.text: to determine the reaches between the main cylinder and the flats.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A new method has been elaborated for the operative control of reaches between the fillets of the card working organs both at halts and in operation. Plates 5-12 m m in diameter and 3 to 5 m m in thickness of a material with high plasticity (ceresin or paraffin) are

elements.label: text
elements.text: used as recording elements. These plates 4 (Fig. 56a) are fixed on

elements.label: text
elements.text: the fillets 1 and 2 of mating carding surfaces of the cylinders 3 and 5. Plates from 12 to 16 m m in diameter are used on the taker-in with a fillet of coarser pitch. Each plate is immersed with the index finger into the fillet; however to avoid the collision between the plates disposed on mating cylinders, the plates are shifted apart to magnitude S (Fig. 566) which is by 10-12 m m greater than the plate diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n checking the reaches on a machine at standstill, the working organs are manually turned for 15-20 s, and in checking the reaches on a working machine— for several seconds. Further, the working organs are stopped and, using the device illustrated in Fig. 57, measure the height of the plate layer protruding above the fillet, which

elements.label: text
elements.text: has not been removed by the fillet of the other cylinder. The device is placed on the fillet 5 of the working organ so as to bring the centre of the plate 1 in coincidence with the measuring tip 4. The readings are taken using the indicator 2 mounted on the base 3 with two bearing platforms. These measurements allow the determination of cylinder run-out and the reach Fig. 57. Device for checking reaches between them. This method on card ensures a better quality repair

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 99

elements.label: text
elements.text: and requires less time forchecking the reaches and for the repairs. The errors in the control of reaches under the dynamic and static conditions of the machine and in checking the cylinder run-out do not exceed ±0.005 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 58. Diagram of cylinder installa­

elements.label: text
elements.text: tion in end bevelling a— cylinder left end; 6— cylinder right end W h e n preparing the main cylinders and doffers for covering with saw-toothed fillet, it is recommended to grind the shell edges with beveling. In this w a y it is possible to ensure the rectilinearity of the cylinder saw-toothed surface generatrix after its covering with a whole metal saw-toothed fillet. For example, when covering the main cylinder with saw-toothed fillet, its ends are ground by an amount of 0.05 m m over a length of 250 mm. Figure 58 shows how the grinder is installed at the generatrix of the main cylinder. The bevel surface of the cylinder ends isobtained by the parallel feed of the cutting wheel using the adjusting screws from both sides of the grinder. Beveling of the cylinder m a y also be achieved with the aid of a special cutter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After covering the cylinder with fillet the evenness and run-out of its toothed surface is checked. The evenness of the covering along the generatrices is checked by means of a rule and feeler, while the run-out is checked by a special instrument operating on the contactless principle.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the fillet teeth are of different height, the protruding teeth are machined with a needle file, while bent teeth are straightened by a grinder. For levelling the surface the filleted cylinders are ground.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Further balancing is carried out, i.e. the licker-in and the doffer are subjected to static balancing, while the main cylinder is dynamically balanced. The static balance of the doffer is checked by turning it in its proper bearings from which the lubricant has been preliminarily removed. In doing so, the heavy weight points causing the disbalance are detected. The doffer is balanced by means of weights fixed to attachments: the doffer comes out of balance when

elements.label: text
elements.text: a weight of not more than 50 g is tangentially attached to it.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The licker-in is subjected to static balancing on knife edges by attaching the balancing weight to its bottoms; a balanced licker-in is disbalanced when a weight up to 30 g is attached to it.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The dynamic balance of the main cylinder is checked in its proper bearings in the card with the main shaft rotating at the working speed, and dynamic balancing iseffected on each of the machine stands in alternating order using a low-frequency balancing arrangement. The device (Fig. 59) is provided with two similar converters having their sensors 1 and 2 attached to the bearing shells. The source of bearing oscillations is the main cylinder 4which is not balanced at the working rotational speed. The device has a stroboscopic lamp S

elements.label: text
elements.text: 100 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: one flash of which corresponds to each revolution of the main cylinder 4. The balancing weight is determined by placing test weights. For instance, it is sufficient to reduce the disbalance of the main cylinder to 250 g/cm in each plane, which corresponds to the vibration shift of 0.008-0.01 mm. Pulley and friction clutch. The pulley and friction clutch (Fig. 60a) are comprised in the main cylinder unit and may be subject to different disarrangements in the course of operation: the bushing 6 turns and causes the wear of the main cylinder shaft 7; the fingers of the driving hub as well as the holes of the friction clutch hub get worn out; the steel disks are torn off. In the first case, the bushing is replaced by a new one and the key 5 is made 12-15 m m longer. In the second case, the worn-out hole is reamed and a new finger is made to suit the new dimension of the hole. The torn-off disk 2 is replaced by a new one which must be perpendicular to the coupling centre line and must ensure a good mating with the other disk.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 59. Diagram of device for balan­

elements.label: text
elements.text: cing card cylinders

elements.label: text
elements.text: For increasing the service life of the finger 3 another fixture is used in the driving hub 1 (it is fixed with a nut instead of pressure fitting). A hole with a diameter up to 25 m m is drilled in the hub of the friction clutch 8 and a polyvinylchloride or rubber bushing 4

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 60. Pulley and friction clutch of card cylinder unit

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 101

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 61. Card flat

elements.label: text
elements.text: is fitted on the finger for attenuating the impacts at the engagement and disengagement of the friction clutch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the card friction clutch the socket, pressure levers and small wheel block are frequently worn-out. The worn-out socket and small wheel block are replaced by new ones at the time of repairs. In order to increase their life, the sockets are made with twelve alveoluses (instead of three ones as in the previous sockets) which allows the use of the socket four times without removal and disassembly

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the friction clutch (Fig. 606). To ensure a better reliability of the clutch fixture, three bolts (or every other of the six bolts used) are replaced with pins 1-3 of greater diameter which safely counteract the shearing efforts created at machine starting (Fig. 60c).

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the doffer engagement clutch the wheel block keyway gets worn out. During repairs a worn-out keyway is replaced by a bronze

elements.label: text
elements.text: bushing (of the same dimensions as the key) which is then welded, and the weld is machined. Owing to this it is possible to avoid the wear of the keyway in the clutch of the doffer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Flats. The main kinds of disarrangements which are observed in flats are the wear and warping of the needle fillet. The flat (Fig. 61) consists of a cast-iron bar 5, the flat needle fillet 7 and the clips 6

elements.label: text
elements.text: by means of which the flat set is attached to the bar. At each end of the bar, there is a boss 4 with a hole for connecting with the chain of flats. The bolt 2 which serves simultaneously as the axle of the chain member passes through the chain plates and the hole in the boss of the bar. At the left and right ends of the bar there are wellfinished shoulders 1 by means of which the flat rests on the flexible bows.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn-out needle fillet is stripped from the bar on a special machine (Fig. 62). Using this machine the worn-out fillet is stripped from seven bars at a time. The flats 3 are attached on the base 5

elements.label: text
elements.text: 402 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: having guides for the carriage 1 on its ends. Fixed on the carriage are the holder 4 and strippers 2 which at the carriage movement strip the worn-out fillet from the flats. There are also machines for stripping the worn-out fillet with a blade. The production capacity of such machines is 40 flats per hour. In modern cards the reach between the flats and the cylinder is 0.12-0.15 mm and with the use of a semirigid flat fillet in combination with a wholemetal saw-toothed fillet the reach is 0.1 mm. Under the action of their own weight the flats are liable to bending to 0.088-0.1 mm. For this reason strict requirements are set towards the shelf of the bar on which the middle fillet is attached: it must be smooth (7th class of finish) and with high planeness. The difference in dimensions in a set of flats should not exceed ±0.025 mm. In the course of operation flat warping is possible, i.e. their planeness is impaired, residual bends up to 1.5-2 m m appear, as well as other defects. In case of warping, a flexible fillet is straightened by grinding (however it leads to a shorter life of fillet needles due to their wear). W h e n semirigid fillets are employed no grinding is effe­

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 62. Machine for stripping fillet

elements.label: text
elements.text: from card flats

elements.label: text
elements.text: cted. Warped bars are straightened by cold dressing prior to being covered with a needle filleti This is carried out in a special dressing machine. Owing to cold dressing it is possible to reduce the residual

elements.label: text
elements.text: bend of bars to 0.1 m m The employment of semirigid flat fillet in modern cards has resulted in stricter requirements towards the precision of bar finishing (up to ±0.025 mm). This proved necessary for the reason that after the semirigid flat fillet has been attached to the bar the needle ends are not to be ground.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To accommodate a semirigid needle fillet the surface of the flat bar is levelled as follows. A layer of polymer material is applied on the surface, and if necessary this new surface is levelled after which the needle fillet is fixed upon it (the use of this method is resorted to because after planing, milling or grinding for levelling the cast-iron

elements.label: text
elements.text: bar surface the bars become warped).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bars with worn-out flats are subjected to building-up with metal by gas or electric arc welding, or with polymer material (for

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 103

elements.label: text
elements.text: instance, styracryl) in moulds after which they are milled and ground.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bars are covered with fillet in a special machine. The needle fillet with clips is brought over the bar base, the clips are inserted

elements.label: text
elements.text: in the machine jaws and the flat base is pressed from the sides by special screws. From the top the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 63. Order of operations in flat

elements.label: text
elements.text: covering

elements.label: text
elements.text: needle fillet is held in special clamps. After tight clamping the needle fillet as described above,

elements.label: text
elements.text: the clips are bent from both sides of the flat by passing pressure rollers several times along the fillet length. The rollers are arranged in the machine bending head. The clips are rolled up in one to-andfrostroke ofthe head (Fig. 63). In the straight stroke / of the head the rollers are bent (item 1)and further the clips are turned-in (item 2) and in the reverse stroke II they are rolled up (item 3). The reverse motion of the head is effected either automatically from a motor or

elements.label: text
elements.text: from a hand drive.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rolling-up of clips must be tight over the whole length of the flats and should be without cracks, folds and burrs. The clip ends are centre-punched according to the flat recesses. The assembled flats are put in a set according to the height of elastic needles

elements.label: text
elements.text: and sent for grinding the needle surface in special automatic m a chines with a production capacity of about 20 flats per hour (for grinding the needle covering to about 0.1 mm). To avoid the deterioration of the flat needle covering at their transport from the carding room to the grinding shop and back, special trucks with shelves are used.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Doffing comb mechanism. It consists of a comb made as a shaft 2 (Fig. 64) with pokers 4, the comb box 1 and the bearing 3. The main function of the doffing comb is the doffing of a thin layer of web from the surface of the doffer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In modern cards the doffing comb performs up to 1900 oscil- Fig. 64. Doffing comb mechanism

elements.label: text
elements.text: 104 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: lations or nips per minute. During the work the following disarrangements are sometimes observed in the comb: the poker fixture in the shaft holes as well as the steel toothed plates 5 on the pokers get slack; burrs appear on the toothed fillet of the plates; the shaft journal is worn out, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the time of repairs the slackened points are riveted once again. The worn-out journal is built-up by metal or chromium plating with subsequent grinding. The pokers of the doffing combs made of whole-drawn pipes are liable to deformation and breakage. In this case they are replaced with tubes of smaller diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 6o. Device for repair of doffing combs

elements.label: text
elements.text: Burrs on the doffing combs are manually eliminated (by a needle file and wooden blocks) or by means of different mechanical means.

elements.label: text
elements.text: One such device is shown in Fig. 65a. Fixed on the stand 1 are two posts 3 with bearings housing the journal of the polishing roller 4 (covered with a card fillet). The comb to be polished 5 is fixed on two other posts 2.Care should be taken that on roller rotation the teeth are not damaged and only the burrs are removed. The roller isbrought in rotation by the motor 7through aV-belt drive 6. The doffing combs may abso be polished by an electrochemical method.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After the repairs the doffing comb is subjected to static balancing. At this, in the parts made heavy the excessive metal is removed by drilling and at light points the metal is built-up by welding or soldering. The most progressive method is the use of a balancing washer

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 65b). The properly balanced position of the comb is determined by shifting the washer 1 along the circumference of the shaft 2. In this position a matchmark is cut on the shaft butt and on the balancing washer. A properly balanced comb works smoother and reduces the run-out in bearings and in the comb box.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After repairs the doffing comb is assembled and set so that its teeth are disposed parallel to the generatrix of the doffer surface. For this, the teeth ends must be set parallel to the shaft journals by means of special devices.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The harmful effect of inertia loads exerted on the doffing comb can be reduced by decreasing the weight of the comb and its shaft (which can be tubular instead of solid) and also by reducing the frequency of comb nips. However, the most efficient is the progressive

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 105*

elements.label: text
elements.text: use of a new principle of comb motion, i.e. the use of roller doffing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The comb boxes in cards of earlier design are with a link mechanism, while in modern cards an articulated four-member mechanism is used. Comb boxes of the first type are with sliding bearings, while those of the second type are with antifriction bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 66. Jaw clutch

elements.label: text
elements.text: During the operation of a comb box, the carriers, cranks, bearings,, carrier sliders, crank bushings and other parts are worn out. At the? repairs of an articulated four-member comb box, it is disassembled, cleaned, washed, the worn-out bearings are replaced, assembled, filled with lubricant and run-in. The link comb box is repaired by disassembly and assembly with faulty parts replaced by new good

elements.label: text
elements.text: ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Calender mechanism and coiler. The calendering mechanism is* intended for transforming the web into a sliver with its condensing. The calender rollers are mounted in sliding bearings with cast-iron bushes which are worn-out in the course of operation. The roller journals are also worn-out. The worn-out bushings are replaced with new ones and the journals are built-up with a steel layer (by welding

elements.label: text
elements.text: or metal coating) and ground to the required dimensions. The use of bushings made of polymer materials, as for instanceof capron (instead of cast iron), in the calender mechanism increases their service-

elements.label: text
elements.text: life.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When the calender rolls are worn out they are either replaced by new ones or repaired, i.e. the worn out surface of the roll is ground and a steel jacket is fitted-on in hot condition. To avoid damaging of the roll end at the time of fitting and removal of calender rolls and not to impair the fitting it is recommended to use a pipe and to knock. against it with a wooden or copper hammer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The calender rolls are put in motion by a jaw coupling. This coupling usually consists of two half-couplings 3 and 1 (Fig. 66) and an intermediate bush 2 connected by flanges. Such half-couplings get rapidly worn out at the points of contact with the intermediate bush,

elements.label: text
elements.text: (made of steel or cast-iron). At the repair the worn-out lugs arebuilt-up, ground and adjusted to suit the recess. For increasing thelongevity of the intermediate bush it is made of capron. This increases its damping capacity and the reliability of the whole driving: unit is improved.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The card coiler serves for coiling the sliver in the can and for its* condensing. The coiler has a couple of calender rollers resting im

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1106 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: •cast-iron bearings. The supporting surfaces of the shafts and bearings are worn out in the course of operation. At repairs, worn-out bearings

elements.label: text
elements.text: are replaced by new ones, and the supporting surfaces of the shafts •depending on the amount of wear are built-up by chromium plating •or metal coating. There is a new more improved method of repair which is carried •out as follows. The supporting part of the shafts is ground to remove the traces of wear and to impart it a regular shape; then it is placed in a mould and poured with polyamide plastic material (capron) after which it is machined in a lathe for imparting the required shape and dimensions to the part. In this way, the longevity of the part and the periodicity of unit lubrication are almost doubled.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The most frequently encountered disarrangement in the operation •of the vertical shaft resting on a thrust bearing and a radial bearing is caused by the wear of the vertical shaft heel and thrust bearing. 'The worn-out thrust bearing isreplaced by a new one and the vertical ;shaft heel is restored by metal coating or building-up. To ensure

elements.label: text
elements.text: better reliability in the sliding thrust bearing operation it is replaced by an antifriction bearing. At repairs, a seat is made for the antifriction bearing in the body of the worn-out thrust bearing, and the vertical shaft heel is turned to suit the bearing ring. From the top the bearing is provided with a cover having a lubrication hole and the cover is placed on the vertical shaft. W h e n the card coiler stands -have a worn-out keyway at the point of its engagement with a gear

elements.label: text
elements.text: they are repaired by planing the keyway or the whole length of the hub to ensure a more rigid connection of the vertical shaft with the gear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly and adjustment of cards. At the time of assembly of •cards the top surfaces of the frames must be disposed strictly horizontally. The side plates of the main cylinder and doffers must be installed at an equal distance from their butt faces. The surface of

elements.label: text
elements.text: the parts coming in contact with processed fibre is cleaned with an abrasive cloth, polished with chalk and wiped with graphite. It is necessary to ^ensure the mutual mobility of the flats in the set.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The set of flats must be assembled and mounted so that its motion is effected by easy turning with hand the socket wrench fitted on the worm shaft of the flat drive.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When adjusting the friction clutch it is necessary to find a position in which the pressure disk m a y easily be displaced by the action •of the levers. The coiler mechanism must easily be turned by hand. •On disengagement of different drives there should be no jamming in the connections. The grid bars under the taker-in and the mote knives must be set with minimum clearances. It is recommended to adjust the following reaches between the working organs of the •cards, m m :
