elements.label: text
elements.text: At present methods have been worked out for the general adjustment of cards comprising the following operations:

elements.label: text
elements.text: antivibration packings are inserted, if necessary, under the frames of the cards taking into account the vibration resistance of the floors;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the ball bearings of main cylinders and licker-ins are replaced by new high precision bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the main cylinders are dynamically balanced in their own bearings of the cards, for which special rings are placed at the ends of the shells on the cross-piece cover for attaching the balancing loads;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the licker-ins are statically balanced on special knife edges, and the doffers— directly on the card in their own bearings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the main cylinders are ground in grinders of high precision in which the run-out of the grinding wheels does not exceed 0.02 mm;

elements.label: text
elements.text: covering of cylinders with a whole-metal saw-toothed fillet is made with an allowance not over ±0.03 mm, and covering of the main cylinders and doffers is effected with a differentiated tension on the roller covering unit. Covering of the doffers with a whole-

elements.label: text
elements.text: metal saw-toothed fillet must be carried out with variable tension

elements.label: text
elements.text: 108 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: (at a distance of 200 m m from the edge the tension should be 50- 60 N and 25-35 N in the middle part of the doffer). The main cylinders are covered with whole-metal saw-toothed fillet taking into account the working speed (so for instance, when the main cylinder diameter is 672 m m and its rotational speed is 800 min-1,the fillet tension should be 67 N). The licker-ins are covered with saw-toothed fillet, and the carding rollers with whole-metal saw-toothed fillet;

elements.label: text
elements.text: levelling of the flat grid bars ismade by means of a polymer coating with subsequent covering with an elastic and semirigid fillet.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The general adjustment of cards is most efficiently done at middle and capital repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Drawing Frames and Sliver-Lap Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: To prepare the drawing frames and sliver-lap machines for repairs, the half-ready goods areremoved and the machines are dusted and cleaned.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The medium repair of sliver-lap machines comes to the following. The machine is put in idle running and the feeding rollers, the calender roll and disks are checked for run-out. Further, the machine

elements.label: text
elements.text: is de-energized, the condition of the chain drive is examined and disarrangements are corrected (chain slackening, sprocket fitting), the condition of all surfaces coming in contact with the fibre is checked (indentations and burrs aresmoothened), the braking arrange­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ment is disassembled, checked and repaired, the antifriction bearings are opened, cleaned, washed and greased, other units and mechanisms are examined for ascertaining their proper condition and the worn out parts are replaced or repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the capital repairs of sliver-lap machines, they are completely disassembled and all worn-out parts and units are replaced. Next, the machine is assembled and adjusted. When proceeding to the adjustment, care should be taken that the pressure rollers on the feeding table turn easily, the top calender roll runs idle without

elements.label: text
elements.text: jerks, the machine treadle with a tensioned belt brake lowers down 60 mm, the counterweight brings down the bobbins on the lapping rollers without impacts, the movable parts in the guides are easily

elements.label: text
elements.text: displaced without jamming, the disks are properly mounted on the shafts, the surface of the braking disk is smooth and the belt uniformly adheres to it.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the medium repairs of drawing frames the following kinds of work are carried out:

elements.label: text
elements.text: thefeeding mechanism— the guide is checked for easy running (if necessary adjusted) and the burrs on the feeding table and feeding roller are dressed;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the drawing mechanism— the line of rollers, pressure rollers and weighting hooks as well as roller stands, inserts and the drive to

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 109

elements.label: text
elements.text: the drawing mechanism are examined, and if necessary, the burrs

elements.label: text
elements.text: are eliminated, faulty parts, coatings and combs are replaced and the reaches are adjusted to a template;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the mechanism for unloading the pressure rollers— the m e c h a n i s m is checked and adjusted, the lines of weight suspension are levelled

elements.label: text
elements.text: and the spring load is checked according to a control weight;

elements.label: text
elements.text: coilerand calender rolls— the shafts and drive to the coiler wheels are disassembled, the shafts are cleaned, all faulty parts are replaced, the main shaft and bearings are examined, the self-stop mechanism is dismantled, checked and adjusted, as well as the manual machine stop; all the machine parts are lubricated and the machine is adjusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the capital repairs of drawing frames the guide mechanism is additionally dismantled, the drawing mechanism is completely disassembled, the rollers are mounted using the ruler, the framework is checked with a level, the can rotating tables are mounted with a plumb bob taking care of the excentricity; the main shaft is disassembled, the bearings are washed, the cleaning felts are replaced and

elements.label: text
elements.text: all the parts which by their state and service term do not satisfy the conditions established for capital repairs are completely replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the adjustment of drawing frames care should be taken that the drawing frame moves smoothly (without jerks); that the load on the rollers is regular and equal, that no stoppage of cans occurs at the moment of reversing motion change-over that the self-stoppage mechanism ensures drawing frame stoppage in the course of two seconds in the event of sliver breakage, and that a strip of paper

elements.label: text
elements.text: may be drawn between the calender rolls with application of a light effort.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disks of the sliver-lap machine. At the time of web doffing (when th (disks are set apart) and its threading (bobbin clamping), the

elements.label: text
elements.text: spindles carrying the disk are displaced. On machine starting, after web threading the bobbin turns between the disks which causes the wear of journals and metal sockets. Worn-out parts are replaced by

elements.label: text
elements.text: new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the disks are broken at the place of fixing, then in repairing the central part of the disk should be bored, threaded and a steel ring

elements.label: text
elements.text: is screwed on. Figure 67 illustrates the method of connecting the spindle 1 and pin 2 with the disk 3 ensuring a reliable operation of

elements.label: text
elements.text: the lap rolling mechanism. The spindle is made with an elongated threaded tail. It is screwed into the disk, and the bobbin pin is screwed onto the protruding part of the threaded tail. The disk is

elements.label: text
elements.text: made with right-hand and left-hand thread and is mounted so as to ensure its self-tightening during operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The calender roll of the drawing frame. In the course of operation the shaft journals are worn out,;the fastening of the hollow cylinders is impaired and there is a run-out of the shaft and cylinders*

elements.label: text
elements.text: no Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 67.^Disks of bobbin clamping Fig. 68. Fixing cylinder on calender mechanisms in sliver lap machines roll by means of tapered bushing

elements.label: text
elements.text: To eliminate thisdefect,thethollow cylinders are attached onto the shaft by aid of cone and bushing (Fig. 68) instead of key joints. A conical hole is bored in the hollow cylinder 1 and a bevel bush 2 is mounted on the shaft 5. The nut 3 is screwed onto the threaded tail, the hush 2 is tightened, and the nut 4 is used as a counternut for final tightening. This kind of repairs ensures the alignment of the shaft and cylinder and allows the easy removal and mounting of cylinders.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drawing frame combs. In wool and flax spinning mills drawing frames are provided with combs consisting of a plate with pressure fitted round needles. At the ends of the comb plate there are provided chamfers by means of which the combs penetrate between the worm coils.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation, the comb chamfers are worn-out, the needles are broken, fall out of the plate which also comes out of order. The combs with worn-out chamfers are restored by gas or electric-arc welding, and in the event of small wear by the electric spark method. The metal overlay is ground. The deteriorated needles

elements.label: text
elements.text: are eliminated and new ones are pressure fitted in their place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In addition to combs with round needles there are also combs with flat needles. Such needles are attached in the comb plate with polymer material and owing to its elasticity they acquire flexibility which is necessary when operating with products passing at a great speed. The method of fixing flat needles in the comb plate by means of polymer materials is shown in Figure 69. The needles 1 are placed in the elastic polymer holders 2,which are introduced in the longitudinal slot 3 of the steel comb 4 and attached by the clamp 5.If one or several needles get out of order all the package is eliminated by

elements.label: text
elements.text: using a special device and replaced with a new one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment m

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 69. Fastening flat needles in comb plate by polymer materials

elements.label: text
elements.text: The defectuous combs are removed from the drawing frame to be checked: the needle plates are checked for rectilinearity in longitudinal and crosswise directions and their heads for twist. The comb resting with its ends on bearers should have no oscillating motion.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If necessary it is straightened in a special device. All the needles must be disposed on the same level, aligned along the axis, and should be vertical and oriented in the direction of fibre drawing. Even one curved needle can bring the entire fillet out of order. If necessary bent needles are straightened by a tubular tool.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly and adjustment of sliver-lap machine and drawing frames. At the assembly of sliver-lap machines the guiding spikes on the feeding table are set so that the slivers before the calender rollers form a regular web. The rest of the bottom cleaner weight is set so that the weighting lever does not reach the shaft when

elements.label: text
elements.text: the cleaner is removed. The pedal of the machine with a belt brake must have the possibility of lowering by 60 m m when the brake is tensioned. The pressure rollers must freely rotate and in the absence of sliver there should be no clearance between the pressure and feeding rollers. The bobbins must come to rest on the lapping rollers without impacts. The top calender roll must freely rotate (without jerks) at idle running. The movable parts should not be clamped in the guides. When adjusting the brake care should be taken that the braking

elements.label: text
elements.text: band uniformly contacts the braking pulley; the surface of the braking disk must be smooth and the disks should not be slack on the shaft. Self-stops should come in action so as to ensure that in case

elements.label: text
elements.text: 112 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: of breakage, the sliver end passes not more than over a distance

elements.label: text
elements.text: of 200 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly of drawing frames the framework position should be checked in horizontal and vertical planes. The fluted roller, top rollers of the feeding couples as well as the smooth roller should be iree of burrs. The rollers must easily rotate and the run-out should not exceed 0.25 mm. The needle bearings must be in good order and

elements.label: text
elements.text: packed with grease. The pneumatic system for fluff elimination must be hermetically sealed and reliably fixed. The feeding trough a -and the working surface of the condensing funnel must be smooth

elements.label: text
elements.text: and well-polished. The calender rolls are set to allow a strip of thin paper to be drawn between them by applying a small effort.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the adjustment of sliver-lap machine and drawing frames it is necessary to observe the admissible allowances in deviations for

elements.label: text
elements.text: the wear of working organs which were established at the repairs and to maintain the allowable reaches according to adopted technological •conditions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4, Roving Frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: For preparing The frames to be repaired, the roving and halfready goods are eliminated from the frames and they are dusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At medium repairs the following work is to be done: the roving creels— these are checked to the pin, the faulty thrust hearings are replaced, the rods, flanges and the feeding roller are checked for rectilinearity, the fastenings are examined ifnecessary tightened;

elements.label: text
elements.text: drawingsystem— the following parts are disassembled, checked and adjusted: gearings, spindles, fluted rollers, stands, bushes, cap bars, guide nebs; the rollers and eyelets are cleaned; the springs, cleaners, covers, deteriorated gears and spindles are replaced; faulty cradles,

elements.label: text
elements.text: forks and belts are examined and replaced; the drawing system is assembled and the reach between cylinders is adjusted according to a template;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the bobbin rail— the flyers are checked and removed, the jack shafts, jack and bobbin gears are checked and straightened, the faulty spindle bushes, the jack couplings and bearings are replaced

elements.label: text
elements.text: and cleaned, the jack shafts are set according to a template, the drive is checked, the faulty gears and spindles are replaced and the leaf chain is washed;

elements.label: text
elements.text: spindle rail— the spindles, jack shafts, jack and spindle gears, thrust bearings and jack bearings are checked, replaced or repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: lifting mechanism— the shaft, couplings, bearings and racks are replaced or faulty parts are repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: reversing motion— the plates, balance, spindles and springs are checked and cleaned, and faulty parts are replaced or repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 113

elements.label: text
elements.text: beveldrums— checking for run-out and easy rotation; the bearings, gear drive, lock and lifting mechanism of the bottom drum are examined and faulty parts are replaced or repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: head drive— the main shaft, differential gear, gear bearings and spindle drive are checked and faulty parts are replaced or repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: hoods and guards— are checked and if necessary repaired. Finally the roving frame is lubricated and put in idle running. Capital repairs (overhauls) of roving frames comprise the following operations: full disassembly of the frames; cleaning and washing of parts; checking the beams, stands and rails; repair of all rollers and checking of each joint; repair of all roller stands, replacement of jack shafts and worn-out jack gears; full replacement of all spindle

elements.label: text
elements.text: bushes, thrust bearings and spindles; examination and restoration of the slots for the rail in the stands; checking and repair of all kinds of transmissions (gearing, chain,and belt transmissions and also of the reversing motion).

elements.label: text
elements.text: For the adjustment of the roving frame after the assembly it must be set in idle running. During idle running it is essential to check the smooth operation of the roving frame, the heating-up of separate parts and units and to ascertain that there are no foreign

elements.label: text
elements.text: noises during the running. Further, the spindle and bobbin rails are checked for horizontality. The stroke of the traverse should be equal

elements.label: text
elements.text: to 75% of the working length of the shafts in the back line, and the distance between the extreme positions of the roving to the shaft ends should be equal. The centre lines of the bevel drums should be strictly parallel and in the same plane.

elements.label: text
elements.text: F L U T E D R O L L E R S . In the course of roving frame operation the fluted rollers are bent, their journals are worn-out, the flutes become damaged and breakages occur at the places of threaded joints.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At machine repair, the rollers are removed from their bearings and placed on supports arranged along the machine. The line of rollers consists of staffs connected by threads. Several jacks are used simul­

elements.label: text
elements.text: taneously for removing the rollers. The rollers taken off from the roving frames are separated in staffs and each staff is checked with an indicator for determining which of them is bent and needs dressing. The roller staffs are dressed by means of a cramp on a lathe, a press or in a special machine. After dressing the roller run-out at the exterior surface of the fluted sections should not exceed 0.1-0.12 m m .

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the supporting journals of the fluted roller are worn-out, they are restored by chromium plating, metal coating or building-up.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rollers with a deteriorated fluted surface are repaired as follows. Different shallow scratches, indentations and burrs are eliminated with a needle file or trihedral scraper and then the rollers are polished with a paste of thin abrasive powder mixed with pure mineral oil.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worn-out flutes of unhardened rollers are restored by plastic deformation, by rolling over the cavities with a steel hardened roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: 114 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: under a high pressure. Worn-out flutes of hardened rollers are

elements.label: text
elements.text: fl!h

elements.label: text
elements.text: deepened by a thin abrasive wheel or a shaped tool of hard alloys in a slitter using a grinding head instead of the top carriage. To restore the service ability of the fluted roller it is sufficient to remove from the cavity a layer of 0.08-0.1 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: i*' -t

elements.label: text
elements.text: SPINDLES. In the course of operation spindles may be bent, heels, necks and seating cones of the flyers may become worn outr the slots for the flyer and eyelets may break. The bent spindle is straightened under press on a straightener or by means of different devices.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 70. Device for repairing roving

elements.label: text
elements.text: frame spindles

elements.label: text
elements.text: The deteriorated spindle heel m a y be repaired by different methods. The spindle end is annealed and dressed on a lathe to obtain the required cone after which the spindle is hardened again and machined. Another more efficacious method consists in grinding without preliminary annealing and with subsequent hardening, but this method requires the use of a special device. When repairing spindles with worn-out heels, care should be taken that the height of spindles in one set used in a roving frame does not differ more than by 1.5 m m .

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn-out neck and seating cone for the flyer are chrome plated. The worn-out slot is repaired by soldering a layer of brass or by electrolytic steel plating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The spindles with broken eyelets are repaired as follows: if one eyelet is broken off (Fig. 70a), then an insert 1 is attached with two

elements.label: text
elements.text: rivets 2 to its place. The points of joining should be soldered with brass or copper. If both eyelets are broken (Fig. 706), the spindle head is cut-off and a new head 1 is threaded to its place and the butt faces 2 are soldered with brass or copper. After soldering the head is carefully finished.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The shift of the slot centre line in respect to the spindle centre line should not exceed 0.15 mm. The run-out in diameter of the fitting cone is 0.15 m m and the run-out in diameter of the fitting cone for the flyer, heel and cylindrical part should not exceed 0.07 m m .

elements.label: text
elements.text: F L Y E R S . In the course of operation the following disarrangements of flyers m a y occur: wearing out of the fitting cone and pin, the flyer seat, and the bottom part of the flyer hollow leg; change in dimensions and deterioration of the shape of the hollow leg slot; strong disbalance, wear and breakage of feet; disbalance of the flyer balancing branches; burrs, indentations, scratches, and other exterior defects.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 115

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. pi. Device for reducing bush of roving flyer

elements.label: text
elements.text: Flyers are repaired in a shop where they are sent to after removal from the spindles. Prior to the repairs the flyers are cleaned from dirt and fluff manually and in special devices. After cleaning, the flyers are washed in a bath with a soda solution. Lately for cleaning flyers ultrasonic units have found application. Reburring of flyers is effected by means of a needle file or emery cloth. A special milling cutter with small teeth disposed on the interior cone is used for eliminating burrs from the flyer head. The milling cutter is fixed in the spindle of a drilling machine, and the flyer— in a special device on the table so that the flyer head is disposed opposite the milling cutter. On the displacement of the rotating milling cutter along the head of the flyer, the teeth remove a very thin layer as if scraping the head.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For repairing a flyer with a worn-out fitting cone, the bushing is reduced. The worn-out flyer bushing is drawn under press through

elements.label: text
elements.text: a calibrated hole of a steel hardened mould. Considering the fact that the bushing m a y be worn-out differently, the press has a set of moulds with holes of different diameters.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Figure 71 shows the device for reducing the'bush on a lathe. Barrel-shaped steel rollers 2 are arranged in special shells 4 in the collet

elements.label: text
elements.text: chuck 1.By rotating the nut 5 the rollers may be approached to the centre or retreated from it. The collet chuck is attached by its tail in a three-jaw chuck screwed on the spindle of the lathe headstock. The flyer 3 is attached in a chuck on the tailstock sleeve. The collet chuck device is rotated and the flyer bush is mounted between the rollers and reduced. If necessary after each passage the rollers are tightened with a nut. Sometimes the bushing is reduced manually

elements.label: text
elements.text: (by knocking with a hammer), but the quality of machining in this case is very low. After the bush cone has been reduced it is calibrated by a conical reamer. The reamed conical hole is checked by a bevel gauge (plug) and spindle. The worn-out pin is replaced by a new one. The flyer head eyelets are ground using a thin emery cloth with chalk and oil and next polished with a paste or fine emery mixed with oil by means of a wooden lap attached in the drilling machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 116 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worn-out seats and locks of the flyers are repaired by building-up (soldering) with brass and are sawn to a template. The vertical displacement of the foot on the seat should not exceed 0.6-0.8 mm. The bottom worn-out part of the flyer hollow leg is sawn off and a tubular insert is

elements.label: text
elements.text: butt-welded after which it is carefully dressed and polished. The slot in the flyer hollow leg with modified initial shape and dimensions is bent in by means of a special plate and copper hammer, or spread using a special g mandrel. The slot profile at dressing is checked with a gauge. The distorted flyer legs are a straightening die under press. In dressing the rectilinearity and parallelism of the flyer legs are checked by means of the instruments shown in Fig. 72. The flyer

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 72. Instrument for controllin

elements.label: text
elements.text: roving flyers

elements.label: text
elements.text: straightened as usual or in

elements.label: text
elements.text: and template 2are fitted on the instrument spindle 1 and the template recess is applied to the spindle.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The radius of the flyer leg bend is measured by a gauge. After the flyer legs have been repaired and straightened, the flyers are polished and the finish of theirsurfaces should be rather high not under the 9-th class of finish. The flyer foot has two legs: the horizontal one for guiding the roving to the bobbin and the vertical one for pressing the foot to the bobbin (by centrifugal force) so as to ensure the required density of yarn winding on the bobbin. The following conditions are essential for the normal operation of the flyer foot: unchanged mass and proper disbalance of the foot, as well as its clean surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation feets change their shapes and may become sometimes broken. The deformed feet arerestored by straightening with a copper or lead h a m m e r using special techniques (Fig. 73a-e) and a device with a set of plates (Fig. 73/) suiting the dimensions of the flyers. For straightening and bending new and restored feed different kinds of dies are used. The yarn guide eyelets are polished first with fine emery cloth using chalk and oil and then with wood­

elements.label: text
elements.text: en laps using fine emery and oil. At present, use is made of electropolishing and ultrasonic processing. The broken feet grippers are made anew and then welded or soldered to the rod, taking care that the supporting edges of the gripper are fitted to the flyer seat so that the foot is 1 m m away from the instrument disk and comes in contact

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 117

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 73. Procedures for straightening roving flyers

elements.label: text
elements.text: with the spindle at rotation. The deviation of the foot on the seat in vertical direction should not exceed 0.8 mm. The eyelets of repaired feet in fitting onto the flyer must coincide with the matchmark on the

elements.label: text
elements.text: disk of the control spindle. The method of fixing the foot on the flyer is shown in Figure 73e. The foot clearance should not exceed 0.8 mm. Roving flyers are subjected to static and dynamic balancing. Figure 74 illustrates the diagram of an instrument for the static balancing of roving flyers. The flyer 1 with the foot 2 is fitted on the spindle 3 attached in the bushing that freely rests on the bearings 4 in prisms 9 mounted on the stand 8.The stand is placed in a strictly horizontal position according to a level by means of adjusting screws 7.The pointer 6connected with the bush slides on the circular scale 5 graduated for reading the disbalance. If the flyer is not properly balanced the

elements.label: text
