elements.text: DIFFERENTIAL MOTION. The main function of the roving frame differential motion is the addition of component speeds, i.e. of the constant speed of the main shaft and the variable speed of bevel drums as well as the transmission of the speed to bobbins. The differential motion consists of main members (central gears and carrier) and satellites— gears with shafts moving in space.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 119

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of the differential motion operation the following disarrangements may be observed: cracks and crushing of holes in the body and cover, wear of gear shafts, teeth and other rubbing surfaces of gears, wearing of bushes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In case of small cracks in the body and cover of the differential, the crack is opened and soldered with brass by means of a gas flame. Crushed seating holes are restored by a hole trueing multiflute drill and a repair bushing manufactured of antifriction cast iron to suit the new size of the hole.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 75. Method of attaching blocks in reversing motion of roving frame

elements.label: text
elements.text: The gears with a shank and the gear shafts are carburized, hardened and ground to the seventh class of finish. Sometimes grinding and chromium plating are used. W h e n repairing gears with a spindle (due to the wear of the spindle) the deteriorated spindle is cut off, the gear is drilled, reamed and a thread is cut. Next, a new spindle with thread is manufactured, both parts are connected by threading and pinned. When the toothing of internal gears is worn out they are repaired by built-up with further machining on a gear shaper. If such machines are not available, machining is carried out on a pla­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ner with special devices.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the recent time when repairing the roving frame, the differential gears are mounted on antifriction bearings which considerably improves the reliability of the differentials and reduces parts consumption.

elements.label: text
elements.text: R E V E R S I N G M O T I O N . This is an intricate mechanism controlling the process of roving winding on the bobbins. In the course of operation the fastenings of the swinging rocker sliding blocks become slack and the following parts are subject to wear: spindles, rol­

elements.label: text
elements.text: lers, rockers, swinging levers, toothed racks, gears, pawls, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn pawls are replaced by new ones or repaired by buildingup. The slack fixture of the rocker blocks is tightened and the worn blocks are replaced by new ones. In order to ensure a more reliable fixing of the blocks 2 (Fig. 75) they are dovetailed on the swinging lever 1 and tightened with screws 3.As the reversing motion is assembled, the pawls and rockers are mutually adjusted so that each pawl contacts the rocker with its full working surface. In locked position the clearance between the pawl and the rocker should not exceed 0.2-0.25 mm; at change-over one of the pawls must perfectly be en-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 420 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: gaged, while the other must simultaneously be disengaged, and vice versa. It is convenient to carry out the repairs and adjustment of the reversing motion on a special stand in a workshop.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ASSEMBLY AND ADJUSTMENT OF ROVING FRAMES. Asthe roving frames are assembled and adjusted the roller beam should be strictly in horizontal plane. The allowable deviations in cross and longitudinal directions should not exceed 0.1 mm per running metre of the beam. The drawing system should operate smoothly and without jerks. The feeding roll must be smooth and free of indentations and burrs. The slider of the roller stand must be easily displaced with an allowable clearance not in excess of 0.3 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The flyers are washed, examined, balanced and carefully ground. The bobbin rail is checked for horizontality with a plumb bob and the spindle rail with a template. The rail lift is checked according to the bobbin working height. The bobbin rail must move smoothly. The shafts of the bottom and top conical drums must be strictly parallel and in one plane. The drums should be easily rotated by hand.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reversing motion comb is set horizontally with the foot in middle position on the bobbin and the reducer shafts parallel to the beam of the spindle rail; the run-out of the reducer should not exceed 0.15 m m and of the licker-in 0.3 mm. The reversing motion screw is set vertically. When the gear is removed, the reversing motion screw must easily rotate in bearings. The longitudinal slot of the stop is set parallel to the reversing m o tion screw so that the protrusions of the shells fitted on nuts would penetrate in the longitudinal slot.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At any position of the bobbin rail the preliminarily fixed shell stops must not be clamped. The stop is set in height so that when adjusting the rail for the preset height of nut lift, it is disposed s y m metrically to the screw cut-out. The bracket of the roller with a flywheel for manual cranking of the reversing motion should be set so that when the roller is completely pushed inside, its key is opposite the bushing of only one gear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The mechanism of the shifter must operate smoothly without jamming and the shifter must move over the full length of the conical drums. When the shifter is in the position corresponding to the beginning of winding, the weight on the reversing motion block must be in upper position. When the shifter is in opposite position, the weight must not touch the floor. It is necessary to check the reversing motion for easy running. All the spindle heads must be disposed on one horizontal line. The rollers must rotate easily, their surfaces must be properly ground and the loads on the rollers must be maintained strictly the same along the lines. Deviations in the reach of the nebs should not exceed 0.2 mm; the carrier eyelets must not letthe web approach closer than at a distance of 3-4 m m to the ends of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 121

elements.label: text
elements.text: top roller elastic part. Allowable deviations in rectilinearity of the drafting field, i.e. of the tangent in respect to the roller working surface should not exceed 0.25 mm; the web condensers should be free from indentations and burrs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 5. Combers

elements.label: text
elements.text: When preparing the combers for repair, the lap is knocked off, the half-ready products are eliminated, the wastes are removed and the combers are cleaned and dusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In medium repairs of combers the following jobs are done on thefollowing units:

elements.label: text
elements.text: feeding arrangements— examining and tightening the unwinding rollers, deburring the feeding rollers;

elements.label: text
elements.text: nippers, detaching rollers, needle segments and combs— c h e c k i n g t h e detaching rollers, segment drums and combs, nippers, ratchets, leverage systems, fingers, bearings and bushes; replacing worn parts; straightening bent needles on drums and combs, and rubbing separate rollers with chalk;

elements.label: text
elements.text: headgearings— examining the transmissions, replacing faulty parts,, and the adjustment of meshing;

elements.label: text
elements.text: draw box— disassembling and checking the top and bottom rollers and bearings, cleaning with chalk and deburring the rollers, replacing worn coatings, inspecting the draw box drive and replacing faulty gears and spindles;

elements.label: text
elements.text: coiler— checking the drive, replacing worn parts (gears, spindles and others), cleaning the cover in the trumpet with chalk;

elements.label: text
elements.text: cleaning brushes,doffersand combs— the examination of brush and doffer bearings, fixing the brushes and combs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: self-stop motion-checking and disassembling the motion, replacing worn parts and their adjustment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the time of adjusting the comber after the repairs, the reachesare checked with gauges. Using an indicator and gauges adjustment is made of the nippers, detaching rollers, top combs and feeding rollers. The proper interaction of working organs is determined by the cycle diagram and cycles dial. The following requirements should be met: the half laps must be attached on the shaft in strictly fixed position so as to obtain a clearance of not over 2 m m between the comb segments.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NIPPERS. Each comber deliveryisprovided with nippers. The lap* is clamped between the lower and bottom nippers (called a cushion plate and a nipper knife correspondingly). In the course of operation the nipper edges or lips become worn. The clamping part 1 (Fig. 76)> of the upper nippers I comes out of order, while in the lower nipper II— the clamping lug 2 is worn. This impairs the combing quality

elements.label: text
elements.text: and causing an irregularity of the combed sliver.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 122 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the wear is inconsiderable the surface of the nippers is smoothened with a file or emery paper. In case of bad wear, the worn parts of the upper nippers are planed with a shaped cutter or milled with a shaped milling cutter, taking care to strictly maintain the dimension A.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After planing or milling, the nipper surfaces are rubbed with cast iron or wooden laps and paste (abrasive and oil). The uneven surface of lower nippers is scraped and lapped with paste. Next, the nippers are put in pairs (the upper and lower nippers) and are lapped. The accuracy of fitting is determined by

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 76. Nippers

elements.label: text
elements.text: inserting a strip of cigarette paper which must be properly clamped ■at any point of the nipper surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: SLOTTED GAM. This cam serves to impart motion to the back detaching rollers moving on the detaching cylinder. In the course -of operation the cam slot becomes worn. In case of local wear, in re­

elements.label: text
elements.text: pair the deteriorated part of the slot wall is cut-out and in its place (using a gauge and roller) an insert is welded and the slot is carefully filed. If the slot is worn-out throughout the full perimeter, the

elements.label: text
elements.text: slot is straightened, widened by milling and the roller is replaced by

elements.label: text
elements.text: a thicker one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn-out cam slot is milled in a vertical milling machine -equipped with a special device.

elements.label: text
elements.text: C I R C U L A R B R U S H E S . Cleaning of half laps is effected by brushes consisting of two half-cylinders with holes for attaching tufts of

elements.label: text
elements.text: rigid Mexican grass or bristles. In the course of time the grass or

elements.label: text
elements.text: bristles fall out and lose flexibility which results in poor cleaning of the half lap. For levelling the brushes in circumference, they are sheared by a special device mounted on a circular grinding machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For increasing the strength of circular brushes it is recommended to fasten the bristles 1 (Fig. 77a) on a cylindrical solid block by means

elements.label: text
elements.text: of special pins 2. In some cases, the circular brush made of bristles or grass pile is replaced by a circular brush with straight needles of steel or brass wire 1 (Fig. 77b) attached in an elastic rubberized foundation 2, having its ends without needles nailed to the face of the hollow half cylin­

elements.label: text
elements.text: der 3.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 77. Circular brush

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 123

elements.label: text
elements.text: Two such half cylinders are pressed together at the ends by shrink rings. Brushes of this design are reliable in operation and ensure a good cleaning of half laps.

elements.label: text
elements.text: HALF LAPS AND TOP COMB. In operation the needles of comb segments and comb strips are deteriorated or broken and the top combs are also broken.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Faulty comb segments and top combs are repaired in a specialized shop. The comb segments are disassembled, the faulty strips are

elements.label: text
elements.text: unsoldered, checked and straightened, the needles are set, soldered to the strips, washed, dried and scraped, the segments are assembled, checked with a gauge, and ground. The strips removed from the segment are graded, faulty needles are unsoldered and eliminated; the strips are checked for rectilinearity and distorted strips are straightened (dressed) in a straightening die.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Setting of the needles is effected manually by means of a special device.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After setting, the needles are levelled in height by means of a h a m mer and a strip, fixing with screws the position of the latter. Next, the needles are soldered to the strip. The soldered combs are washed, dried, and scraped after which the assembly of half laps is started. At the assembly, the correct position of the strip is checked by passing a 1-mm thick lamellar gauge between the sharp ends of the needles and the setting strip. After the strips have been checked throughout all their length, they are definitely fixed in the segment slot. To accelerate the adjustment of strips, the assembled half lap is ground in a lathe using an eccentric mandrel (with central holes shifted by 1.8 mm). Owing to the center shift the required eccentricity in the position of needle points is obtained. After the assembly, the half lap is polished with circular brushes and oil. To avoid the corrosion of half laps and top combs, they are stored in special cabinets and

elements.label: text
elements.text: powdered with chalk or talc. Prior to the installation on the machine the half laps and top combs are again polished on a special machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ASSEMBLY AND ADJUSTMENT OF COMBERS. At the assembly of combers the half laps are mounted so that the needle points of the first strips and comb segments are in the same plane with the front edge of the upper nipper (when the nippers are closed).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The distance between the upper and lower nipper edges should not exceed 1 mm; the working edges should be well scraped; the reliabi­

elements.label: text
elements.text: lity of nipper clamping is checked by passing a strip of cigarette

elements.label: text
elements.text: paper . . otr The feed of separate portions of fibres must be within 20-35 mm. The top comb is mounted with a clearance of 1 m m in respect to the detaching roller which corresponds to the 62nd division of the cycles dial. In height, the top comb is placed in the position corres­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ponding to the 38th division of the cycles dial. In this position the

elements.label: text
elements.text: 124 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: distance between the top comb and the gauge placed on the generatrices of detaching rollers may be 1 to 3 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The brushes should penetrate in the needled surfaces of the half laps not more than by 2 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The feed of the web into the comber, the rotational speed of separate rollers and comb shaft are adjusted to suit the kind and linear density of processed fibres.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 6. Spinning Frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: Ring Spinning Frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: The ring spinning frame consists of the following'units and mechanisms: the creel for roving bobbins, the drawing unit, the headstock gearings, the builder motion, the ring plate and separators, spindle units, the lappets and yarn guides, tin drums, and tension rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The spinning frame is prepared for repairs by breaking-off the roving, eliminating half-ready products from the frame, doffing the yarn and dusting the frame.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During medium repairs of ring spinning frames the following jobs are carried out on the following units:

elements.label: text
elements.text: creelfor rovingbobbins— the creel is checked according to the skewer, faulty cup-shaped porcelain footsteps are replaced, the creel is reinforced, the rods are examined and the boards are repaired;

elements.label: text
elements.text: drawing unit— overall inspection of the drawing unit; checking, replacing or repairing faulty gearings, rollers, roller stands, inserts, cap bars, cap bar nebs, forks, aprons, springs of clearers and traverse guides; adjusting the traverse guide and scraping the eyelets; removing indentations and burrs in the cylinders, and setting the reaches according to a template;

elements.label: text
elements.text: headstock gearings— disassembling, checking, repairing and replacing faulty gears, spindles and bearings; cleaning and repairing the oil line;

elements.label: text
elements.text: builder motion— disassembling, cleaning, examining, replacing and correcting the pokers, builder arms, chains, builder cams, tierod bowls and rockers, including their lubrication;

elements.label: text
elements.text: ring rail and separators— checking the condition and fastenings of rings; replacing faulty rings; wiping the rings with chalk; checking the ring rail; installing clearers, and travellers, checking and fixing the separators in relating to spindles and ring rail, and replacing faulty separators;

elements.label: text
elements.text: spindleunits— washing and inspecting the spindles; replacing wornout bushings, bolster and spindle blades; and filling the oil in the spindle bolster;

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 125

elements.label: text
elements.text: lappetsandyarn guides— inspecting and reinforcing the lappet beam; checking the condition and replacing worn out lappets and yarn guides; checking the yarn guides in relation to spindles; and dressing the eyelets;

elements.label: text
elements.text: tindrum and tension rollers— checking the d r u m for run-out, inspecting, repairing or replacing faulty tension rollers; and repacking the bearings with grease.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At capital repairs the machine frame is additionally checked using a cord, a ruler, a plumb bob, and a level; the drawing unit is completely disassembled as well as the machine drive, spindles, drum, tension rollers and yarn guides. All faulty parts are replaced or restored, the drum is balanced, the spindles and antifriction bearings are disassembled, washed and lubricated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At machine adjustment a special attention is paid to the tension arrangement, and the drive of the drum and spindles. The quality of repairs is assessed by the quality of produced yarn, its proper win­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ding of the tube and the breakage rate.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The roller beams and spindle rails are checked for horizontality in longitudinal and cross directions, the allowance for deviation being 0.15 m m per m of the stand length. The web should be kept at least 3 m m away from the edge of the roller working surface. When installing the broken-end collector, care should be taken that the clearance between the roller and the broken-end collector tube should not exceed 3 mm. The spindle setting is checked by a special template.

elements.label: text
elements.text: DRAWING UNITS. The main partsofdrawingunitsareroller stands, fluted rollers and top rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Roller stands. In the course of operation, the roller stands serving as a framework for the drawing units are mainly deteriorated in their seats. When repaired, the worn-out parts are usually built up with

elements.label: text
elements.text: bronze brass or babbitt after which they are milled or bored and then filed to the preset dimension.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Installing new linings is the best way of repair. In this case the seat of the roller stand is shaped as necessary and a bushing of antifriction metal or plastic material is inserted under pressure. For example, in the drawing unit of the spinning frame 11-83 (the ring spinning frame with a spindle spacing of 83 mm) the worn seat of a roller stand of 18 m m in diameter is bored to a diameter of 25 m m with an allowance for a shrink fit of a cast iron or plastic bushing. The bushing has an outside diameter of 24 mm, with a length corres­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ponding to the thickness of the stand (38 m m ) and a hole 18 A 3 shifted 3 m m from the center. The ready bushing is pressed into the bored hole in the stand, after which the remaining thin walls of the bushing

elements.label: text
elements.text: are sawed and finished to suit the dimension of the roller neck. The bushing is fixed in place with a screw. The worn bushing may easily be replaced. Practice shows that the most reliable fastening is obtai-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 126 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: A- A

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 78. Method of repairing bushing of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 79. Shape of bush­

elements.label: text
elements.text: roller stand in drawing unit BP-1M

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing with lug

elements.label: text
elements.text: ned by using a bushing of fabric-based laminate in dovetail shape

elements.label: text
elements.text: Capron bushings have found application in many textile enterprises. When repairing apron draw boxes, a capron bushing is poured into the roller stand, as shown in Fig. 78. The roller stand 7resting on the support 2 is placed on the table 1 of the casting press. The rod 3 with a nominal diameter corresponding to the diameter of the roller neck is inserted into the stand hole. The cover 4 with a central hole for pouring the capron is placed at the top. The mould is provided with canals and holes for air elimination (casting system). The casting press nozzle 5 is placed against the cover and melted capron is injected inside. The place of bushing casting has the shape of position 6. After a certain time the mould is splitted, degated, and beads are eliminated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For roller stands of drawing units in flax spinning frames, bronze bushings are used. The wear of these bushings results in non-coaxiality of their position as well as in excessive bending and run-out of weighted fluted rollers. In repair, it is essential to use plastic inserts

elements.label: text
elements.text: (bushings) of antifriction material, which are ten times cheaper than bronze bushings. Moreover, as experience shows, it is efficient to use cylindrical bushings with a lug (Fig. 79) protecting the bushing from shifting. All the set of roller stands on the frame (irrespective of the design of the drawing unit and the type of spinning frames) must have bushings of the same size corresponding to the diameter of the fluted roller necks.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fluted rollers. In combination with top rollers, the fluted rollers serve for the attenuation of sliver or roving. According to their position in the drawing unit, the roller staffs are subdivided into head, intermediate and off-end staffs, and correspondingly the rollers are provided with different flutes (trapezoidal, rhombic, etc.).

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation the journals, necks and fluted surfaces of the rollers are subjected to twisting, bending and rubbing, which can provoke the following disarrangements: residual bend, wear of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 127-

elements.label: text
elements.text: necks, crushing and breakage of tails and seats of the staffs and wear of fluted surfaces.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Residual bending is due to the overloading of the roller or to its improper assembly (when the line of rollers does not rest on all the bearings). The rollers are checked for run-out using a special indicator directly on the spinning frame. The necks are worn because of insufficient lubrication and low rigidity of the roller line. The tails are broken due to the lack of proper threading in the staff seats. The fluted surfaces of the rollers are worn down by rubbing with the top rollers, when the web is cut with a knife or hook and also when the flutes are impaired by the yarn due to the insufficient displacement of the yarn guiding rule.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 80. Devices for disconnecting staffs of fluted rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: Prior to starting the repair of fluted rollers, it is necessary to disconnect the staffs. This is achieved by means of a special wrench with, three cover plates articulated together for the tight gripping of the surface of the roller staff. The roller staffs are disconnected directly on the frame by means of two wrenches. Figure 80a illustrates another device for disconnecting the roller staffs. Grippers A consisting

elements.label: text
elements.text: of two halves 1 and 3 (Fig. 806) are fixed from both sides of the point in which the staffs are to be disconnected. Each gripper has a lug with a saw-cut slit for the wrench. Both halves of the gripper are joined on the smooth necks of the rollers by a collapsible hinged bolt 4. Next, the rollers are placed on special supports 2 (Fig. 80a) and using wrenches applied on the grippers 5 (Fig. 806) the staffs are disconnected.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Straightening of bent rollers may be effected either manually (using a jimmy, sledge or straightening clamp) or by means of different devices which ensure a better quality and higher efficiency of repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Figure 81 illustrates a machine for straightening bent fluted rollers. The roller 2 is plaeed on the supports 1 and 4 and imparted rotation at a speed of 80-100 min-1.The rod 7 carries the bracket 6 with a straightening crank 5 having a bronze cushion. The crank is

elements.label: text
elements.text: brought to the bent point of the roller and with a push by hand the spot is straightened out. During dressing, the roller may be stopped

elements.label: text
elements.text: by simple shifting back the tension roller 8 rather than by disengaging the motor. The hook 3 placed on the non-working neck serves for retaining the rollers both on the supports and during straighten-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 128 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 81. Machine for straightening bent fluted rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing. The hook and the supports may be shifted along the slot in the stand guides. The points of run-out on the cylinder are detected by an

elements.label: text
elements.text: indicator and after straightening the run-out should not exceed 0.05 m m . The machine m a y be provided with a special screw press for straightening rollers with local flexure.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In some cases fluted rollers are straightened out directly on the spinning frame by means of a special device consisting of the claws 5

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 82), the traverse 3 and power transmission screw 2.The claws Jare connected by the hinge 4with the traverse. The thrust part of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: power transmission screw has a collar step bearing 6 with a rubber

elements.label: text
elements.text: damper. The claws are placed at both sides of the roller deflection so that the screw bears against its protruding part and by turning the

elements.label: text
elements.text: crank 1 the deflection is gradually straightened out.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The restoration of worn roller necks m a y be effected by different methods. If the rollers have been subjected to surface hardening by

elements.label: text
elements.text: high-frequency currents, or carburizing and hardening, the wear in •diameter does not exceed 0.1 m m . In this case, the initial dimensions of the necks are restored by building-up in an electroplating bath with a coat of chromium up to 0.08 m m thick from each side. The necks of unhardened rollers are liable to have a greater wear (>0.01 m m ) and therefore they are restored by building-up with electrodes or by metal

elements.label: text
elements.text: spraying. The rollers may also be restored by applying a layer of polyamide material (capron) under pressure. Sometimes regrinding of worn roller necks is done to obtain a new size (repair dimensions),

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 129

elements.label: text
elements.text: and adequate bearing linings are chosen to suit the new dimensions. Also half-bushings turned

elements.label: text
elements.text: and ground to the same dimensions are welded to the roller necks.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The method of restoring ajoint between the roller end and seat d e pends on the wear of the joint. If it is inconsiderable, then the threaded parts of the end and seat are built up by copper deposition. After this, using a die and tap the thread is given the required dimensions, checked with gauges and a control unscrewing is carried out. In the event of great wear, the size of the seat is expanded to the repair dimensions (using a tap) and the worn end isbuiltup with steel or brass. After boring the built-up roller end, a thread is cut to suit the repair dimensions of the seat thread. If the roller end is broken, it has to be built-up. For this, to ensure the centring of the built-up part, a hole is bored, reamed and threaded in the broken end of the roller after cutting it off. The built-up part isturned with an allowance in the diameter to permit finish of the assembly. The thread

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 82. Device for straightening bent

elements.label: text
elements.text: fluted rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: direction should be such that the joint cannot get unscrewed. The extension piece is screwed into the roller shell, turned, threaded and finally adjusted to suit the seat of the coupled staff. It should be taken into account, that the coaxiality of joined staffs greatly depends

elements.label: text
elements.text: on the proper machining of the seat holes. W h e n machining the holes, the operations are carried out in the following order: drilling the holes, boring the holes for the guiding neck, boring the holes for the thread, reaming the holes for the guide, chamfering and cutting the threading.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In some cases repairs are designed to increase and improve the longevity and service ability of the fluted rollers, for example, the use of split fast shafts in the first line of fluted rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing fluted rollers with deteriorated ends certain requirements are to be satisfied. The outside and inside threads must be made according to the third class of accuracy so as to permit easy unscrewing up to the half of the thread length. Thread stripping is allowed on not more than 1/8 of the circumference of one coil.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 130 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: The eccentricity of the thread must not exceed 0.15 mm and there must be no play at the points of connection. Local clearances should not exceed 0.25 of the circumference length and should not allow the passage of a feeler over 0.05 m m thick. In checking the roller staffs for rectilinearity, run-out, and twisting the allowable values should not be exceeded. Rollers with damaged fluted surface are to be restored by roll forming, planing, milling, grinding and chromium plating. When restoring the rollers by roll forming or knurling, their surface is subjected to the pressure of one or several steel hardened rollers owing to which the metal is redistributed according to the profile of knurling rolls. This method may be used only for unhardened fluted rollers (middle and back rollers of drawing units in cotton spinning frames). Knurling is carried out by means of single- and multiroller devices minding that the latter ensure a better knurling of worn flutes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 83. Device for restoring roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: fluted by knurling

elements.label: text
elements.text: Figure 83 shows the simplest device of this kind— a two-roll device mounted on a carriage. The roller 1is fixed at the centres of the headand tail stocks of a lathe. Two steel hardened fluted rollers 2 are freely mounted on shafts attached in movable stands 3.Holes in the base of the stands are provided with oppositely directed threads through which the screw 4 with a right- and left-hand trapezoidal threads (corresponding to the stands) is passed. By turning the screw it is possible to bring together or to shift apart the stands with rollers or to clamp the rotating fluted roller between the rolls.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The rollers of drawing units in flax spinning frames are machined on a planing machine equipped with an automatic divider, or on a longitudinal milling machine by means of a shaped milling cutter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To restore hardened rollers they must priorly be annealed and on restoring of the flutes they must be subjected to heat treatment. H o w ever, this kind of processing is costly and time consuming. For this reason, in such cases a flute planer is used with a divider and a grinding head attached in the planer stock.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the restoration of fluted rollers made of stainless steel (for flax wet spinning frames) a double chromium plating is applied which allows a 30 to 40 percent increase in the rollers life and ensures an economy in expensive stainless steel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repaired fluted surfaces ofthe rollers must be clean and smooth (polished), without indentations, burrs, circular scratches and other defects; the dimensions and profile of the rollers must meet standards.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 131

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 84. Device for pressure fitting of elastic!cots on top rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: Top rollers. The wear of top rollers greatly depends on their design. Used in the drawing units of cotton spinning frames are solid top rollers with loose sliding friction bushings and antifriction bearings. Solid rollers present a high inertia and therefore their slippage is stronger (the drawing unit has couples consisting of a fluted roller and a top roller, which must rotate both with the same speed without slippage). The rollers with loose sliding bushings are better lubricated and they slip less than solid rollers. The rollers with antifriction bearings have a minimum slippage. At slippage the elastic cot of top rollers becomes worn more in the middle than at the edges, so that a worn top roller acquires a saddle shape. The rollers with worn cots are ground for restoring their initial cylindrical shape. The cots

elements.label: text
elements.text: are replaced with new ones after multiple regrindings or on cracks appearance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It should be kept in mind that when rubbing parts such as bushings, hall hearings and spindles are worn the top rollers also come out of order. The cots are made of rubber and their surface must he smooth, without scratches, cuts, scores and visible hard inclusions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In cot regrinding the following operations are carried out: exterior examination; cleaning, washing and sorting; grinding (in assembly with the roller); checking for run-out.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the roller cot is to be replaced by a new one, preliminarily the new rubber cots are checked to ascertain that they correspond to specifications. After changing the cot (using special devices) the rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: are run in assembly with metallic bushings and then sorted and checked for run-out. W h e n choosing couplings (or cots) of synthetic rubber for press-fitting on top rollers it is necessary to take into account that the coupling stretch should not exceed 10-15%. Different devices are available for fitting the cots on the top rollers. One of them is illustrated in Fig. 84. The stand of this device carries the main parts: the power transmission screw 5 with the rod 6 screwed upon it, and the tip 8 provided with a helical spring. The rod has a stationary guiding bush 7. At the right end of the stand there are

elements.label: text
elements.text: 132 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: supports 9 and spring-loaded rest 10. The screw is rotated by

elements.label: text
elements.text: the electric motor 1 through the V-belt drive 2,the reducer 3 and clutch 4. The elastic cots or couplings coated with special glue are

elements.label: text
elements.text: fitted from both sides on the roller which is placed on the supports after which the motor end switch is engaged. Next, the power transmission screw and further the rod with tip are put in motion. After pushing the cots on the roller the rod butts against the end switch 11 and automatically disengages the device. Automatic devices are also available for the replacement of the elastic cots on the rollers of spinning and roving frames. The most efficient among them is the

elements.label: text
elements.text: automatic universal machine for replacing elastic cots of top rollers. The following operations are carried out in the machine: coating the inside surface of cots with glue, removal of worn cots from the bushing and putting on new cots.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rolling of top rollers with new cots is effected in different devices and machines. Figure 85 illustrates this process. The roller 3 is placed between three rolls: the two bottom ones 1 and 4 being driving rolls and the top one 2 being the pressure roll.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Got grinding is effected for imparting them a cylindrical shape and the required surface finish. The top rollers are ground in a circular grinding machine. Depending on the roller design, different grinding

elements.label: text
elements.text: procedures are employed for machining the cots, i.e. centreless grinding is used for top rollers with antifriction bearings, and centreless grinding for rollers of other designs. For instance, rollers with cylindrical through-holes are fitted on special mandrels and centred by means of bevel bushings which are also pulled-on mandrels. Centres in which the mandrel with rollers is fixed, are inserted into the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 133

elements.label: text
elements.text: front and back heads of the machine. Solid top rollers having no centre holes are attached in chucks inserted in the bevel holes of the front and back head spindles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Figure 86 shows the device for centreless grinding of top rollers with antifriction bearings. The device body 8is mounted on the swivelling frame 9 of the machine and attached by means of the bolt 10.The driving roller 1 is actuated from the spindle of the front head. The top roller 2 to be ground is placed in the slot of the hook 4 for which it is necessary to push away the spring 6 by means of the crank 5. A threaded connecting coupling 7is provided for setting the driving roller 1 and supporting roller 3 in working position. The top roller to be ground rotates in opposite direction to the rotation of the grinding wheel. For grinding elastic cots flat grinding wheels are used; these wheels of straight profile, 250 m m in diameter and 32 m m in width are made of synthetic corundum of medium hardness and with grain size from 12 to 16. In grinding, the surface of the elastic cot must not heat above 80°G, as otherwise the structure and property of the rubber are badly impaired. For this reason, grinding is effected in two stages: first, coarse grinding leaving an allowance of 0.2-0.4 m m for further machining and next fine grinding. After grinding it is recommended to powder the roller with mica or other similar material. The roughness of the ground top rollers should not exceed 0.4-0.6 pm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 87. Kinds of deviation in cylind­

elements.label: text
elements.text: rical shape of elastic cots

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of elastic cot surface grinding there might be deviations from the preset cylindrical shape and dimensions, i.e. eccentricity, faceting, and conicity. Eccentricity (Fig. 87a) is caused by the misalignment of the mandrel and worn centre holes. The allowable eccentricity for soft cots is 0.3 m m and for hard ones— 0.02 mm. Facetingm a y be caused by an excessive pressure applied at grinding

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 87b). The allowable deviations in radii R-r for soft cots is 0.03 m m and for hard ones— 0.02 mm. Conicityresults from the improper adjustment of grinders. It is especially evident on long cots (Fig. 87c). For fixed rollers the conicity in diameters D-d must not exceed 0.06 m m and for loosely rotating ones — 0.04 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To increase the service life the rubber and P Y C top rollers should be turned. The top rollers of flax spinning frames differ in their design

elements.label: text
elements.text: 134 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: from the rollers of cotton spinning and other frames. For this reason their repair is carried out in a different way. At repairs the semi-ebonite disks are cleaned and the necks of shafts are turned and ground. Moreover, the shafts of the top rollers used in the drawing units of wet spinning frames are subjected to corrosion. When the semiebonite disks are completely worn they are replaced. In this event, the nuts are unscrewed, the deteriorated semi-ebonite disks are pulled off from the shafts, new disks are pressure fitted, the nuts are tightened and the disks are turned to required dimensions. Special machines are available for unscrewing and screwing-on the nuts, for removing deteriorated and fitting new semi-ebonite disks on the shafts. The top rollers with pressure-fitted semi-ebonite disks are turned and flutes are knurled upon them. The width and diameter of disks must be constant and the same for all disks.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 88. Diagram of reinforced roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: clothing of “arch” type

elements.label: text
elements.text: Rubber cots for top rollers of drawing units as compared with PVC cots present a greater elasticity, are less apt to changes with time and therefore their useful life is longer. Yet, the working surface of rubber cots has a great deal of microirregularities which results in the increased number and breakage rate of windings of the front roller of the drawing unit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The surface processing of elastic cots reduces the surface irregularities and consequently improves the operational features of the cots. On heat treatment of elastic rubber cots, their surface layer becomes smooth and glossy. The optimum conditions for thermal treatment of rubber cots are: a temperature of 300°C and time of treatment— 10 s. A method has been developed for the thermomechanical treatment of elastic cots by a progressive increase in the temperature from 200 to 400°G. In this case, the coated rollers are rolled between plates for 25-35 s on the machine at different heating temperatures. The use of cots subjected to such heat treatment increases their life by 30%.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Reinforced cots are used for heavily loaded drawing units. The combination of reinforcement with interference fit ensures a more reliable fixing and smaller deformation of the rubber coating. Figure 88 shows schematically the reinforced coating of the “arch” type. Serving as a reinforcing element the cord thread helically runs inside the coating 7, which is placed with an interference fit on the top roller 2 with an overlap a at the edges. The useful life of such coatings is twice as that of usual ones. •

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 135

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 89. Device for straightening bent

elements.label: text
elements.text: spindles

elements.label: text
elements.text: SPINDLES. The rotational speed of spindles in spinning frames of different designs reaches 15 000 min'1 and more. For this reason the main requirement set towards the spindles is the absence of strong vibrations leading to an increase in yarn breakage. In the course of operation, the following disarrangements may be observed: residual deflections of spindle blades, wear of rubbing surfaces and spindle

elements.label: text
elements.text: breakage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Bent spindle blades are repaired by straightening. To begin with, the point and amount of deflection are determined. For this, the spindle blade is placed on knife edges or fixed between the centres of the lathe, after which the spindle blade is turned around its axis and the point and amount of deflection are determined by means of an indicator. Straightening may be effected either manually by means of a hand press and copper hammer or by employing different special devices. For straightening bent spindles the so-called static method is used, while for straightening spindles with an inconsiderable residual deflection the dynamic method finds application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In Fig. 89a a universal device is illustrated designed both for static and for dynamic straightening. In the case ofdynamic straightening a split bevel bushing 2 is fitted on the spindles. Then together

elements.label: text
elements.text: with the spindle the bushing is inserted into the bearing with a conical hole 3.The spindle foot bears against the footstep 1 attached on the movable stand 12. Next, the motor is engaged imparting the spindle rotation with a speed of 3000-4000 min-1. The spindle is straightened by turning the lever 5. Static straightening using the

elements.label: text
elements.text: 136 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: device is carried out as follows. The stand is shifted into the slot disposed at an angle of 90° to the longitudinal slot 11.The spindle rests on the footstep, the bed 7 and strap 8 attached in the prismatic m o vable stand 9.From both sides of the point of maximum deflection, collapsible hooks 4 are provided which are articulated by means of

elements.label: text
elements.text: hinges pressed to the spindle by the nut 6;between the hooks there is the lever 5 which presses on the delivery part of the spindle. The precision of straightening ischecked with an indicator. After straighten­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing the hooks are pushed aside on the hinges 10 to release the spindle.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the event of mass repair of spindles, the bent spindle blades are straightened out using a more efficient method of cold work obtained

elements.label: text
elements.text: by reiterated pressure exercised by balls on the spindle, which are pulled out by centrifugal force. The balls 1 (Fig. 896) are arranged radially at a regular distance on the edge of the disk 2 and m a y move

elements.label: text
elements.text: in seats, on disk rotation, each ball rolls out and hits the spindle 3 and rebounds. Here the rotation of the disk is combined with the rotation and longitudinal displacement of the spindle. Therefore, the balls hit each time a new point of the spindle. The straightening process may be adjusted by modifying the rotational speed of the disk and spindle, the diameter and number of balls, the amount of longitudinal feed, the number of passages and the interference fit, i.e. the amount of positive rejection of the ball by the spindle. This method of spindle straightening ensures a sufficiently high accuracy of the operation (up to 0.01 m m in the run-out). The finish class of a cold-worked surface is 1-2 classes higher than that of a ground surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For repairing worn spindles the following methods are used: regrinding, chromium plating, metal plating, building-up, as well as mechanical methods of repairing and restoring with polymer materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Most often the wear of spindle heel results in deformation of its shape. The spindle with a worn heel is regroundby means of a special device or on a machine using intensive cooling.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In chromium plating the surface of worn-out spindles is prepared for the job of grinding on a circular grinder. Next, the spindles are mounted on a suspension, degreased, chromium plated, washed, neutralized and taken off from the suspension. Provided the spindle surface has been thoroughly prepared for chromium plating no further machining is required after plating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n repairing spindles by metalsprayingthe following work is to be done. The worn out surfaces are turned on a lathe and sand blasted, then the spindles are fixed on the lathe and metal sprayed by means of an electric arc or gas-flame metal sprayer attached on the lathe carriage. During metal spraying the spindle is imparted rotation while the carriage with a metal sprayer effects a longitudinal trans-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 137

elements.label: text
elements.text: latory motion. The spindle with the sprayed metal layer is turned on a lathe and ground.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Big and heavy spindles are restored by the building-up method. Prior to building-up the spindles are annealed in a furnace for several hours at a temperature of 740-760°C and left in the same furnace for cooling. After cooling, a small layer of metal is removed with a cutter so as to obtain the required thickness of the built-up layer (1-2 mm). Building-up is carried out by the gas-flame method using a neutral flame by means of a burner of reduced power (by 1-2 Nos.). The built-up spindle is forged, roasted and machined on a lathe leaving an overlap for grinding of 1-1.5 m m taking into account the possibility of strong warping at the subsequent heat treatment (hardening and tempering).

elements.label: text
elements.text: In some cases, to repair worn-out spindle heels different mechanical methods are applied, including the replacement of heels (skeleton spindles). If the hole in the spindle stem has distorted dimensions

elements.label: text
elements.text: and shape, it is primarily reamed and then a ground heel is pressed in. To avoid the violation of centring the heel is finally ground in assembly. Worn large-size spindles are sometimes restored by regrinding to repair dimensions. In this case, the bearings are set for the new dimensions of the spindle. Damaged wooden sleeves for tubes are restored by means of polymer materials. First, the damaged part of the sleeve is turned to obtain a circular groove and then the spindle with the groove is placed in a special mould which is filled with melted capron. After the capron has hardened the worn-out place is restored and the spindle is ready for use.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Broken spindles are repaired only when there are no spare spindles available at the mill. The repair is effected by electric-butt, arc and gas welding. Prior to electric-butt welding, the broken spindle is annealed and then cut for obtaining a proper shape in the broken part. A steel blank is produced with an allowance of 5-7 m m in length for partial melting and burning at welding and of 3-4 m m for machining after welding. The workpiecejis turned with an allow­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ance of 1.5-2 m m for the machining of cylindrical surface after joining. The spindle is welded on an electric-butt welding machine with a power depending on the diameter of the spindle to be repaired. If no such machine is available, the spindles are restored by manual electric-arc or by gas-flame welding. Prior to welding, the spindle is again annealed and the ends to be joined prepared for welding. To ensure a good coaxiality and to reduce the possibility of warping, welding is carried out in jigs which are made to fit the dimensions of the repaired spindles. After welding, the spindle is annealed, dressed, turned, and ground according to required dimensions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The technical requirements set towards the spindle after repairs are: sufficient elasticity and absence of residual deformations; vibra-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 138 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: tions should not exceed allowable values (the run-out of the spindle blade should not exceed 0.06 m m at the top of the sleeve); sufficient resistance to wear; strict correspondence of design dimensions to standards; absence of exterior defects, cracks and others.

elements.label: text
elements.text: TIN DRUMS. Intended to transmit the motion to spindles and consist of a rigid shell,* tin diaphragms and cast-iron flanges (sleeves). In the course of operation, the tin drums are liable to develop the following defects: the vibration, dents on the tin shell, fractures and opened seams, chipping and cracks on the cast-iron flanges, and spindle wear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Tbe vibration (run-out) is determined directly on the spinning frame by means of an indicator (Fig. 90). The watch type indicator 1 is fixed on the rocker 2 with a hinged support 3 arranged on the bracket 4,which is provided with an adjusting screw 7, nuts, and a stop screw 6.The instrument is fixed as a C-clamp on the spindle rail 5 of the spinning frame. The indicator is set by means of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: adjusting screws strictly on the vertical line passing through the centre of the drum which is manually rotated. If the radial run-out of the drum does not exceed 0.7 mm, it may be considered fit for operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: All other defects are detected by inspection and ifit proves necessary the drum is repaired in a special shop. Prior to starting the repair, the tape is removed from the tension roller, as well as 4 or 5 spindles disposed opposite the intermediate bearings of the drum.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Next, the back board of the frame isremoved and using a wrench the connecting bolts of the drum are unscrewed taking care to support the line of drums during this operation by means of a special truckjack. The line of drums is separated in sections by a pinch bar which is placed between the drums or by means of a special separating device. The drum spindle is extracted by a puller (Fig. 91a, b). The puller is fitted with its conical split bushing 3 on the free end of the spindle, and using the screws 1 passing through the traverse 2, the puller is pressed against the drum flange. W h e n the screws are tightened, the conical bushing grasps the spindles and draws it out of the drum. The main shaft is extracted from the head drum by means of the puller illustrated in Fig. 91c. The dismountable traverse 3 with removable inserts 4 is attached on the shaft by the tie 2.The shaft is tightened by two power-transmitting screws 1.

elements.label: text
elements.text: * For wet spinning frames the drum shells are made of tin plate.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 139

elements.label: text
elements.text: n\

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the kind of fault, the repair of spinning frame tin drums involves the following work: dents are flattened, the seams are resoldered, some members are replaced, broken flanges and spindles are restored. The drums should be balanced after repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Dents are straightened out manually (using a hammer, a soldering lamp (blow torch), and mauls) or by means of other devices. For instance, the device shown in Fig. 92 has two wooden or plastic blocks 1 tied together by a frame 4 of angular iron. In the frames slots are provided along which the traverse 5 connected by the screw 2 is moving. A screw passes through the nut 3 attached in the frame crosspiece. The hook 6is attached to the traverse. The device is placed with its wooden blocks on the butt joints of the drum m e m bers; the hook foot is soldered in the middle of the indentation and turning the screw the hook is raised; simultaneously the edges of the indentation are flattened with a wooden hammer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Resoldering seams is done in the case where the seams have become opened or broken in the course of operation. The point of soldering is cleaned with a file, emery cloth or by any other method and the member is tap-soldered in several points. After careful checking on the machine the whole seam is preliminarily coated with flux and soldered. To avoid the deformation of the drum, each quarter of the circumference should be soldered, alternating the operation in diametrical direction. Gross-seams are reinforced by additional soldering through holes drilled in the top sheet of the shell. The distance between two holes should not exceed 75 mm. The diaphragms are tightly fitted to the drum and soldered to its shell. The clearance

elements.label: text
elements.text: 140 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 93. Straightening steady rest

elements.label: text
elements.text: along the circumference should not exceed 0.2 m m and should not appear more than in three points. The length of the clearance should not exceed 25 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When soldering the cast-iron flange to the drum shell, the point of soldering should be preliminarily prepared. Soldering is done flush with the drum surface taking care to obtain an even and clean seam. Adjacent flanges (of the head drum) are soldered so as to obtain the keyways on the same straight line. (The allowance for

elements.label: text
elements.text: displacement is not to be over 0.2 mm.) In terms of economy welded seams may be used taking into account their high strength. However the repair of such drums is a complicated job and their overhaul becomes practically impossible. Therefore, a special device (Fig. 93) is used for simultaneous straightening and resoldering of drums. This

elements.label: text
elements.text: device is made as a steady rest comprising a steel frame 6 (the frame upper brace 5 is collapsible) provided with three straightening rollers 3 (bearingballs).The rollers m a y be displaced in radial direction by means of the screws 2.In the bottom part of the steady rest there is provided a micrometric screw 1 which serves to check the vibration of the drum. The steady rest is mounted on a balancing machine and may be displaced along the guide of the machine 8 and fixed at the required point by the stop screw 7. The drum 4 fixed in the balancing machine and passed through the straightening steady rest is slowly rotated and the point of soldering is uniformly heated along its circumference. Next, by turning the screws 2 the roller is brought to this point. The drum heated at the point of soldering is easily straightened by the rollers. The straightened point is cooled and

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 141

elements.label: text
elements.text: soldered. All the other seams

elements.label: text
elements.text: are straightened and soldered in the same manner. Next, the drum dynamic balancing is carried-out in the same device. The aforementioned device ensures sufficiently accurate soldering so that the drum run-out (vibration) does not exceed 0.7 mm. Recently the method of drum glueing with synthetic glues has found application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the repair of a damaged drum is unfeasible, the drum members are replaced by new ones. In this case, the old m e m ber is eliminated, while the new one is soldered and welded. When spare members are not available, they are produced in the shops of the textile enterprise. A blank is cut-out from a sheet of tin plate 1 (Fig. 94a) in accordance with the dimensions of the member, and passed between the rollers 2 and 3 to impart it a cylindrical shape after which the ends are flanged. Further, the seams are soldered and welded with overlapping (in a spot- and seam welding machine) and carefully dressed. Ready members must engage each other without play. The reinforcement diaphragms are made of the same material as the drum shell. The diaphragm blank is cut out of a sheet and extruded by means of a pressing mould (Fig. 94&) attached in the spindle of the lathe. After the extrusion of diaphragm contour, its edges are flanged.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 94. Rolls and pressure mould

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation the shank (hubs) of the flanges made of gray cast iron may get broken, and the chipping of the rims might occur. Repair of flanges with broken shank is carried out in the following manner: the shank is cut off, holes are bored, a fine thread is cut in the sleeve cup, a new shank is screwed in and welded.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The assembled flange is attached on the lathe, the shank is turned to definite dimensions, a hole is made for the sleeve, and using a milling cutter (a lathe cutter or a saw) a slit is made. The new shank (hub) may be attached to the flange also by six bolts. The flanges with chipped rim are surfaced and then turned on a lathe. If the flange has no other defects except the chipped rim, it is repaired without being separated from the drum. In this case, a kerf is made at the chipped points of the rim on the circumference of the flange, a dovetail groove is sawn and an insert is put into this groove and

elements.label: text
elements.text: 142 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 95. Machine for dynamic balancing of tin drums

elements.label: text
elements.text: soldered. Prior to their installation on the drums, the flanges are subjected to balancing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The head and off-end spindles of the drums come out of order due to the wear of rubbing surfaces. In this case they are repaired as axles and shafts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Special attention in the repair of drums should be paid to balancing (static and dynamic).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Static balancing of drums is carried out on knife-edges. The drum is set with its spindles on the knife-edges and rotated manually. If the drum is not properly balanced, its heavier part always comes to occupy the bottom position. In this case, a recess is made on the opposite side of the drum and filled by soldering with lead until the d r u m is statically balanced. Next, the dynamic balancing of the d r u m is carried out in a special machine (Fig. 95). The drum 4 is placed with its spindles on two split bearings 3 having a prismatic base. One half of the coupling 2 is fixed to the end of the spindle and the second by means of a sliding key— on the driving shaft 1. Next, the motor isengaged to impart rotation to the drum through the pulley 8. Then the coupling is disengaged by the crank 7, i.e. the motion is not any more transmitted to the drum which continues to rotate by inertia. At the same time, one of the bearings is released from rigid fixing (the bolts 5 are loosened). If the drum is not properly balanced the released bearing deviates from initial position and causes the deformation of the spring 6.The heavy part of the drum which has provoked this deviation is marked with chalk. A recess is made on the opposite side of the drum to be filled with lead to achieve drum balancing. With this aim it is possible to use a rubber tyre which is fitted on the drum. After determining which of the drum sides is heavier, a weight is placed under the tyre at its opposite side. By displacing the weight and changing its mass the necessary solder mass and points ofsoldering are determined. Further, all the soldered points are carefully dressed. Balancing is done at high rotational speed of the drum (10% higher than the working rotational speed).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 143

elements.label: text
elements.text: The deviation of the repaired drum diameter after assembly and balancing from the nominal one should not be more than ± 0 5 mm, and the deviation from rectilinearity of the drum generatrix at its installation on the axles as well as the radial run-out should not exceed 0.7 m m (the run-out is checked at the flanges and diaphragms, i.e. in the rigid parts of the drum). The exterior surface of the drum should be smooth, without burrs and indentations. Small dents with a diameter not over 20 m m and a depth not over 0.5 m m are allowable, but in a number not more than five indentations per section.

elements.label: text
elements.text: T E N S I O N R O L L E R S . Ensure a regular tension of the tape in the drive from the drum to spindles. In the course of operation certain defects may appear on the roller rim made of tin plate or thin galvanized steel and on corrugated washers of tin plated or galvanized iron 0.7-1 m m thick, such as indentations, wear of hardened steel shaft and bearings (sliders), loose fastenings, hook wear, etc. When repairing them, the tension rollers are disassembled, dressed and

elements.label: text
elements.text: assembled.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In disassembling the roller, the nuts are unscrewed, the shaft is drawn out, and the rim is flanged. A special device shown in Fig. 96a is used for unscrewing the nuts. The shell 6 mounted on the bear 7 is provided with a recess corresponding to the profile of the tension roller. The roller is placed in this recess so that the bottom nut is in the hexagonal hole of the change plug 4 and is centred with three screws 5.The socket wrench 3 attached on the rod 2 is placed on the top nut of the roller, and turning the crank 1 this nut is unscrewed. Then the roller is ejected by the pusher 9 using the crank 8.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n it is necessary to straighten out the rim or disks of the roller, the latter must be flanged and one part must be separated from the other. For this, the device shown in Fig. 966 is used. The roller with its shaft removed is placed into the recess of the shell 7in which the pusher 6 with head is inserted. The profile formed by the head together with the recess bottom corresponds to the profile of the roller disk. At the end of the rod 3 there is a pin 4which passes through the hole of the roller and is driven into the pusher threaded hole, thus fixing it in the device. Mounted freely on the rod isthe bushing 2 carrying the holder 1with wrench 5 for flanging the roller. The wrench is retained on the holder by means of a bolt round which it may freely turn along the arc of the roller circumference which allows the adjustment of the cutting blade feed during flanging. The cutting blade of the WTench is ground wedgewise in the shape of an oval so that its pointed end penetrates under the edge of the rim flange, while the back part of the wrench by bending the flange straightens it in vertical direction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: This done, the roller is started to be straightened out. The crushed rim is straightened out in a device operating on the rolling principle

elements.label: text
elements.text: 144 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 96. Devices for repairing tension rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 96c). Steel hardened rolls 1 and 2 rest in bearings; the top roll 2 slides on the shaft, while the bottom roll 1 is stationary. A recess provided at the butt of the top roll serves to accommodate the protrusion of the roller half to be straightened. The roll diameter corresponds to inside diameter of this roller half. The clearance between the rollsis adjusted by the screw 3 serving to raise or to lower the upper roll. The crushed rim is placed between the rolls 1 and 2 which are brought together with the screw 3 thus pressing the rim wall. Using the crank 4 the roll 1 is turned and by friction the rim and roll2 are rotated. The rim isstraightened and acquires a correct cylindrical shape. Crushed corrugated roller washers are straightened in a press tool (Fig. 96d) comprising a die 5 with a pusher 1 and a punch 2 attached to the traverse 4;the latter can be displaced along the guiding columns 6 by means of the screw 3. The roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 145

elements.label: text
elements.text: half with the crushed washer is placed in the die and using the screw 3 the punch is pressed, and as the die and punch have the shape corresponding to the washer profile the latter acquires the necessary shape. After straightening the workpiece is ejected by a pusher using the crank.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The assembly of the roller halves after straightening is effected manually. Then the rim flange is crimped in a special device

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 96e). The roller halves are inserted in the seat 6 and the pin at the end of the rod 4 is passed through the hole of the assembled rol­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ler and screwed into the hole of the pusher 7. The pin tightly presses the halves of the roller so that the flange of the exterior roller half protrudes by 1.5-2 m m . W h e n the bushing 3 with the crank 2 is turned the rollers 1 placed on the rim flange cause its rolling-up. To crimp the flange, the crank must be turned several times. The quality of rolling-up depends on the shape of the rollers. It is efficacious to use one conical roller and one double-flanged roller. After rollingup the roller is ejected with a pusher. Then the shaft is inserted and the roller is balanced in assembly.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the case of inconsiderable wear (less than 0.3 m m ) shaftsare restored by chromium plating, but in the event of heavy wear they

elements.label: text
elements.text: are surfaced by spraying or built-up. Frequently worn-out shafts and bearings are replaced by new ones. Worn hooks are restored by using capron bushings. Cotton or capron tape is used as a flexible drive. The longevity of the cotton tape is two months and that of capron tape is two or three times longer. Capron tape is joined by glueing and applying electrical heated tongs. To avoid slippage of the capron tape, the shape of the tension roller is modified by knurling two folds at its butts. Sometimes the tension rollers m a y get out of order to the loosening of the bolt fixing the tape holder. In the course of operation the tape holder is pressed to the tension roller whose wear is caused by rubbing. To avoid this trouble, the tape holder fork is provided with a limiter protecting it from contact with the tension roller and thus ensuring a considerable increase in the useful life of tension rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Open-End Spinning Frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: Lately high-efficiency open-end spinning frames of the type have acquired a widespread use. These spinning frames are available in different modifications. The most typical one is the open-end spinning frame 6,3,-200? with a spinning head spacing of 200 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: This spinning frame is intended for producing cotton yarn with a linear density of 62.5-15.4 tex and yarn with a linear density of 50-20 tex from synthetic and man-made fibres 40 m m long. The spinning frame Bfl-200P consists of the yarn delivery mechanism, the headstock and tailstock gearings, the yarn draw-off ar-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 146 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: rangement with traverse, the building mechanism, the mechanism for threading adjustment and the spinning heads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For preparing the frame to be repaired it is cleaned from wastes and rests of semi-finished products. Repairs should be made strictly according to the schedules. In some cases the centrifuges of the spinning frame Efl-200 are repaired on stands.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Medium repairsare carried out every three months and involve: checking the arms of the building mechanism, the centrifuges (with partial dismantling), the delivery mechanism and yarn traverse with the replacement of faulty parts and units; the adjustment of the severing knives of the reserve bunching mechanism, the inspection of all tension and guiding rollers and the replacement of faulty ones; checking of all belts and the replacement of worn-out ones; checking the fastenings of electric equipment and all other units and parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The complete overhaul of the spinning frame is carried out once a year. All the main units with the exception of the stand are completely disassembled; the all broken and worn-out parts and units are replaced. If necessary the stand is also checked and readjusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Characteristic troubles in the unit of the spinning frame and methods of their elimination are given in Table 4.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Special fitter’s shops are provided at the mills for repairing the spinning heads of spinning frames B^-200. Every fitter in the shop has a specially equipped bench with an electric instrument for checking the sensor and the centrifuge as a whole. Mounted on the bench are pivotable mechanisms for installing the centrifuges in any required position, and plug sockets are provided for connecting vacuum cleaners and soldering irons. The bench has a drawer for keeping tools in it. The working posts have pullers for extracting rotors from centrifuges as well as different tools, soldering irons, gauges and indicators.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Every shop has a work bench provided with vices, tables and a tester for accurate checking of the centrifuge electrical parts. The efficient cleaning of centrifuges is ensured by vacuum cleaners and the tables are equipped with a system for the removal of contaminated air and dust. The centrifuges are transported from the spinning frame to the shop in three-deck trucks accommodating up to 50 spinning heads. Multi-deck racks are available for storing 600 spinning heads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The periodicity of centrifuge repairs in the case of the spinning frame B^-200 is as follows: overhaul— every year (duration— five days); medium repair— every six months (duration 2.5 days); thorough cleaning— every three months (duration one day). At thorough cleaning the spinning heads are cleaned and checked directly on the spinning frame.

elements.label: text
elements.text: spinning head consists of the feeding cylinder 1 (Fig. 97), the funnel 10, the feeding table £, the adjustment screw 8, the spring 7, the combing drum 6, the separator 5, bearing 4, rotating centrifuge 3 and transport canal 2. The main units of the spinning head are: the feeding unit, the combing drum and the twisting and building unit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The feeding unit consists of the feeding roller 1 and the table 9.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kinds of disarrangements are: breakage of the table and funnel wear of the worm gear actuating the feeding roller.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Because the feeding unit cannot be disassembled, it must be completely replaced when its parts come out of order.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The state of the combing drum 6 is determined by the condition of its closing. Its main disarrangements are brokenteethand deterioration of the whole-metal saw-toothed fillet. In this case the combing drum is replaced by a new one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 10 IHi1

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 97, Diagram of spinning head in

elements.label: text
elements.text: open-end spinning frame

elements.label: text
elements.text: The twisting and building unit consists of the centrifuge 3 rotating on a shaft, the bearing 4 and separator 5. The main disarrangements

elements.label: text
elements.text: are: contamination, oil penetration and carbon deposit. In this case, the centrifuge is replaced by a new one. Bearings wear and loose separator fastenings are also a frequent case.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reliability of the spinning head is highly dependent on the strict adherence to establish dimensions in assembly and operation of its units. For this the control and measuring devices shown in Fig. 98a-c find application in maintaining the preset dimensions 7+0.3 an(j 2.6io.’! mm, as well as a clearance of 0.3 mm. In installing the feeding table it is necessary to maintain the dimension A within the minimum and maximum clearances between the table and the feeding cylinder as well as the established pressing effort of the roller to the cylinder. The dimension A is adjusted by means of a special device depending on the kind and length of the processed fibre: for cotton fibre it is equal to 69.2 ±0.1 m m and for main-made fibre— 68.5 ±0.1 mm. The spring effort is checked by a dynamometer, the control effort being equal to 24 ± 1.5 N.
