elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n installing the separator, care should be taken that its shaped cut-out is properly positioned in respect to the inlet hole of the transport canal. For controlling the position of the shaped cut-out use is made of a special device. The separator may be set to two positions: for processing cotton fibre at an angle of 15°, and for processing viscose fibre and its blends with cotton at an angle of 45°.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To ensure the easy rotation of the combing drum, there must be a clearance of 0.3 m m between its end face and the applied gauge.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly of the spinning head in an open-end spinning frame it is necessary to check with a special feeler the clearance of the electromagnetic clutch of the feeding unit, as the proper engagement and disengagement of the feeding cylinder depend on thisclearance. It is also important to check the proper installation of the yarn breakage sensor (in particular, using a special gauge it is ascertained that the carrier does not impede the passage of the yarn into the centrifuge at mass threading).

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is observed that in open-end spinning frames Bfl-200-M69 the yarn sometimes winds on the drawing-off roller causing its scoring. This results in a higher breakage rate and lower yarn quality. For grinding the drawing-off roller the spinning frame should be stopped and the roller taken off.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To increase the machine efficiency it is recommended to grind the drawing-off rollers in the cause of machine operation. For this,, at the point of scoring the pressure roller with elastic cot is removed and in its place a wooden block is put; the block has two working: surfaces coated with emery paper of different grain sizes. The block.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 154 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 99. Vulcanizer for belt glueing

elements.label: text
elements.text: is pressed to the drawing-off roller by a spring. Grinding is first 'done with a coarse emery paper and then with fine emery paper for

elements.label: text
elements.text: which the block is turned about 180°.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Vulcanizer for belt glueing. It has proved efficacious to glue the belts of open-end spinning frame B71,-200-M69 which have come out of order. For this, a special vulcanizer is used consisting of the housing 1 (Fig. 99), the shell 7, terminal 2, insulator 3, cover plate 4, heating element 5 (for 24 V), jimmy bar 8,clip 9 and thrust bearing 10. Prior to glueing the belt is machined to conical shape over a length of 40 mm. Next, it is coated with glue, inserted in the vulcanizer, pressed with bolts 6 and after switching-on the current kept at least two hours at a temperature of 110-120cC. The glue employed for belt glueing consists of hydraulic alcohol, resercine and formic acid ethyl ether.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Note another device available for glueing simultaneously two belts. The device consists of a square 250 X 250 m m sides and •60 m m long made of textile-based laminate; one heating and one ironing element with a thermoregulator are mounted in the hollow middle of the square. On the working part of the iron four flanges are attached forming two grooves in belt width; at the top on stands, .secured in the body of the textile-based laminate a steel strap is

elements.label: text
elements.text: attached having two holes with a thread M14. Spring bolts with washers for pressing the belt through the cover plate are screwed into the hole of the strap.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Device for lubricating the bearings in the centrifuges of the spinning frames Bfl-200. The main cause of disarrangements in the centrifuges •of the spinning frame E,H,-200 is the insufficient lubrication of bearings. A device has been designed for replacing the lubricant under pressure without dismantling the centrifuges.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The device consists of a cylindrical chamber 5 (Fig. 100) housing in its interior part 9 the centrifuge 12, and of a shell 10 having its butt face packed with a gasket 8. The shell 10 is arranged on the annular protrusion before the pulley 17. On the butt face of the pulley there is provided the gasket 6.The interior part of the chamber

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 155

elements.label: text
elements.text: is of the same configuration as the shell 10 and pulley 77 of the centrifuge 12 with gaps for the passage of the lubricant. Fixed to the chamber 5 is the pressure lever 13 with spring 15 and fixing arrangement 14 ensuring a tight adherence of the butt faces of the shell 10 and pulley 17 to the gaskets 8 and 6 and their fixing

elements.label: text
elements.text: in preset position. The injector 19 with a crank 18 and hose 4 is connected to the branch pipe 7 provided in the interior part of the chamber in which the

elements.label: text
elements.text: pulley 77 is arranged between the packing gaskets 8 and 6.The chamber 5 is designed so that on

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 100. Device for lubricating bearings of centrifuges in 6^-200 spin­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ning frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: installing the centrifuge 12 inside it, the top butt face 16 of its shell 10 and the spindle 77 protrude from the chamber long enough to allow the visual control over the discharge of the lubricant excess from the chamber. The injector 19

elements.label: text
elements.text: is mounted on the base 7 to which the chamber 5 is attached by means of the bracket 2 and nut 3. The crank 20 of the injector 19 serves for periodically pumping the grease which is fed by means of

elements.label: text
elements.text: the crank 18 into the cavity of the shell 10.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The device operates as follows: the centrifuge 12 is placed into the interior part 9 of the chamber 5 so as to obtain that the shell 10 bears with its butt face against the gasket 8 and the pulley 77 bears against the gasket 6. Using the lever 13, the centrifuge 12 is pressed by means of the spring 15 and fixed in place by the locator 14. The butt faces of the shell and pulley must be tightly pressed to the gaskets to avoid the leakage of lubricant through the clearances bypassing the cavity of the shell 10. Using the crank 20, the grease is pumped by the injector 19 through the holes 4 and pipe union 7 into the cavity of the chamber 5, i.e. into the zone of the pulley 77 between the gaskets 8 and 6. As a result the grease passes under pressure through the clearances into the cavity of the shell 10, and displacing the old grease lubricates the bearings. The amount of lubricant is controlled at the spindle 77 on the upper butt face 16 of the shell 10. When the bearings are amply greased, the lubricant oozes out from the cavity of the shell 10 in the zone of the spindle 77.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 156 Chapter Five

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly and Adjustment of Spinning Frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly and adjustment of ringspinningframes a special attention should be paid to the rectilinearity of the stand by checking it with a calibrated roller along a string tightly drawn between the

elements.label: text
elements.text: exterior ribs of spindle rails. The difference in the distances between the exterior ribs and the string should not exceed 0.5 mm. The horizontality of the top surfaces of roller beams is checked in longitudinal and crosswise directions by means of a three-metre ruler, a level, and a feeler (the deviation should not exceed 0.15 mm). The ring plates should be mounted strictly horizontal. The total stroke of the condenser should be 18-19 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The deviation of the drafting fields in apron drawing units should not exceed 0.25 m m ; the bottom apron plate should be by 0.2-0.5 m m higher than the level of the working fluted parts of the rollers in the first and third lines; the roller flutes must be smooth without indentations and burrs; separate staffs of rollers should be without longitudinal shift. It is necessary to check the proper adherence of rollers to the stand. Lamellar yarn separators and antiballooning rings must be smooth and without burrs. The deviation of the spindle driving tape in length should not exceed 3 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The web condensers should be free of such surface defects as burrs and indentations. The clearance between the roller and the tube of the broken-end collector should not exceed 3 mm. The tin drums, lines of fluted rollers, tension rollers, gearing in the frame headstock should be easily rotated by hand. The poker bushings are installed strictly vertical, and the yarn separators— in the middle between spindles. Side shifting of the yarn guide along the spindle axis is

elements.label: text
elements.text: not allowed; the yarn guides are set strictly according to a plumb bob. The fluff catchers are mounted according to a gauge at a distance of 1 m m from the traveller.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly and adjustment of spinning-and-twisting frames (of the type I1K-100 with a spindle gauge of 100 m m and IIK-100M), the first drum is mounted according to a gauge so that the distance from the drum butt faces to the flats of the off-end frame is 245 m m ;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the intermediate shafts of the drums must be mounted also using a gauge at a distance of 202.5 and 167.5 m m from the spindle rail.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A distance of 30 m m should be maintained between the butt faces of adjacent drums. The misalignment of the drum head shaft must not exceed 0.05 mm. The stroke of the delivery roller carrier should be equal to 10-13 mm. The load applied on the top roller of the drawing unit should be 80-90 N in the first line, 50-60 N in the second and 40-50 N in the third line. The total shift of the bobbin holder lever along its axis due to the gaps in the joints should not exceed 1.5 m m . The left side of the bobbin holder lever and of the building unit lever must coincide in one plane (the deviation should not exceed 1 mm).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 157

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the assembly and adjustment of open-end spinningframes the following should be taken into consideration: during the adjustment of the brakes, the clearance between the magnetic solid and the

elements.label: text
elements.text: interior part of the adjusting nut should not exceed 0.3 mm; the centrifuge and separator must be strictly coaxial; the play of output shafts in the gear box should not exceed 1 mm; it is not allowed to open simultaneously more than five centrifuges in one section.

elements.text: CHAPTER 6

elements.label: text
elements.text: REPAIR AND ADJUSTMENT OF WEAVING MACHINERY

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Warping Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warping of yarn and threads is carried out in warpers which depending on the method employed for warping are subdivided into beam, section and section-beam warpers (the latter are rarely used).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Preventive scheduled repairs of textile equipment, including those of warping machines, comprise current medium and overhaul repairs. Carried out correctly and in due time current and medium repairs increase the warping machines life.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Current repairs are carried out by shop personnel and consist in the preventive inspection of the equipment by the foreman, assistant foreman and fitter of the shop, for locating and eliminating faults which can provoke the breakage of separate parts and of the machine, as a whole. Such disarrangements are as follows: loose driving belts and pulleys; breakage or loss of protecting guards; loose bolts, keys, and wedge joints; breakage and overheating of bearings; misalignment of brakes and automatic machine stops; breakage of auxiliary parts— braking, yarn guides, etc.; misalignments, indentations and scores on the reed dents, and on the measur­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing roller and warper’s beams; cracks and deformation of parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The adjustment of starting, stopping and braking mechanisms, on which depends the quality of warping is also carried out at current repairs. The current repair of warping machines is carried out according to schedule. The results of inspection and current repairs carried

elements.label: text
elements.text: out on any of the machines are registered by the assistant foreman in the log book.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Medium repairs are effected by a team of repair workers at least every six months when working in two shifts, and at least every four months when working in three shifts. For the time of medium repairs, the warper is stopped and excluded from the production plan. The following jobs are carried out during medium repairs: checking all machine mechanisms; repair of separate units and replacement of worn-out parts; cleaning and checking of ball bearings; turning the shafts, conditioning of drums and cylinders with elimination of indentations and burrs; replacement of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 159

elements.label: text
elements.text: braking belts, cables and chains; checking of repair and chain drives; checking the setting and adjustment of mechanisms by means of gauges; disassembly, checking and adjustment of starting and stopping mechanisms, and replacement of worn-out parts; adjustment of stopping mechanisms; repair and replacement of auxiliary machine mechanisms, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Overhaul repair of warpers is carried out every two years by a team of repair workers and includes: the replacement of all wornout parts and units or their restoration, bringing them to dimensions established by specifications; careful examination, centring and balancing of the units and parts of the machine; checking the machine frames and creels.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Beam Warpers

elements.label: text
elements.text: Beam warpers are intended for high-speed warping of yarn from bobbins onto warper’s beams. As the warper operates, each yarn coming from the corresponding bobbin passes through the yarn guide eyelet, the yarn tension, and yarn guides which support and separate it from adjacent yarns. Further it is guided into the hook of the warper self-stop which comes in action in the event of yarn breakage (signal frame). The hook retains the yarn in raised position and, in case of its breakage, moves down and closes the circuit causing machine stoppage. Yarns pass in a certain order behind the warping reed between the glass guiding rods through an expanding

elements.label: text
elements.text: zigzag-shaped reed, run round the measuring roller and come on the warper’s beam which is rotated from a d.c. motor through a clutch, a two speed box and a V-belt drive. As the diameter of the warper’s beam increases, the condensing roll is displaced and, through the intermediate of the slider connected with it, changes the rotational speed of the warper’s beam, thus ensuring the maintenance of the preset warping linear speed. The machine is provided with independ­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ent braking systems for the warper’s beam, the condensing roll and measuring roller owing to which it may be quickly stopped in case of yarn breakage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A modern beam warper consists of the following units and mechanisms: the stand, the drive, the starting and stopping mechanism, the condensing roll, the warper’s beam changing mechanism, the reed, the measuring roller, the warper’s beam, the manual stop mechanism and the electrical equipment with a unified electric drive system.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The framework consists of cast side frames and several braces. The side frames are provided with reinforcement ribs along the perimeter and surface which considerably reduces their vibration and are tied together by braces, i.e. in the bottom part of the framework there are five braces (three round and two channel braces). Owing to this reinforcement of the frames all the parts of the frame-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 160 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: work present high stability and ensure reliable fixing of mechanisms mounted on it. At adequate points flats are provided on the machine frames to ensure the accurate installation of shaft bearings and

elements.label: text
elements.text: brackets.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drivetransmits the motion from the motor to all mechanisms engaged in the warping process. It must maintain the preset rotational speed of working organs during machine operation. A simple and

elements.label: text
elements.text: reliable circuit is employed in the unified drive for automatically maintaining the preset linear speed of warping independently from the change in the winding diameter on the warper’s beam.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The starting and stopping mechanism is intended for starting the warper and stopping it in case of interruptions in the warping process or for other causes. This mechanism must ensure the rapid enga­

elements.label: text
elements.text: gement and disengagement of motors and warping organs of the warper. It consists of the following independent mechanisms: for

elements.label: text
elements.text: the engagement and disengagement of the drive; for braking the warping organs; and a self-stop coming in action on yarn breakage, and when a warp of preset length has been produced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The condensing roll serves for compacting the winding on the warper’s beam. It consists of the left half 1 (Fig. 101) and right half 4 of the cylinder connected together by the steel ring 3 (new models of warpers are equipped with whole-metal condensing rolls of stain­

elements.label: text
elements.text: less steel). Inside the cylinder at its ends there are bolted cast-iron rims 7which serve for braking the condensing roll. The ball bearings 6 are attached on the disks 5 secured to the rims; these bearings are

elements.label: text
elements.text: fixed in conical bushings on the shaft 2 around which the condenser roller is rotating. During warping the condenser roller is constantly displaced deep into the machine (progressively with the increase of winding diameter of the warper’s beam).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warper's beam change mechanism. Intended for rapid and easy replacement of the full warper’s beams.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The warper’s beam consists of the stemi (Fig. 102) made of steel pipe 240 m m in diameter. At the stem ends there are screwed or threaded 800 m m dia. flanges 2 cast of light alloys. Couplings 3 attached by pins and screws with the stem are inserted in grooves provided inside the pipe at its ends. Locks 4 for joining the warper’s beam with tailstock sleeves are screwed to the couplings. The steel axle 5carrying the ring 6 for reliably fixing the locks on the axle is inserted into the locks and the ring itself is pinned on the axle. The flanges are cast as a whole with the pulleys 7 serving for braking the warper’s beams on the sizing machine. The flanges are provided with reinforcement ribs. The run-out of a 240-mm diameter stem must not exceed 0.5 m m and the end play of flanges 800 m m in diameter must not exceed 1 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is necessary to systematically check the working condition of warper’s and weaver’s beams. Checking of the end play of flanges on

elements.text: F i g . 1 0 1 . W a r p e r c o n d e n s i n g r o l l

elements.label: caption
elements.text: F i g . 1 0 2 . W a r p i n g b e a m

elements.label: text
elements.text: 162 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: warper’s or weaver’s beams is carried out by means of a device with a measurement range from 0 to 15 mm. The readings are obtained with a precision of 0.01 mm. This device is placed with its base 1 (Fig. 103) on the

elements.label: text
elements.text: barrel of the weaver’s beam iTso as to have a small clearance (1-2 mm) between the pins 3and 4 and flange surface. Next, tightly holding the device in place (to avoid its shift in respect to the weaver’s beam barrel), the crank of the meter 6 is turned until one of the lamps of the signalling arrangement 5 lights up indicating that one of the pins 3and 4 comes in contact with the flange surface. Then, the first reading is taken on the scale of the meter 6. After this, the crank of the meter 6 is rotated again until another lamp of the signal arrangement 5 starts burning and a second reading is obtained on the meter scale. The absolute difference between the first and second readings is the run-out of the weaver’s beam

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 103. Device for checking end play of warping beam or weaver’s

elements.label: text
elements.text: beam flanges

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 104. Section warper reed

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 163

elements.label: text
elements.text: flange (or warper’s beam) in the given plane of^measurement. Measurements are made at least in four different points of the flange circumference.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reedserves for guiding and regularly spreading the yarns on the warper’s beam and also for ensuring the preset warping width and the density of yarn winding on the warper’s beam. A special mechanism imparts reciprocal motion to the reed along the axis with

elements.label: text
elements.text: a maximum stroke of 8-10 m m which ensures a regular winding of the yarn on the warper’s beam. (The reeds of latest designs are displaced in two mutually perpendicular planes.) The reed consists of the combs 1 (Fig. 104) inserted into the stand 2 of the staffs 3 articulated together and forming a zigzag line. This line is screwed on the nuts 4fitted on a screw roller 5mounted on the beam. On the right- and left-hand ends of the screw roller hand wheels are provided: the first one is used for adjusting the width and density of warping and the other for adjusting the position of the reed in respect

elements.label: text
elements.text: to the warper’s beam.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The mechanism for braking the warper's beam and the condensing roll and measuring roller is constituted of powerful double-shoe

elements.label: text
elements.text: brakes disposed at both ends of the beam and rollers. During the time the warper is in operation the whole braking mechanism is

elements.label: text
elements.text: disengaged and the brakes are engaged at machine stoppage. Braking and unbraking of the warper’s beam, the condensing roll and the measuring roller occur simultaneously. The disarrangements most

elements.label: text
elements.text: often encountered at warping in beam warpers are listed in Table 5.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Section Warpers

elements.label: text
elements.text: Section warping machines are intended for warping the yarns in sections on the drum with subsequent beaming them on the weaver’s beam. Each section is laid on the drum by means of a reed

elements.label: text
elements.text: provided on the warping table, which at each drum revolution is displaced over a nominal distance. A certain number of sections form a warp which iswound onto the weaver’s beam. As sections are produced, the machine shifts so as to ensure centring of the warping table in respect to the creel. There are two types of section warping machines: type I— machines for warping woolen and cotton yarn;

elements.label: text
elements.text: type II— machines for warping yarns of natural and synthetic fibres as well as glass fibres.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The section warping machines consist of the following main mechanisms: the framework, the drive, the drum, the warping table; the drum starting mechanism, the counter, the feeding mechanism, the beaming mechanism, and the warp length counter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The framework is assembled of channels. It carries the frames, braces and all the machine mechanisms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: consists of an electric motor, a speed variator, a reducer with electro­

elements.label: text
elements.text: magnetic couplings and a speed regulator. The drum and weaver’s beam are imparted rotation from the electric motor through V-belts, the speed variator, a chain drive, the reducer with electromagnetic couplings and a V-belt drive for the drum, and friction coupling for the weaver’s beam. A mechanical friction clutch is additionally provided on the weaver’s beam drive. The speed of warping and beaming is maintained automatically. A stepless procedure is employed to regulate the speed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drum of the first type warping machine is a whole-metal cylindrical part with a cone the angle of which changes from 6 to 26°. The cylinder is made of aluminium sheet, and the variable cone consists of 24 telescopic wedges. The cone angle is modified by means of a leverage system and a movable coupling.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drum of the second type warping machine is a whole-metal cylinder with a constant cone. The cylinder and cone are made of

elements.label: text
elements.text: aluminium sheets and from both sides the drum is provided with belt brakes ensuring the rapid stoppage of the machine and normal braking of the drum in warp beaming. The brake is equipped with

elements.label: text
elements.text: an automatic regulator to maintain a constant warp tension in beaming. The braking force is adjusted by the brake regulator.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The warping table consists of a carriage with a reed, a measuring ruler, a friction clutch and a bracket for mounting the static elimin­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ator. Mounted on the warping table is the lease reed and the shedding motion for laying the lease. The warping table together with the carriage rests on the guide and travels in ball bearings along it. Serving as a second support for the table, the stands connected with

elements.label: text
elements.text: the car house the end switches for the automatic engagement of the machine displacement motor. The machine is periodically displaced with a speed of 2.03 m/min. The deviation of the warping table from the creel centre is equal to 70 mm, i.e. to the distance between the end switches.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drum startingmechanism effects the engagement and stoppage of the machine. The engagement and disengagement are effected from one treadle running along the machine. The mechanism has treadle levers loosely fitted on the shaft. Through pawls they are connected with the unbraking levers and are fixed in working position by a locator connected with the electromagnet and disengagement pawl.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The counter mechanism ensures machine stoppage after a preset number of revolutions and when a complete section isfinished. A tachometer is provided to determine the warping speed. The warp length counter and tachometer are actuated from the drum through a chain drive, a friction speed variator and a reducer; and the counter of revolutions— from the drum through a chain drive, a reducer and a worm couple.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During overhauls, the warping machine is completely dismantled with the exception of the framework. After dismantling the parts are washed, wiped and examined for wear. The machine framework is checked with a lever. As they are assembled, the mechanisms are checked for easy rotation by hand and their operation is adjusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kinds of disarrangements in section warping machines, their causes and methods of elimination are listed in Table 6.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Adjustment and Lubrication of Beam Warpers

elements.label: text
elements.text: Adjustment. The adjustment is carried out without the warper’s beam, proceeding in the following order:

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. The treadle 1 (Fig. 105) is depressed with the foot at which the pawl 9 moves behind the tooth of the catch 10. The clearance between the levers of the treadle 1 and the brace must be 5-8 mm. The clearance is adjusted by changing the length of the rod 12 using the tie with subsequent fixing it with nuts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When the treadle is released by taking off the foot, it must be raised upwards by the spring IS.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. By adjusting the length of the rod 18 a position is obtained in which the braking pulley of the warper’s beam may be easily turned

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 105. Diagram of section warper brakes

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 169

elements.label: text
elements.text: by hand. The left-hand braking pulley 19 is adjusted in the same manner.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. By adjusting the length of the bolt 8 a position is obtained in which the normally open contacts close with a 2-3 m m overrun of the rod of the end switch 1BK.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4. On engagement of the machine, the lug on the left lever of the treadle 1 must press against the roller of the end switch 2BK and shift it over an angle ensuring a sharp change-over of the contacts. On return of the treadle upwards the lug must release the roller of the end switch 2BK. The position of the end switch is adjusted by displacing it along the frame together with the bracket.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 5. By disengaging the machine which is made by turning the catch 10and releasing the pawl 9 it is necessary to check: (a) clearance between the head of the bolt 8and the rod of the end switch 1BK. If there is no clearance it must be obtained by modifying the length of the rod 17. The clip of the rod 17 must be pressed to the brace under the action of the return spring 13. If the clip of the rod 17 does not reach the brace, it is necessary to locate the rod wdiich impedes the motion and to release it; (b) clearance of 1.5-2 m m between the levers 15 and 16. The clearance is adjusted by modifying the length of the rod 18; (c) clearance between the butt tooth of the bushing of lever 16 and the tooth of the bushing of the lever on the treadle 1; the clearance from the right and left sides of the machine must be equal to 1.5-2 m m to protect from teeth impact on machine stoppage. The clearance is adjusted by modifying the length of the spring of treadle 1.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 6. On machine engagement the condenser roll and measuring roller are checked for easy rotation. By adjusting the length of the rod 11 it is possible to obtain easy rotation by hand of the condenser roller. A clearance must be maintained between the braking plate 6 and the roller of the condensing roll 7. W h e n the machine is disengaged the condensing roll must be braked. By adjusting the length of the rods 3 the easy rotation of the measuring roller by hand is

elements.label: text
elements.text: achieved and when the machine is in disengaged position the force of its braking is adjusted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 7. The braking of the warper’s beam and of the condensing roll and measuring roller is definitely adjusted so as to obtain their simultaneous stoppage; the adjustment is effected by modifying the tension of the springs 2, 4 and 5 when processing the first warper’s beam.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 8. The rapid rotation of the lever 14 with the roll on machine stoppage, ensuring a reliable operation of the brakes, is obtained by adjusting the spring 13.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In gaiting the machine the yarns are passed in each reed dent. The ya ns may also be placed every other tooth, but in that case the reed must necessarily be shifted. The amount of reed shift must

elements.label: text
elements.text: 170 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: be equal to the yarn laying pitch. In installing the warper’s beam, the machine must be engaged in the power line, the warper’s beam must be rolled on the lifting levers and the push button “warper’s beam” must be depressed. The lifting levers will butt against the rests and the safety clutch will turn. Next, the button “tail spindle” must be depressed and the safety clutch will be brought in operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In case of improper operation of the safety clutches, they must be adjusted, for which it is necessary to loosen the counter nuts, to tighten the clutch screws as far as they will go and then to turn out the screws over 0.5-1 coil. At the same time, the warper’s beam must be checked for proper lifting, lowering and clamping by the tail spindles. The warper’s beam should be rotated by its flange so as to obtain that the tail spindle catches engage the beam recesses. The extreme position occupied by tbe tail spindles when they are set apart, is set by means of an adjusting bolt which butts against

elements.label: text
elements.text: a finger when the coupling ratchet comes in action. It is not allowed to rotate the tail spindles by motor without the warper’s beam in place.

The amount of grease packed in the ball bearings shells should be equal to about 3/4 of their free space. Open gearings should be greased at least once a week; and articulated joints and chains should be lubricated by means of a hand oiler with industrial oil after each machine cleaning, but not fewer than once a week.

elements.text: Adjustment and Lubrication of Section Warping Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drum brake* The adjustment is started with the drum braked. Using the handwheel 2 (Fig. 106) the spring is tightened so that its length is about 340 mm. Next, by modifying the length of the rod 3 a clearance of 1.5-2 m m is set between the roller 5 and the lever 4. The drum should be braked at 3/4 of a turn which is achieved by the definite tensioning of the spring (its length may be in this case somewhat greater than 340 mm). When the drum is unbraked, the braking belt must retreat from the surface of the braking pulley. The clearance is adjusted by shifting the fingers 1.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drum revolution counter. Prior to machine running-in after the erection, it is necessary to adjust the normal tension of the mechanism driving chain and to check the easy displacement of the slider 7

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 107) along the thread of the drum 4 and the guiding shaft 6. For checking, the slider 7 must be retreated, so that the operator must pull the crank 1 until it comes out of the drum helical groove and must manually displace it several times along the shaft 6.Next, the slider must be set at the beginning of the groove so as to bring its butt face in coincidence with the match mark (the beginning of count). Releasing the drum the worker must rotate it from himself until the slider passes the whole thread (it must be an easy displacement along the drum). Then it is necessary to insert the stopping pins (pegs) according to the preset operational cycle. The distance between the pin holes is equal to one revolution of the warper’s drum (3 m). If there is deviation of the slider for laying the leases the indicator “Lease Laying” lights up, and for warp replacement two other lamps “Lease Laying” and “End of Warping” start burning which is achieved by adjusting the screws under the lugs 3 and 2. Prior to warping the butt face of the slider 7 must be brought in coincidence with the match mark on the drum and the handwheel 5 after which the drumlis to be fixed on the shaft. At this time, the section must be attacked on the warper’s drum. For passing from warping to beaming, the drum must be released and the slider should be shifted away outside the drum limits, as otherwise mechanism breakage might ensue.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The counter of warp length is engaged individually for each new section, proceeding in the following order: (1) the handle 1 (Fig. 108)

elements.text: is set in the fixing slot on the guards at wnich the friction disk 2 must retreat from the cone 8; (2) turning the handle 3 the finger 4 is engaged in the vertical slot of the carriage 5, at which the slider 6 must be disengaged with the screw 7; (3) the carriage is shifted in left-hand extreme position after which the handle 3 is pressed and turned to the right until the finger 4 passes into the horizontal slot of the carriage 5 as far as it will go; (4) the handle 1 is brought out of the slot and as a result the friction disk 2 is pressed to the cone 8. At machine operation the carriage 5 is displaced to the right along

elements.label: text
elements.text: the screw 7 together with the friction disk which actuates the counter and tachometer.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drum starting mechanism. The proper position of the mechanism elements is adjusted by pressing the treadle 1 (Fig. 109a). The treadle plate must be 4-5 m m higher than the deck. The rest 3 provided in the bracket 2 must press on the lever 10 (the lever is shifted under the rest 3 by means of screws 4 and 5) which resting on the finger 9 turns together with the lever 8 and shaft 7 over about 8° from the horizontal (20 mm), this being achieved by setting the rest 3.The lever 6 turns the drum brake lever causing drum unbraking. The vertical arm of the lever 1 (Fig. 1096) moves behind the plate 2 and fixes in place the starting and braking systems. To avoid the action of the pawl 4 on the lever 1 at starting, it is necessary

elements.label: text
elements.text: 174 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 109. Section warper drum starting mechanism

elements.label: text
elements.text: to set the rest 3 so that the pawl 4 goes past the lever 1.O n repeated pressure of the treadle the pawl 4 must engage the lever 1 and bring it in disengagement with the lever 8 (see Fig. 109a). At this time, under the action of braking springs (not shown in the drawing) the drum brake lever turns all the systems in reverse direction and the mechanism will be ready for starting. The general stroke of the lever 8 is about 14 m m .

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warping table. The warping table is mounted on the top guide 1 (Fig. 110a, b) of the machine-framework. The lead screw la is to be set parallel to the drum cylinder generatrix by shifting the left-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 175

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 110. Warping table of section warper (a) warping table arrangement; (6) lead screw adjustment

elements.label: text
elements.text: hand bearing. The engagement of the gear 3a with the lead screw must be without oscillation but not tight. The adjustment is effected by displacing the guide 1 and turning the eccentric fingers 7. The carriage 4 of the warping table should not oscillate. The clearance between the guide 1 and bearings attached on fingers is adjusted by turning the eccentric finger 5. The warping table can be displaced over the entire length of the guide. The engagement and disengagement of the gear 3a with the lead screw la is effected by turning

elements.label: text
elements.text: the lever 2a. W h e n the gear is engaged with the lead screw the warping table to which a force of 700 N is applied cannot be displaced along the guide.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When the first section is processed, the warping table is set so that the extreme yarns accurately coincide with the beginning of the drum cone. For this, the rule 3 must be released by turning the lever 6 and fixed again after setting at a distance equal to the section width. To avoid overlapping when warping yarns of synthetic fibre the rule is placed at a distance much superior to the section width

elements.label: text
elements.text: (as determined in practice). In this case, the slider 2 must be released by turning the lever 8 and fixed again according to the guide. When placing the following section, the carriage should be brought up to butting against the slider 2 and fixed in place. The slider 2 should be set in the same way as when processing the firstsection. W h e n laying the leases the frame with guiding rods should be collapsed in back position to allow all the yarns to assemble in one section. Then, turning the handle the lease reed is to be raised or lowered for forming a shed. The reed must easily move and must be balanced with weights.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 176 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: Beaming mechanism. For weaver’s beam installation, it is necessary to proceed as follows: shift the complementary stock 3 (Fig. Ill) in right-hand extreme position (by the flywheel or manually).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Using the flywheel 5 put the gear out of meshing with the worm 6; insert the weaver’s beam pin in the stock bushing, and bring the second (driving) stock 2 close to the weaver’s beam. Both stocks are

elements.label: text
elements.text: to be joined together by the strap 4 and the weaver’s beam adjusted according to the warp width, i.e. the weaver’s beam disks should be set opposite the width of the top winding layer on the drum and the ends of the warp are to be threaded on the weaver’s beam. It is necessary to check that the switch “Warping”— “Beaming” is set

elements.label: text
elements.text: at the mark “Beaming”.Adjust the counter and shift away the levers for rolling-out the weaver’s beam. The treadle should be depressed, and using the microscrew 1 the weaver’s beam must be adjusted according to the warp, after which using the flywheel the gears are to be engaged with the worms. The weaver s beam may be stopped by actuating the treadle or by the counter after the predetermined length of warp has been produced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Weaver’s beam starting mechanism. The coupling disks must be compressed and the lever 10 (Fig. 112a, b)must bear with its vertical arm against the strap 7.When the pedal 6 is in bottom position, the clearance between the pedal rings and the bottom channel (tie)

elements.label: text
elements.text: must be 3-4 mm. The pressing ball 4must be set so that the pawl 5 would lower and press on the finger 9.The pawl 8must deviate from the horizontal arm of the lever 1 which is obtained by the displacement of the boss on the pawl 8. The head of bolt 2 must be 35 m m away from the lever 3, while the lever itself must be in vertical position. At the second lowering of the pedal the pawl 8must engage the lever 10 and bring its vertical arm out of engagement with the lever 7, thus causing the coupling disengagement. In the event of coupling disk wear, the dimension 122 between the axes of the ties must be reduced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Construction of magnetic clutches. T h e r e d u c e r c h a n g e - o v e r m e c h a n ism is a device with two magnetic clutches consisting of a shell, a pack of friction disks, and an armature.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The coil is attached in the slot of the shell by means of a grouting mass on the basis of epoxy resin. A plastic insulation ring with a pressure-fitted contact ring inside it is mounted on the clutch shell. The reliable fixing of the insulation ring on the shell is ensured by knurling the seating surface, the use of epoxy resin glue and cylindrical pins. The contact ring ismade of steel hardened to Rockwell C 60-62 and reliably joined with the insulation ring made of fabricbased laminate or glass reinforced plastic. One outlet wire of the coil is soldered to the butt face of the contact ring and the other to the clutch bobbin.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Friction disks are made of steel with a hardness of Rockwell G

elements.label: caption
elements.text: F i g . 1 1 1 . D e v i c e f o r w a r p b e a m i n g f r o m d r u m t o w e a v e r 's b e a m

elements.label: text
elements.text: 178 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: 40-45. Provided between the inferior disks are wave-shaped springs releasing the friction disks on clutch disengagement.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The clutch armature consists of three parts. The interior bronze bushing insulates the armature from the shaft owing to which the dispersion of the magnetic flow through the shaft is reduced and the armature can freely move on clutch engagement and disengagement. The bronze bushing is pressure-fitted into the interior armature ring with which the exterior armature ring is joined with a clearance fit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: This design, ensures tight adherence of the armature to the friction disks and compensates for the possible irregularity in the thickness of the pack of friction disks at the level of the inside and outside diameters.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Maintenance of the magnetic clutches. It is guaranteed that at a rotational speed of 500 min^1 the clutch will make at least two million switchings. In this case, the disk wear is 2 5 % from the initial mass which is to be considered as the maximum admissible value. A greater wear is dangerous for the disk strength.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The clutch is lubricated with industrial oil. Prior to filling the oil, the clutches as well as the tank must be carefully cleaned from fine chips, cast iron dust, etc. From 8 to 9 litres of oil are to be filled into the reducer, and the magnetic clutch disks must be immersed to 15-25 m m in the oil. The disk cooling and oiling would be much worse for the low oil level. The examination of oil condition and its level is done with the reducer cover removed and the machine at standstill. The lubricant oil ages quicker with the operation of units equipped with clutches than with gearings. For this reason, it is necessary to take care that the oil temperature in the tank does not exceed 50°C and should be maintained within the limits of 30-40°C. During the work it is necessary to establish the most adequate regularity of oil replacement. The brush wear should also be periodically checked by determining the travel remaining in reserve. For this, the brush holder is unscrewed one turn and the broken contact (no voltage) means that the central part of the brush holder must be replaced. The brush can be made of brass ribbon and fine net wound into a roll.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sequence of clutch assembly. The clutch operation greatly depends on the sequence in which the disks and spring washers are to be installed. First, the movable armature is fitted on the shaft and upon it in consecutive order: the external friction disk, the internal disk, then again an external disk carrying the first spring washer, and so on. The last internal disk is placed on the external disk and spring washer, and the clutch coil is put in place. It is not allowed to use deformed disks. The disks prior to installation are checked on a smooth Hat plate without dents and scratches and distorted disks must be straightened. The armature free stroke must

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 179

elements.label: text
elements.text: not exceed 5 mm. A greater travel of the aimature increases the time for putting the clutch in action and bringing the machine to

elements.label: text
elements.text: speed at starting. An increased free travel of the armature may be the cause of its misalignment on the slotted bushing, the non-engagement of the clutch and the overheating of its disks. For reducing the armature travel before its installation, a flat ring of any antimagnetic material (bronze, aluminium, fabric based laminate, etc.) of adequate thickness is fitted on the shaft.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Sizing Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sizing machines are intended for applying the size on the warp yarns, squeezing out the excess of size, drying the warp yarns and winding them on the weaver’s beam with preset density. These machines are complex ranges equipped with devices for the automatic adjustment and control of processing parameters. The main parts of any sizing machine are: the creel for warper’s beams (or weaver’s beams); the framework and drive; the sizing unit, the drier, the separating rods and reed for separating the glued warp yarns; the winding mechanism, the measuring and marking mechanism, complementary arrangements (emulsifying unit or waxing unit); the automatic devices for controlling the sizing process and maintaining preset parameters.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sizing unit consists of the size box, squeezing rolls, and immersion device. It may have one or two couples of squeezing rolls. The sizing boxes in the main are without size circulation with the exception of machines for sizing man-made yarns and yarns from a blend of man-made fibres.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drying unit is the main part of the sizing machine that serves for drying sized yarns. Drying of yarns in the drier is done by the

elements.label: text
elements.text: contact, convection, or combined methods. Depending on the drying method employed, the sizing machines are classified into cylinder, hot air, combined, and special sizing machines. Most largely used in the cotton, flax and silk industries are cylinder sizing machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: (from 2 to 13 cylinders). The cylinders are arranged in two vertical rows. The cylinders which are the first from the sizing box have

elements.label: text
elements.text: antiadhesive coatings. Hot air sizing machines are most widely applied in the flax and woollen industries; in these machinesthe sized yarns are dried with hot air. Combined sizing machines were

elements.label: text
elements.text: 182 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: manufactured before for the silk industry. Sizing machines in which special drying methods are employed (high-frequency currents, ultraviolet rays, and gas) have not yet found wide practical application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sizing machine is prepared for repairs by cleaning it from threads, disengaging the steam supply and discharging the size. The following operations are carried out during medium and over­

elements.label: text
elements.text: haul repairs of sizing machines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Medium repairs. Medium repairs of mechanisms are the same both for cylinder and hot air sizing machines and include the following jobs:

elements.label: text
elements.text: replacing the worn-out bearings of the warper’s beams pins, repairing devices for longitudinal displacement of bearings, checking the frames setting and fastenings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: cleaning and examining the size trough, and carrying out necessary repairs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: examining the guiding rollers, draw roller, skeleton roller, the mechanism for lifting and lowering the skeleton roller and making required repairs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: taking off the squeezing rolls, checking the copper jackets for proper fastening and examining the rollers, the glands and bearings, machining the worn-out shaft necks, repairing all faulty parts, removing the old coating from the top squeezing rolls, cleaning the

elements.label: text
elements.text: rolls and painting them with white then placing a new coating, inspecting the squeezing roller lifting mechanism and making necessary repairs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: checking the condition of the parts in the measuring and marking unit and the counter;

elements.label: text
elements.text: removing winding and examining the delivery roller; disassembling and examining the friction clutch, and repairing its parts, replacing gaskets between the friction clutch disks with new ones that must be oiled and rubbed with graphite prior to their installation, replacing the felt and checking the belt braking;

elements.label: text
elements.text: dismantling and examining the equalizing mechanisms, the differential and speed box, and making necessary repairs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: checking the parts of the pressure arrangement; ascertaining that the guards are in place and in good order, examining and cleaning all the gearings, and replacing worn-out gears;

elements.label: text
elements.text: checking the condition of belt drives and making necessary repairs, dismantling the drive for idle and slow run of the machine and making necessary repairs, examining and repairing the speed variator;

elements.label: text
elements.text: examining the guiding rollers, their bearings, straightening bent and crushed rollers, repairing the worn necks and replacing worn-out bushings;

elements.label: text
elements.text: examining the bearings of machine rotating parts, and after the elimination of defects, washing and lubricating them;

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 183

elements.label: text
elements.text: packing the bearings and grease cups with fresh grease; checking the operation of the reducer, safety valve, pressure gauge, and their three-way cocks;

elements.label: text
elements.text: examining the pipelines and checking devices, eliminating leakages and steaming in pipe connections, and lapping all faulty valves and inserting the glands;

elements.label: text
elements.text: examining and repairing automatic devices, such as thermoregulators, level and humidity regulators, including the electrical wiring.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing drying cylinders it is necessary: to examine their bearings and necks, to eliminate the defects, to wash the bearings and to fill them with fresh oil; to examine the drive of the drying cylinder, to check the condition of gears, the operation of buckets

elements.label: text
elements.text: in drying cylinders and to repair the faulty ones; to check the condition of the drying cylinder surface and the shell fastening; to check the operation of safety and air valves in the cylinder bottoms;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to replace the grease in the glands of drying cylinders; to examine, to clean, and to repair the steam traps; to inspect the cover of drying cylinders and the hood above the sizing trough; to make necessary repairs; to repair the insulation of the drying cylinder bottoms and steam lines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When repairing the drying chamber of sizing machines it is necessary; to examine and repair the reels; to check the windmill operation, to inspect the fixtures and condition of blades; to check the operation of the exhaust fan; to examine the air heaters and to replace the faulty ones; to replace the gaskets with steam leakage; to examine the cover of the drying chamber and the hood above the sizing trough and to make necessary repairs; to examine the guiding rollers and to clean them from clogged dirt; in hot air sizing machines— to examine the heating and ventilation systems, the nozzles, ducts, air heaters and filters and to make necessary repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The list of operations carried out at medium repairs is not full and depending on the kind of machines it must be established more precisely. For example during medium repairs of a hot air sizing machine the following jobs are carried out: the repair of the friction clutch, reducer and speed variator with partial dismantling; the inspection of the working condition of reels, cylinders and wind mills checking the fixtures of the reel ties and the blowers for run-out; dismantling the squeezing rolls and checking the axle boxes, links and drawing rolls; examining and adjusting the creel for warper’s beams; repairing the reed and counter; checking the good sealing of air heater and steam line connections; checking the size line and coils; repairing the wooden panels of the machine hood; examination of the condition of exhaust fans with their disassembling, washing and lubrication of ball bearings and of the machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 184 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: In a cylinder sizing machine the following additional jobs are carried out: the differential is repaired with partial dismantling, the cylinder man-holes are opened, the pouring ladles are examined, the pressure vacuum belts are lapped, the working condition of glands is checked and the grease is replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Overhaul. During overhaul repairs it is necessary: to disassemble and examine the entire machine, to clean and select the parts which are not fit for repair;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to check the condition of frames of warper’s beams, the size trough, the drying cylinders (or drying chamber), the front part of the machine, and to ascertain their proper installation using a plumb bob and a water level as well as their reliable fastening (the frames must be mounted strictly symmetrical to the machine axis);

elements.label: text
elements.text: to take out the perforated pipes from the size trough, to disassemble the pipelines, to clean and repair them; to examine the size trough and if necessary to repair it;

elements.label: text
elements.text: the bent rollers, shafts and the skeleton rollers are to be straightened and checked on a lathe.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In case of cavities and defects on the surface of the bottom squeezing rolls the latter must be turned and ground (as considering that the roll diameter will be reduced, it is necessary to use another drive for maintaining the same speed of the rolls), the felt must be removed from the top squeezing rolls, the surface must be cleaned, coated with white paint, and the rolls must be covered with new felt;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to put in place the drying cylinders, check the proper installation of the cylinder with a water level and the parallelism of the rolls to each other and in respect to the squeezing roll (the bearings must be packed with fresh grease and the cylinders must easily turn in the bearings), check the proper fixing of the toothed gear sectors on the cylinders and the correct balancing of drying cylinders;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to examine and repair the ladles and safety devices of the drying cylinders;

elements.label: text
elements.text: in sizing machines with air drying, the reels and fans (blowers) are to be put in place and the bearings filled with fresh oil. In hot air sizing machines it is necessary to examine and repair rollers,

elements.label: text
elements.text: ventilation and heating devices (nozzles, ducts, filters, air heaters), to examine the heating batteries and to replace the faulty ones;

elements.label: text
elements.text: using a level to install the side shaft with gears parallel to the machine centre line;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to check the conical driving pulleys, the condition of the necks and fixing of gears on the shafts and to install the shafts in place;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to inspect and repair drives for transmissions, conoids and slow running. In transmissions with a speed variator, it is necessary to repair the variator, the centrifugal clutch, and the slow-speed reducer;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to repair the delivery roll and install it parallel to the squeezing roll and drying cylinders;

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 185

elements.label: text
elements.text: to examine and if necessary repair the equalizing mechanisms and the speed boxes;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to carry out the repair of counters, pressure mechanisms reeds and emulsifying unit;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to repair guards and air ducts; to check and repair the steam lines, the flange connections and the insulation of the drying cylinder pipelines;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to take off the pressure gauges, to send them for checking and toreturn them in place after checking;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to return in place after examination and repairs the reducer, the safety valve and steam traps, the temperature and size level regulators, as well as the humidity regulators;

elements.label: text
elements.text: to fill the oilers and to lubricate the entire machine; to check the condition of the electrical equipment, the wiring of starting devices, the groundings, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: after machine assembly is completed it must be tested at slow running, the defects must be eliminated and the whole unit must be checked after which the machine must be tested at working speed. The list of overhaul operations is not complete and when compiling-

elements.label: text
elements.text: the list of defects for repairs, modifications m a y be introduced taking into account the type and condition of the equipment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Characteristic faults in sizing machines and methods of their elimination are given in Table 9.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Cylinder Sizing Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: Modern cylinder sizing machines (of the beam and section type)> consist of the following units and mechanisms: the creel for warper’s beams (beam warper’s sizing machines) or creel for the weaver’s beam (section warper’s sizing machines); the lease rod mechanism; the sizing unit; the cylinder drier (7-9 cylinders); the steam and condensate line; the lease rod field and the delivery unit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The creel for warper’s beams is made of rolled steel and accommodates 8-12 beams with a flange diameter up to 800 mm. The braking of warper’s beams is effected by elastic brakes arranged on the outside diameter of the beam flanges. During creel repair, therigidity is restored by welding the defectuous places, the brakes are-

elements.label: text
elements.text: adjusted and if necessary the braking belts and springs are replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The lease rod mechanism is intended for separating the warp yarn and laying between them lease rods; it consists of the rack for the lease rods and the reed. During the repair of this mechanism, the faulty reed isreplaced by a new one. If the worn reed may be repaired

elements.label: text
elements.text: it is restored by soldering the teeth, and if the feed is worn out it isreplaced with a new one.

elements.text: 192 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: means of squeezing rolls. The sizing unit consists of the framework, the tank for the size, the tank lifting mechanism, the immersion and measuring rollers, the top squeezing rubber-coated roll and the bottom squeezing metal roll (the driving one). A special tank with a size pipeline is provided for size circulation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Theframework is a structure made of two cast-iron stands mounted on a common welded frame of rolled steel, these stands being braced

elements.label: text
elements.text: together. The framework carries all the assemblies and mechanisms of the sizing unit. Arranged inside the stand guards are the mechanism for lifting and lowering the immersion roller and the control panels of the tank lifting mechanism and of the squeezing roll pressure mechanism. During repair of the framework its rigidity is restored by welding the defectuous points.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sizetank is made of stainless steel sheet. A special mechanism consisting of a double-stroke pneumatic cylinder and a leverage system ensures its lift and lowering. The tank is filled with size through two branch pipes of the size duct and also from the system supplying the size in the roller nip. The tank design ensures a const­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ant circulation of the size, i.e. the size coming into the tank from the reservoir reaches the level of the tank edge and overflows into the discharge opening, after which it is returned into the reservoir via the discharge mains. For discharging the size remaining below the level of the tank edge, an outlet is provided in the tank which is connected by pipelines with the circulation tank and the sewage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The size remaining in the tank may be discharged back into the reservoir and the water after washing— into sewage. The aim of tank repairs is to eliminate possible leakages. After repair (welding) the joint tightness is checked by flooding the tank with water and the circulation pump and size duct are cleaned.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The immersion roller (130 m m in diameter) is made of stainless steel and mounted in sliding friction bearings which are connected with the racks of the immersion roller lifting and lowering mechanism. The racks are actuated from the drive consisting of an a.c. motor and a worm reducer. The top and bottom positions of the immersion roller are fixed by end switches through the intermediate of two rests mounted on the right-hand rack. If necessary the bearings are replaced and the rack and rests are repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The top squeezing rollmade of a steel pipe with an elastic rubber coating is mounted in antifriction bearings on the pressure mechanism levers. The top squeezing roll ispressed to the bottom one through a leverage system from two pneumatic chambers. A special locator is provided for fixing the roll in upper position when the machine is stopped for a long time.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During the operation of the sizing machines cavities are formed on cast iron squeezing rolls which renders difficult the squeezing of warp yarns. To avoid this defect the roll is usually turned on a lathe,

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 193

elements.label: text
elements.text: but after the second turning the rolls must be replaced by new ones. It has been suggested to fill the cavities with aluminium. For this, using a chisel, a hole is made at the point of the cavity and an aluminium rod of adequate diameter is inserted in this hole and riveted over (Fig. 113). This done the riveted cavity is filed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 113. Method of repairing squeez­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing rolls of sizing machine

elements.label: text
elements.text: The sizecirculation tank is made of stainless steel and consists of an exterior bath with an interior bath inserted into it. A coil with blind steam is arranged in the space between the two baths which is filled with glycerin (the latter being a heat carrier ensuring the uniform heating of the size in the tank). The repair of the tank comes

elements.label: text
elements.text: to the restoration of its tightness. After repairs, the tank and coil are checked for good sealing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cylinder drier is intended for drying the warp to be impregnated with size and squeezed. It consists of the framework, several drying cylinders (5, 7, 9, 11 and more), two transfer rollers, a steam and condensate pipeline and the drying cylinders drive. The transfer roller at the entry into the drier and the first four or three cylinders have an antiadhesion coating (Teflon, fluoroplastic) to avoid the adherence of the size on the surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drierframework is a structure made of cast iron stands connected together by braces. The framework carries all the units and mechanisms of the drier.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The drying cylinder (Fig. 114) consists of the shell 7 m a d e of steel sheets. Elliptical bottoms 6 are welded to the shell and have flanges to which the journals 3 are attached. Provided on the left-hand journal is the silphon seal 4 for supplying the steam and elimination of the condensate, while on the right-hand journal there are the vacuum valve 2 and the driving sprocket 1. All drying cylinders are rotated by means of chain drive. In the bottom of the cylinders a discharge cock is provided for the elimination of the condensate.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During repairs, a check is made on the drying cylinder ladles, the vacuum valves and the discharge cocks; the manholes of the cylinders are closed. When carrying out any work inside the drying cylinder measures are taken to avoid unrestricted supply of steam or condensate into the cylinder, i.e. the steam line and condensate lines are disconnected from the cylinders and reliable locks are provided on starting valves. The bearings are washed (one of the bearings must have an axial clearance of 4-5 m m so as to allow the free elongation of the cylinder shaft on heating). The balancing of cylinders is checked at the site and the insulation of their butt faces is restored.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The delivery part of the machine consists of the framework, the ribbed roller, the delivery roll, the measuring and pressure rollers,

elements.label: text
elements.text: 196 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: the smoothening roller and the mechanisms for setting and removing the weaver’s beam.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The ribbedrolleris made of a steel pipe and is provided with ribs of wooden planks which are attached to the roller periphery and form a ribbed contour. The roller is repaired by restoring the plank fixtures.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The delivery roll (welded), 250 m m in diameter, is made of a steel pipe with rubber coating. Provided on the delivery roll pin is an overrunning clutch which in weaver’s beam replacement impedes the slackening of warp tension in the zone: drying cylinders— delivery roll. When repairing the delivery roll the worn-out coating is replaced and the overrunning clutch is restored or replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The smoothening roller arranged before the w e a v e r ’s b e a m reciprocates for shifting the layers of warp wound on the weaver’s beam in respect to each other.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The weaver's beam setting mechanism (Fig. 115) consists of two guides 3 mounted on the framework of the delivery section along which the right-hand tailspindle 1and left-hand tail spindle 6 are moving; the driving shaft with chuck plate 2 for rotating the weaver’s beam; the mechanism for centring the weaver’s beam; and the mechanism for displacing the tail spindles. The weaver’s beam centring mechanism has a reverse box 5, a mechanism controlling the lead screw reverse box 4,the worm reducer 7and the motor. The mechanism for tail spindle displacement consists of the same units as the centring mechanism, but in addition it is provided with a coupling

elements.text: Adjustment and Lubrication of Sizing Machines

elements.label: text
elements.text: After the repairs and assembly of the machine it is put in idle running. Prior to starting the machine it is necessary: to ascertain that all the parts are in place and properly fixed; to fill oil in the reducer and variators and to lubricate the bearings, gears, chain drives and all rubbing parts; to check for easy rotation the transfer,

elements.label: text
elements.text: measuring, pressure and smoothening rollers, and also the adjusting handwheels of the reed mechanism; to check the operation of pneumatic devices; the membranes of the top squeezing roll, the weaver’s beam removal mechanism, the pressure roller (when compressed air is let in, its pressure should not exceed 0.4 MPa) as well as the mechanisms for lifting the immersion roller, the mechanism for displacing the weaver’s beam setting brackets and so on; to take away all unnecessary articles and tools so that they do not get inside the machine working organs; to check the proper engagement of motors and push-button stations. This done, the machine isstarted for slow running and further for running at working speed. At the same time it is necessary to ascertain that the interlocking devices operate in due time and that the machine smoothly passes from slow to working speed and vice versa. For checking, compressed air is supplied into the pneumatic chambers of executive mechanisms. Simultaneously checks are done for air leakage in the connections; it is necessary to make sure of easy rotation of transfer rollers, draw ing, squeezing and delivery rolls, cylinders, immersion rollers, and the adjusting handles of the reed mechanism, etc. All the defects detected during machine inspection at idle running should immediately be eliminated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After all disarrangements have been eliminated, the machine is ready for running. The tank (trough) is filled to the required level with a size solution and steam is supplied in the interbottom space of the tank (trough); if necessary live steam is fed into the coil for heating the solution to the preset temperature. Prior to feeding steam into the driving cylinders they are blowed, the filters and condensate eliminators are checked and cleaned from contamination; supplied from a separate compressor or from the mill centralized system compressed air is fed into the systems for controlling the machine, mechanisms; the automatic regulators are adjusted for

elements.label: text
elements.text: Chapter Six 198

elements.label: text
elements.text: the preset temperature and for a certain level of the size solution according to the instructions supplied with the instruments and to the adopted sizing routines. After sounding a warning the machine is started for slow speed running.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The further adjustment of the machine is done at working speed. After starting the machine for running at working speed it is necessary:

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. To adjust the warp tension: between the drawing and squeezing rolls by adjusting the drawing roll; between the squeezing rolls and

elements.label: text
elements.text: big cylinder by adjusting the back equalizing mechanism; between the drying cylinders and delivery roll by adjusting the front equalizing mechanism or by winding a bunch on the delivery roll; between the delivery roll and weaver’s beam by modifying the tension of braking belts or by means of the movable friction weights. Moreover, it is necessary to adjust the stretch of warp yarns in accordance with the adopted technological conditions of the sizing process. Special attention should be paid to the tension of moist warp.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. To check the amount and regularity of squeezing and the density of warp winding on the weaver’s beam. If squeezing and winding density are insufficient it is necessary to increase the air pressure in the corresponding pneumatic chambers.
