elements.text: 3. Looms

elements.label: text
elements.text: Classification of Looms and Kinds

elements.label: text
elements.text: of Their Repairs

elements.label: text
elements.text: The loom mechanisms may be classified according to their application into three groups: (1) the main working mechanisms for the execution of the principal technological operations in the process of fabric formation (shedding and weft insertion motions, slay, fabric drawing-off and winding mechanisms, warp tensioning and releasing arrangements); (2) complementary working mechanisms taking no direct part in the process of fabric formation and mounted on the loom mainly for increasing its efficiency (the weft feeding mechanism); (3) safety mechanisms effecting control over loom operation, precluding fabric faults in case of disarrangements, and

elements.label: text
elements.text: 200 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: protecting loom parts from breakage (warp and weft controllers, warp protection motion, etc.).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Classification of looms. Looms are classified by the method of weft insertion in the shed and the method of fabric formation on the loom.

elements.label: text
elements.text: According to the method of weft insertion in the shed, the l o o m s are grouped into shuttle and shuttleless looms (AT)*. In their turn the shuttleless looms are subdivided into looms with smallweft inserters (type CTE>)**, pneumatic looms (type P) and hydraulic looms (type H)***, rapierand pneumatic rapier looms (type ATIIP)****. In shuttle looms the weft yarn is laid in the shed by a shuttle carrying a bobbin with a reserve of weft yarn. Unlike the shuttle looms, shuttleless looms effect weft laying by weft inserters (small size inserters, by water or air jet and by rapiers) which carry no reserve of weft yarn. In this case the weft yarn is unwound from big stationary packages disposed outside the shed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: According to the method of fabric formation the looms are subdivided in two types: looms with an intermittent frontal (over the whole width of the warp) fabric formation (shuttle and shuttleless looms in which beating-up of the weft yarn is effected by the reed simultaneously over the whole width of the warp); and looms with continuous fabric formation (flat and circular multi-shed looms in which the weft yarn is laid by the inserters in the sheds consecutively formed along the width of the warp; beating-up of the weft yarn is

elements.label: text
elements.text: effected by special devices simultaneously at several points of the warp width correspondingly to the number of weft insertersmoving

elements.label: text
elements.text: in sheds).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The design features of the looms are determined by the kind of raw materials, the end use of the fabric and the design of loom’s individual mechanisms. At present the following kinds of looms are manufactured: for the production of cotton, woollen, silk and linen fabrics,

elements.label: text
elements.text: as well as fabrics of glass yarns and wire meshes, for the production of light, medium and heavy, narrow and wide fabrics; single shuttle and multishuttle looms, tappet, dobby and Jacquard looms, including versatile looms. So for instance, shuttleless looms of the CTB type are successfully employed for manufacturing fabrics of manmade, silk, cotton, and woollen yarns of different linear density. These looms may be used for manufacturing not only narrow fabrics

elements.label: text
elements.text: in several webs but also wide fabrics in one and two webs. The automatic rapier looms type ATIIP with weft insertion by pneumatic

elements.label: text
elements.text: * AT— automatic shuttle loom. ** GTE— shuttleless looms. *** Pneumatic (P) and hydraulic (H) loom*. (manufactured in CSSR) are mainly of similar design, and therefore, only pneumatic looms are discussed in the present manual as they are most widely used in the textile industry.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ATIIP— automatic rapier looms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 20i

elements.label: text
elements.text: rapiers and the pneumatic looms of the type P with pneumatic weft insertion are intended for the manufacture of cotton and silk fabrics-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Kinds of loom repairs* The looms are subjected to current, preventive maintenance, medium, and overhaul repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Currentrepairsare carried out by the assistant foreman and come to the elimination of disarrangements and certain failures of parts in the course of operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Preventive maintenance repairsare carried out also by the assistant foreman which establishes every day a schedule for the inspection and repair of the looms in his charge so as to preclude any disarrangements in the looms and part breakage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During current and preventive repairs, complementary and small' parts are replaced, the parts and mechanisms are checked for fastening, adjustment, and interaction. The following points are checked: the fixing of the loom stand to the floor and the reliability of bolt,

elements.label: text
elements.text: connections; the easy starting of the loom, the proper adherence of braking blocks to the braking pulley, the smooth stoppage of the loom in closed shed position; the tension of V-belts transmitting motionfrom the motor to the pulleys; the clearances in bevel gears; the oil level in the boxes of the rapier drive as well as in the systems^ ensuring oil feed to different parts and mechanisms of the loom; the position of the rapiers with respect to their guides and clearance between the rapier cover plates and the reed; the operation of the conveyor and the proper condition of the weft inserter tips; the tightness of the torsion shaft and beginning of picking; the settingof weft inserters and the operation of their brakes; the work of the loom brake and the degree of braking; the pressure of the weft inserter lifter in top and bottom positions; the pressure of the lever of the weft feeder in top and bottom positions; clearance between the picker and the butt face of the weft inserter; the regular feed of warp and fabric rolling-up; the operation of the selvedge binder mechanism; the proper installation and operation of the nozzle; the faultless^ work of the weft brake; the proper installation of the scissors and

elements.label: text
elements.text: the quality of weft yarn trimming; the correct installation of the fabric fell controller in respect to the fabric fell and the amount of fabric drawing-up; the reliable fixing of the warp stop motion in the* seat and the plugs of the dropper stop motion; the mounting and operation of temples; the amount of binder loop tucking-in; the proper operation of the leno device; the operation of the fluff exhaust;, the tension of the cloth between the cloth roller and take-up roller;, the operation of rapiers, nozzles and inserters (check that they are not clogged with fluff); the correct motion of rapiers and inserters in* the shed; the position of the confuser. All the observed disarrangements are to be immediately eliminated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The medium repairs are carried out according to the schedule at. least twice a year, and in case of the loom’s heavy wear more fre-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 202 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: quently. The medium repairs involve cleaning and checking the loom with the partial dismantling of main units, and the replacement or restoration of some badly worn-out parts which cannot ensure loom normal operation. The time assigned for medium repairs is usually not more than one shift. The repairs are carried out by a team of two workers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The overhaul is carried out once in two or three years by a team of workers. In overhauling, the loom is completely disassembled, the worn-out parts are replaced and the units are checked and cleaned. After the overhaul, the loom technical condition slightly differs from a new one. If after the overhaul some old parts are left for further use, these parts must be restored to good technical condition and a special statement should be made in the reception certificate. The volume of work to be performed during medium repairs and ^general overhaul of looms is determined in special instructions. The foreman of the mechanical repair department stops the equipment for medium and general overhaul repairs at the dates called for

elements.label: text
elements.text: by the repair schedule. Before submitting the looms to repairs, they must be cleaned and the gaited warp removed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Parts,

elements.label: text
elements.text: Units and Mechanisms

elements.label: text
elements.text: Frames, Braces and Breast Beam

elements.label: text
elements.text: The frames, braces and breast beam when assembled together form the loom framework. Usually they are cast of iron or steel. To ensure the adequate rigidity and stability of the framework, the frames

elements.label: text
elements.text: and braces are provided with reinforcement ribs along the whole

elements.label: text
elements.text: contour, thus forming a trough or double-Tee section.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of loom operation cracks, cuts, worn-out holes for shafts, inserts, etc. may be observed and breakages may occur. •Cracked and broken frames are repaired by welding or by machining. The welding method depends on the place of cracks and chipping.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If they are disposed at sharp curvatures in the frame profile, hot electric arc welding (with preliminary heating) is used; while in all other places it is advisable to use cold welding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In hot welding the places to be repaired are cleaned from dirt and oil, the crack is made up asan Y-shaped seam and at its sides .graphite plates are fixed in place with fire clay to protect melted

elements.label: text
elements.text: cast iron from spreading about. The frame prepared in this way is .subjected to local heating to 600-650°C using a gas burner. The heated

elements.label: text
elements.text: points are closed with an asbestos sheet and the cracks are welded

elements.label: text
elements.text: after which the frame is slowly cooled and the seams finished.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In coldwelding the points to be welded and the adjacent surface .are cleaned from dirt and oil after which Y-shaped bevels at an

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 203

elements.label: text
elements.text: angle of 90° are cut, their depth being equal to 0.25-0.5 frame wall

elements.label: text
elements.text: thickness. Broken parts are joined along the line of breakage. In each chamfer a row of holes is drilled and threaded for pins to be disposed in checkered order (the hole spacing of 25 to 30 m m , the depth of 1.5 wall thickness, and the diameter of 5 to 8 mm). The pins must

elements.label: text
elements.text: he screwed to the end and protrude from 3 to 4 m m above the surface. To begin with the pins are welded with annular beads and then

elements.label: text
elements.text: longitudinal beads are formed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: There are other methods of frame repairs, for instance a steel cover plate is cut and bolted or riveted to the frame with subsequent welding along the contour. The frame with a worn-out hole for the shaft is repaired by changing the hole size into the repair size or by press-fitting a repair bushing. In this case not only the corresponding size is to be maintained, but also the geometrical axes of the frame

elements.label: text
elements.text: holes must coincide so that shaft misalignment is avoided. The hole size may be made of a repair size by turning and reaming in a drilling machine or by means of other devices. In the first case, the frames are removed and bolted together so as to bring in co incidence the holes for the shaft, after which depending on the amount of wear and the deterioration of the hole shape they must be reamed on the drill. Other methods may be also used by applying hand or motordriven boring bars. Worn-out frame surfaces for the inserts of a crankshaft or any other shaft are filed, metal sprayed or built-up with brass after which they are machined to accommodate the inserts. A broken thread in a frame hole for a pressure bolt is cut to accommodate a bolt of greater diameter. Worn-out seats for the take-up roller journal arebuilt-up by welding and carefully filed. Broken and cracked bracesand the breast beam are mainly repaired by welding and reinforced by steel cover plates.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Drive

elements.label: text
elements.text: In CTB shuttleless looms and the ATIIP automatic rapier looms the braking force of the main shaft is adjusted by means of the bolt 7 (Fig. 117): to increase the main shaft braking the bolt is to be tightened and to reduce it the bolt must be loosened. Turning of the shaft by inertia at the moment of loom stoppage should not exceed 25°. For checking, the weft yarn is removed from the feeler of the weft controller and the main shaft is turned by hand— in this case the disengagement of all CTB shuttleless looms must occur when the main shaft has turned over 255° (but not later than at 280°). To avoid rubbing of the exterior part of the braking flywheel 5 against the braking belt 6 at the moment of shaft rotation, it is necessary to adjust a clearance of 0.5 m m over the entire circumference of the braking flywheel between the braking belt and the flywheel. This clearance is adjusted by means of the bolts 3 provided in the station-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 204 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: ary block 4. The distance a between the lever 1 and the support roller2must be equal to from 3 to 5 m m (when the loom is engaged).

elements.label: text
elements.text: When mounting the braking strap (not shown in the drawing) intended to retain the flywheel against rotating during loom operation, its end must protrude

elements.label: text
elements.text: (at the point of contact with the flywheel rim) by 6 to 7 m m from the rim and the side face of the flywheel should be from 3 to 4 m m away from the main shaft face. If the braking strap is not correctly installed, an excessive friction is created between the main shaft and the flywheel pedestal due to which it is excessively worn out. The distorted hole of the flywheel pedestal is turned and a new bushing is press-fitted into it. To increase the life of the bushing an annular groove and longitudinal lubrication canals are cut in its hole.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The irregular lubrication and excessive tension of V-shaped belts cause the wear of the pulley holes. The worn holes in the pulleys are restored as described above. V-shaped belts are tensioned by the motor mass. For this, the bolts fixing the motor on the loom frame

elements.label: text
elements.text: are released and the belts are tensioned by the weight of the motor, after which the bolts are retightened.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In shuttleloomsthe wear of parts is caused by slackened fastenings in the course of the drive operation. Usually, the fixing of the small gear on the main shaft becomes stack due to the wear either in the gear keyway or in the key, to tight meshing of intermediate gears

elements.label: text
elements.text: and the wear of drive gears toothing. For this reason when need occurs the gears should be turned on the shafts. The small gear is placed on a new keyway. For this, the guard hood and the friction clutch are removed, the burrs and dents on the main shaft are elimin­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ated especially on the keyway, the key is driven out and the small gear is brought out of engagement with the big gear, the small gear is turned round with the new key hole upwards, brought in engagement with the big gear after which the key is inserted. The main

elements.label: text
elements.text: and medium shafts should not turn in bearings so as not to impair the beginning of picking.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n the place of the big gear on the middle shaft is changed, it is necessary to remove the guards and the friction clutch, to bring the slay in position corresponding to the beginning of picking from the right side of the loom, to unscrew the nut for releasing the big gear

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 205

elements.label: text
elements.text: on the shaft and to bring it out of meshing with the small gear;

elements.label: text
elements.text: next the big gear on the shaft is to be turned through several teeth,

elements.label: text
elements.text: brought again in meshing with the small gear. Then the big gear is to be secured on the shaft with a bevel bushing by tightening the nut. Care should be taken that the middle shaft carrying the picking cam is not shifted from its place (as otherwise the beginning of picking will be impaired), and that the friction gear easily turns on the hub of the small gear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When adjusting the friction clutch it is necessary to obtain the same force of pressure of all screws on the pressure disk (otherwise the

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressure disk may be misaligned in respect to the thrust disk which will lead to an irregular running of the loom). The pressure of the screws is adjusted by slightly shifting them with a screwdriver in

elements.label: text
elements.text: the holes of pressure pawls. If the loom operates for a long time, the unequal action of the screws on the lugs of the pressure disk causes the premature wear of the ferrodo rings at the points of strong

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressure applied by one of the screws, so that the loom begins to “clatter”. In this case, the ferrodo ring is to be replaced and the

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressure screws should be properly adjusted. When the disks are slightly pressed, a strong noise is emitted in the friction clutch during loom operation and during the first weft laying the shuttle fails to fly in the box. When the disks are strongly compressed at the moment of loom starting the keys of the driving gears may be broken and the noise continues in the friction clutch after the loom is off. The working surfaces of the friction clutch disks are periodic­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ally cleaned with emery paper from dirt, fluff, and oil.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In high-speed pneumatic looms the drive parts are worn quicker than all the rest. Most often it proves necessary to replace the slotted shaft 1 (Fig. 118), the disk 2, the key 6, the rod 4, the bearing 5

elements.label: text
elements.text: and the ring 3.These parts may be easily restored by building-up the worn places by oxyacetylene welding with subsequent manual finishing or on a lathe. An exception to this are the slotted shaft 1 and disk 2 as pn the shaft 1 usually the slots are worn out and it is easier to replace the shaft, rather than to restore the slots. The slots are also worn in the disk 2,but they may be restored. For this

elements.label: text
elements.text: a cut-out is made in the hub of the disk, a bushing is prepared and press-fitted inside with welding of edges followed by broaching the slots on a special machine. This kind of restoration is timeconsuming operation and therefore it is.resorted to very rarely.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the starting arrangement replaced or restored most frequently are the following units: the trigger 3 (Fig. 119), the sector 4Vthe shafts of the bearings of lever 6 and the starting crank pin. These

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts may easily be restored by building-up with subsequent finishing. The springs 2 and 7 are very often broken and their replacement

elements.label: text
elements.text: is labour and time consuming. These springs can be replaced by more simple devices. The holt joining the cams 1should carry a small

elements.label: caption
elements.text: F i g . 1 1 8 . D i a g r a m o f d r i v e f o r t y p e P l o o m

elements.label: caption
elements.text: P i g . 1 1 9 . D i a g r a m o f s t a r t i n g d e v i c e i n t y p e P l o o m

elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: stand having a hole at the end and the end of a small helical spring is to he fastened to this hole, while the second end of the spring is to be fixed on the frame. This spring will replace the return spring 2.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is convenient to adjust with it the tension, and what is more important it may easily be replaced. Instead of the humped spring 7 which is very inconvenient for replacement, a spring-loaded pawl may be used (Fig. 120a, b). The pawl is reliable in operation and may be replaced only with the lapse of several years. As the starting device is assembled, the roller 5 (see Fig. 119) should have no axial displacement and must easily rotate.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shedding Motion

elements.label: text
elements.text: The following three types of shedding motions find application in modern looms: tappet motion, dobby, and Jacquard mechanism (Jacquard shedding motions are not discussed in this book).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 208 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 121. Diagram of motion transmission to healds

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shedding motion of the CTB shuttleless and ATOP automatic rapier looms. As the shedding motion is adjusted, the angle of shed opening, the shed height relative to the comb teeth and the moment of shed closure are adjusted. The angle of shed opening may be from 18 to 26° depending on the kind of processed raw materials. During loom erection this angle is adjusted to 21°, for which the shackles 4 (Fig. 121) on the heald levers 3 are displaced downwards

elements.label: text
elements.text: over a distance of a = 35 mm. The shed angle decreases with the increase in the dimension a and vice versa. The shed height in relation to the slay comb teeth is adjusted by modifying the dimension b which is usually set equal to 10-15 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the produced assortment of fabrics, the closed shed position is set when the main shaft turns from 0 to 20°. For adjusting the closed shed position, the bolts fixing the change sprocket are released and the heald frames are turned (using the bolt) ip closed .shed position (on one level), while the sprocket must remain station­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ary. After the closed shed position has been adjusted the sprocket is bolted. The clearances in the articulated joints of horizontal drawbars 7and rods 6 are eliminated by replacing bushings or rollers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the holes in the guide plates 5 are worn-out, the distorted part is •cut-away and a metal plate of corresponding thickness is fitted into the hole and welded into the guide plate. This done, the welded points are finished, and the holes are drilled to the size indicated in the drawings. To eliminate the clearances between the rollers 2 and the shedding tappets 1 it is necessary to replace the worn-out

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts in this point of the mechanism. If after the replacement of worn-out parts the clearances are not eliminated, the bushing in

elements.label: text
elements.text: the levers 3 are replaced by accentric bushings. Prior to making such

elements.label: text
elements.text: bushings, the clearance between the rollers and tappets must be measured. At the moment of measuring, the bottom roller must be

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 209

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressed to surface of the counter tappet. The obtained size of the clearance is divided by two and the hole in the newly manufactured bushing is shifted over the obtained dimension. The ready bushing is press-fitted in the lever so that its hole is shifted to the right.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn parts of the tappet surfaces are restored by buildingup. For obtaining the tappet of required dimensions a special device is used consisting of the stand 7 (Fig. 122) with two shafts 6 and 4.The top shaft 4 may be displaced in vertical direction in the stand slot and fixed with

elements.label: text
elements.text: the nut 3. For checking, the J- - - - - - 1- - - - - - tappet 5 is fitted on the shaft Fig. 122. Diagram of device for impart- 6 and the heald lever 2 on the ing tappet required dimensions shaft 4. Next, the shaft 4 is lowered until the roller 1 contacts the surface of the tappet 5 and fixed with the nut 3;the tappets are turned over a full revolution on the shaft 6 in order to find the wear which would be restored by building-up with welding. Further, the excessive layers of metal are removed and the restored parts are gradually brought to required dimensions. After the tappet has been finished the rollers must easily run on its surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To avoid oil leakage through the glands of the tappet pipe shaft it is necessary to raise the gland above the surface of the shaft 6 as the leakage is caused by the excessively deep annular groove under the gland. The gland is raised by inserting a rubber ring in the groove. The gland surface should protrude 0.4-0.6 m m above the roller surface. The sharp edges of the gland groove must be rounded by filing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A tappet shedding motion with rigid heald displacement finds application in pneumatic looms. In this motion it is necessary to replace the shaft 5 (Fig. 123) and spring protectors 1 more frequently

elements.label: text
elements.text: than in other mechanisms. In the course of every two or three years of operation, the bottom drive shaft 4 causes heavy wear of the seat in the frame 3tso that the frame 3 must be restored or replaced. W h e n repairing the frame, the seat is bored to a greater size, a bushing is made with all the necessary slots and after press-fitting in the frame it is locked in place. After dismantling, washing and replacing the worn-out parts, the tappet motion is assembled taking

elements.label: text
elements.text: 210 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 123. Diagram of shedding motion of type P loom

elements.label: text
elements.text: care that the levers 2 do not contact each other in their movement, that there is no swinging on the shafts 4 and that the levers are on the same level. Prefabricated metal shafts 5 are rapidly worn-out and may be replaced by capron ones of the appropriate shape.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation, the surface of the tappet is worn and cracks may appear. The distortion of the tappet contour brings changes in the law of heald displacement which m a y result in defectuous fabric. The worn surface of tappets are repaired by building-up with an allowance of 2 to 3 m m for further machining. First, after

elements.label: text
elements.text: building up, the tappet surface is machined by grinding wheel and then finished according to a template on a lathe. As a template, is

elements.label: text
elements.text: employed an accurately machined new tappet having a rim which is 3 or 4 m m greater than that of the repaired tappet (for cutter overrunning). The tappet to be repaired is imparted the same profile as the template. In turning, an allowance of 0.15-0.2 m m is provided for subsequent grinding on the lathe. The tappet profile is checked

elements.label: text
elements.text: by means of a gauge. After preliminary local heating, the cracks in the tappet rim are welded. If spare tappets are available they are used to replace the worn-out tappets.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Dobbies. Most largely used in the textile industry are knife dobbies which being of different designs are similar in their principle of operation. The most typical are PK-12-1 dobbies for twelve healds used in shuttle looms and new type C K H dobbies with 14 to 18 healds

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 211

elements.label: text
elements.text: for the CTE shuttleless looms*. The dobbies of both types relate to

elements.label: text
elements.text: double-lift dobbies (the dobby operation cycle is effected during two revolutions of the loom main shaft).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The high-speed C K H dobby consists of the following main parts and mechanisms: the frame, the drive, the heald driving mechanism, the knives turning mechanism and the programming mechanism. The main mechanism is the heald driving mechanism with jacks 2 and 15 (Fig. 124), the balks 4, the stationary rests 5 and 12, the movable rods 3 and 13, and leverage system 6-10. In accordance with the pattern design the jacks 2 of the top row or jacks 15 of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: bottom row are set on the line of action of knives 1 and 14. The moving knife catches the jack and displaces it together with the

elements.label: text
elements.text: balk 4. The middle part 02of the balk on its displacement shifts the heald through the intermediate of the carrier 11, shackle 7, rocker 6, lever 10, the latch 8 and the horizontal drawbar 9.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In dobbies the following parts come out of order the most: the jack rods, balks, jacks, knives, and sliders in the grooves of driving

elements.label: text
elements.text: gears.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The jack rods are intended for transmitting the motion to the healds. In the course of operation their pins and forks, sometimes

elements.label: text
elements.text: also the flats, are worn. The pin is worn by rubbing against a jack or balk, the fork by rubbing against the shaft and the flats due to the mutual rubbing of jack rods. Jack rods are repaired by different methods depending on their design. For instance, worn pins are drilled out or cut away on a milling machine. Further, holes are drilled

elements.label: text
elements.text: and counterbored in the jack rods and new pins are inserted in the holes. New pins are welded from the side of counterboring and the

elements.label: text
elements.text: • The dobby C K H is available in the following executions: CKH-14— for 14 healds, CKH-14A— for 14 healds with drive to the colour change motion, CKH-18— for 18 healds and CKH-18A— for 18 healds with drive to the colour change motion. C K H — high-speed dobby of the double lift type.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 212 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: weld is carefully ground on a grinding wheel. According to another method of jack rod repairing the worn pin is cut off by means of a disk milling cutter, and a hole is drilled in its place for a rivet which is countersunk from both sides. Next, a steel washer is cut

elements.label: text
elements.text: out and fixed in the jack rod jaws with a rivet or by welding a steel rod. The worn jack rod fork is built-up and manually finished to suit the shaft.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The worn-out hole in the jack rod is drilled, reamed and a cast iron repair bushing is press-fitted inside. The worn-out flats are ground on a surface grinder and during assembly washers are inserted between them, the thickness of which is equal to the double thickness of the flat.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The balks are liable to develop the following faults in the course of operation: the holes and pins are worn-out and the eyelets broken. The worn-out holes are drilled, reamed, and bushings are press-fitted inside them. Worn-out pins are built-up and filed. In other cases the worn-out pins are cut off on a milling cutter. In the place of the cut-off pin through-holes are drilled in which steel washers are riveted or steel rods are welded. Damaged eyelets are cut off and in their place new ones are welded or soldered after which holes are drilled and finished in the eyelets.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The knivesare liable to wear on the following places: the working surface of the shafts on which the jacks are operating, places on which knives rest on the frame guiding slots, and the ends to which the drawbars and draw jacks are attached. The worn-out working surface of the knife is built up and ground on an emery wheel and finished in a special device on a surface grinder in cross direction. The points where the knife rests on the frame guiding slots are built-up with cast iron. The built-up surface is worked to suit the slots and to ensure the easy displacement of the knives inside them. The worn-out ends of the knife are built up, ground and holes are drilled for cotter pins. In the course of operation the ends of jacks get worn or broken. The jack worn ends are built up and then carefully machined for proper fitting. Broken ends are welded.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation the capron sliders in the slots of the driving gear in the CKH-14 dobby become worn and gaps are formed. As a result, there may occur wedging and consequently the breakage

elements.label: text
elements.text: of mating parts. As the lubrication of sliders is difficult, it is good practice to make the sliders of a textile based laminate with oil impregnation (by keeping in an oil bath for 4-5 days).

elements.label: text
elements.text: For the repair, adjustment and running-in of the dobby a special stand has been designed. It is a rigid structure made of steel angles and channel with a motor from which the motion is tfan£mitted through chain drive to the dobby shaft. The dobby is fixed in channel fecesses on the stand. During running-in, the rotational speed of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: dobby shaft is somewhat reduced to 160-180 min-1.The running-in

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 213

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the dobby is effected during 2-3 shifts. The dobby is transported in the weaving shed and from the shed to the shops by means of a special car (Fig. 125) in which the dobby is suspended.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The lubrication charts for dobbies must be carefully followed. For each type of dobby special routines of lubrication have been established, but they

elements.label: text
elements.text: are constantly modified and improved. For example, the driving gear rotating in two middle bearings must be oil lubricated once per shift. However, lubrication of the same gear with cup grease and the provision of a special oiler on the shaft allows lubrication to be made once every six months.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 125. Car for dobby transport

elements.text: Picking box of the C T B shuttleless loom. The tension of the spring 3 (Fig. 126) of the braking plate 1 should be such that the distance a when the adjusting bolt 4 is properly tightened is equal to 3, 5, and

elements.label: text
elements.text: 8 m m for processing weft yarns of low, medium, and high linear density, correspondingly. W h e n the loom main shaft isturned through 255° (for narrow and wide looms), the adjusting bolt 7 is unscrewed to the end and the braking foot 2 is set (with the nut of bolt 6 released) so that it makes a depression of 1-3 m m on the braking plate (the thicker is the weft yarn, the deeper must be the plate depressed). W h e n the main shaft turns through 320° (for narrow and large looms) the adjusting bolt 7 is unscrewed until the foot depresses the braking plate by 2-4 mm. The final adjustment is effected by modifying the position of the foot 2 in relation to the height of the adjusting nut 5. The compensating lever 1 (Fig. 127) when in bottom position must be 3-8 m m above the line of weft displacement. This position is adjusted by means of bolts attaching the compensating lever to the lever 2.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Most frequently encountered defects in weft inserters are cracks in the frame causing the shift of spring grippers and tip wear causing the unsteady fixing of the weft inserter in the receiving box. When the weft inserter spring comes out of order it is replaced by means of a special device consisting of a steel plate with the groove 1 (Fig. 128) accommodating the weft inserter. The holes 4 of a diameter, which is by 1 m m greater than the diameter of the weft in-

elements.label: text
elements.text: serter spring rivets, are disposed opposite the holes in the weft

elements.label: text
elements.text: inserter frame. Prior to the insertion of a new spring in the weft inserter frame, it is necessary to check the coaxiality of the holes 4 with the gripper jaws according to the match mark on the control pins 3. Peening of tubular rivets is done by means of three cones with angles of 60, 90 and 120° and the protruding rivets are to be filed in longitudinal direction with subsequent sand-papering. If there appears a gap between the gripper jaws of the weft inserter spring, they must be lapped with paste.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Picking motion of CTE shuttleless loom. The picking force of the motion is determined by the potential energy of the wound-up

elements.label: text
elements.text: 216 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: torsion shaft and does not depend on the loom speed. With the main shaft set for narrow looms at 80° and for wide looms at 50° the clearance a= 0.2 mm is adjusted between the picking cam 2 (Fig. 129) and roller 8 (with the torsion shaft untwisted). The clearance a is adjusted by means of the bolt 9 and checked with a feeler through the aperture in the picking box provided on its right-hand side. Further, with the main shaft turned to 135° (for wide looms—

elements.label: text
elements.text: 100°), the scale attached on the housing 7is set so that its division, corresponding to 0°, should coincide with the match mark on the winding coupling after which the torsion shaft is wound up. In narrow looms the beginning of picking must be at the angle of (140 + 3)° and in wide looms at the angle of (105 + 3)° of the main shaft rotation. For adjusting the moment when picking starts (to avoid the breakage of comb toothing and of other parts, the weft inserters are extracted), the main shaft of a narrow loom is set to 250° and that of the wide loom to 220° and the torsion shaft is untwisted. Through the left-hand open aperture in the bottom section of the picking box, the bolts fixing the cam 2 to the three-slotted cam (not shown in the drawing) are released and the cam 2 is turned counterclockwise in case of early shed closure and clockwise in case of late shed closure. The cam is fixed, the torsion shaft is wound up and the moment of picking start is checked. Further, a clearance b = 0.2 ... 0.4 m m is set between the boss of the picker 5 and the side face of the weft inserter 6 (with the main shaft at 100° for narrow looms and 75° for wide looms). For this, the bolts 1 fixing the picking stick *?.are released and the latter is turned until the picker bears against the weft inserter side face. After tightening the bolt, the picking stick is displaced to the left and the necessary clearance is formed. This done, a clearance cfrom 0.05 to 0.1 m m between the lateral surfaces of the picking sticks and the striker 4 is adjusted by moving (the bolts being released) the fixture of the picking stick 3 along the picking tube.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For the adjustment of the oil damper a device is used consisting of the bracket 1 (Fig. 130) with spring-loaded insulated contact 2, a battery for a flash light, and a lamp 3 for 3.5 V. These elements

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 217

elements.label: text
elements.text: are connected as shown in the diagram. Prior to the installation of this device on the loom, the right-hand holt 4 fixing the weft feeder guide (or the feeder guide shifter in wide looms) is unscrewed and the same bolt is used for fixing the bracket 1 of the oil damper adjusting device. The torsion shaft is wound up to an angle of 30°. After the installation and connection of the device, the shaft of a wide loom is set to 145° and that of a narrow loom to 110°. In this case the picking stick in front position should be without clearance and the weft fork feeler (not shown in the drawing) should not catch the contact 2. Further, the loom is engaged in running. If the lamp lights up brightly it means that the piston damping is weak, and if the lamp does not light up at all the damping of the piston is excessive. In the former case, the needle is turned in until the lamp ceases to light up, and in the latter case it is first unscrewed until the lamp starts blinking and then turned-in until blinking ceases. This method of checking ensures a precise adjustment and reduces loom downtime required for damper dismantling.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The oil pump atomizer (Fig. 131) is intended for spraying oil to* lubricate the weft inserter, the weft feeder guiding surfaces, the striker and other parts located in the picking box. If the side face of the cylinder 1 is worn (burred) by the action of the cam 3 more than over 2.5-3 mm, it must be repaired. The worn-out part is machined and a brass or bronze plate is fixed to it with two screws* At the replacement of the piston 2 or cylinder 7, they are checked for easy running of the cylinder on the piston (with sufficient com* pression). In case of tight fit the working surfaces of the cylinder and pistons are to be wiped with paste.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Picking motion of a shuttle loom. As the picking motion is adjusted care should be taken that the spindles 4 (Fig. 132) are mounted strict­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ly horizontal, easily rotate in bearings, and have no radial swing; their axial shift should not exceed 0.7 m m . The picking bowls 3must tightly adhere without misalignment to the working surfaces of the

elements.label: text
elements.text: picking cam 1; the bowl at maximum lift should protrude over 4-12 m m from the edge of the picking nose bit and it must freely turn •on the spindle; its longitudinal displacement should not exceed 1.5 mm. The picking cams should be 44 m m away from the flats on the frames. The surface of the picking cam should be free from indentations and protrusions. At the point of butting the picking nose bit and picking cam should be flush and the points of their

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 219

elements.label: text
elements.text: contact should be well finished. The working surfaces of the tongue

elements.label: text
elements.text: and block must be smooth. The blocks on the bracket must be mounted so that a clearance of 10-15 m m is formed between the lug 9 of the bracket 8 and the interior wall of the cut-out in the block 7. The surface of the bracket on which the block is moving must be smooth and rectilinear and the bracket should not have longitudinal

elements.label: text
elements.text: shift. The picking stick should be 25-30 m m away from the slay end plate 5.The stirrup 12 on the spindle should be mounted so that the distance from the top of the small shackle to the spindle lug is equal to 90-100 m m . W h e n the picking stick is in extreme back posi­

elements.label: text
elements.text: tion the clearance between the pickers and the metal race must be equal to 1 mm. The picker movement must be parallel to the race.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For this, the picking stick must be inclined until the shuttle separates from the picker and then the bolt 10 is tightened until the picker

elements.label: text
elements.text: lifts the shuttle 1 m m above the race. This done, the counter nut of the bolt 10 is secured and the bolt 6 is tightened. If the picker lifts the shuttle tip more than 1 m m above the race, the bolt 10 must be unscrewed until the picker lowers to form the necessary clearance, after which the counternut is secured and the bolt is tightened.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The beginning of picking is more easily adjusted from the left side of the loom with the main shaft turned through 70°, and from the right side of the loom to 75°. The beginning of picking is adjusted by displacing the picking cam on the coupling by means of the setting bolt 2. For adjusting an earlier picking, the picking cam is

elements.label: text
elements.text: turned in the sense of middle shaft motion. To adjust the beginning of picking at a later moment the picking cam must be turned in opposite direction. The force of picking is adjusted by the stirrup 12

elements.label: text
elements.text: and blocks 11. For increasing the picking force, the stirrup and block are lowered so that the big shackle is 20-25 m m above the small one.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For reducing the picking force the stirrup with the block is raised to a distance of 20-25 m m between the shackles. It should be noted that the smaller is the picking force, the smoother is loom operation and the less is the wear of loom parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When the picking nose bit is worn out, its curve is made steeper or the bit is replaced by a new one. When the picking bowl is worn out, it is replaced by a new one after oiling its spindle and checking its rotation on the axle.

elements.text: The system for supply and distribution of compressed air in pneumatic looms* As the air supply system is repaired, it is frequently necessary to replace the air pipelines. Fig. 133 shows how the pipe end is to be prepared for replacement. The end of the pipe 1 of adequate length is tapered by filing and the nut 2 and pressure ring 3 are fitted upon it. Then, using a centre punch or any other bevel tool, the ends of the pipe are expanded thus forming the head 5. This pipe end is inserted into the hole of the coupling 4 and the nut 2 is fitted upon it pressing with its lug on the ring 3 thus shifting it

elements.label: text
elements.text: 220 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: and pressing to the lugs of the coupling 4 the side face of the pipe 1. Next the nut 2istightened and a checking for air leakage is made. In case of air leakage the operation is repeated so as to completely eliminate it.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reducer is usually repaired in the fitter’s shop after disconnecting it from all pipes and removing it from the loom. After dismantling the reducer, the bottom part of the frame, the hole in the box, the valve and plug surfaces are cleaned. In this mechanism the diaphragm is replaced more frequently than all other parts as it is forcedthrough in the middle part, distorted and lets air pass through the exterior walls. All other parts are replaced or restored when they are worn out. In the course of operation, capron pipelines are frequently deteriorated at the places of expansion and the nut becomes broken. Expansion of pipelines is made with an electric welding torch provided with a special nozzle.

elements.text: Welt laying mechanism in ATIIP automatic rapier looms. The mechanism operates as follows. Two tubular rapiers penetrate into the open shed from both sides of the loom. When the rapiers meet in the middle of the shed, the weft yarn passes from the right rapier to the left one and is laid up to the left-hand edge of the fabric. The weft yarn is unwound from a stationary fixed bobbin with a constant speed by means of a measuring mechanism. With the aid of a compensator the yarn is supplied at variable speed first into the righthand rapier and then to left-hand one. The rapiers are actuated by a drive and the air jets in the right- and left-hand rapiers are created either by an individual compressor mounted on each loom or by a centralized air supply system. The weft laying mechanism consists of three parts: the rapier displacement mechanism, the weft

elements.label: text
elements.text: yarn supply mechanism (measuring mechanism and compensator) and the air supply mechanism (compressor and air ducts).

elements.label: text
elements.text: As the rapier mechanism is adjusted (Fig. 134) it should be taken into consideration that in meshing gears the generatrices of their conical surfaces must completely coincide. The proper meshing of bevel gears is checked by the contact stain (Fig. 135). A thin layer of paint is applied on the teeth of the gear zlyafter which the gear zt is turned while the gear z2 is slightly braked. A normal contact stain (Fig. 135a) must be disposed in the middle of the tooth profile and must occupy at least half of its height; in length it must be displaced to the thin part of the tooth (without coming out of its limits).

To begin

elements.label: text

elements.label: text
elements.text: with four bolts fixing the sleeve of the vertical shaft and four bolts fixing the sleeve of the main shaft are to be unscrewed; after the adequate gasket has been chosen, the bolts are tightened again. The allowable minimum side clearance between the teeth is from 0.1 to 0.2 mm. During loom operation in the weaving shed, thisclearance may be checked by means of an indicator at four points in every 90° of main shaft rotation. When the arm length is 250 m m the side clearance must be equal to 0.5-0.8 m m . The clearance is adjusted using the same gaskets under the sleeves: the normal meshing of bevel gears is characterized by noise emitted during mechanism operation, i.e. a light hissing or buzzing. W h e n adjusting a m i n i m u m side clearance in the meshing of the sun gear z3 (see Fig. 134a, b) the satellite gears zkand the planetary gear z5, the clearance is determined by the slight manual swinging of the connecting rod and the clearance is eliminated by displacing the shafts of the satellite gears in the elongated side hole provided in the carrier plate.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The carrier in assembly with the connecting rod is checked for run-out prior to the installation on the loom using a special device

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 136). A bevel support and measuring instrument (a calliper square or a gauge) which may be displaced on the plate are placed on the smooth surface 1of the checking plate not lessthan 500 X 500 m m in size. The carrier 4 in assembly with the connecting rod 2 are inserted in the hole of the bevel support. The run-out of the surface 3 in respect to the surface 1 is checked by rotating the connecting rod in respect to the axis aa. The distance from the surface 1 to the surface 3is measured at the end of the connecting rod at four points.

elements.label: text
elements.text: On each rotation of the main shaft through 90°, the run-out should not exceed 0.25 mm. If the run-out is greater than is allowable, the carrier is to be replaced or straightened. When checking the carrier and connecting rod for proper mounting on the loom, a gauge and a ruler are used. The distance from the connecting rod surface to the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 223

elements.label: text
elements.text: ruler is checked at four positions of the carrier. The difference in readings should not exceed 0.6 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The rapiers are mounted at the moment of picking when the main shaft is in 0° position (here, the rapiers must completely be set apart).

elements.label: text
elements.text: If the position of the rapiers is to be adjusted, the unfixed carrier is turned in respect to the vertical shaft. After the adjustment has been completed, the carrier is secured with bolts and a pin. The axes of symmetry of the rapiers, connecting rod, planetary and sun gears must be on the same straight line. An adequate adjustment is made by turning the sun gear in the slots in respect to the sleeve. The proper displacement of the rapiers is checked by the manual smooth turning of the sleeve shaft.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The penetration of the rapiers into the shed or their displacement to the level of the extreme reed dents must occur simultaneously from both sides (the admissible difference is not more than 5 mm). As they enter into the shed, the rapiers must not come in touch with

elements.label: text
elements.text: the reed and must slide on the reed only with their cover plates made of textile-based laminate. The clearance between the nozzle of each rapier and the interior top wall of the guide must be equal to 2 m m . The rapiers are adjusted in height by changing the number offgaskets

elements.label: text
elements.text: between the carrier flanges and the shaft. The clearance between the nozzle and the interior wall of the guide from the side of the breast beam must he at least 1 mm. When the main shaft is at anJangle of 180°, the rapiers must occupy the extreme position in which they are brought together, and the distance between the rapier ends must be equal to 2-5 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When checking the air duct system, the loom main shaft is turned to 270°* the right- and left-hand top guards are opened and inserting

elements.label: text
elements.text: 224 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: a wooden bar between the carrier and the back wall of the guard one of the planetary mechanisms is braked, which is followed by brak­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing of the loom main shaft. It is necessary to ascertain the reliability of braking when the friction clutch is fully engaged since checking and adjustment are carried out with the motor on. Next, the righthand starting crank is shifted to the left along the slot, but in no case should it be drawn towards the operator. In its new position the orank is locked by inserting a wooden wedge. When the compressor

elements.label: text
elements.text: is working, the pressure according to the gauge connected with the receiver should not be under 35 kPa at full stroke of the compressor piston. If the pressure is lower, it is necessary to locate the point of air leakage by feeling with the palm the jet of leaking air. The leakage is eliminated by tightening the bolt joints and by replacing the gasket or packing rings, especially under the carrier and rapier.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the loom in the same position, the rapiers are checked for maximum rarefaction. For this, the hose connected with the compound pressure-and-vacuum gauge is fitted first on the nipple of the right-hand rapier and the nipple is turned until a zero reading is obtained on the gauge scale. For creating the vacuum, the nipple is tightened clockwise over a quarter of a turn at which the pressureand-vacuum gauge readings should not be under 25 kPa. Next, the hose from the pressure-and-vacuum gauge is introduced through the shed and fitted on the pointed end of the left-hand rapier. Turning

elements.label: text
elements.text: the nipple a maximum vacuum is created in the rapier; the readings of the pressure and vacuum gauge should not be under 10 kPa. After the adjustment of the rapiers is completed, the loom must be released from the stop and the guards are to be closed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The preventive inspection and repairs of the rapier drive is carried out in the following order: the level of oil and its quality are checked in the drive box; the clearances and meshing of bevel gears and planetary drive gears are checked; the position of the rapiers in respect to their guides, the clearance between the rapier cover plates and reed, and the proper displacement of the rapiers throughout the length are checked; the good sealing of the system is ascertained and the adjustment of the rapiers for maximum rarefaction as well as the good and clean condition of air canals is checked; the proper lubrication; and the good state of all bolted joints are verified.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The rapiers to be repaired are removed from the loom and sent to special repair shops where it is established whether the rapiers must be partially or completely disassembled, the worn-out parts are replaced and the rapiers are assembled and adjusted. The adjustment of the rapiers after repairing is carried out on a special stand made as a table with air duct from the shop mains 4 (Fig. 437). The left rapier nozzle is inserted in socket 6 to which the compressed air is supplied and using the pressure regulator 3 connected by hose with the pressure gauge 2,readings of 40 kPa are obtained. On the rapier

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 225

elements.label: text
elements.text: end a rubber hose 5 is fitted running from the pressure and vacuum gauge 1.The maximum vacuum in the rapier is adjusted by tightening and unscrewing the nipple. The readings on the pressure and

elements.label: text
elements.text: vacuum gauge scale should not be under 20 kPa, and if the readings are lower, the rapier should be assembled anew or rejected. During rapier checking, the pressure gauge readings may deviate and in this case the air supply must additionally be adjusted according to pressure gauge reading (40 kPa).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The right-hand rapier is mounted in the same way, with the difference that the rubber hose 5 is fitted on the rapier nipple. The pressure according to the gauge must be equal to 60 kPa and to the pressure-and-vacuum gauge not under 34 kPa.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The timely and properly dozed lubrication of the pneumatic rapier mechanism ensures a long and trouble-free operation. Lubrication is

elements.label: text
elements.text: carried out in conformity with the schedule in which the periodicity of lubrication and the kind of lubricant used are stipulated. For the lubrication of the right- and left-hand rapier driving boxes, automobile gear box oil is used. Oil is changed every six months and

elements.label: text
elements.text: added as need occurs. The oil level in the shells must correspond to the middle of the scale on oil indicators. The right-hand box is filled with 250 c m 3 and the left-hand box with 750 c m 3 of oil. The plugs, oil indicators, inspection covers must properly be tightened and fitted to bearing surfaces to avoid oil leakage. The ball bearings of the vertical shaft, of the planetary gear shafts, of the carrier and rapiers are to be lubricated with cup grease every six months. For greasingthe vertical shaft bearings, it is necessary to turn out one of the bolts attaching the carrier to the shaft and to insert in its place a special

elements.label: text
elements.text: adaptor reducer with an oiler. Oil is supplied with a grease gun until

elements.label: text
elements.text: 226 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: it appears in the bearing clearances. The grease coming out of the bearing must be eliminated. The penetration of the grease in the air ducts to the rapiers is absolutely unallowable because the conditionsfornormal yarn laying would be impaired. If nevertheless grease has penetrated in the air ducts it must be carefully eliminated by wiping the canals of the rapiers, connecting rod, carrier, and vertical shaft. It is also necessary to check the presence and condition of oil packing rings and collars.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Slay Mechanism

elements.label: text
elements.text: JSlay mechanism of the CTB shuttleless loom. The slay serves as a guide for the flight of the inserter with the weft yarn through the shed and effects beating-up of weft yarns to the fabric fell. The main condition for the long and trouble-free operation of the slay guide consisting of a row of plates forming a canal for the passage of the weft inserter is its coaxiality with the picking and receiving boxes and its proper mounting. The adjustment is carried out as follows. With the main shafts at 0° in narrow looms, or at 35° in wide looms, the weft inserter is extracted through the plug and next having turned the main shaft to 70° (50°) from the side of the receiving box, the gauges AyB and C are consecutively introduced into the guiding dents of the slay (Fig. 138). Further, the shaft is turned to 150° (110°) and the gauge A is displaced along the slay guide in the sense of the picking box. The dents impeding the free passage of the gauge are replaced by new ones. When the gauge reaches the picking box it is shifted in the weft inserter guide. The gauge must freely enter into the guide. On the displacement of the gauge horizontally in respect to the guide aperture, the extreme slay swords are released by shifting the slay beam in horizontal direction, or steel gaskets

elements.label: text
elements.text: are inserted between the slay swords and beam. If the slay is mounted higher, the two extreme swords are removed and the coaxiality is obtained by sawing off the point of seating. The displacement of the gauges B and C is effected in the same way.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The backlash is eliminated by

elements.label: text
elements.text: disassembling the slay mechanism. Worn-out bushings are replaced by new ones. For bushing replacement a special puller

elements.label: text
elements.text: (Fig. 139) is used consisting of a shaped nut 2, bolt 5, pipe 4 and washer 3. The shaped nut 2 is inserted inside the bushing so as to have its rims butting against the edges of the bushing. Next, the bolt 5 is inserted in the hole of the washer 3 and the latter together with the bolt is placed in the pipe 4 so that the washer rims rest on the pipe. When the bolt 5 isturned into the shaped nut 2 the latter begins to move to the right pressing out the bushing 1 from the box 6.For inserting a new bushing into the box 6,the shaped nut 2 is placed inside the bushing and inserted in the interior part of the box 6; the bushing edges are preliminarily pressed into the box opening by slightly knocking with a copper hammer. After this, the washer 3is pressed to the exterior box and the bolt 5 is inserted into the washer hole by screwing it into the shaped nut 2 mounted from the interior side of the drive and thus displacing (press-fitting) the bushing in the hole of the box 6.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 139. Diagram of puller for replacing bushes of slay mechanism for

elements.label: text
elements.text: CTE loom

elements.label: text
elements.text: If both cams (the cam and countercam) are turned over a full revolution and the clearance remains the same but exceeds the allowance of 0.03 mm, it is eliminated by choosing an adequate top roller (the bottom rollers must remain the same). If the clearance between the cam and roller varies in magnitude the greatest clearance shows the wear of their surface. In this case, the camshaft must be replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When replacing the gland body in slay boxes or the gland in the frame, the latter is pressed out from the slay box. For this, in the side face of the gland body, holes are drilled with a thread M6 cut inside. The screws are then turned into the holes so as to have their side face butting against the ball bearing shell. On further rotation of screws, the gland body is pressed out. After the gland has been repaired and its body press-fitted in the slay box, the drilled holes are closed by screws and glue to avoid oil leakage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The slay mechanism ol shuttle looms. The slay mechanisms may be subdivided into fast reed and loose reed mechanisms; mainly a crank fast reed slay mechanism finds application.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To adjust the slay mechanism, the following requirements are to be satisfied. The slay shaft must be horizontally disposed, and must easily rotate in the bearings; its axial displacement should not

elements.label: text
elements.text: exceed 1 m m and radial swing — 0.5 mm. If the swing exceeds the

elements.label: text
elements.text: 228 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: allowable value, the bearings of the bottom shaft must be replaced. Longitudinal shift is eliminated by means of setting rings fitted on the slay shaft. The distance from the centre of the slay shaft to the flat on the slay sword heads must be equal to 600 m m and from theinside surface of the frame to the exterior surface of the sword— 25 mm. The carriers must be connected with the sword without misalignment. When the mainshaft crank is in back position, the swing of the swords with carriers must not exceed 1 mm, as otherwise the stud or bushing of the carrier bearing must be replaced. The angles between the reed and the wooden race as well as between the front and back of the shuttle boxes and metal races must be equal to 90°. For angle checking a square is used. The exterior ends of metal races 1 (Fig. 140a) must be 1.5 m m higher than the interior ends of the wooden race. The races (two metal races and a wooden one) form a smooth curve throughout the whole length. In the middle of the wooden race 2 the clearance is equal to 2.5 mm, on both sides at a distance of 250 m m from the middle— 2.3 mm, and at points of metal race abutment with the wooden race— 1.5 mm. These clearances are checked with the control ruler 3 placed on both ends of the metal races. The gap between the bottom edge of the ruler and the surface of the races must correspond to the dimensions indicated in Fig. 140a. If the actual dimensions differ from the recommended ones, the wooden race is replaced by a new one. The surface, of the wooden race must be free from indentations; the place of metal race

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 140. Positioning of slay recess and declination of shuttle boxes backs

elements.label: text
elements.text: abutment with the wooden race is made flush. When the ruler 3 (Fig. 140b) is placed on the ends of the shuttle backs, a clearance formed between the ruler 3> the reed 4 and the shuttle walls 5 is called the slay declination. T h e declination in the middle of the w o o d en race is equal to 2 mm, at a distance of 275 m m on both sides from the middle— 1.6 mm, and at the points of shuttle backs abutment with the reed— 0.5 mm. When the ruler is laid on the shuttle

elements.label: text
elements.text: box swells, the clearance should show from 4 to 5 m m which is called the swell declination.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The centre of the shuttle tip in the box must be in the middle of the metal race slot. The clearance between the shuttle box fronts and shuttle must be equal to 2-3 m m at the entry of the shuttle into the box. The exterior surface of the weft fork grate must coincide with

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 229

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1ZT#

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 141. Diagram of slay mechanism in type P loom

elements.label: text
elements.text: the smooth curved line of the shuttle backs and reed declination. The angle of sword oscillation must be equal to 11°. The deflectors guiding the shuttle into the shuttle box must be mounted on the sword so as to obtain a distance of 2 m m between the upper edge of the shuttle back wall and the deflector. The rod protecting the shuttle from falling-out must be disposed 10 m m above the temple and must not come in contact with the warp yarn. When the swell belts and the check strap are worn out (the wear is allowable over 1/3 of the belt initial thickness) they must be replaced. Broken carrier rods are repaired by welding or replaced by new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Slay mechanism of a pneumatic loom. The upper part of the mechanism carries the confuser and the reed attached by special bolt-pins. When the bushing 5 is worn-out (Fig. 141), it is replaced by a new one which is press-fitted into the connecting rod 6.For the installation on the loom of the rocking pipe 8, the crank 4 with the gland 2 is inserted into the sleeve and the set ring 3 is put in place. Next, the bolts 1 are screwed into the crank 4 leaving a gap of 40 m m

elements.label: text
elements.text: 230 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: from the bolt head to the crank surface. After greasing the crank

elements.label: text
elements.text: bevel surfaces and the pipes, the rocking pipe 8 is drawn by the bolt 1 over the crank 4 until the distance from the bolt to the crank surface is equal to 14-17 mm. If in this case the bolt turns easily enough, it means that the bevel surfaces are not mating correctly and that the pipe is not fixed on the crank and must be replaced. If no spare rocking pipe is available, a soft foil is inserted under the bevel surfaces, the pipe is again fitted, the bushing is shifted to the left, the nuts 7 are tightened and the setting conductor is extracted. This done, the pipe must easily rotate, but without axial shift.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In pneumatic looms, to avoid air leakage from the left-hand cabinet, glands of different sizes are used. At the time of repairs, these glands must be replaced. Usually the glands are fitted on the shaft

elements.label: text
elements.text: neck from smaller to greater diameter which may cause damage of the gland inside surface.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For fitting the glands on the shafts special bushings with one tapered end may be used. The exterior diameter of the polished bushing must strictly suit the diameter of the shaft on which the gland is to be fitted. In this case, the gland will easily pass from the bushing onto the shaft surface. The field of use of such bushes and their dimensions are given in Table 12.
