elements.label: text
elements.text: The reed attached in the slay beam is subjected to considerable loads especially in high speed looms (up to 1000 N and more) and also to vibrations. Moreover, the reed dents are rapidly worn out by running against the warp yarns. The main disarrangements of the reed are: the failure of soldered seams, slackening of fixtures, shattering and breakage of dents. The longevity and reliability of reeds m a y be increased by using reinforced (wider) chromium-plated dents (of 4 m m rather than 2.8 m m wide), or by employing glues instead of soldering to fix the reed dents. The second method is the most efficacious from the point of view of reed reliability. Moreover, the

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 231

elements.label: text
elements.text: reed worn-out parts can easily be replaced without wasting much time. In silk looms available are reeds having dents coated with wear-resistant and anticorrosive chromium. The reeds working in the conditions ofhigh humidity have dents of stainless steel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warp protector motion of a shuttle loom. This motion pro­

elements.label: text
elements.text: tects the warp yarns from breaking if in weft beating-up the shuttle would remain in the shed or would not completely enter into the shuttle box. W h e n the warp protector motion comes in action it causes loom stoppage.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The adjustment of the warp protector motion must be carried out so as to satisfy certain requirements. The stop rod must easily rotate in bearings and its longitudinal shift must not exceed 1 mm. At the moment when the warp protector nibs exercise their action on the stop pad frogs, the distance from the fabric fell to the reed must be 65-67 mm. (Knocking of the warp protector nibs against the frogs.) The distance between the warp protector pad and the frame must be equal to 20 mm. At the moment when the warp protector nibs come in contact with the pads, the latter should move forward not more than 10 m m , as otherwise knocking against the frame can occur. W h e n the shuttle completely enters into the shuttle box, the warp protector nibs should be 2-3 m m above the stop pad frogs. When there is no shuttle in the box, the warp protector nibs must be 1-1.5 m m above the edges of the pads and simultaneously must approach both frogs;

elements.label: text
elements.text: if this clearance is impaired, the protector pad nibs come in touch with the pad which is unallowable. There should be no clearance between the adjusting bolts of the protector fingers and the swells of the shuttle boxes. The springs of the shuttle box swells must be adjusted for a minimum effort just sufficient for returning the swell and stop rod in initial position after the working travel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: W h e n the stop rod nibs knock against the frogs, the warp protector motion must rapidly disengage the starting cranks; for this it is necessary that a clearance of 1-2 m m is maintained between the lug 1 (Fig. 142) and the stand 2. Provided the stop rod is properly set, the warp protector nibs must freely lower on the pads without spring assistance. The proper adjustment of the warp protector motion is checked as follows: with the loom motor off, the starting cranks are

elements.label: text
elements.text: 232 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: engaged and turning the main shaft the warp protector nibs are brought to the frogs; having ascertained that the nibs approach simultaneously the frogs, using the handwheel the operator should turn the main shaft and the warp protector nibs must knock off the starting handles through the intermediate of the stop pads.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the absence of the shuttle in the shed both nibs must tightly rest on the frogs. If one nib does not rest on the frog, it is necessary to release the shell fixture, and slightly turning the stop rod press it to the frog, after which the shell must again be rigidly fixed. If the pads move with difficulty or the springs are slack, the warp protector nibs may be broken. In this case, they must be replaced with new ones. The stop protector pads may be broken if the rubber dampers are worn-out, the rods 3 (see Fig. 142) of the pad 4 are improperly mounted, and the pad strongly swings on the frame. The insufficient liftof nibs causes the wear of their bottom parts and of the pads. In case of improper adjustment and lengthy operation of the loom, the working faces of the frog nibs, as well as the rubber damper of the pads, become worn-out and must be replaced with new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warp Delivery and Cloth Take-up Motions

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warp delivery motion in the CTB shuttleless and ATIIP rapier looms. The warp delivery or let-off motion used in these looms is of the negative action, i.e. it lets off the warp from the weaver’s beam depending on the tension applied. This motion is designed to maintain the adequate tension of the warp and to ensure its automatic supply in accordance with the fabric winding by the cloth take-up motion.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The adjustment of the warp delivery motion is effected as follows. With the main shaft at 200° the highest point of the boss 9 (Fig. 143) should be opposite the roller 1.At this moment, the roller must be

elements.label: text
elements.text: pressed to the highest point of the boss and the link 7 must occupy the middle position in respect to the shaft 6 or must be somewhat higher. The distance between the neck of the backrest and the thrust

elements.label: text
elements.text: plate 3 must be 15-20 m m . W h e n the link is lowered (before the roller presses against the boss) the backrest neck must closely fit the thrust plate 3 and the dimension ashould be equal to 50 mm. This dimension is set by turning the eccentric bushing 11.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disarrangements in the warp delivery motion result in irregular warp supply or jamming of weaver’s beams. The causes of warp irregular delivery and consequently of fabric defects such as set marks, starting marks, cross streaks, may be the result of boss wear, i.e. the appearance of a horizontal area on the surface (see Fig. 143); the wear of friction cover plates 10 causing a slight braking of the driven disk and its slippage by inertia; the getting of oil on the fric-

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 233

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 143. Diagram of warp delivery motion for CTB and AT IIP looms

elements.label: text
elements.text: tion disks; a strong wear of friction rings on the driving and driven disks and the jamming of weaver’s beams.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The boss wear is eliminated by building up a metal layer on the horizontal areas with further grinding on a grinder so as to obtain

elements.label: text
elements.text: a strictly adequate profile. For removing the disk with the boss, the nut attaching the disk 8 to the roller 4 is released, and by tapping on it the disk is disconnected from the roller. Next, the cover of the weaver’s beam bearing is removed and the disk is extracted. When the friction cover plates are worn, the warp delivery motion is dis­

elements.label: text
elements.text: assembled, the worn-out cover plates are removed and new ones are fixed in their place. The best results are obtained by using cover plates cut out from a copper-asbestos (woven) belt. Worn-out fric-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 234 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: tion rings are also replaced by cover plates cut of copper-asbestos

elements.label: text
elements.text: belt. By using such cover plates the useful life of the friction clutch is increased 5-6 times.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Weaver’s beams jamming is usually caused by articles accidentally fallen in their gearing, by weaver’s beams catching the medium bearing bracket, the radial run-out of gears due to the absence of one bolt in the weaver’s beam barrel, gears, or weaver’s beam shaft couplings and also by the noncoincidence of the weaver’s beam bolts with the gear and coupling bolts. With the proper assembly, the bolts must be on one side. In the course of loom operation, the link

elements.label: text
elements.text: lowers due to the progressive wear of the friction cover plates. H o w ever, the friction cover plates are not completely worn out and may be still used. In this case the body 5is removed, the wedge is knocked •out (the one which is usually driven from outside) as well as the fixing lever 2, and a wedge is driven in from the inside which allows the inclination of the lever with the roller in the direction of the boss. This displacement of the wedge ensures a considerable increase in the useful life of friction cover plates.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The warp delivery motion in automatic shuttle looms. These looms are provided with two types of warp delivery motion or regulators for tensioning and letting-off the warp, i.e. planetary and worm wheel let-off motions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Planetary regulator or selected let-off motion. At the installation and adjustment of the planetary regulator, it is necessary to observe the following recommendations. The regulator shaft 1 (Fig. 144) and the roller 17 of the warp feeler must easily rotate in the bearings without misalignment and longitudinal shift. The weaver’s beam gear 27 and the underbeam gear 25 must mesh with their initial circumferences so as to have a clearance of 2 m m between the head of the teeth on one gear and the tooth root on the other gears. Both gears must be flush in width. The flange of the beam 26 must not contact the underbeam gear 25,the bottom link 23must easily rotate on the regulator shaft and the top link 5 on the spindle 6. No longitudinal displacement of links is allowed. The clearance between the rims of the top and bottom links must be equal to 8 m m and the tie rod 24 must easily move inside this clearance. The link roller 4 must also easily move along the slots of both links. The warp feeler 15 and lever 22 must be attached on the roller 17 so that the distance (L) between the centre of the top link spindle 6 and the link roller 4 should be as follows:

elements.label: text
elements.text: L, m m

elements.label: text
elements.text: Winding diameter of warp on the beam, m m

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 235

elements.label: text
elements.text: Thus, the size L depends on the winding diameter of the warp on the weaver’s beam: the smaller is the warp winding diameter, the greater is the dimension L and vice versa. The foot 14 of the warp feeler must rest on the warp yarn wound on the weaver’s beam. When the weaver’s beam is empty, and the feeler foot rests on the beam pipe, the link roller 4 must not fall out from the link slots and must be 4-5 m m above the bottom slots. The pawls 3 and 2 of the bottom link must be disposed on the ratchet feet over all their width

elements.label: text
elements.text: 236 Chapter Six

elements.label: text
elements.text: so that one pawl butts against the tooth and the second is in the middle of the adjacent tooth.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The bottom link is adjusted in working position with the slay in extreme front position and the warp released. The link is adjusted so that it butts with its upper arm against the limiter arranged in the bottom part of the left-hand frame. At this, the eyelet 20 is rigidly connected with the drawbar 21 leaving a clearance of 2-3 m m between the interior surface of the eyelet slit and the exterior surface of the finger 19. Next, the slay is shifted in extreme back position at which the finger 19 must easily and freely move in the eyelet slit and the eyelet must shift in the direction of slay sword movement only under the action of the back rest 11. The drawbar 21 and eyelet 20 must not contact the roller 17. For increasing the warp tension the springs 8 and 7 are clamped by the nuts 16. Rarely the warp tension is increased by shifting over the back rest 11 in the seats of the bracket 10 in the direction of the shaft 12 or also the drawbar 9 in the extreme right-hand hole of the pressure lever 13. The tension of springs 8 and 7 is checked by pressing with the hands on the back rest; when the pressure is released, the link and leverage system of the regulator must return into initial position. The angle between the pressure angle 13 and the draw­

elements.label: text
elements.text: bar 9must be equal to 90° and the warp beam rod must freely rotate in bearings without longitudinal shift. The longitudinal shift of

elements.label: text
elements.text: the back rest should not exceed 2 mm.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation the following disarrangement may occur: wear of the ratchet teeth and pawl working surfaces; pawl breakage; oil penetration on the brake pulley; wear of the leather on both braking blocks; thread deterioration on both end nuts. The worn-out parts are repaired or replaced by new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Worm-type warp let-offmotion. In this kind of motion the planettype mechanism is replaced by a worm couple, which is simple in design, reliable in operation and easy to adjust. The instructions for the adjustment of the worm-type warp let-off motion are the same as those for the planet type motion, because the process of warp yarn let-off and tensioning remains unchanged.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Warp delivery motion in pneumatic looms. The initial warp tension is created by the force of the spring 6 (Fig. 145) which may

elements.label: text
elements.text: be adjusted by the nuts 10. The force of the springs 6 must be the same from both sides, as otherwise the back rest will misaligned which will affect the loom operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To ensure the normal operation of the warp tension and let-off motion the initial clearance between the head of the adjusting bolt 5 and the finger must not exceed 8 mm. By turning the nuts 10 actuating the spring 6 through the intermediate of the screw 8 and the rest9itispossible to adjust the warp tension during machine running. To obtain a smooth operation of the motion provided on

elements.text: the shaft from the exterior side of the frame are inertia disks 7 with a mass ensuring slight slippage of the braking block at the time of braking. The disks have a crank for turning the weaver’s beams by hand.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the warp delivery motion the most liable parts subject to wear are the gear shafts, the braking wheel 7, the adjusting bolt 5, the brake block 2 and the shaft 3. The mechanism parts which have been removed during disassembly should be washed and cleaned from fluff and dirt (especially the gear toothing). All the other parts are replaced when they are worn out. The glueing of plugs on the brake block is facilitated by a simple arrangement. The brake blocks are fitted on a rod and a metal plate is pressed above by wing nuts leaving them in this position for 15-20 hours until the glue has completely dried.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cloth take-up motion of the CTE shuttleless and ATI1P rapier looms. This take-up motion is of the positive type. At the time of repairs, the take-up motion is disassembled and worn-out parts are replaced by new ones, or restored. Due to the difficult rotation of parts in the bearings or to gears tightly connected with each other, thick places may appear on the produced fabric. In this case, the take-up motion is disassembled, worn-out parts are replaced and using

elements.label: text
elements.text: a handwheel the take-up motion is checked for easy running. If

elements.label: text

elements.text: the motion turns easily without jamming itmeans that the cloth take-up motion is properly operating.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The cloth take-up motion of a shuttle loom. The proper adjust­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ment of the cloth take-up motion is checked as described below. The take-up roller 3 (Fig. 146) must be easily turned by hand and

elements.label: text
elements.text: its axial shift must not exceed 1 mm. There must be an equal clearance over the entire length between the take-up roller and the breast beam. The meshing of gears must be such that ensures a clearance of 1 m m between the tooth head of one gear and the tooth cavity of the other gear; all the gearsmust be properly engaged

elements.label: text
elements.text: in teeth width and must easily rotate. The pawl must engage the ratchet over the full width of the teeth, as otherwise the ratchet and pawl teeth will prematurely be worn-out. The proper engagement of the slide block 2 and ratchet is achieved by turning the bushing on which the take-up drawbar 1 is mounted with a clearance not over 1 m m . W h e n the slay is in back position, the distance from the slide block 2 to the tooth of the ratchet 9 must be 5-8 mm. This distance is adjusted by shifting the lever 4 and modifying the length of the rod 6. The amount of fabric letback is adjusted with the bolt 7 by increasing or reducing the free stroke of the mispick control pawl 5.When the slay is in rear position the clearance between the end of lever 4 and arm 8must be equal to 3 mm. The same clearance is set between the right-hand end of the rod 6 and arm 8.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main kinds of disarrangements are: fixture slackening, wear of take-up roller bearings, wear of the slide block <2, gear toothing, pawls and ratchets. As the take-up motion is repaired, worn-out parts are replaced by new ones.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The wind-up motion of pneumatic looms. This motion is intended for winding the produced fabric on the cloth roller. At the time of repair, the take-up roller mechanism is disassembled to get the wornout parts replaced. Disassembling is started by turning off the nuts of the screws 3 (Fig. 147). Next, the bearings 2 are lifted, the pressure roller with coating 5 is extracted, the screws 6 are turned out, the bushing 12 is shifted to the right, the left-hand pin is removed from

elements.label: text
elements.text: If a complete disassembly is necessary, the screws 14 are turned out, the cover 15 with the packing ring 13 is taken-off and the worm gear 1 with the shaft is extracted from the recess. The screw 3 is turned into the eyelet 11. After complete disassembly, the parts must be washed and worn-out parts are to be replaced or restored.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Most frequently it is necessary to completely replace the grater 9 and partially the technical felt. After removing the grater, the take-up roller is cleaned and a new grater is wound bearing in mind that the cut on the grater may he straight and inclined. If the cut is straight, winding may be started from any side of the take-up roller, but if the cut is oblique, the pointed part of the cut must be

elements.label: text
elements.text: directed in the sense of movement as otherwise the fabric will slip on the surface of the grater. The right-hand side of the take-up roller may be wound over a length of 200-300 m m with one or two layers of fabric (above the grater) to avoid clogging of the grater with weft threads from the fringe. The grater must be tightly and smooth­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ly tensioned on the take-up roller and must be attached from both sides with screws or nails, for which purpose end wooden plugs are provided on the take-up roller.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Technical felt on the pressure roller 4 is rarely worn out over its whole surface and most frequently its right-hand side is worn out and replaced. To ensure a better fastening of the felt on the rollerr a complementary winding of one or two fabric layers may be made and impregnated with joiner’s glue. To avoid folds a whole piece of technical felt should not be wound on the pressure roller. The felt should be cut in strips 80 m m wide and 5400 m m long.

elements.text: During the operation of the cloth roller friction clutch, the spiral spring bent ends might become broken and the tension roller and

elements.text: its shaft worn. Worn-out parts are replaced by new ones.

elements.text: Cydograms of Loom Operation

elements.label: text
elements.text: The normal work of looms is possible only when the operation of all mechanisms and devices is strictly timed. It means that the beginning and end of all operations of mechanisms, devices and parts must take place at certain moments which are correlated with the action of the loom, as a whole.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The loom adjustment may most easily be discussed by correlating the action of its mechanisms with only one unit the operation of which is strictly determined and does not depend on the operation of all other mechanisms and devices. Such a working unit is the loom main shaft, one revolution of which corresponds to the loom working period, i.e. to the period when one fabric element is formed. The circumference corresponding to one revolution of the main shaft is divided by 360°, and the extreme front position of the reed is adopted as the beginning of motion, i.e. the moment of weft beating-up to the fabric felt. Expressing the beginning, duration and end of loom mechanism action by means of the main shaft angle of rotation, we obtain a cyclogram of loom operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For the correct and reliable operation of the loom the precise Interaction of its individual parts and mechanisms is essential. For this, zero match marks are used which must coincide at the time of assembly. The mark on the cam side face must be set opposite the zero match mark on the shaft. To check the operation of separate parts and mechanisms of the loom, their proper assembly during erection and repair, and work interaction of any mechanism,

No deviations in the operation of mechanisms from the established parameters of the cyclogram are allowed.

In shuttleless C T 6 looms the count is started at the moment of slay displacement from the back position (0°). elements.text: CHAPTER 7

elements.label: text
elements.text: METHODS AND KINDS OF REPAIRS

elements.label: text
elements.text: OF TEXTILE EQUIPMENT

elements.label: text
elements.text: 1. Methods of Textile Machinery Repairs

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair methods employed determine the procedures carried out during the restoration of textile machinery. There are two main kinds of repair methods: the individual repair method and the unit repair method.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The individual method of repair is a procedure when parts and units removed from the machine for repair are mounted on the same machine after repair (with the exception of those parts and units which are worn out and have to be replaced by new ones). This method presents the following disadvantages: lengthy idle time, high cost and low quality of repairs. With individual repairs, parts are repaired and manufactured on a separate basis, the machine assembly and adjustment after repair is a difficult and complicated operation and takes a great deal of time and effort; the mechanization of repair is hard to achieve because the design dimensions of machine units and joints are changed; no interchangeability of parts is possible. The individual method of repair is presently used only for huge and nonstandard machines.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The unit repair method is that at which preliminarily prepared, adjusted, and tested new or repaired units and parts are installed on the machine instead of the removed units and parts. The dismantled parts and units are sent to specialized workshops for processing and repairs. In the case of the unit repair method, the idle time is shorter than at individual repair, the cost of repair is lower and its quality higher. There is no idle time due to the absence of units and parts as the repair and manufacture of parts and units are made in advance and with partial interchange; for mounting the parts and units inconsiderable machine adjustment is required and the repair operations may largely be mechanized.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The unit repair method is most efficacious in the case when the equipment is of the same type and when the main units ofthe machines manufactured by different machine-building plants and of differ­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ent models are unified. If the equipment is of different types and its basic units are not unified, the repair method by unit is rendered difficult as a great reserve of different units and parts must be kept

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 247

elements.label: text
elements.text: in stock. The parts cannot be interchanged so that a careful adjustment must be carried out. Therefore in these cases the repair method

elements.label: text
elements.text: by unit involves only the preparation of requisite units in advance.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The in-line unit repair method comprises the restoration, mating and working-in of the most labour-consuming units and mechanisms in workshops equipped with special machines, stands and fixtures. In these special workshops the repairs are carried out in-line, thus ensuring their high efficiency and good quality. The repair teams in this case have only to mount the units on the machines to be repaired and to proceed to their adjustment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The duration of unit repairs that find application in the textile industry may be of one shift and two shifts; and may be carried out on stands and by sections.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With one-shiftrepairmethod,the machine s repaired only by one team of workers during one shift (usually, the first shift) independently of the shifts in the main production departments. Repairs during one shift involve the longest downtime, though the duration of repair m a y be short. This kind of repair m a y be used for machines of any purpose and design. With repairsduringtwoshiftsan enlarged team is divided in two subteams; each subteam would repair the machine continuously during the first and second shifts. The duration ofrepair remains the same, but the machine idle time is twice less as compared with the idle time involved in one-shift repair. With standrepairthe machine isremoved from the base and transported to the repair platform or into the repair shop where all the necessary operations are carried out on a specially equipped stand. A reserve machine is installed instead, and the repaired machine is sent for keeping in reserve. The idle time of the machine in repair does not practically affect the production capacity of the department, as the working post remains idle only during the time which is necessary to remove the old machine and to install the new one. Stand repair is mainly carried out in the case of looms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With by-sectionrepair separate large parts or sections are repaired in consecutive order. The repairs are carried out during nonworking days and shifts (usually, during days-off); and in the periods between these days and shifts the machine continues to work. The main ad­

elements.label: text
elements.text: vantage of the by-section method of repair is that there is no idle time during the working hours. When repairing separate sections, the scope of work to be done should be chosen so that it can be fulfilled in the course of a day-off, and the machine after repair may be prepared for operation for the next work shift. The by-section repair may prove more time-consuming than any other type of repair as it is necessary to disassemble the preliminarily repaired sections or units for their adjustment and mating with those section

elements.label: text
elements.text: and units which have been repaired during the given day-off. The by-section repair method requires the especially careful preparation

elements.label: text
elements.text: 248 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: of parts, units, materials, tools, devices, etc., good organization of work, and is used mainly for those machines which are not numerous at the enterprise, and their stoppage for repair during working days may interfere with the work of the enterprise (for instance,

elements.label: text
elements.text: opening ranges, cards and sizing machines).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 2. Purpose and Structure of the Repair Service in the Textile Enterprises

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair service in textile enterprises operates according to the system of scheduled preventive repairs comprising preventive technical measures, the maintenance and inspection of equipment. Thus, the system of scheduled preventive repairs includes the technic­

elements.label: text
elements.text: al maintenance, current, medium and overhaul repairs of textile machinery.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Technical maintenance comprises cleaning and oiling of machines, elimination of small disarrangements, adjustment of units and mechanisms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Current repairs provide for the elimination of small disarrangements, the adjustment of units and mechanisms, and the repair of rapidly wearing parts and units according to schedule.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With medium repairs the machine is partially disassembled, the worn-out parts are replaced, the units and the machine as a whole are inspected and adjusted (see the list for the medium repair of CTE shuttleless looms in the Appendix).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The overhaul repair comprises full disassembly of the machine, replacement of all the parts, assembly, checking and adjustment of

elements.label: text
elements.text: all units and mechanisms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The duration of periods and cycles between repairs for the equipment in different fields of the textile industry is established depending on the kind of machines and the working conditions. In most cases, at three shift work the periodicity of medium repairs is from 3 to 6 months, and that of overhauls from 2 to 3 years. The repair service at textile enterprises carries out not only the repair of equipment, but also its modernization, erection, manufacture ofnew parts, and the restoration of worn and broken parts, and executes the orders of the maintenance service for keeping the equipment in good working condition.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair service at a textile enterprise comprises central repair workshop and mechanical repair department workshop. Central repair workshops are organized at integrated mills and large enterprises with several production departments. At small enterprises repairs and the maintenance of machinery in different departments

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the enterprise are carried out by mechanical Tepair workshop.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 249

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main purpose of the central repair workshop is to supply nonstandard spare parts for the main and complementary textile equipment operating at the enterprise. All standard’and some nonstandard

elements.label: text
elements.text: (difficult to manufacture) parts of the technological equipment are supplied to the enterprise through centralized cooperation with plants producing these spare parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The central repair workshop repairs intershop (interfactory) service lines, intershop transport and power equipment, and is responsible for the modernization of equipment, mechanization of labourconsuming processes, the introduction of new techniques, rationalization and inventions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Textile enterprises are equipped with various machines of Soviet and foreign make different in design, precision, and finish of their parts. The requirements set towards the service life of machine parts demand use of stronger materials. Moreover, the manufacture of textile goods requires the use of a great number of technological equipment and machines'at an enterprise. This means that thousands of different spare parts must be available at a textile enterprise.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3. Repair Shops in Spinning Mills

elements.label: text
elements.text: The central repair workshops of large textile enterprises are producing new, nonstandard and spare parts, while the repair workshops of smaller enterprises repair and restore units and parts, and manufacture the simplest special-purpose parts. The repair workshops of most enterprises may be subdivided into general-purpose and specialized repair workshops. In general purpose workshops various jobs relating to the production and repair of parts are carried out, while in specialized shops a limited number of units and parts are restored and repaired (they are frequently called unit repair workshops). Fig. 152 illustrates the structure of a repair workshop in a cotton spinning mill.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair workshops make use of versatile equipment and tools mainly. The system*of multipurpose assembly devices is designed to assemble equipment for metal-cutting machine tools exclusively from standard parts. Owing to the efficacious choice of the part design and of the materials and thermal treatment employed for their manufacture it is possible to create convertible devices allowing a multiple use of standard parts. The parts of the versatile assembly

elements.label: text
elements.text: devices run the following course of closed cycle: storage of parts— assembly of devices— use of devices— disassembly of devices— storage of standard parts— assembly of devices (of another design), and so on. The basic parts of versatile assembly devices (plates, angles, supports, straps, and so on) are manufactured of high-alloy steels, heat-treated, and have a high wear resistance and strength so as to serve on the average not less than five years. Devices are

elements.label: text
elements.text: 250 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 152. The composition of repair workshops in a spinning mill

elements.label: text
elements.text: assembled from such elements practically obviating the stage of design and the process of part manufacture from metal. For instance, versatile assembly devices are used for drilling, milling, grinding, and turning.

elements.label: text
elements.text: During assembly, it is necessary to have a drawing of the part and the description of technological process indicating the sequence of operations, and also the blank of the part. Technological charts are essential for assembly fitters to follow the sequence of operations and choose the proper processes. The precision of part processing using the versatile assembly devices is dependent on two factors: the precision with which the parts of the versatile assembly devices have been manufactured and the adjustment of the device dimensions by the fitter. As a rule, all the parts of the versatile assembly devices have a high class of precision, so that the deviation of two slots in

elements.label: text
elements.text: a plate from the nominal value is to be within ± (0.01-0.02) mm. The deviations in the parallelism and perpendicularity are approximately the same. On combining several parts in one device, the parts are chosen with positive and negative allowances and the total deviation in the dimensions of parts used in the device does not exceed 0.01 mm. This is achieved by adequate choice of parts and by the use of measuring plates for assembling the versatile assembly devices, so as to obtain parts with a finish of second and third classes of accuracy.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 251

elements.label: text
elements.text: General Purpose Repair Workshops

elements.label: text
elements.text: The composition of general purpose repair workshops is almost the same for all enterprises in different fields of the textile industry.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The fitting shop. This shop deals with repair and manufacture of most different parts. For this reason, the technological process is based on the production of separate parts by versatile equipment. All the jobs connected with the restoration of machine spare parts

elements.label: text
elements.text: are carried-out on orders received from the repair workshops and operating personnel. In some enterprises separate parts are manufactured according to quaterly or monthly requisitions. The establishment and employment of standard process charts for the restoration of standard parts ensures better quality and lower cost

elements.label: text
elements.text: of machine repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The washing and defect locating department. Worn-out and broken parts which have been removed from machines sent for repairs have their surfaces coated with lubricant, dust, and fluff, showing the traces of wear and corrosion. This renders difficult the location of defects, impairs the quality of repair and labour conditions. Hard dirt particles are eliminated by scraper and metal brushes. To remove fluff, dust and unhardened lubricants the parts are washed in ordinary alkali baths which are cheap and fire-safe. Good quality and high efficiency of part degreasing are obtained through the employment of ultrasonic baths.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Gleaned and degreased parts are checked for defects at testing posts equipped with instruments, repair templates and gauges. Thus, ball bearings are inspected by means of a special instrument,

elements.label: text
elements.text: and the gear tooth thickness, by a repair gauge. The run-out of spindle blades, axles and other cylindrical parts is determined by means of a setting prism and indicator. The interior defects (cracks

elements.label: text
elements.text: and cavities) are detected by means of ultrasound and magneticfield flaw detectors. For storing during a lengthy time the most important parts (such as ball bearings, chains, etc.) are coated with slushing compounds.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The welding department. In the welding department, worn-out and broken parts are restored by electric arc d.c. and a.c. welding units. Practical experience in many enterprises has shown that for better welding the department must be equipped with the following machines and units: a movable welding transformer for a.c. welding or a d.c. welding rectifier, a welding post, a fitter’s bench, a roughing and tool grinding machine with flexible shaft and a rack for storing materials, tools, and parts. In repair departments of large enterprises it is efficacious to provide a unit for dip transfer surfacing of worn-out shafts and fluted cylinders.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The tool dispersing room. This room serves for keeping materials and restored parts prior to their sending to the shop store. High-

elements.label: text
elements.text: 252 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: precision instruments and tools are kept in the tool dispensing room of the central repair workshop from which they are received when necessary for temporary use in the departmental repair workshops.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Specialized Repair Workshops

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair of spinning machine units is rather time-consuming. This is explained not only by the great number and the complicated unit design, but also by the need of their repair either directly at the machine, or in a fitter’s shop. It is good practice to release the repair teams from this job and to pass this work to a special staff of fitters working in a specialized workshop. In this way, repair is made less laborious, its quality improves and the idle time of machines during repair is reduced because of replacing the units from the machine sent for repair by other units which have been preliminarily repaired and run-in.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The card repair workshop. The design of cards is convenient for repair by units. The most complicated units requiring labour-con­

elements.label: text
elements.text: suming repair may be removed from the card and transported to a special workshop usually consisting of two departments— the flat repair department and the department repairing all other units.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Flat repair departments are available in all cotton spinning mills equipped with cards. The following operations are carried out at the time of repair of flats in the workshop: cleaning the needle fillet from dust and fluff; wiping the grid bars with rags; sorting out flats to determine the wear of the needle fillet; straightening bent grid bars; removing the worn-out needle fillet and covering grid bars with a new fillet; restoring seats; grinding flat needles, and inspection.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The department is equipped with a machine for removing fluff and dust from the carding fillet, with fillet grinders, and a machine for stripping and covering with carding fillet. The machine production speed inflat coating stripping is 40 flats per hour. If the grid bars are slightly bent they are straightened in a screw press.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The quality of carded cotton sliver may be strongly affected by the wear of grid bars, which is eliminated by metal building-up or by coating with styracryl with subsequent milling or grinding the recesses.

elements.label: text
elements.text: There has been established a process for repairing the bearing surfaces of card flats and for levelling the base of flat grid bars by using polymer materials. Here, the life of repaired grid bars is three or four times that of new ones, moreover these grid bars allow the use of modern semirigid and rigid fillets that require no grinding due to which quality of the card fillet rises. A specialized production department (the equipment lay-out in this department is shown in Fig. 153) has been created for the repair and straightening of flat grid bars with polymer materials, and a polymer composition using

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 253

elements.label: text
elements.text: Special departments for the repair of other card units a r e o r g a n i z e d at enterprises where the number of cards is more than 300. The repair of combing boxes, licker-in units, speed boxes, doffer couplings, combs, licker-in reducers, feeding arrangement and drive of flats is most efficient in workshops equipped with special devices ensuring, rather than on cards themselves.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the course of operation, the following disarrangements frequently occur in the comb box: the wear and breakage of glands, oil leakage, wear of the shackle, sector and cam shafts. In the lickerin unit the whole-metal saw-toothed fillet becomes blunt and destroyed, and the ball bearing clogged and worn-out. The main defect observed in the speed box is the wear of the lead-gear spindle, gears, and bearings. In the reducer of the licker-in, the reducer shaft bearings, and toothed gearings are worn-out. In the flats feed and drive reducers the worm shaft is frequently jammed and broken due to the clogging of lubrication ports. Burrs appear on the doffing combs and the needles are broken.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The repair of machine units is accelerated by employing different devices. A device has been designed for the rapid pressing-in of bushes and rollers into the hubs of pulleys and sprocket gears. The

elements.label: text
elements.text: 254 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fig. 154. Device for press-fitting of bushings and rollers in hubs of pulleys,

elements.label: text
elements.text: gears and sprockets

elements.label: text
elements.text: device (Fig. 154) consists of two stands 1 with welded-on four ribs 2 (for reinforcing the rigidity of stands made of channel 124), the nut 3 rigidly fixed in the stand, the screw 4 with a small pitch 2 = 4 m m and with a diameter of 40 m m for progressive pressing-in and -out of the cone of thrust hearing 6 (which freely rotates on a 20 m m diameter ball) and of the stop-screw for allowing the bearing to freely rotate at the end of the screw without slipping down during the operation. The device is rigidly fixed to the bench 8. In pressing-in and -out the bushings with different diameters, flange inserts 7 with inside holes of different diameters are used, and in pressing-out the rollers from pulleys and gears— steel fingers of various diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When pressing-in a bush into a gear, a flanged insert of adequate diameter and without interior hole is chosen and is inserted in the aperture of the ribbed stand. Next the gear is placed so as to make its interior hole coincide with the thrust bearing centre. Turning the crank the worm is put in motion and by the intermediate of the thrust bearing it presses in the bushing into the gear. Pressing-out is done in the same way, the only difference being that the flanged insert is chosen with a hole of adequate diameter. This device facilitates the work of turners, reduces the time necessary for the replacement of bearings and protects the hubs from premature wear.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The slotting of interior key-ways in gears of big diameter (up to 1000 mm) may be carried-out by means of a special device. A lathe chuck is attached with three bolts on a special angle which has its other surface attached on the table of a planer by means of two bolts with the vice removed. The gear to be machined is attached in the

elements.label: text
elements.text: lathe chuck by cams on the exterior diameter of the column. The mandrel with the cutter passes through the interior hole of the chuck and effects slotting.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 255 Methods and Kinds of Repairs

elements.label: text
elements.text: Comb repair shop. Such shops are available in flax and woollen spinning mills, for repairing the needle fillets of cards, drawing and roving frames and scutchers, blenders, spreading machines, and beamers. In the flax spinning mills the needle plates are repaired by replacing broken needles, eliminating hooks on thejneedle ends and dressing the combs and plates. In combers new needles

elements.label: text
elements.text: are soldered to the plates and set in the drums. For removing the combs from the plates of Fig. 155. Diagram of unit for restora drawing frame an eccentric ing needle fillets by electropolishing manual or a mechanical press is used to shear the rivets. Different gripping and other devices are employed for repairing combs. Straightening is effected on fitter’s benches. Blunt needles and bent needle ends are restored by a honing stick and more rarely by electric polishing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Electric polishing makes the needles sharper and improves the class of roughness (up to 0.63) owing to which the produced fibre is of higher linear density. The bath for electric polishing (Fig. 155) is installed either in the electroplating or comb shop. The bath dimensions correspond to the maximum size of comb plates. This process is carried out with high speed as several combs may be simultaneously charged into the bath and the time of electropolishing does not exceed 2.5 min.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Depending on the method of their fixing broken needles are removed by pressing-out, unsoldering or by heating and removing

elements.label: text
elements.text: all the fillets on the plastic base from the plate. The holes in wooden plates are drilled in a table top drilling machine. The plates of the combing segments in combers are repaired by dressing and the needles are soldered. For this reason, enterprises in which such machines are available make use of a muffle electric furnace of laboratory type in the repair shop.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Spindle and flyer repair shop. Spinning and twisting spindles are the main parts of a spinning frame. Considering the high speed of spindle rotation which must be effected with great precision strict requirements are set towards the manufacture and restoration of spindle separate parts. Especially strict rules should be observed in the manufacture of the spindle blade, as its amplitude of oscillationsmust not exceed 0.15-0.3 m m depending on the whirl diameter. The thrust bearing and the spindle blade heel cone are subjected to heavy and rapid wear, while the seat under the roller bearings and

elements.label: text
elements.text: 256 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: the exterior surface of the whirl experience much less wear. The wear of thrust bearing and heel cone as well as the residual flexure

elements.label: text
elements.text: of the spindle increases the amplitude of spindle blade oscillations which results in an increase of the breakage rate. The main technological operations at the time of spindle repair are as follows: cleaning and degreasing; disassembly and sorting of defective parts; spindle blade straightening; eliminating the wear of the seating under the roller bearing and of the heel cone by grinding, electric spark building-up or chromium plating; restoring or replacing the thrust bearing; replacing the roller bearing; grinding the whirl surface; assembly and running-in of spindles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: At the time of repair of roving flyers the following operations are carried out: cleaning the slots and pipes from fluff and dirt; restoring the bushing, saddle, and reversing motion by clamping and buildingup; dressing the feet and repairing the branches; checking the distance between the branches set apart, static and dynamic balancing of flyers.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Prior to the repairs, the spindles and flyers are cleaned and degreased in the washing department. The following equipment is provided in the workshop for spindle and flyer repair: tables for dismantling and sorting the units; a machine for straightening spindle blades, a machine for grinding the heels of spindle blades; a unit for electric spark hardening of parts; a machine for lapping and polishing spindle blade heel cones after electric spark building-up and for removing the burrs from the flyer branches; a device for pressing-out and -in thrust bearings; a device for flaring bushings in and out, and a stand for spindle running-in. A universal machine has been devised for flyers repair. Moreover, the shop has at its disposal a set of tools and instruments for sorting defective parts, an electric grinder and racks for storing units and parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The electric spark building-up of the heel cone surface is made with an electrode of hard alloy. Building-up is begun with three course layers and wound up with one or two finish coats. In this case, the thickness of the built-up layer is 0.2 m m which allows further machining to be made by lapping and polishing the heel cone.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair shop for fluted rollers, shafts and rods. The quality of produced goods and the machine efficiency greatly depend on the quality of repairs of fluted rollers in spinning, roving and drawing frames. Specifications allow the following run-out of fluted rollers: 0.15 m m for spinning and roving frames and 0.1 m m for drawing frames. The fluted rollers of cotton spinning frames aremade of carburized steel or of surface hardened steel. The roller shafts of flax spinning frames are made of chromium plated steel and the fluted posts of stainless steel or chromium plated steel.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main defects in the working rollers are: flexure, wear of necks and fluted surface, damaged threads and breakage of shanks.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 257

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shaft corrosion in the fluted section is observed on the rollers of flax wet spinning frames. The restoration process depends on the kind of deterioration, but dressing is obligatory for almost all rollers. Worn necks are frequently restored and in flax spinning frames the post fluted surface is knurled.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In addition to fluted rollers different shafts and rods are restored in that workshop. As the fluted rollers and shafts are restored many operations require the use of the equipment installed in the fitter’s workshops (for straightening, building-up and machining). For this reason, usually no separate workshop for roller repair is provided and the rollers are repaired in the fitter’s shop. Disassembling, dressing and assembling of fluted rollers are most conveniently carried out on machines of a spectral design and the restoration of a fluted surface, by means of knurling devices. The restoration of the flutes on the heat-treated front drawing roller is possible after staff annealing, and in the event of inconsiderable wear— by chromium plating. The building-up of worn necks can efficiently be carriedout by using a welding unit mounted on the lathe slide.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Workshop for repairing small units of spinning frames. Such a shop or department is organized in big mills for more than 150 000 spindles. In workshops of this kind tension rollers, ring plates, lappets, cradles and separators are repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Tension rollers are made of tin or carbolite. Tin rollers have a short useful life and their repair requires the use of special devices for unscrewing nuts, reaming of beads, dressing, elimination of indentations on the side face and rim. All these operations are carriedout on a universal stand. In carbolite tension rollers, the roller and shaft ball-bearings are worn-out, the rims are broken and contaminated, and the grease hardens. These rollers are inspected at the time of overhaul and medium repairs of the frame. The rollers are disassembled, washed in straw oil and packed with new grease and the worn*out bearings are replaced. For repairing such rollers the shop

elements.label: text
elements.text: must have a mechanized washing unit and also hand presses for press-fitting and pressing-out ball bearings.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The ring plates are mainly repaired at the time of overhauls when rings, ring holders and antiballooners are replaced. The shop where

elements.label: text
elements.text: the ring plates are repaired must be equipped with devices for rapid screws turning— in and out. Before removing spindle brackets or weighting arrangements from the spinning frame they must be cleaned from fluff and dirt, and if necessary the bearings must be replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Roller eovering shop. These workshops are intended for the repair of top or pressure rollers of spinning, drawing and roving frames and combers, as well as cleaning rollers and the drawing unit aprons. As rollers are repaired the following main operations are carriedout: cleaning and sorting; washing and wiping of bushings and shafts; checking the wear of rollers and selecting roller couples; stripping

elements.label: text
elements.text: 258 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: and covering with new coatings; grinding of new coatings; cold and hot rolling-up of rollers; lubrication of spindles; cutting-off the felt from the clearers and glueing on a new felt, checking the rollers for hardness, cleanliness and machining precision; selection of the roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: set in the frames.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The roller covering shop must be provided with the following equipment: a machine for stripping the elastic covering from the top pressure rollers of spinning and roving frames and fitting on new ones (production speed of 500 pcs/h); a device for stripping and fitting elastic coatings on top rollers with solid bushings (production capacity of 800-1200 pcs/h); a device for hot rolling of coverings in assembly with a metal bushing (production capacity of 300 pcs/h); a semiautomatic machine for sorting the coatings according todiameter in assembly with the bushing of top rollers of spinning and roving frames (production capacity of 900 pcs/h) and a semiautomatic machine with production capacity of 2000 pcs/h, a grinder with production of 150 pcs/h; a device for grinding the coatings of top rollers for spinning and roving frames in assembly with metal roller

elements.label: text
elements.text: and spindle; a machine for coating, washing (production capacity of 1400 pcs/h); a device for fitting elastic coatings on drawing rollers

elements.label: text
elements.text: (production capacity of 120 pcs/h; a device for cutting away the coatings from metal rollers of drawing frames and combers (production capacity of 300 pcs/h); a device for cutting the felt for clearers; a device for cleaning the clearers of roving and spinning frames; a device for applying glue on clearers; an instrument to check for run-out the top rollers and coatings in assembly with the bush in spinning, drawing and roving frames; a machine for hot calendering of the top roller coatings (production capacity of 800 pcs/h), etc. In addition to the main equipment there are also provided drying and exhaust cabinets, a bath, an electric stove for glue preparation* tables, racks for roller storage, and trucks for their transport.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Repair workshops for the spinning heads of the frame Efl-200. The design of the open-end spinning frames Bfl-200 differs from that of ring spinning frames. The main working organ of these frames is the spinning head (centrifuge), which serves for the supply, opening and attenuation of the sliver and for the formation and reinforcement ofthe yarn by twisting. As the repair of the spinning heads directly on the frame is difficult, a high labour efficiency and good quality of repairs cannot be ensured.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The workshop for repairing the centrifuges of the B3-200 spinning frame is provided with the following equipment: stands for the pneumatic cleaning and balancing of the combing drum; a device for polishing the centrifuges and separators and also for rolling-up the centrifuges; tables for dismantling and assembling centrifuges and units; a table drilling machine; racks for storing reserve centrifuges and parts. All the assembly posts are provided with a set of

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 259

elements.label: text
elements.text: tools, gauges and devices. Cars accommodating 60-70 centrifuges

elements.label: text
elements.text: are used for their transport to the working posts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The frame 5/1,-200 comprises also other units, the repair of which is more conveniently carried-out in repair workshops, as for instance, the reversing box, reducer, yarn guides, etc. At the time of repairs, these units are washed and ball bearings, glands, gaskets, gears and shafts are replaced. The free running bush and ball bearings of guiding pulleys are also replaced.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 4. Weaving Equipment Repair Workshops

elements.label: text
elements.text: The structure of these workshops is almost the same as that of spinning equipment repair shops. The repair workshops in flax and silk weaving mills somewhat differ from those mentioned above as they have departments for the repair of Jacquard machines and of the winding heads of automatic weft winders.

elements.label: text
elements.text: General Purpose Repair Workshops

elements.label: text
elements.text: The main purpose of fitter’s shops is the restoration of worn parts and the manufacture of single spare parts of simple design. The fitter’s workshop comprises several departments: the machine department has one or three screw-cutting lathes, a milling cutter, a shaper,

elements.label: text
elements.text: an upright drilling machine with a drilling diameter up to 35 mm; the fitter’s department is equipped with a fitter’s bench, table

elements.label: text
elements.text: drilling and tool grinding machines, a hydraulic erection press for up to 100 kN, mechanical and hand lever shears or a metal sawing machine.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The welding compartment is equipped with a welding transformer or converter, a welder’s table, a rough grinding machine with flexible shaft, a bench and a rack for storing parts, electrodes, tools and devices.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the washing and defect detecting department, the same equipment is used as in the similar department of the spinning enterprise. The store of materials and the tool dispensing room are also organized in the identical manner.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Specialized Repair Workshops

elements.label: text
elements.text: In weaving enterprises special repair shops have been created for the labour-consuming restoration of separate most largely used units.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the case of shuttle looms the following units and parts should be repaired in specialized shops: the batteries, dobbies slays, crankshaft with bearings and carriers, the picking motion and reed; in pneumatic looms— the driving box; in rapier looms— the compressors, rapiers and shedding motion; in automatic weft winders— the yarn tension

elements.label: text
elements.text: 260 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: devices and conveyors; and in sizing machines— the speed variators and reducers, etc. Most of these units are restored at the time of overhaul.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Loom units repair shop. In this shop the loom units are prepared and run-in. For restoring the shuttle loom units (type AT looms) stands are used for repairing and running-in the weft change motion, the dobby, the Jacquard machine and for the assembly and checking of the crankshaft with bearings. The box of the pneumatic loom (type P) is run-in on a stand of frame design. The compressor of pneumatic rapier looms (type ATIIP) is repaired on a special control stand equipped with instruments for measuring the pressure of air supplied into the rapiers and for determining the temperature in the cylinder and piston rubbing zone. Rapiers are repaired on a stand, on which they are straightened and a plastic T-piece is fitted on the rapied rod.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Provided in addition to the stands are fitter’s benches and table top drilling and tool grinding machines. Heavy units are placed on the stands by means of a hoist with a lifting capacity up to 0.5 t. Racks and cabinets are provided for storing small units, spare parts, tools and material. Hand and special cars are used for transporting the units. Moreover, different enterprises have designed devices and appliances for various kinds of repairs such as a device for cutting splined shafts for looms ATI1P-100 on a gear milling cutter. With this aim, the device made as a three-cam chuck 2 (Fig. 156) with a centre 3 is fixed on the mandrel 4 screwed into the table of the gear milling cutter 5. The cut splined shaft 1 is fixed in centres and its end is clamped in the chuck. This universal device may be used for cutting toothing of different diameter gears.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Shop for the repair of equipment on stands. Unlike the individual method of equipment repair, the repair of equipment on stands ensures a sharp reduction of equipment idle time, a considerable amelioration of working conditions at repairs, as well as the high quality of repairs and improved organization of work at the time of loom repairs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 261

elements.label: text
elements.text: When looms are repaired on stands, they are lifted and transported by a special bogie-crane above the equipment and further the loom is transported in the shop on a hand or electric car. The loom is lifted or lowered by a winch or a motor supplied with current from the line or accumulators arranged in the bogie. If the width of the passages is sufficient for driving-out the loom from the row, simple jack bogies are employed which are attached to the frames. The loom is lifted and transported either manually or by an electric car. The equipment is repaired on stands at the time of overhaul which is very time-consuming. The number of stand platforms must suit the number of spare looms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In addition to the stands for loom repair, stands are also available for the repair and running-in of separate units. For carrying out small fitter’s jobs there are provided table drilling and grinding machines, fitter’s benches, electrified erection tools and devices, control tools and racks. The workshop comprises three departments, i.e. the washing department, the department for repair, running-in

elements.label: text
elements.text: on stands and for painting, and the store for keeping the parts.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Slay and shuttle repair workshop. This shop is provided in all enterprises equipped with shuttle looms, and serves for carryingout the repair of slay and shuttles and also for the manufacture and repair of different wooden parts. The workshop is equipped with a slotter, a scroll saw, a circular saw, a planer, a milling machine, an electric drill with a drill 23 m m in diameter, an electric glue boiler,

elements.label: text
elements.text: a table drilling machine, an electric grinder, scales for shuttle weighing, a universal machine for shuttle repair, joiner’s benches, and racks for storing slays and different materials.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Healds and reed repair workshop (pertains to the weaving mill only). It is equipped with a reed cleaning machine, a drop wire and heald cleaning machine, racks and tables for storing and repairing these units and parts. Frequently, reeds, healds and drop wires are cleaned and repaired in the premises of the drawing-in department of the mill.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 5. Organization of Repair Working Posts

elements.label: text
elements.text: The proper organization of the working posts is one of the essential conditions ensuring high labour efficiency of repair workers and excellent repair quality. The repairworkingpostis part of the workshop occupied by one worker orteam, by the equipment and other means which the worker or a team is using for repairs. A properly arranged working post must be equipped with all necessary technical facilities conveniently disposed for carrying-out the given process. Bepair workers have to operate either directly at the machine

elements.label: text
elements.text: to be restored (disassembly or assembly of units and mechanisms), or on vices for mating the parts, carrying-out small repairs, etc.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 262 Chapter Seven

elements.label: text
elements.text: When working at the machine, repair workers must have individual transportable cases with a set of necessary tools, gauges, small parts, wiping materials and others. A team must have at its

elements.label: text
elements.text: disposal a bench with vices (it is advisable to have a movable bench).

elements.label: text
elements.text: A movable general purpose bench has been proposed for use by repair fitters. It is made as a cabinet of 1000 X 630 X 850 m m in sizewith special boxes and drawers for storing fitter’s tools and spare

elements.label: text
elements.text: parts. The upper part of the bench is made of boards 40 m m in thickness, covered with 1-2 m m thick sheet steel and edged with steel angles to ensure strength and rigidity. Under the upper part of the bench there are provided two top drawers, each divided in four or two sections for storing small parts and fixtures. At the sides, there are cabinets with collapsible doors for storing fitter’s tools (files, drifts, cutting tools, etc.). Inside, the bench is divided by a shelf and wall in four sections. The top sections are intended for storing big tools (hammers, pullers, electric tools, and so on) and the bottom ones for storing big spare parts. At the front, the bench is closed with two doors. All the bench doors are made of 10 m m thick plywood and edged with a plank. To facilitate its displacement, the bench is mounted on a metal frame with four rubber-coated wheels. As an example, a list of tools, devices for repair teams and auxiliary materials is given below:

elements.label: text
elements.text: fitter'stools— fitter’s hammers (220 and 500 g), copper hammers (500 and 1000 g), chisel, grooving chisel, bastard and smooth files of different sections, a sawing machine and blades, screwdrivers, a set of standard spanners and socket wrenches, a set of special wrenches

elements.label: text
elements.text: (depending on the type and model of the machine), pliers, punches and different drifts, drills, centre punches, twist drills (in set), tap wrenches, threading dies and screw taps (set), tommy bars and mark­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing tools;

elements.label: text
elements.text: control and measuring instruments— steel straight edges (from 100 to 1500 mm), a steel metre and measuring tape, level, plumb bob, thin cord (string), caliper, internal gauge, micrometer, watch indicator with stand, feelers, a thread gauge, angle gauge, standard square, a set of special gauges (depending on the type and model of

elements.label: text
elements.text: the machine);

elements.label: text
elements.text: devices and auxiliary arrangements— standard and special pullers, jack, hooks, brushes, oilers and pans;

elements.label: text
elements.text: auxiliary materials—lubricating oil, chalk, emery paper, cup grease, rags, lining and wedges.

elements.label: text
elements.text: It is necessary to provide the working post with electric current supply and a socket to plug electric tools (electric drills, grinders,

elements.label: text
elements.text: etc.).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Methods and Kinds of Repairs 263

elements.label: text
elements.text: 6. Failure Prediction for Parts, Units and Mechanisms

elements.label: text
elements.text: Any assistant foreman knows that the preventive repair is a guarantee of trouble-free machine operation. Proper failure prediction is of great importance. There exist several methods of failure prediction, but they are all aimed at detecting the disarrangements in due time by their outward symptoms.

elements.label: text
elements.text: So for instance, let us discuss such a symptom as repeated breakages on the same spindle of a spinning frame. W h e n using the existing

elements.label: text
elements.text: method of yarn breakage determination in spinning frames, the repetition of yarn breakages on the same spindles is not registered and the causes of these breakages are not detected. However, this symptom means that some spindles do not properly operate. The existing methods of control must be replaced by control of each spindle at which the technical condition of spinning frames is si­

elements.label: text
elements.text: multaneously checked. When the breakage rate is irregularly distributed it may be considerably reduced, if in the course of check­

elements.label: text
elements.text: ing first of all faulty spindles are located and the disarrangements

elements.label: text
elements.text: are eliminated. For this in checking the Nos. ofthe spinning frame faulty spindles are registered indicating the date of checking and the No. of the side. These data are submitted to the foreman as­

elements.label: text
elements.text: sistant servicing the frame who must take the necessary measures for eliminating the disarrangements in spindle operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The aforedescribed method should be used everywhere as the prediction of disarrangements and defects in parts, units and mechanisms allows their location and elimination in due time, thus ensuring much saving in time and finance.
